# AUD-024 — Expanded full-scope audit of mhfe against the current coding guide

Original audit outcome: **159 confirmed findings** (6 medium, 153 low), 1 release-blocking.

Current remediation: **140 verified within the authorized scope**, **9 implemented pending real-browser verification**, **9 owner-deferred**, and **UI019 retained**. See [Remediation continuation](#remediation-continuation).

## Finding register

| Finding ID | Category | Kind | Severity | Recorded status | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AUD-024-SEC001 | SEC | finding | medium | open | An isolated secret command can still change the file system through extended attributes, file modes and timestamps (and through truncate by path on Linux 5.13 to 6.1), while SECURITY.md, README.md and the command summary state that every file write is refused (kernel-enforced) |
| AUD-024-SEC002 | SEC | finding | low | open | Every threaded Argon2 call (the browser package's fast-mode build argon2-mt.js and the native engine) leaves each lane's last block, unwiped, on the stack of the thread that ran that lane. The call's output, a round key, can be rebuilt from these bytes with one BLAKE2b. In the browser the residue survives the known answer that ends every operation and stays through session waits until the worker is terminated. Natively it stays until the next Argon2 call or until the process exits. Nothing wipes it, no check looks for it in the threaded build, and no document names it. |
| AUD-024-SEC003 | SEC | finding | low | open | The browser package's worker never zeroes the WebAssembly's dead shadow stack. The BIP39 seed, the BIP32 master private key and chain code, and the BIP39 passphrase (in PBKDF2's salt block) therefore stay in the worker's linear memory after a call returns and while a session waits for the page, although zeroing that stack between calls removes them and leaves the module and its sessions working. |
| AUD-024-SEC004 | SEC | finding | low | open | A seed phrase or password given as a command-line argument by mistake is repeated in full in the usage error on standard error. This includes the --path and --coin values, which the library deliberately refuses without repeating them (AUD-016-SEC001). |
| AUD-024-SEC005 | SEC | finding | low | open | The SHA-256, SHA-512, HMAC and BLAKE2b states that mhfe feeds with secrets are built without their crates' zeroize feature, so they are not wiped on drop. Measured: SHA-256's padded block of the BIP39 seed stays in the dead stack after wallet_check::phrase_passes. |
| AUD-024-SEC006 | SEC | finding | low | open | check_word::Repair derives Debug, so formatting a repair with {:?} prints the word of the password it restores or replaces, and the byte range of the typed word |
| AUD-024-SEC007 | SEC | finding | low | open | Every standard-input reader of the command-line tool goes through io::stdin().lock(). So a pasted secret line, and with --stdin every answer of the script (password, seed phrase, passphrase), stays whole in the standard library's 8 KiB stdin buffer, unwiped and unlocked, until a later read overwrites it or the process ends. Reading the descriptor into the tool's own locked buffer leaves no copy. |
| AUD-024-SEC008 | SEC | finding | low | open | The check-word repair answers, which show words of a password, are drawn through style::paint and a line format! that grow ordinary Strings, so each draw frees unwiped heap blocks holding the restored, replacement or typed word |
| AUD-024-SEC009 | SEC | finding | low | open | When the kernel refuses an isolation boundary a secret command needs (the Landlock write ruleset on a kernel without Landlock, or the seccomp socket filter), the refusal is reported nowhere: mhfe self-test still says 'Isolation enforced' without a '!', the startup checks pass silently, and the command summary leaves the boundary out with no warning |
| AUD-024-SEC010 | SEC | finding | low | open | The Windows build locks no secret memory and takes no step against crash dumps or other processes reading its memory, and the macOS build does not deny debugger attachment, although both systems offer equivalents |
| AUD-024-SEC011 | SEC | finding | low | open | On Linux, a zram swap device whose sysfs entry cannot be read (sysfs not mounted, or no sys/class/block/zramN) is treated as in memory, so mhfe gives no swap warning even though it cannot tell whether the device writes back to a plaintext disk |
| AUD-024-SEC012 | SEC | finding | low | open | On Windows the swap check returns an inspected, empty inventory without inspecting anything, so an unencrypted page file never triggers the swap warning before Argon2 runs |
| AUD-024-SEC013 | SEC | finding | low | open | mhfe new copies the chosen word out of its locked buffer into an ordinary heap string and keeps it there, unlocked, while it waits for the person to type the word never to use |
| AUD-024-SEC014 | SEC | finding | low | open | A random source is checked only by check_source's one-time two-block probe: a source that is then stuck makes uniform_below retry with no limit (a password draw never returns), and a source that is then stuck or fills only part of each buffer gives out a fixed or half-zero 24-word phrase without an error |
| AUD-024-FUN001 | FUN | finding | medium | open | The missing-word search with a master key fingerprint of the container's own wallet returns the first candidate that matches and never looks for a second. When two missing words of a 12-word container leave another candidate with the same 32-bit fingerprint before the real one, the tool shows that other container as the found container phrase, unqualified, and tells the owner to write its words on the copy. |
| AUD-024-FUN002 | FUN | finding | medium | open | compare_candidates starts the missing-word search's workers with Scope::spawn, which panics when the system refuses a thread. Under a process or pids limit, the CLI's start-up self-check then reports a false failure for every secret-handling command, and the search with the container's own wallet aborts the command. The wallet-check draw goes on with the threads it gets. |
| AUD-024-FUN003 | FUN | finding | medium | open | The password strength estimate counts every repeat of a group of characters that is not a list word in full, so passwords such as '1234 1234 1234 1234 1234' (51.76 bits, above four random dice words) or 'abcd' eight times are rated 50 bits or more and get no weak-password warning |
| AUD-024-FUN004 | FUN | finding | low | open | When a control group's memory limit can be read but its usage cannot, the Linux free-memory check takes the usage to be the limit and reports a measured-looking figure (the group's inactive cache, or 0 bytes) instead of none, so mhfe refuses every memory level for lack of memory it never measured |
| AUD-024-FUN005 | FUN | finding | low | open | Both fast-mode launchers (mhfe serve and packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py) read the checksum file and the page whole, with no size limit and no check that they are regular files. A checksum file of one valid line followed by megabytes of blank lines is accepted. A checksum file or page that links to /dev/zero is read until memory runs out, and a FIFO hangs both launchers. Where mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 or the page is oversized or not a regular file, the Python launcher ends with a MemoryError traceback instead of its documented refusal. |
| AUD-024-FUN006 | FUN | finding | low | open | The Python fast-mode launcher reads its checksum file in universal-newline mode, so a lone CR ends a line there but not in mhfe serve. A checksum file whose one line has only whitespace and a CR before the digest is served by mhfe-fast-mode.py and refused by mhfe serve. The comment that says the split matches Rust's str::lines is wrong, and no test covers the case. |
| AUD-024-FUN007 | FUN | finding | low | open | The Python fast-mode launcher reads a request head differently from mhfe serve. It serves heads that mhfe serve refuses: a Host name or value with U+001C to U+001F around it, a request line ending in more than one CR, a Host header found only after a bare-LF end of the head. It refuses or leaves unanswered heads that mhfe serve serves: a UTF-8 header value, a second Host after a bare-LF end, an LF-then-CRLF end. SECURITY.md and the launcher still say both keep the same rules, including the exact-Host rule. |
| AUD-024-FUN008 | FUN | finding | low | open | A rekey compares a wallet reference only with the reading the length rules give, not with every reading as the rehearsal check does. A 24-word phrase that also reads as a 12-word one is refused with REFERENCE_MISMATCH by its own fingerprint when the length is detected, although the rehearsal check of the same container says it matches. After AMBIGUOUS_LENGTH at a stated length, the address or fingerprint that the documents prescribe is likewise compared with that one reading only. |

## Review evidence

### Scope and methodology

The whole repository at the reviewed commit: the Rust library and command-line tool, the WebAssembly bindings and browser package, the check and build scripts, packaging, CI, the documents and the audit records, against the workspace rules and the current coding guide (every rule, the review-only ones included, applied to the whole repository), the specification in mhfe_spec, and the audit procedure above. The expanded workflow of the workspace audit rules ran on the owner's explicit request: every `CHECK-*` item had an owner; three waves (security and correctness; implementation, contracts and guide conformance; build, documents, records and an AUD-023 regression check) each ended with deduplication and adversarial verification of every candidate (one skeptic for low, three lenses — reproduction, contract, impact — for medium and higher, two of three needed); a completeness critic named uncovered areas for six gap reviewers; a second round was named but stopped, and the coordinator compared the confirmed findings for duplicates and severity. Review only: no tracked file changed during the audit; probes ran in a scratch folder, with a separate cargo target directory, and no full-cost Argon2 run.

Reviewers: secrets-native (60 files read), browser-isolation (71 files read), core-crypto (71 files read), spec-parity (65 files read), wallet-derivation (59 files read), api-contracts (61 files read), cli-ux (61 files read), guide-lib-core (59 files read), guide-lib-wallet (50 files read), guide-cli-infra (53 files read), guide-cli-commands (47 files read), guide-browser (60 files read), guide-tooling-js (92 files read), guide-tooling-other (75 files read), build-release (75 files read), docs-claims (74 files read), audit-records (27 files read), regression-aud023 (49 files read), gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue (52 files read), gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide (69 files read), gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser (39 files read), gap-1-unapplied-review-rules (52 files read), gap-1-aud023-required-verification-and-remediation-diff (81 files read), gap-1-cli-browser-feature-parity (71 files read).

Reviewers kept the commands their findings rely on through `AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh` (933 records in 205 evidence folders, local).

### Findings

#### SEC

##### AUD-024-SEC001 — Medium — An isolated secret command can still change the file system through extended attributes, file modes and timestamps (and through truncate by path on Linux 5.13 to 6.1), while SECURITY.md, README.md and the command summary state that every file write is refused (kernel-enforced)

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** medium.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI process isolation (src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs, protect/landlock.rs, protect/seccomp.rs) and its documented guarantee
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-07, RUST-10
- **Affected files and builds:** Native mhfe on Linux. Affected: every command with Needs::NOTHING, that is encrypt, decrypt, check, rekey, new, wallets, repair, repair-words, password and self-test (src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:299-303, 337-349), whether started directly (own namespace) or from the start menu (thread, src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:270-281).
  
  Code:
  - src/bin/mhfe/protect/landlock.rs:1-4 (module doc 'handles every right to change the file system'), 48-63 (handled rights: WRITE_FILE, REMOVE_DIR/FILE, MAKE_*; REFER only from ABI 2; TRUNCATE only from ABI 3).
  - src/bin/mhfe/protect/seccomp.rs:1-5 and 52-60 (the filter refuses only x32, socket, socketpair and io_uring_setup/enter/register).
  - src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:248-256 (Isolation::names 'no new file writes'), 385-393 (writes_refused relies on one probe), 455-460 (that probe only opens /dev/null O_WRONLY), 572-590 (isolate_thread).
  
  User-facing claims:
  - src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:419-437 (isolation_text: 'no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)').
  - src/self_check/process.rs:24-29 ('no network, no writes').
  - SECURITY.md:120-129 (123-124 'a Landlock ruleset that refuses every write to the file system (Linux 5.13 and later ...)'; 127-129 quote the summary).
  - README.md:133-134 ('kernel restrictions against new sockets and file writes').
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:788-789 ('no file writes').
- **Reproduction:** On Linux, from the repository root at b6fca69, with a scratch folder on ext4:
  
  1. Build: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<target> cargo build --locked --release.
  
  2. Real binary, command started directly: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-isolation-writes-repro/check.sh <target>/release/mhfe <scratch>.
  - The script compiles preload.c into <scratch> and runs `mhfe self-test` and `mhfe decrypt` (stdin /dev/null; decrypt is refused for want of a terminal before any round) with LD_PRELOAD=<scratch>/preload.so and AUD024_TARGET set to a 0600 file of 20 bytes.
  - On the first write()/writev() after PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS returns 1, the preload reports NoNewPrivs, Seccomp and whether uid_map is empty.
  - It then tries, in order: a socket, opening /dev/null and the target O_WRONLY, O_CREAT of a new file, setxattr(user.aud024-path, <public BIP39 'abandon ... about' phrase>), chmod 0644, utimensat to 1000000000, truncate(path, 7), and fsetxattr and fchmod 0640 through a read-only descriptor it opens after isolation.
  - The script then reads the attributes, mode, size and mtime back from outside.
  
  3. Menu-thread case: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<target> cargo run --offline --locked --release --manifest-path docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/isolation-writes/Cargo.toml -- <scratch>. This compiles landlock.rs and seccomp.rs unchanged through #[path] and applies them in a thread, as protect::isolate_thread does.
  
  4. ABI 1-2 truncate: check.sh also runs abi2-truncate.c, which applies the mask landlock.rs:48-60 builds for ABI 2 (and the ABI 3 mask as a control) and calls truncate(path, 0).
- **Expected behavior:** Sources for the expected behaviour:
  - SECURITY.md:122-124: a secret command runs 'under a Landlock ruleset that refuses every write to the file system (Linux 5.13 and later ...)'.
  - SECURITY.md:127-129 and settings.rs:427-436: its summary states 'no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)'.
  - README.md:133-134: 'kernel restrictions against new sockets and file writes'.
  - RUST-10 (Check: review): 'Landlock refuses writes to files other than the outputs it was asked for'; secret commands ask for no output file (Needs::NOTHING).
  - DOC-07 (Check: review): documents, help and messages 'claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides' ('an overstated guarantee is itself a security defect').
  
  So either every new change to the file system made from an isolated command is refused, or the documents and the summary say exactly which changes are refused.
- **Observed behavior:** Host: Linux 7.0.0-38, Landlock ABI 8.
  
  Real binary (v02, v03 and h01-check): Seccomp 2, NoNewPrivs 1, uid_map empty (own user and network namespace). Refused with EACCES: the socket, open /dev/null O_WRONLY, open target O_WRONLY, creating a file, and truncate (ABI 3+ handles TRUNCATE). ALLOWED: setxattr, chmod 0644, utimensat, and fsetxattr and fchmod 0640 through a read-only descriptor opened after isolation. Read back from outside: user.aud024-path and user.aud024-fd both = 'abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon about'; mode 640 (was 600); mtime 1000000000; size 20. In the same run, self-test printed 'Isolation  enforced', and decrypt went on to its normal 'no terminal' refusal.
  
  Menu-thread case (v04): with namespace false, setxattr, chmod and utimensat are ALLOWED as well; attributes user.mhfe-probe-direct and user.mhfe-probe-menu hold the phrase.
  
  ABI 1-2 mask (v05): truncate(path, 0) ALLOWED and the file went from 20 bytes to 0. The ABI 3 mask refuses it.
  
  Cause: Landlock has no right for extended attributes, mode, ownership or timestamps in any ABI, and none for truncate before ABI 3 (Linux 6.2). The seccomp filter refuses only socket, socketpair and io_uring calls. The only write read-back, writes_refused (protect.rs:387-393 via 455-460), opens /dev/null for writing. So the startup check and self-test confirm the 'no new file writes' boundary, and the summary keeps stating it, while these changes get through. On this host the baseline terminal suite shows that summary text on a real secret command (b11-terminal-suite-fast.log:23; scripts/terminal_suite/passwords.py:180-198).
- **Impact:** Defence in depth; the tool's own code writes no secret.
  
  Code running inside an isolated secret command (a compromised dependency or build, the case these boundaries exist for) can still store a phrase or password on the offline computer's disk. It can write it as a user extended attribute of any file the user owns, up to the per-attribute limit of the file system (64 KiB on ext4), or encode it in modes and timestamps; a later process with network access can collect it. On Linux 5.13 to 6.1 it can also truncate any writable file by path (data loss, or encoding data in file lengths).
  
  The documented guarantee, the '(kernel-enforced)' summary and the self-test's 'Isolation enforced' are stronger than what the kernel enforces.
  
  Prerequisites:
  - code already executing inside the mhfe process;
  - for attributes, a file system with user extended attributes (ext4, btrfs, xfs, tmpfs from Linux 6.6);
  - for the data to leave, a later networked process on the same system (on a live system without persistence the data is lost at shutdown).
  
  Why medium, not high: SECURITY.md:132-136 already says the boundaries 'restrict new access rather than guarantee containment of arbitrary compromised code', and the channel stays on the local computer. AUD-008-SEC001 (high) was a network egress bypass.
- **Evidence:** Evidence folder: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-isolation-writes-repro/, each log with its .command.json.
  - v01-release-build.log: cargo build --locked --release --offline is a no-op, so the binary is current at b6fca69 (sha256 1e29adfd59b7eba6995fc160bfabe273274f03c58a6ee843c4a3c683ffc2e33f).
  - v02-preload-self-test.log (exit 1): real `mhfe self-test` with the preload.
  - v03-preload-decrypt.log (exit 1): real `mhfe decrypt` refusal with the preload.
  - v04-harness-isolation-writes.log (exit 1): independent rerun of docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/isolation-writes; direct and menu-thread cases.
  - v05-abi2-truncate-mask.log (exit 1): ABI 1-2 mask lets truncate through, ABI 3 mask refuses it.
  - h01-check.log (exit 1, sha256 c462da7d…): kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-isolation-writes-repro/ (check.sh, preload.c, abi2-truncate.c, README.md).
  
  Scratch copies: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verifier-isolation-writes-repro/.
  
  Supporting:
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/secrets-native/h01-isolation-writes.log, s03-landlock-coverage.log and s11-self-test.log.
  - Baseline b11-terminal-suite-fast.log:23 ('isolation: a command started directly runs with an empty network', which asserts the summary 'isolated network, no new sockets or file writes').
  - Static trace of the line ranges listed under affected.
  - Kernel Landlock documentation (Documentation/userspace-api/landlock.rst): chmod, chown, setxattr and utime cannot be restricted, and truncation could not be denied before ABI 3.
- **Recommended fix:** Make the claim true, or make it exact.
  
  Preferred:
  - Extend the seccomp filter (seccomp.rs, tests list) to refuse with EACCES the calls that change the file system without opening a file for writing:
    - setxattr, lsetxattr, fsetxattr, removexattr, lremovexattr and fremovexattr, plus setxattrat and removexattrat where the architecture has them;
    - chmod, fchmod, fchmodat and fchmodat2;
    - chown, lchown, fchown and fchownat;
    - utime, utimes, futimesat and utimensat;
    - truncate, needed below Landlock ABI 3.
  - Consider ftruncate and fallocate as well. Secret commands open no file for writing (Needs::NOTHING), so none of these calls is needed.
  - Add a read-back of the new refusals to writes_refused/IsolationCheck, for example an fsetxattr on a read-only descriptor of a file the process can read, which must fail with EACCES from the filter.
  
  In any case, word SECURITY.md:122-129, README.md:133-134, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:788-789, landlock.rs:1-4 and the summary text in settings.rs:427-436 so that they state exactly what is refused, for example 'no file opened for writing, created, renamed or removed', and any remaining metadata channel.
- **Required verification:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-isolation-writes-repro/check.sh <mhfe> <scratch> prints 'PASS: every file-system change tried was refused' and exits 0. If truncate below ABI 3 is handled by seccomp, the ABI 1-2 part also passes.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/isolation-writes exits 0 in both the direct and the menu-thread case.
  - A unit test in protect.rs shows each added call refused with EACCES in an isolated thread, while the unisolated test thread can still do them.
  - mhfe self-test still reports 'Isolation enforced', and a probe-downgrade unit test covers the new read-back.
  - cargo test, clippy and the terminal suite fast cases pass.
  - SECURITY.md, README.md and the summary text match what the harness shows (DOC-06/DOC-07).
- **Related findings:** AUD-008-SEC001
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 on the real release binary (sha256 1e29adfd…, rebuilt as a no-op with --locked; tree clean apart from untracked harnesses). I loaded a probe with LD_PRELOAD into `mhfe self-test` and into `mhfe decrypt`, which is refused for want of a terminal before any round. The probe stands for code running inside an isolated command, and it ran after isolation was in force: NoNewPrivs 1, Seccomp 2, empty uid_map, so the process had its own user and network namespace. Inside it, the socket, opening /dev/null or the target for writing, and creating a file were all refused with EACCES. setxattr, chmod, utimensat, and fsetxattr and fchmod through a newly opened read-only descriptor were all ALLOWED. Read back from outside, both user.* attributes held the public test phrase, the mode was 640 and the mtime 1000000000, while self-test still printed 'Isolation enforced'. Rerunning the kept secrets-native harness gave the same results in the start-menu thread case. Applying the exact Landlock mask that landlock.rs:48-63 builds for ABI 1-2 lets truncate through: the file went to size 0; the ABI 3 mask refuses it.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - ruleIds: CORE-24 does not apply (the tool's own code writes no secret), and RUST-11 is not clearly breached (the Landlock ruleset itself is read back; what is wrong is how far the claim reaches). The rule actually broken is DOC-07 (claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides), along with RUST-10.
  - SECURITY.md:24 ('never writes them to files') is about the tool's own behaviour and is not contradicted, so I removed it from expected.
  - The self-test does not say 'every write refused'; it reports 'Isolation enforced' on the strength of a single open() probe.
  - Added locations: protect.rs:248-256 and 450-460, process.rs:24-29, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:788-789, and the fd-based variants (fsetxattr, fchmod).
  
  Severity stays medium per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: the defect is reproducible, but the prerequisite is code already running inside the process, the channel stays on the local disk, and SECURITY.md:135-136 already disclaims 'containment of arbitrary compromised code'. That falls short of the 'serious security impact' required for high.
  
  None of the earlier audits reported this: AUD-023 CHECK-SEC-002 recorded 'Landlock handles every file-system-changing right' as passed.; confirmed: I confirmed this on the real release binary at b6fca69, not only through the harness. I preloaded a hook on socket() into the release build of mhfe; the tool's own probe calls socket() after isolate() has run. Inside the isolated thread (NoNewPrivs 1, Seccomp 2), setxattr wrote the public test phrase to a file. chmod, utimensat, fsetxattr on a read-only descriptor and ioctl FS_IOC_SETFLAGS also got through. Opening for writing and truncate were refused with errno 13. In the same runs, `mhfe self-test` printed 'Isolation enforced' and the summary of `mhfe encrypt --stdin` printed 'isolated network, no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)'. The encrypt command was refused before any Argon2 round. The reporter's harness reproduces this unchanged (exit 1).
  
  The contract really does say otherwise. SECURITY.md:122-124 states a Landlock ruleset 'that refuses every write to the file system (Linux 5.13 and later ...)'. The summary (settings.rs:427-434) states 'no new ... file writes'. src/self_check/process.rs:24 says 'no network, no writes'. DOC-07 forbids claiming 'stronger guarantee than the code provides'. The kernel's own header (/usr/include/linux/landlock.h:314-319) says Landlock cannot restrict chmod, chown, setxattr or utime. It also says TRUNCATE exists only from ABI 3 (landlock.h:232-235; landlock.rs:61-63). The seccomp filter (seccomp.rs:52-60) refuses only socket, socketpair and io_uring, so nothing else covers these calls. An extended attribute holding arbitrary bytes, written by a new path-based call, is a write to the file system in any reading. It is not an already-open descriptor, which is the only exception SECURITY.md:132-135 names. The finding therefore stands.
  
  I narrowed it in four ways:
  - I dropped RUST-11. The Landlock ruleset that is applied is read back; the defect is the scope of the claim, not an unverified protection.
  - I dropped CORE-24 and SECURITY.md:24. They concern the tool's own handling of secrets, and the tool writes none.
  - I added DOC-07 as the governing rule, with RUST-10 as secondary.
  - I added variants and locations: fsetxattr and inode flags through read-only descriptors, process.rs:24, BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:788-789 and self_test.rs:246.
  
  I corrected the claimed extended-attribute capacity: a 4 KiB block on a default ext4, 64 KiB with ea_inode. Severity stays medium. This is a reproducible break of a documented security guarantee, but it stays on the local computer, needs code running inside the process, and is bounded by the disclaimer in SECURITY.md:135. It is not an AUD-023 finding: AUD-023 CHECK-SEC-002 passed Landlock coverage of Landlock's own rights only. The truncate variant on Linux 5.13 to 6.1 rests on the kernel header and was not run (this host has ABI 8). No full-cost Argon2 run is needed.; confirmed: I tried to refute this and could not. I reproduced it on the real release binary at b6fca69, not just on the modules compiled alone. I preloaded a probe into `mhfe encrypt --stdin --pim 0 --mem 0` and fed it three words, which it refuses before any Argon2 round (exit 2). The summary printed 'Isolation  isolated network, no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)'. Inside the isolated process, /proc/self/status showed NoNewPrivs 1 and Seccomp 2. Opening /dev/null for writing, opening a UDP socket, opening the file for writing and truncate were all refused with EACCES. setxattr by path, fsetxattr on a descriptor opened read-only, chmod and utimensat all succeeded. Read back from outside: both extended attributes hold the BIP39 test phrase, the mode is 644 and the mtime 1000000000. Rerunning the candidate's own harness reproduces both the direct case and the menu-thread case. linux/landlock.h (lines 312-319) states that chmod, chown, setxattr and utime cannot be restricted by Landlock. TRUNCATE exists only from ABI 3 (lines 232-235), so the truncate variant on Linux 5.13 to 6.1 rests on the kernel documentation; I did not execute it on this ABI 8 host.
  
  Novelty: no earlier mhfe audit record mentions xattr, chmod or utimensat isolation. AUD-023 CHECK-SEC-002 passed with the wrong statement that 'Landlock handles every file-system-changing right for each ABI'. AUD-008-SEC001 (io_uring network bypass) is a different channel with a different root cause. None of the 58 AUD-023 findings touches the isolation. So this is one root cause, not a duplicate: the write boundary is only Landlock's rights, but the boundary is documented, summarised, self-tested and labelled as refusing every file-system write, and it is read back only by opening /dev/null.
  
  The strongest counter-argument is SECURITY.md:135-136: 'restrict new access rather than guarantee containment of arbitrary compromised code'. That sentence follows from inherited descriptors. The xattr, mode and time changes are new access by path, which the same paragraph says is refused. DOC-07 explicitly treats an overstated guarantee as a security defect.
  
  Category: SEC, because AUDIT_STANDARD lists 'broken isolation, incorrect security guarantees' under SEC. The fix can be in code (seccomp) or in the documents, but the defect is the security guarantee.
  
  Severity: medium, not high, because it needs code already running inside the isolated process. The channel stays on the local disk, and SECURITY.md disclaims full containment, so this is not a 'release-blocking failure of a mandatory isolation guarantee'. Not low either: it is more than wording. Arbitrary data, up to 64 KiB per attribute on ext4, persists on disk through an isolation reported as 'enforced'.
  
  Corrections to the candidate: CORE-24 and SECURITY.md:24 are dropped. The tool's own code writes no secret, so that rule and sentence hold. DOC-07 is added. fsetxattr on a descriptor opened read-only is added as a variant. The locations are completed: Isolation::names, the isolate doc comment, the self-check part's description, and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md.

##### AUD-024-SEC002 — Low — Every threaded Argon2 call (the browser package's fast-mode build argon2-mt.js and the native engine) leaves each lane's last block, unwiped, on the stack of the thread that ran that lane. The call's output, a round key, can be rebuilt from these bytes with one BLAKE2b. In the browser the residue survives the known answer that ends every operation and stays through session waits until the worker is terminated. Natively it stays until the next Argon2 call or until the process exits. Nothing wipes it, no check looks for it in the threaded build, and no document names it.

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Argon2 engines: the vendored reference code as mhfe builds it. This covers the Emscripten threaded build with the page's bridge (browser package, fast mode) and the native engine (Linux x86-64 measured).
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-24, WEB-04, RUST-13, DOC-07
- **Affected files and builds:** Root cause, in the vendored code that mhfe compiles and ships unchanged:
  - vendor/phc-winner-argon2/src/ref.c:39-41. fill_block keeps `block blockR, block_tmp;` (2 KiB) on the stack.
    - ref.c:79-80 compute next_block = block_tmp ^ blockR, and neither local is wiped.
    - This code runs in both Emscripten builds and in native non-x86-64 builds (build.rs:114-116).
  - vendor/phc-winner-argon2/src/opt.c:186 (`__m128i state[ARGON2_OWORDS_IN_BLOCK]`, the block just computed, used at :274-279) and opt.c:112 (block_XY). Neither is wiped.
    - This code runs natively on x86-64, in both the SSE2 and the SSSE3 copy (build.rs:74-111; src/engine/argon2_simd.c).
  - vendor/phc-winner-argon2/src/core.c:280-289 and :292-357: each segment runs on new lane threads, which are joined after it.
    - finalize (core.c:155-187) wipes only blockhash and blockhash_bytes.
    - free_memory (:115-124) wipes only the work area.
    - No code clears the lane stacks.
  
  mhfe adds nothing that clears it:
  - web/argon2-engine.js:22-61 (derive): the finally at :54-60 wipes and frees only the bridge's password, salt and key buffers.
  - scripts/build-argon2-wasm.sh:57-69: the threaded flags (-pthread, PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=4).
    - Lane stacks lie in the shared linear memory.
    - In dist/core/argon2-mt.js, returnWorkerToPool calls _emscripten_thread_free_data(pthread_ptr), and establishStackSpace reads the stack bounds at pthread_ptr+48/+52.
  - src/engine/ffi.rs:172-193 (run) and src/engine/native.rs:99-108 (derive): no stack clearing, and natively no Argon2 call follows an operation's last round.
  - src/wasm_api/core.rs:681-684 (`verified`): the 1 MiB known answer runs after the last round. Its lane stacks lie elsewhere, so it does not overwrite the residue.
  - src/wasm_api/core/hidden.rs:53-72: a hidden-wallet session waits for the page with the residue in place.
  
  No check covers the threaded build:
  - scripts/package-check/argon2-faults.mjs:132-151 (checkArgon2Wipe) measures only the single-threaded build, against a 16 KiB byte-count bound.
  - The native test reuses_one_work_area_and_leaves_it_wiped covers only the work area.
  
  Documents that do not name the residue:
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1023-1031, shipped as dist/README.md.
    - It says the Rust code and the Argon2 bridge overwrite "the keys and the states they hold".
    - Its general sentence on copies that dependencies leave on "the WebAssembly's stack" gives only BIP39/BIP32 examples.
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:730-734 gives Argon2's post-call residue as "about 2 KiB" for the single-threaded build only.
  - SECURITY.md:243-247: the worker's end "frees the Argon2 memory". The only unwiped cases it names are a cancel and a failed round.
  - SECURITY.md:256-268 (browser).
  - SECURITY.md:39-41: dependency buffers are "short-lived" and not wiped. SECURITY.md:68-74 instead lists "buffers inside dependencies" among copies "wiped when dropped".
  - docs/API.md:450-455.
  
  Builds:
  - Browser package in fast mode (cross-origin isolated pages, dist/core/argon2-mt.js), in every browser.
  - Native mhfe: measured on Linux x86-64. macOS aarch64 (ref.c) and Windows are inferred.
  - The single-threaded build (standard mode) is not affected in the key-rebuild sense: only one lane's block stays, and the known answer overwrites it.
- **Reproduction:** All steps run from the repository root at b6fca69, at 32 MiB with one pass and public or synthetic data only. Probes are in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verifier-argon2-lane-residue/.
  
  1. Build the reference ref-last-blocks.c and ref-hex.c:
     - Sources: vendored argon2.c, core.c, encoding.c, ref.c and blake2b.c, with -DARGON2_NO_THREADS.
     - It sets FLAG_clear_internal_memory = 0 and prints each lane's last block from the free callback.
     - Its 1 MiB tag of "public test password"/"0123456789abcdef" is e0e8eba3...5df2, the repository's OpenSSL known answer.
  2. Bridge: `run-bridge.sh threaded 32768` and `run-bridge.sh single-threaded 32768`.
     - bridge-residue.mjs loads web/argon2-engine.js with vm and requires dist/core/argon2-{mt,st}.js, as scripts/package-check/package.mjs does.
     - It derives a synthetic secret at 32 MiB, then the 1 MiB known answer.
     - After each call it searches HEAPU8 for each lane's last block, as a copy or as an XOR of windows 1024 bytes apart.
     - rebuild.py rebuilds the tag as hashlib.blake2b(LE32(32) || XOR of the found blocks, digest_size=32) (RFC 9106 3.2/3.3) and compares it with the key.
  3. Operation: `run-ops.sh threaded 32768` and `run-ops.sh single-threaded 32768`.
     - The package core's encrypt of the public "abandon ... about" phrase.
     - Every round runs at 32 MiB with one pass; the known answers keep their own cost.
     - After encrypt returns, the heap is searched for the last round's lane blocks.
  4. Native: `run-native.sh <CARGO_TARGET_DIR>/release/build/mhfe-experimental-1ebf7d5f2c253740/out/libargon2.a 32768`.
     - native-scan.c calls argon2_ctx with 4 lanes and 4 threads, with bit 31 set where the CPU has SSSE3, as ffi.rs does.
     - It copies every rw-p mapping through /proc/self/mem, page by page, skipping unreadable guard pages, and searches the copies.
     - It repeats the search after a later 1 MiB call.
  
  Each step was run as `docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-argon2-lane-residue <name> <script> ...`.
- **Expected behavior:** Sources:
  - mhfe_spec README.md:561-562 (Sensitive memory): implementations SHOULD "minimize and erase copies of the entropy, states, salts, password, BIP39 passphrase, BIP39 seed, Argon2id outputs and masks where the runtime allows it".
    - The lanes' last blocks give the Argon2id output with one public hash, so they are a copy of it in all but form.
    - In C the runtime allows wiping them, for example with a volatile stack burn after fill_segment.
  - CORE-24: a secret, keys included, "lives in a type that owns it and wipes it when its work ends".
  - WEB-04: a secret "leaves the page's memory when its operation ends".
  - RUST-13: secret values are wiped, with their pages locked where their size allows.
  - DOC-07: claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides.
  
  The project's own claims:
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1023-1025: "The Rust code and the Argon2 bridge overwrite their own buffers of these bytes, the keys and the states they hold".
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:730-734: Argon2 wipes its memory after a call, leaving about 2 KiB of allocator records and stack (stated for the single-threaded build).
  - SECURITY.md:243-247: the worker's end frees the Argon2 memory. The unwiped cases named are a cancelled operation and a failed round.
  - SECURITY.md:39-41: every buffer holding an Argon2 key is wiped; dependency buffers are short-lived.
- **Observed behavior:** Threaded browser build (dist/core/argon2-mt.js sha256 8763fd80..., web/argon2-engine.js 5a35926f...), bridge, 32 MiB secret call:
  - Each of the four lanes' last blocks is in the heap once, as an XOR pair at 33694896, 33770912, 33846928 and 33922944.
  - The tag rebuilt from these heap bytes equals the secret key 95403b9e...c5f3, both right after the call and after the 1 MiB known answer that follows ("tag rebuilt from heap equals secret key: True" at both moments).
  - There are 0 copies of the password or key.
  
  Threaded build, whole operation:
  - encrypt runs derives in the order KA, 24 rounds, KA.
  - After it returns, the last round's key 9b2b6ef4...fba4 is rebuilt from the same four XOR-pair offsets. It equals round 1's key: the rehearsal's last round recomputes K_1.
  
  Single-threaded build:
  - Bridge: only lane 3 is found (XOR pair at 62544), and none after the known answer.
  - encrypt: no lane is found. The key is never rebuilt.
  
  Native (libargon2.a sha256 507fbba5..., SSSE3 copy, Linux x86-64):
  - After argon2_ctx returns, each lane's last block lies once as a direct copy in one 32 MiB + 16 KiB mapping of cached thread stacks.
  - The four copies are 8 MiB + 4 KiB apart; lane 3 is 7616 bytes below the mapping's end.
  - The tag rebuilt from memory equals the key.
  - After a later 1 MiB call, 0 lanes are found.
  - Native operations run no Argon2 call after their last round, so the residue stays until the next call or exit. That includes while the start menu (src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:271-287) or `mhfe wallets` waits for the person.
  
  Corroborated by the role's harness logs, which I did not rerun:
  - Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Firefox 157.0 rebuild the key after the known answer in a real cross-origin isolated Blob worker. The lane workers end with the operation worker: 5 workers before terminate, 0 after.
  - A hidden-wallet session after one wallet rebuilds its last round's key while it waits for the page, and still after free().
  - The package check's byte-count measure gives 12,613 bytes for the threaded build, below its 16 KiB bound, so the check could not tell this residue apart.
  
  Documentation:
  - The general sentences at BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1025-1027 and SECURITY.md:263-266 say that dependency copies on the WebAssembly's stack stay until later calls overwrite them or the worker ends.
  - But no document names Argon2's lane stacks, or says that a round key can be rebuilt from what Argon2 leaves.
  - The only Argon2-specific statement (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:730-734) presents the post-call residue as about 2 KiB, for the single-threaded build only.
- **Impact:** Who can use it: an attacker who can read the browser worker's memory, or the memory that termination frees without overwriting it (also through swap, a hibernation image or a browser crash report). Natively the same applies to the process memory, which needs root or the kernel because the process is non-dumpable on Linux, or to swap, since lane stacks are not locked.
  
  What that attacker gets: the output of the last Argon2id call, one round key.
  
  What that key gives at the end of an operation: in every flow that ends an operation this is K_1, because encryptions end with their rehearsal and recoveries end with round 1. K_1 alone neither decrypts a container nor speeds a password test, because its salt comes from half of the phrase's state.
  
  At other moments:
  - During an encryption's rehearsal the rebuildable key is K_12, whose salt comes from the container. Captured at that moment, it would let a password be tested with one Argon2id call instead of twelve: the leak the specification warns of at README.md:566-567.
  - But at that moment the password itself is in memory.
  - During session waits the worker also holds the passwords and passphrase it keeps on purpose.
  
  So the residue gives no new capability by itself. It is still Argon2id output material that the runtime allows to be erased (spec SHOULD), kept past the operation's last round and through session waits, never tested for in the threaded build and never disclosed.
  
  Severity low, not release-blocking.

(same documents, different omissions)
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced the defect independently at b6fca69 at reduced cost, using my own reference and probes rather than the candidate's harness.
  
  My reference is a native single-threaded build of the vendored ref.c with FLAG_clear_internal_memory = 0. It reads each lane's last block in the free callback, and its 1 MiB tag equals the repository's OpenSSL known answer e0e8eba3...5df2.
  
  Threaded browser build:
  - Setup: the real web/argon2-engine.js over dist/core/argon2-mt.js (sha256 8763fd80...).
  - Each lane's last block of a 32 MiB secret call is in the Emscripten heap as one XOR pair of adjacent 1024-byte windows, at 33694896, 33770912, 33846928 and 33922944. These are the exact offsets the candidate gives.
  - The pairs are still there after the 1 MiB known answer. BLAKE2b-256(LE32(32) || XOR of the four blocks) rebuilds the secret key.
  - No copy of the password or key is found.
  
  Single-threaded build:
  - Only lane 3 is found, at 62544, and the known answer removes it. The key is never rebuilt.
  
  Whole operation:
  - The package core's encrypt with its rehearsal, rounds at 32 MiB, the known answer after the last round, threaded build.
  - The last round's key, K_1 (equal to round 1's key), is rebuilt from the heap after encrypt returns.
  - Nothing is rebuilt in the single-threaded build.
  
  Native:
  - Setup: argon2_ctx of the release libargon2.a, four lanes on four threads, SSSE3 bit set.
  - After the call returns, each lane's last block lies once as a direct copy in the four cached lane-thread stacks, which are 8 MiB + 4 KiB apart. The tag is rebuilt.
  - A later 1 MiB call removes them.
  
  Code trace:
  - ref.c:41 and :79-80 hold blockR/block_tmp, opt.c:112 and :186 hold block_XY/state, and none of them is wiped.
  - core.c:155-187 and :115-124 wipe only blockhash and the work area.
  - The bridge's finally (web/argon2-engine.js:54-60) wipes only its own buffers.
  - The glue frees thread data at join (returnWorkerToPool -> __emscripten_thread_free_data).
  - The only wipe check (scripts/package-check/argon2-faults.mjs:139-151) runs on the single-threaded build alone, with a 16 KiB bound.
  
  Why a finding and not a duplicate:
  - The spec's Sensitive-memory SHOULD names Argon2id outputs, and in C the runtime allows erasing stack locals.
  - The confirmed AUD-024 DOC finding is about the AUD-023 record leaving this out (a record-keeping root cause), not about the product defect.
  - AUD-023 kept the native half only as an informational observation.
  
  Corrections I made:
  - The title is narrowed to threaded calls. In the single-threaded build no lane threads exist and the key cannot be rebuilt.
  - TS-07 is dropped, since it concerns TypeScript owner types.
  - The documentation part is reworded. BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1025-1027 and SECURITY.md:263-266 do say, in general terms, that dependency copies on the WebAssembly's stack stay until later calls overwrite them or the worker ends. The defect is that no document names this residue or says a round key can be rebuilt from it. They also say the bridge overwrites "the keys", and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:730-734 gives the post-call residue as about 2 KiB for the single-threaded build only.
  
  Not rerun by me:
  - The Playwright Chromium/Firefox runs, the hidden-wallet session wait, the rekey owner and check onNoLength waits, and macOS or Windows. The candidate's logs cover the first two.
  - Placement at 2 GiB is inferred.

##### AUD-024-SEC003 — Low — The browser package's worker never zeroes the WebAssembly's dead shadow stack. The BIP39 seed, the BIP32 master private key and chain code, and the BIP39 passphrase (in PBKDF2's salt block) therefore stay in the worker's linear memory after a call returns and while a session waits for the page, although zeroing that stack between calls removes them and leaves the module and its sessions working.

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package worker (web/worker-runtime.js, web/core-worker.js) and the WebAssembly linear memory of dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-44, CORE-24, RUST-13
- **Affected files and builds:** Every build of the browser package. There is one dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm for both standard and fast mode. global 0 (__stack_pointer) starts at 1048576 and the first data segment at 1048576, so [0, 1048576) is shadow stack only. The native command-line tool is not affected.
  
  Worker:
  - web/worker-runtime.js:153-183. self.onmessage runs each operation and does not zero the dead stack after it. At :165, bindings.initSync's returned exports, including the memory, are discarded, so the worker keeps no handle to scrub with.
  - web/worker-runtime.js:100-105. host.ask posts a question and awaits the page with no scrub.
  - web/core-worker.js:154-160. check: compare(), then await host.ask("noLength").
  - web/core-worker.js:288-296. rekey: recoverConfirmed, then await host.ask("ownerCheck").
  - web/core-worker.js:391-396. confirmAgain: await host.ask("confirmAgain").
  - web/core-worker.js:330-353. hiddenWallets: session.open, then await host.ask("opened"/"refused").
  
  Rust paths that leave the copies before those waits:
  - src/wasm_api/core/hidden.rs:71 (PhraseJson::of)
  - src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:475 (passes_wallet_check) and :478 (PhraseJson::of)
  - src/wasm_api/core.rs:543-552 (PhraseJson::of -> master_fingerprint_text)
  - src/wallet.rs:560-570
  - src/wallet/keys.rs:91-94 (bip39_seed, to_seed_normalized) and :117-146 (ExtendedKey::master, from_hmac's mac.finalize().into_bytes())
  
  The residue is documented instead of removed:
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1025-1030
  - SECURITY.md:263-267
  - docs/API.md:450-455, which calls such stack copies outside the crate's control
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with the baseline build of scripts/build-wasm.sh in dist/ and target/wasm-bindgen/:
  
    node docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-wasm-stack-residue/stack-residue.mjs
  
  The harness reads the stack top and the data segments from dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm. It computes its needles with node:crypto: the BIP39 seed halves, the BIP32 master key and chain code, and the 'mnemonic'+passphrase salt block. It then runs three cases on fresh instances of the package's own glue:
  1. walletFingerprint('abandon' x11 'about', 'TREZOR').
  2. walletCheck('abandon' x23 'art', 'TREZOR').
  3. A HiddenWalletSession on REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER at the package check's reduced cost, scanned right after session.open returns, where web/core-worker.js:353 awaits the page.
  
  In each case it counts the copies below the stack top, zeroes [0, stack top) and checks that the module or the session still works.
  
  The candidate's harness, docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/wasm-stack-residue.mjs, gives the same result for case 1.
- **Expected behavior:** The specification's Sensitive memory rule (mhfe_spec README.md:561-563) says implementations SHOULD minimize and erase copies of the BIP39 passphrase, the BIP39 seed and the other secrets 'where the runtime allows it'.
  
  CORE-24 says a secret (seed, key, passphrase) is wiped when its work ends. RUST-13 says secret values are wiped. CORE-44 says: 'When the choice is between documenting a quirk and fixing it, fix it'. CHECK-SEC-005 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md) asks for practical zeroization and explicit inspection of WASM linear-memory residuals.
  
  In a browser, the dead shadow stack is ordinary linear memory, which the worker can zero whenever no WebAssembly frame is active. That is the case after every operation and at every await host.ask. So the runtime does allow these copies to be erased, contrary to docs/API.md:450-453, which calls them outside the crate's control.
- **Observed behavior:** Case 1, walletFingerprint (b4e3f5ed): one copy each of the master private key and the chain code stays at 1048129 and 1048161, below the stack top 1048576. They are still there after a later non-secret call (suiteParameters).
  
  Case 2, walletCheck: the BIP39 seed (halves at 1045104 and 1045136) and two copies of the 'mnemonicTREZOR' salt block (1046888, 1047288) stay.
  
  Case 3, hidden-wallet session wait: the opened wallet's master key and chain code (fingerprint 00bf17d6) stay at 1047937 and 1047969 while the session waits. The same happens after a second open (fingerprint 67a73cd5).
  
  In every case, zeroing [0, 1048576) leaves 0 copies, and the module still works: a later walletFingerprint gives 73c5da0a, walletCheck gives false again, and the session refuses a reused password with PASSWORD_ALREADY_USED and opens another wallet.
  
  The worker scrubs nothing. web/worker-runtime.js wipes only the transferred request Uint8Arrays (wipeSecrets, :260-265). The three documents state that these copies stay 'until later calls overwrite them or the worker ends, also while a session waits'.
  
  The documentation route was taken in 253ca3c (2026-10-14T05:38Z), after CORE-44 entered the guide in 1491885 (01:15Z), although AUD-023's observation O1 had shown that the scrub works.
  
  The candidate's run also shows that rebuilding with the zeroize features of sha2, hmac, blake2 and sha3 leaves the same copy (wasm-residue-zeroize-variants.log).
- **Impact:** During a session's wait for the page, the worker's memory holds a wallet's BIP39 seed, BIP32 master private key and chain code, or the BIP39 passphrase. The waits are: a hidden-wallet session between passwords, a rekey waiting for the owner or for onConfirmAgain, and a check waiting for onNoLength. A wait can last as long as the page leaves it open. The material can be read by anything that reads the browser process's memory, and a browser locks no memory, so it may reach swap. At the end of a one-shot operation, the worker is terminated and the browser frees this memory without overwriting it.
  
  The exposure is bounded. It ends with the worker, and in these sessions the worker also holds, or the page receives as a string, the phrase from which the same keys follow. Hence low severity.
- **Evidence:** Verifier logs in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-wasm-stack-residue/, each with its .command.json:
  - harness-stack-residue.log: exit 1, all three cases and their controls; the last line is 'FAIL: 8 copies of a seed, master key, chain code or passphrase salt block stay below the stack top after the calls'.
  - probe-residue.log: exit 1. The independent master key equals the published xprv. The independent fingerprints are b4e3f5ed and 73c5da0a. The layout reads global 0 as mut, init 1048576, with data segments 1048576+431532 and 1480108+468.
  - probe-wallet-check.log: exit 1, seed and salt blocks.
  - probe-hidden-session.log: exit 1, session wait.
  
  Candidate's logs in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/: wasm-stack-residue.log, harness-run.log and wasm-residue-zeroize-variants.log.
  
  Build under test: b12-build-wasm.log (scripts/build-wasm.sh at b6fca69, 2026-10-14T06:52Z, buildId de06b919b42eae2f).
  
  Static trace: web/worker-runtime.js:153-183 and :100-105; web/core-worker.js:154-160, :288-296, :391-396, :330-353; src/wasm_api/core/hidden.rs:71; src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:475-478; src/wallet/keys.rs:91-94 and :117-146.
  
  History: git -S shows CORE-44 added in 1491885 (2026-10-14T01:15:16Z) and the documented residue text added in 253ca3c (05:38:24Z). AUD-023 informationalObservations[57] (O1) recorded the same scrub at a hidden-session wait.
- **Recommended fix:** 1. In serveOperations, keep the exports that bindings.initSync returns, including memory. Take the initial stack pointer from the module: read global 0 from the compiled module's bytes, or have the build export __stack_pointer or __heap_base.
  2. Zero [0, stackTop) in the worker after every operation, in the onmessage finally, and in host.ask before posting the question. Both points run with no WebAssembly frame active. Never scrub inside a callback that the WebAssembly calls (progress, post, the self-check callbacks).
  3. Update docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1025-1030, SECURITY.md:263-267 and docs/API.md:450-455.
  4. Extend the package check's residue cases (scripts/package-check/phrase-wipes.mjs) to search for the seed, master key, chain code and passphrase salt block at the hidden-session, rekey-owner and check-noLength waits. Run them through the worker's own call path.
- **Required verification:** 1. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-wasm-stack-residue/stack-residue.mjs, adapted to call through serveOperations, prints PASS and exits 0.
  2. A Node package-check case, run through the worker's call path at the reduced cost, finds no seed, master key, chain code or salt block below the stack top at a hidden-session wait, a rekey owner wait and a check noLength wait. The same sessions still complete.
  3. The browser suite (scripts/verify-browsers.mjs) passes in Chromium and Firefox, in standard and fast mode.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-DOC006, AUD-023 informationalObservations[57] (O1: shadow-stack copies of derived wallet secrets), AUD-024 confirmed: the browser documents list incompletely the endings that free a worker's secrets and the work that holds secrets in a worker for longer
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 against the baseline build of dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm (b12-build-wasm, buildId de06b919b42eae2f), using the package's own wasm-bindgen glue. The needles were computed independently with node:crypto, and the master key matches the published xprv9s21...UsAF. The module's layout puts global 0 (__stack_pointer) at 1048576 and the first data segment at 1048576, so [0, 1 MiB) is shadow stack only and is entirely dead when no WebAssembly frame is active.
  
  After walletFingerprint, one copy each of the master key and the chain code stays at 1048129 and 1048161, and a later non-secret call does not remove it. After walletCheck, the BIP39 seed and two 'mnemonicTREZOR' PBKDF2 salt blocks stay. At a reduced-cost hidden-wallet session's wait, the opened wallet's master key and chain code stay at 1047937 and 1047969. web/core-worker.js awaits host.ask("opened") at exactly that point. Zeroing [0, stack top) removes every copy, and the module and the session keep working: 73c5da0a, PASSWORD_ALREADY_USED, and a further wallet opens.
  
  The worker has no scrub anywhere. web/worker-runtime.js:165 even discards the exports that initSync returns. No owner decision accepts the residue. CORE-44 (in force since 1491885, 2026-10-14T01:15Z) predates 253ca3c (05:38Z), which settled AUD-023-DOC006 by documenting the residue although O1 had already shown the scrub works.
  
  This is not a duplicate. The confirmed TS-07 finding concerns JavaScript request objects with no owner type. The confirmed finding on the browser documents concerns which endings and waits they list. Neither covers the unscrubbed WebAssembly stack.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - BROWSER-PACKAGE.md lines are 1025-1030, not 1026-1031.
  - The residue also covers the seed and the passphrase salt block, which the specification's Sensitive memory rule names.
  - TS-07 is dropped from ruleIds: it governs JavaScript owner types, which a confirmed finding already covers.
  - The specification's SHOULD and CHECK-SEC-005 are added as sources.
  
  Severity stays low. The exposure is bounded to the worker's lifetime and to secrets whose phrase the page already receives as a string.

##### AUD-024-SEC004 — Low — A seed phrase or password given as a command-line argument by mistake is repeated in full in the usage error on standard error. This includes the --path and --coin values, which the library deliberately refuses without repeating them (AUD-016-SEC001).

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: usage errors (clap) of every command
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-API-003
- **Rules:** CORE-24, DOC-07
- **Affected files and builds:** Native mhfe CLI, every build and platform (debug and release, Linux, macOS, Windows), every command. The browser package is not affected. src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:247-249 (Cli::try_parse().unwrap_or_else(exit_unparsed)) and main.rs:281-295 (exit_unparsed passes error.render().to_string(), clap's own text, to style::usage_error at :293). src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:293-295 (usage_error) and :297-327 (usage_error_lines, which escapes control characters, per the comment at :298-299, but keeps the quoted argument or value). Value-taking options whose clap error quotes the value: check --path and --coin (src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:53-56 and :71-73, parsed by wallet.rs:178 FromStr for Coin and :322 FromStr for DerivationPath), --words (check.rs:62-69, decrypt.rs:28-33, rekey.rs:55), --pim (settings.rs:22), rekey --new-pim and --new-mem (rekey.rs:47, :51). Stray positional arguments and unknown subcommands of every command are affected too.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with mhfe built by CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --bin mhfe, and P='abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon about' (public test phrase), run each of these with NO_COLOR=1 and </dev/null: mhfe decrypt "$P"; mhfe encrypt "$P"; mhfe wallets "$P"; mhfe "$P"; mhfe check --fingerprint "$P"; mhfe check --address --path "$P"; mhfe check --address --coin "$P"; mhfe decrypt --words "$P"; mhfe rekey --new-pim "$P"; mhfe encrypt --pim 'public test password'. Every one is refused by clap with exit 2 before any command code runs. Probe scripts: tmp/aud024/verify-argument-echo/probe.sh and probe-public-fields.sh. Kept harness: python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/cli-ux/verify_cli_ux.py <mhfe>, check a_phrase_argument_is_not_repeated.
- **Expected behavior:** SECURITY.md:24-25: 'The tool never takes secrets from command-line arguments, never writes them to files and never logs them. Error messages never contain a phrase, a password or any part of them.' CORE-24 (code-core.instructions.md, Check: review): 'text a person typed is never repeated in a message, since a phrase pasted into the wrong field would be shown and kept.' RUST-xx in code-rust.instructions.md:48: an error's Display 'never repeats text a person typed (CORE-24)'. The project's own fix for AUD-016-SEC001 (docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:171-172; src/error.rs:201-208 and the test at :530-533): 'A refused master key fingerprint, derivation path or coin no longer repeats what was typed: a seed phrase pasted into the fingerprint field by mistake was printed in the error.' DOC-07: a document claims no stronger guarantee than the code provides.
- **Observed behavior:** Every case exits 2 and writes the whole phrase or password to standard error, wrapped over two lines. 'mhfe decrypt "$P"' writes "✗ Error: Unexpected argument 'abandon abandon ... abandon about' found". Stray arguments of encrypt, wallets and check --fingerprint give the same; 'mhfe "$P"' writes "Unrecognized subcommand 'abandon ... about'". 'check --address --path "$P"' writes "Invalid value 'abandon ... about' for '--path <PATH>': invalid derivation path: it is not a path like m/84'/0'/0'/0/5": the library's reason, which omits the text, is wrapped by clap's quote of the text. 'check --address --coin "$P"' gives the same with '--coin <COIN>'. --words, --new-pim and --new-mem give 'Invalid value '<phrase>' for ...'; encrypt --pim 'public test password' gives "Invalid value 'public test password' for '--pim <N>': invalid digit found in string". For contrast, 'new --never-use "$P"', whose value clap accepts and the library refuses, does not repeat it. The only usage-error unit test (style.rs:800-834, a_usage_error_reads_as_an_error_of_the_tool) checks escaping of a mistyped option name and nothing about repeated values.
- **Impact:** A seed phrase or password pasted onto the command line by mistake, such as into --path, --coin or --words or as a stray argument, is written again to standard error. A script's log, a CI log or a terminal session log keeps it there. This is the same exposure AUD-016-SEC001 removed from the library refusals of those fields. SECURITY.md's promise that error messages never contain a phrase or password does not hold for the CLI. Impact is bounded: the same text is already in the shell history and briefly in the process list, and the tool does not ask for secrets as arguments.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-argument-echo/build-debug.log (cargo build --locked --bin mhfe, exit 0, up to date at b6fca69). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-argument-echo/argument-echo-probe.log (+ .command.json): decrypt, encrypt and wallets with a stray phrase, check --fingerprint with a phrase, the phrase as subcommand, check --words with a phrase and encrypt --pim with a password; all exit 2 with the full text in stderr; '--password=<pw>' is shown only as '--password'. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-argument-echo/public-field-echo-probe.log: check --address --path/--coin, decrypt --words, rekey --new-pim/--new-mem all quote the full phrase, and new --never-use does not. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-argument-echo/harness-one-check.log: the kept harness check a_phrase_argument_is_not_repeated run alone fails because the phrase is found in the collapsed stderr (exit 2), not because of a harness fault. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-argument-echo/library-public-field-test.log: cargo test --locked --lib a_refused_public_field_does_not_repeat_the_text passes, so the library refusal omits the text and clap re-adds it. Original role evidence: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/argument-echo.log and verify-cli-ux.log. A search of every docs/audits/AUD-0*.json and of the docs found no earlier finding, decision or accepted risk about clap repeating argument values.
- **Recommended fix:** In exit_unparsed (main.rs:281-295), build the usage error from clap's ErrorKind and context instead of error.render(). For InvalidValue/ValueValidation, name the option (ContextKind::InvalidArg) and give the library's or parser's own reason (the error's source, which never repeats text). Never give the value (ContextKind::InvalidValue). For UnknownArgument/InvalidSubcommand, repeat the token only when it is a short option-like name ('-' prefix, no white space, bounded length) so the '--stdn' tip still works. Otherwise say that the command takes no such argument and that secrets are typed at the prompt or given with --stdin. Keep the Usage and --help lines, which hold no value.
- **Required verification:** The kept harness check a_phrase_argument_is_not_repeated passes, and is extended to check --address --path/--coin, --words, --pim, --new-pim, --new-mem and an unknown subcommand. A unit test of the usage-error lines feeds a phrase-like unexpected argument, a phrase-like --path value and a password-like --pim value, and asserts that no word of them appears while the option name does. style.rs a_usage_error_reads_as_an_error_of_the_tool still passes for an option-name typo (--stdn with its tip) and still escapes control characters.
- **Related findings:** AUD-016-SEC001
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with the debug build and only commands that clap refuses before any Argon2 round. Every usage error repeats in full the argument or value that clap quotes. That includes a 12-word phrase given as a stray argument, as an unknown subcommand, as the value of --words, --pim, --new-pim or --new-mem, and as the value of check --path or --coin. The last two are the strongest variant. For those fields the library's own refusal leaves out the typed text on purpose (AUD-016-SEC001, error.rs test a_refused_public_field_does_not_repeat_the_text, which passes), but clap wraps that refusal in "Invalid value '<text>' for '--path <PATH>'". So the CLI undoes the earlier fix. The comment at style.rs:298-299 shows the authors knew clap repeats the argument but only escaped control characters. No earlier audit, decision or test accepts the repetition (I searched AUD-0* JSON and docs). None of the confirmed findings covers it.

##### AUD-024-SEC005 — Low — The SHA-256, SHA-512, HMAC and BLAKE2b states that mhfe feeds with secrets are built without their crates' zeroize feature, so they are not wiped on drop. Measured: SHA-256's padded block of the BIP39 seed stays in the dead stack after wallet_check::phrase_passes.

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Library dependencies (Cargo.toml) and the Feistel, packing, BIP32 and wallet-check code. All builds: native library and CLI, browser WebAssembly.
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-13, CORE-44, CORE-24
- **Affected files and builds:** Manifest: Cargo.toml:29 (blake2 = "=0.11.0"), :32 (hmac = "=0.13.0") and :37 (sha2 = "=0.11.0") enable no `zeroize` feature. Cargo.toml:39 (sha3) has none either, but it hashes only public keys. Cargo.lock:355-365: digest 0.11.3 has no zeroize dependency. The features are not target-specific, so the native release, the library and the browser WebAssembly (--features wasm) are all affected.
  
  States fed with secrets:
  - src/feistel.rs:246-255 round_salt: BLAKE2b-256 over DS_SALT || settings || R. Its block buffer holds the Feistel half R, which in the first rounds is the phrase in all but form, as the code's own comment says above it.
  - src/feistel.rs:257-268 round_mask: HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the round's Argon2 key K_i, over a message ending in R. The ipad/opad cores are as good as K_i for computing masks. At :265, the temporary that mac.finalize() returns (CtOutput) holds the full HMAC output, of which the mask is the first bytes. Only its clone `digest` is zeroized (:267).
  - src/wallet/keys.rs:132-148 from_hmac: HMAC-SHA512 over the BIP39 seed (called from master at :122), keyed with the chain code over the parent private key (child at :162) or over the public key (:164). At :140 the CtOutput temporary holds IL||IR, the child key tweak and the chain code, and is not wiped.
  - src/wallet_check.rs:100-111 tagged_digest: SHA-256 over DOMAIN || BE32(bits) || seed.
  - New variant: src/packing.rs:80-83 sha256, documented there as secret for a short phrase. It is SHA-256 over a phrase's entropy, called by pack (:72) when a 12- to 21-word original is encrypted (src/mhfe.rs:335, 517), by unpack (:92) for each length tried in src/detection.rs:43 after decryption, and by with_checksum (:48) for a new phrase with chosen words (src/word_wishes.rs:242).
  
  Dependency gating (crate sources at the pinned versions):
  - sha2-0.11.0 src/block_api.rs:89-101 and 208-219 (Sha256VarCore/Sha512VarCore Drop)
  - blake2-0.11.0 src/macros.rs:251-258 (Blake2bVarCore Drop)
  - block-buffer-0.12.1 src/lib.rs:424-441 (BlockBuffer Drop)
  - digest-0.11.3 src/mac.rs:241-253 (CtOutput Drop)
  All wipe only under cfg(feature = "zeroize"). sha2's and blake2's core wipes are gated on their own crate's feature, not on digest's.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69, with Rust 1.99.0 and the crates fetched:
  1. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo tree --locked --offline --target all -e features -i digest@0.11.3 prints no 'digest feature "zeroize"' for any target (tree-digest-features.log: 0 matches).
  2. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-hash-state-zeroize/run.sh exits 1.
     - drop-probe: built with blake2/hmac/sha2 at the pinned versions and features. It drops in place, in a heap slot, an HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with a stand-in K_i and fed a stand-in R, a BLAKE2b-256 over R, an HMAC-SHA512 over seed bytes, a SHA-256 over seed bytes, and a CtOutput. It prints '5 of 5' states with every non-zero byte unchanged after drop and the secret pattern still in the slot.
     - residue-probe: links the mhfe library and calls the public mhfe::wallet_check::phrase_passes('abandon' x11 'about', 'TREZOR') on a thread whose stack it first cleared. It then finds SHA-256's padded last block, seed[36..64] followed by 0x80, 2 times in the dead stack. A control confirms that the published seed is the one BIP39 computes.
  3. The same harness with --features wipe exits 0: 0 of 5 states keep bytes and the block is found 0 times.
- **Expected behavior:** Rule texts:
  - RUST-13 (code-rust.instructions.md:95-98, Check: review): 'Secret values live in types that wipe them on drop (zeroize)'.
  - CORE-24 (code-core.instructions.md:180-183): a secret 'lives in a type that owns it and wipes it when its work ends'.
  - CORE-44 (code-core.instructions.md:324-327): 'When the choice is between documenting a quirk and fixing it, fix it'.
  
  Why these states count: an HMAC state keyed with K_i is as secret as K_i for computing masks. The other states and outputs hold R, a phrase's entropy, the BIP39 seed, the parent private key, or the child key tweak with the chain code.
  
  The project's own documents claim more than the code does:
  - docs/API.md:449-452 says every buffer the crate owns that holds a key or mask is wiped when dropped, and calls dependency working buffers 'outside its control'. For these states that is not so: blake2, hmac and sha2 offer the wipe as a `zeroize` feature, which adds no new crate, since zeroize 1.9.1 is already a dependency.
  - SECURITY.md:39-41 says the same about buffers that hold an Argon2 key or mask.
- **Observed behavior:** The zeroize feature is off for digest, sha2, hmac and blake2 in every target. The drop probe measures that none of the five state types wipes on drop: SHA-256, SHA-512, HMAC over each, BLAKE2b-256 and the MAC output CtOutput. Every non-zero byte stays, and so does the secret pattern. With the features on, every byte is cleared.
  
  Through the public API, wallet_check::phrase_passes leaves SHA-256's padded last block of the BIP39 seed in the dead stack twice, and 0 times with the features on. The program's explicit wipes cover only the clones of the final digests (feistel.rs:254 and 267, keys.rs:146), not the states or the CtOutput temporaries.
  
  Inconclusive in both configurations: the residue probe did not find the HMAC-SHA512 block of master_fingerprint, because the later elliptic-curve work overwrites that stack. A probe for the K-xor-ipad/opad key block that hmac 0.13's new_from_slice builds on its stack found none either.
- **Impact:** Defence in depth, bounded. In the native tool, the stack is not in a core dump (limit 0, non-dumpable process), but it can reach swap. In the browser worker it stays readable in linear memory until overwritten or the worker ends. Until later calls overwrite them, freed stack frames keep these copies:
  - the Feistel half R;
  - the K_i-keyed HMAC states and full HMAC outputs;
  - a short phrase's entropy;
  - the BIP39 seed (measured);
  - the parent private key, and the child key tweak with the chain code.
  Compiler move copies are outside this finding and remain best effort, as documented.
- **Evidence:** Folder docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-hash-state-zeroize/, each log with its .command.json:
  - tree-digest-features.log: cargo tree --target all, no zeroize under digest 0.11.3.
  - tree-zeroize-users.log
  - drop-probe-as-pinned.log and drop-probe-as-pinned-release.log: 5 of 5 kept, exit 1.
  - drop-probe-zeroize-features.log and -release.log: 0 of 5, exit 0.
  - residue-probe-as-pinned.log: phrase_passes SHA-256 block found 2 times after the call, 0 before; exit 1.
  - residue-probe-zeroize-features.log: 0 times, exit 0.
  - harness-as-pinned.log: exit 1.
  - harness-zeroize-features.log: exit 0.
  - hmac-key-block-as-pinned.log and hmac-key-block-zeroize-features.log: K-xor-pad key blocks 0 in both, inconclusive.
  
  Kept harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-hash-state-zeroize/, with run.sh, README.md, drop-probe/ and residue-probe/.
  
  Crate sources read at the pinned versions: sha2-0.11.0 src/block_api.rs, blake2-0.11.0 src/macros.rs, block-buffer-0.12.1 src/lib.rs, digest-0.11.3 src/mac.rs and Cargo.toml, hmac-0.13.0 src/block_api.rs and src/utils.rs.
  
  The original role's logs agree: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/digest-features.log and harness-run.log.
- **Recommended fix:** 1. Enable features = ["zeroize"] on sha2, hmac and blake2 in Cargo.toml, then update Cargo.lock. This adds zeroize to digest and block-buffer and no new crate. sha3 is optional, since it hashes only public keys.
  2. Enable all three features, not hmac's alone. hmac/zeroize turns on digest's feature, but sha2's and blake2's core Drop wipes are gated on their own crates' features.
  3. Narrow docs/API.md:449-452 and SECURITY.md:39-41 to the dependency buffers that really cannot be wiped (bitcoin_hashes' PBKDF2 in bip39, Unicode normalization, compiler copies).
  4. Optionally, add a regression test that asserts ZeroizeOnDrop for Hmac<Sha256>, Hmac<Sha512>, Sha256 and Blake2b<U32> at compile time.
- **Required verification:** docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-hash-state-zeroize/run.sh exits 0 at the fix commit, without --features. Two notes:
  - The first check of the original role's run.sh (digest feature zeroize present) is not enough on its own. It also passes after a partial fix that enables only hmac's feature, which leaves the SHA-256, SHA-512 and BLAKE2b cores unwiped.
  - The licence and notices checks and the canonical build stay consistent, since no crate is added.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[9] (hash and MAC states of dependencies are not wiped; dispositioned as covered by SECURITY.md:39-41 before RUST-13 and CORE-44 existed), AUD-010 observation at docs/audits/AUD-010-2026-10-07.md:852 (recommended the zeroize features of hmac 0.13, sha2 0.11 and blake2 0.11)
- **Verification:** confirmed: I confirmed this at b6fca69 and went beyond the candidate's evidence.
  
  1. Static trace: Cargo.toml pins blake2, hmac and sha2 without `zeroize`. Cargo.lock:355-365 gives digest 0.11.3 no zeroize dependency. `cargo tree --target all -e features -i digest@0.11.3` shows no zeroize feature for any target.
  2. Dependency sources: the crates wipe their cores, block buffers and CtOutput only under cfg(feature = "zeroize").
  3. A drop probe with the exact pinned versions shows 5 of 5 states keep every non-zero byte after drop, and the secret pattern is still in the slot. This covers HMAC-SHA-256 keyed like round_mask, BLAKE2b like round_salt, HMAC-SHA512 like from_hmac, SHA-256 like tagged_digest, and CtOutput. With the features on, 0 of 5 keep bytes.
  4. The candidate measured no residue that it could attribute to these states. I did, with an end-to-end probe that links the mhfe library. After the public `wallet_check::phrase_passes` (BIP39 vector abandon x11 about, passphrase TREZOR), the dead stack still holds SHA-256's padded last block twice: seed[36..64] followed by 0x80. With the features on, it is found 0 times.
  
  The rules are new since AUD-023 (guide added 2026-10-14 01:15 UTC): RUST-13, and CORE-44 (fix rather than document). docs/API.md:449-452 calls dependency buffers "outside its control", but for these states a feature flag controls them. No owner decision accepts this; AUD-010 and AUD-023 both recorded it only as an observation.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - sha3 holds only public data (Keccak-256 of public keys), so it is not part of the defect.
  - New variant: packing.rs:80-83. SHA-256 over a phrase's entropy, run at encryption of a short original, at length detection after decryption, and for a new phrase with chosen words.
  - New detail: the CtOutput temporaries at feistel.rs:265 and keys.rs:140 hold the full HMAC output, the mask and the child key tweak with the chain code. The code wipes only the clone.
  
  The master_fingerprint HMAC-SHA512 block was not found in either configuration, because later stack use overwrites it, so that check is inconclusive. A probe for hmac's K-xor-pad key block also found nothing either way.
  
  No full-cost Argon2 is needed.

##### AUD-024-SEC006 — Low — check_word::Repair derives Debug, so formatting a repair with {:?} prints the word of the password it restores or replaces, and the byte range of the typed word

- **Category:** SEC.
