- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Library password check word (src/check_word.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-13, CORE-24
- **Affected files and builds:** src/check_word.rs:86-93: `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct Repair { position: usize, word: &'static str, typed: Range<usize> }`, public as mhfe::check_word::Repair (src/lib.rs:35). Repairs are built at src/check_word.rs:281-285 (read, closure repair_at) and returned by PasswordReview::repairs at src/check_word.rs:173-176. They are used by the CLI (src/bin/mhfe/check_word.rs:135-181, the Action::Restore/Replace(&Repair) answers) and by the WASM API (src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:106-115). All builds that contain the library are affected: native library, CLI and WASM (browser-core/browser-passwords). Types that already redact, for comparison: src/password.rs:88-92 (Password(hidden)), src/memory.rs:143-147 (LockedBytes(hidden)), src/word_wishes.rs:86-90 ('The words themselves are never named in a refusal or in Debug').
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root (/home/user/.../mhfe), with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target: build the scratch probe /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-repro/repair-debug with `cargo build --offline --locked --release --manifest-path <probe>/Cargo.toml`, then run target/release/aud024-verify-repair-debug. The probe calls PasswordReview::of on public specification vectors: 'jovial trailing ? pavilion cresting ninth' (Restorable), 'abacus abdomen abdominal zoom abiding aids' (Mismatch, the first vector with 'abide' typed as 'zoom') and 'jovial trailing chokehold pavilion cresting ?' (Restorable check word). It prints format!("{:?}") of each repair next to {:?} of a Password, and exits 1 when any repair's Debug text names its word. The kept harness reproduces the same: `cargo run --offline --release --manifest-path docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/repair-debug/Cargo.toml` (password 'zookeeper zoning zoologist zoology zoom ?').
- **Expected behavior:** RUST-13 (.github/instructions/code-rust.instructions.md:95-98): 'A secret type prints as redacted in Debug and Display.' CORE-24 (code-core.instructions.md:180-183): a secret (password) stays out of errors and logs. SECURITY.md:110-115: the check-word offer 'shows words of the password, so it is made only on the private screen', and the check word 'is as secret as the rest of the password'. src/check_word.rs:271 wipes the list positions because they 'reveal the password'.
- **Observed behavior:** verify-repro/v02-repair-debug-run.log (exit 1): 'Repair { position: 3, word: "chokehold", typed: 16..17 }'; for the mismatch, six lines including 'Repair { position: 4, word: "abide", typed: 25..29 }' (the true word); 'Repair { position: 6, word: "ninth", typed: 44..45 }'; next to 'Password {:?} = Password(hidden)'. 8 of 8 repairs name their word in Debug. The `typed` field also prints the byte offsets of the typed word, which give away word lengths. No production code at b6fca69 formats a Repair, PasswordReview or the CLI's Action with {:?} (a grep of src for {:?}, {:#?}, :?} and dbg! next to repair/review/action finds nothing), so the leak is latent.
- **Impact:** Low and latent. Any later log line, panic or assert message, error detail or derived Debug of a type that holds a Repair (for example if Action in src/bin/mhfe/check_word.rs or PasswordReview gained #[derive(Debug)]) would print a word of the person's password, and the true word in the Restorable case, outside the private screen that SECURITY.md promises. There is no exposure at b6fca69.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-repro/v01-repair-debug-build.log (exit 0) and v02-repair-debug-run.log (exit 1), each with its .command.json; scratch probe at /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-repro/repair-debug/src/main.rs. Original evidence: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/secrets-native/h04-repair-debug.log (exit 1, 'Repair { position: 6, word: "wool", typed: 40..41 }' next to 'Password(hidden)') and s08-repair-debug.log; kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/repair-debug/. Static trace: src/check_word.rs:87 derive, 90 word field, 92 typed field, 281-285 construction, 173-176 accessor.
- **Recommended fix:** Replace the derived Debug on Repair with a hand-written impl that prints the position only, for example `Repair { position: 6, .. }`. This is what Password, LockedBytes and WordWishes do: it leaves out both `word` and the `typed` range. Keep Clone, PartialEq and Eq. Add a unit test in src/check_word.rs that formats every repair of a Restorable and a Mismatch review with {:?} and asserts that the text contains neither the repair's word nor the typed byte range.
- **Required verification:** The kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/repair-debug and the verify-repro probe both exit 0. A new unit test asserts that the Debug text of each repair names no word and no range. cargo test --locked check_word passes.
- **Related findings:** AUD-014-SEC002
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read the code at b6fca69 and the defect is real. Line 87 of src/check_word.rs puts `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]` on the public `pub struct Repair { position, word: &'static str, typed: Range<usize> }` (lines 88-93), which is reachable as mhfe::check_word::Repair (src/lib.rs:35). The derived Debug prints the field `word`. That word is a word of the password: in the Restorable case it is the restored word, and in the Mismatch case one of the six repairs is the true word. The project itself treats this as secret. SECURITY.md:110-115 says the offer "shows words of the password" and is made only on the private screen. src/check_word.rs:271 wipes the list positions because they "reveal the password". RUST-13 asks for redacted Debug, which Password (src/password.rs:88-92) and LockedBytes (src/memory.rs:143-147) do but Repair does not. I wrote my own probe against the specification's public vectors and it confirms the leak: all 8 repairs from three reviews print their word, for example `Repair { position: 3, word: "chokehold", typed: 16..17 }`. A Password next to them prints `Password(hidden)`. The `typed` byte range also gives away the offsets and lengths of the typed words. No production code formats a Repair, PasswordReview or the CLI's Action with {:?}, so the defect is latent and low fits AUDIT_STANDARD.md. It is not a duplicate: no AUD-023 finding is about check_word or Repair.

##### AUD-024-SEC007 — Low — Every standard-input reader of the command-line tool goes through io::stdin().lock(). So a pasted secret line, and with --stdin every answer of the script (password, seed phrase, passphrase), stays whole in the standard library's 8 KiB stdin buffer, unwiped and unlocked, until a later read overwrites it or the process ends. Reading the descriptor into the tool's own locked buffer leaves no copy.

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI input (src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs, src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-13, CORE-24, CORE-44
- **Affected files and builds:** src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:100 and :107: read_line calls edit_line(&mut io::stdin().lock(), ...) for hidden and shown prompts (passwords, phrases, passphrases, chosen words). LineEditor::edit reads one byte at a time at :491, so std's BufReader receives each terminal read first. hidden_input.rs:148: with_keys builds TerminalKeys over io::stdin().lock(). Its next_byte at :341-361 copies std's buffer into its own Zeroizing pending with fill_buf (:347) and consume (:355) but leaves the bytes in std's buffer; the comments at :315-318 and :332-333 claim no unwiped copy is left. src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:74: Input::Script(io::stdin().lock()) for --stdin. :164: visible prompts. :440-444: read_bounded_line reads through reader.take(LINE_CAPACITY).read_line(line) on the StdinLock. The comment at :438-439 states that std keeps an unwiped buffer. Documents: SECURITY.md:44-47 calls std's stdin buffer 'beyond the program's reach', although the program can bypass it. SECURITY.md:57-59 lists 'the line a secret is typed into at a terminal or read from standard input' among the secrets held in locked memory. Builds: every native build. Reproduced on Linux. macOS uses the same std path. On Windows, std's console reader converts UTF-16 into the same BufReader buffer (static reading only, not reproduced).
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-stdin-buffer-residue/run.sh (std-only probe, no Argon2, public text 'public test password' given reversed). The probe reads one line in three ways. 'bytes' reads one byte at a time from io::stdin().lock(), as edit_line does. 'line' runs take(8192).read_line into a String reserved at 8192, as read_bounded_line does. 'descriptor' reads one byte at a time from fd 0 (control). It wipes its own copy with volatile writes, keeps it allocated, and scans the heap and anonymous mappings through /proc/self/mem. It prints each copy's address and whether that lies inside std's buffer, whose address it takes from fill_buf before reading. run.py runs it through a pipe (as with --stdin) and through a pseudo-terminal set raw with VMIN=1 (as hidden_input/unix.rs:50-52 sets it), the line pasted in one write and then typed one key at a time. strace confirms std reads stdin in 8192-byte calls.
- **Expected behavior:** RUST-13: 'Secret values live in types that wipe them on drop (zeroize), with their pages locked (mlock) where their size allows.' CORE-24: a secret lives in a type that owns it and wipes it when its work ends. CORE-44: 'When the choice is between documenting a quirk and fixing it, fix it.' SECURITY.md:57-59 says the line a secret is typed into or read from standard input is held in locked memory. Reading fd 0 directly into the tool's locked LINE_CAPACITY buffer, with its read-ahead in a wiped, locked pending buffer, leaves no copy (control: 0 copies).
- **Observed behavior:** Pipe, 'public test password\nsecond line\n' in one write: read(0, ..., 8192) = 33. The 'bytes' and 'line' modes each leave one whole copy after the program's wipe, located at the first byte of std's stdin buffer (e.g. buffer 0x59088f886f60, copy 0x59088f886f60). The second line is in the same buffer, so with --stdin every answer of one read stays there. Pseudo-terminal, pasted in one write and then CR: 'bytes' leaves one whole copy at the start of std's buffer. Typed one key at a time: no whole copy, because each keystroke's read overwrites offset 0. 'descriptor' control: 0 copies in all cases. The buffer is a process-lifetime static. Only later reads overwrite it, and only from offset 0 for their own length: a pasted password followed by a separate Enter keeps all but its first byte. At EOF (--stdin) nothing overwrites it.
- **Impact:** A pasted container password, seed phrase or BIP39 passphrase stays in an unwiped, unlocked heap block for the rest of the run. With --stdin this covers every answer of the script (encrypt --stdin: the phrase and the password twice). The run includes all Argon2 rounds, whose 2 GiB work area makes it likely that this unlocked page is swapped out. This undercuts the locked-memory guarantee of SECURITY.md:57-59 for exactly those inputs. Prerequisites for exposure: swap or a hibernation image, or a reader able to access the process memory. On Linux PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 keeps out same-user readers, and core dumps are off, so practical impact is bounded. A password typed one key at a time is not kept whole. SECURITY.md:45-47 discloses std's stdin buffer, but it calls the buffer beyond the program's reach, whereas the program chooses to read through it and has a direct alternative.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-stdin-buffer-residue/stdin-buffer-residue.log (+ .command.json, exit 1): run.sh output with the addresses inside std's buffer for pipe/bytes, pipe/line and pty-pasted/bytes, 0 for the descriptor and for typed keys. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-stdin-buffer-residue/std-read-size.log: strace shows read(0, "public test password\nsecond line"..., 8192) = 33. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-stdin-buffer-residue/static-trace.log, at HEAD b6fca69238344dd2525b06270ee6ff3b055e68c1: every io::stdin().lock() reader (hidden_input.rs:100, 107, 148, 347, 355, 491; terminal.rs:74, 164, 444), the comment at terminal.rs:438-439, and SECURITY.md:45-46 and 58-59. Harness kept: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-stdin-buffer-residue/ (README.md, run.sh, run.py, probe/). The gap role's earlier evidence agrees: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/stdin-buffer-residue.log and harness-run.log:20-23. That probe's non-volatile wipe before a free left open whether its copy was the program's own. This probe pins the copy to std's buffer address.
- **Recommended fix:** Add one standard-input reader for the tool over the raw descriptor. On Unix use libc::read on STDIN_FILENO with an EINTR retry. On Windows use ReadConsoleW for a console, converting UTF-16 to UTF-8 itself (a surrogate pair may split across reads), and ReadFile for a pipe or file. Its read-ahead goes into a Zeroizing buffer of LINE_CAPACITY, locked like the line buffers. Route edit_line, TerminalKeys (its select/PeekConsoleInput test of waiting input then sees no hidden std buffer), read_bounded_line and Input::Script through that one reader. Leave no io::stdin() read anywhere in the binary, with a test that keeps it so. Then correct SECURITY.md:44-47 and the comments at terminal.rs:438-439 and hidden_input.rs:315-318 and :332-333.
- **Required verification:** Run the verify-stdin-buffer-residue probe with its 'bytes' and 'line' modes switched to the tool's new reader: no copy through a pipe or a raw pseudo-terminal paste (exit 0). Add a unit test that a line read through the reader leaves nothing in the reader's pending buffer after it is dropped. Re-run scripts/verify-hidden-input.py (Linux, macOS) and scripts/verify-hidden-input-windows.py (including a pasted non-BMP character) and the --stdin terminal-suite cases. Confirm that a grep or test finds no io::stdin() read left in src/bin/mhfe.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[12] (Typed secret lines pass through the standard library's stdin buffer at a terminal too), The Windows build locks no secret memory and takes no step against crash dumps or other processes reading its memory (Windows variant of the same buffer)
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced it at b6fca69 with my own probe. Unlike the gap probe, it wipes with volatile writes, keeps its own buffer allocated, and takes the address of std's stdin buffer from fill_buf. Through a pipe (the --stdin path) and through a raw-mode pseudo-terminal with the line pasted in one write, the one whole copy left after the program's wipe sits at the first byte of std's buffer. The 8192-byte read is confirmed by strace. The descriptor control leaves none. Every stdin reader of the CLI goes through io::stdin().lock(): hidden_input.rs:100, 107, 148 and terminal.rs:74, 164. So pasted or piped secrets (password, phrase, passphrase, and with --stdin every answer of the script) stay unwiped and unlocked in that buffer through the Argon2 rounds until a later read overwrites them. The project documents this (terminal.rs:438-439, SECURITY.md:45-47) when it could avoid it. That breaches RUST-13/CORE-24 (secrets live in wiping, locked owners) and CORE-44 (fix, do not document). Two corrections to the candidate. First, a password typed one key at a time leaves no whole copy, because each keystroke's read overwrites offset 0. Second, SECURITY.md does disclose the std buffer, so the defect is the avoidable unwiped and unlocked copy and the false 'beyond the program's reach' claim, not an undisclosed contradiction. Not a duplicate of any confirmed finding. The nearest ones (paint/format! residue of check-word repairs, the unlocked chosen word, Windows without memory locking) have other root causes.

##### AUD-024-SEC008 — Low — The check-word repair answers, which show words of a password, are drawn through style::paint and a line format! that grow ordinary Strings, so each draw frees unwiped heap blocks holding the restored, replacement or typed word

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI lists (src/bin/mhfe/choice.rs, check_word.rs, style.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-13, CORE-24
- **Affected files and builds:** Native mhfe, all platforms. The allocation pattern does not depend on the platform; survival of the residue was measured with Linux glibc. The browser package is not affected. Reached at a terminal with a private screen whenever a typed container password has the six-word shape (check_word::review, src/bin/mhfe/check_word.rs:66-93, then decide 107-174), called by terminal::read_password (src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:535, call at 556) and encrypt::read_typed_password (src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:515, call at 568).
  
  Two variants of one root cause: list lines that may hold words of a password are built in Strings that grow by reallocation, and Zeroizing wipes only the final buffer.
  
  (1) src/bin/mhfe/choice.rs:394 `(paint(ACCENT, "›"), Zeroizing::new(paint(STRONG, label)))` for the highlighted answer, with src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:65-69 `pub fn paint(...) -> String { format!("{style}{text}{style:#}") }`. Its doc comment says "For public text only: the result is an ordinary string, which is not wiped".
  
  (2) src/bin/mhfe/choice.rs:401-411, the line's format!. When the note is non-empty, the `{padding}  {}` written after the label grows the String again; this happens in every restore answer row, highlighted or not, because its note is "restored by the check word".
  
  The labels come from src/bin/mhfe/check_word.rs:188-210 (Action::answer): "Word {}: {}" (restored word) and "Word {}: {} instead of {}" (fitting word and the word as typed; in a mismatch five of the six typed words are the true password's). The answer is moved into Zeroizing at choice.rs:58-72. draw (choice.rs:245-265) runs at the first draw (148) and after every arrow or help key (168, 177-178). The comment at choice.rs:392 ("The label and its line are wiped as the label is") holds only for the final buffers.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with the pinned toolchain 1.99.0, build and run the verifier probe (source kept as docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-check-word-labels/probe-main.rs, SHA-256 58627410a2918ee28acf02e663eea9c2313734af522a0684c31ff22ece1e5b71, Cargo.toml beside it as probe-Cargo.toml; dependencies anstyle =1.0.14 and zeroize =1.9.1, as in Cargo.lock):
  
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target cargo build --offline --release --manifest-path <probe>/Cargo.toml
  <target>/release/verify-check-word-labels criterion
  <target>/release/verify-check-word-labels system
  
  'criterion' counts the blocks freed while they hold a watched password word: GlobalAlloc's default realloc (alloc, copy, dealloc), as the test typed_line.rs:497-566 counts, with allocations zero-filled so that stale bytes never count. 'system' passes realloc to glibc, counts the blocks it moved and freed, and reads what they still hold after the free.
  
  Static trace of variant 1. core::fmt::Arguments::estimated_capacity gives 0 for a format string that starts with an argument. The bold code \x1b[1m (4 bytes) makes the capacity 8, the label grows it to 4+len, and the reset \x1b[0m makes it 2*(4+len). The last growth therefore frees the block that holds the code and the whole label.
  
  Static trace of variant 2, a non-highlighted 'Word 3: zebra' row. After the marker, the number (10 bytes) and two spaces, the capacity goes 8, 16, 32 with the label written, then the padding grows it to 64, which frees the 32-byte block holding the label.
  
  The candidate's own harness (docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/check-word-labels) also still exits 1.
- **Expected behavior:** SECURITY.md:39-41: "Every buffer the program owns that holds a password, phrase, passphrase, entropy, state, Argon2 key or mask is wiped when it is dropped".
  
  RUST-13 (Check: review): secret values live in types that wipe them on drop. CORE-24 (Check: review): a secret lives in an owner type that wipes it.
  
  The project's own contracts:
  - style.rs:65-66: paint is "For public text only ... Secret words are painted by [`boxed_words`]". boxed_words reserves its line so that "writing never reallocates and leaves a copy behind" (style.rs:486).
  - The AUD-023-SEC001 rule at typed_line.rs:161-163: a row that may hold words of a typed password is built in buffers "reserved at its final size and wiped when dropped".
- **Observed behavior:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-check-word-labels/v06-labels-criterion-final.log (exit 1, 52 blocks):
  - A, '?' typed, restore answer highlighted at the first draw: paint(STRONG, label) frees 1 block holding the restored word for every word tried (zoo, zone, zebra, zoning, zoology, zookeeper). The line's format! frees 1 more for 3- to 7-letter words and 0 for 'zookeeper'.
  - B, misspelt word, restore answer reached with two Down presses: paint frees 1, and the line's format! frees 4-5 across the three draws, from highlighted and non-highlighted rows alike.
  - C, mismatch, Down through all eight answers: paint frees 6, one per replacement answer. The line's format! frees 0 because the note is empty.
  - The label's format! frees 0, and the wiped final buffers free 0 (controls).
  
  v07-labels-system-final.log (glibc realloc, exit 1): moved blocks freed by glibc still hold whole words after the free, for example "rd 3: zookeeper", "rd 3: zebra", "rd 3: zoology", "er instead of dandelion", "ing instead of eagle" and "eeper instead of fabric". glibc's tcache overwrote only the first 16 bytes of each.
  
  The candidate's harness reproduces too (v08-candidate-harness.log, exit 1: paint 1 block, other steps 0).
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  1. Its harness label 'zookeeper instead of zookeepr' cannot occur. A replacement is offered only when all six typed words are list words (src/check_word.rs:285-294); a misspelt word gets the restore label 'Word N: zookeeper'.
  2. A repair answer is highlighted at the first draw only when the word was typed as '?' (src/check_word.rs:188-193, check_word.rs:147-151). Otherwise it is painted when the person moves to it, but a restore row's line (variant 2) is built at every draw.
  3. The bytes left after the free start at 'eeper', not 'keeper'.
- **Impact:** Low. Whole words of a password stay in freed, unlocked heap memory until the memory is reused, and can reach swap or a hibernation image: the restored word, the fitting replacement, and in a mismatch the typed words, five of which are the true password's. Reading them needs root or kernel access, a swap device or a hibernation image; the process is non-dumpable and core dumps are disabled. The class is the one rated Low in AUD-023-SEC001 and earlier. AUD-023 recorded the label-format residue as an observation only, after its heap scan found no complete word. At b6fca69, whole words survive the free in paint's block and in the line's block, and the rule set by the AUD-023-SEC001 fix for hint rows is not applied to these list rows.
- **Evidence:** Logs in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-check-word-labels/, each with a .command.json:
  - v06-labels-criterion-final.log: criterion mode, exit 1.
  - v07-labels-system-final.log: glibc realloc with the content read after the free, exit 1.
  - v08-candidate-harness.log: the candidate harness rerun, exit 1.
  - probe-main.rs and probe-Cargo.toml: the probe source.
  - v01-v05: development runs, superseded. v01-v03 counted stale bytes of earlier frees; v05 counted the probe's own copy.
  
  The candidate's logs docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/secrets-native/h03-check-word-labels.log and s06-check-word-labels.log agree.
  
  Static reads at b6fca69: choice.rs:58-72, 136-186, 245-265, 383-415; style.rs:65-69, 481-511; check_word.rs:66-210; src/check_word.rs:164-193, 266-294; typed_line.rs:161-219, 497-566; SECURITY.md:39-41. git status shows no tracked change.
- **Recommended fix:** Build each list line that may hold a secret label in one Zeroizing<String> reserved at its final size: marker, number, colour codes, label, padding and the painted note. Write the style codes straight into that buffer, as boxed_words does at style.rs:497-501, and never pass a label through paint. Alternatively, write the parts directly to the terminal.
  
  Build the check-word labels in buffers reserved at their final size too, and correct the comment at choice.rs:392.
  
  Add a binary test with the freed allocator of typed_line.rs (moved to a shared test module). It should draw a check-word list with a restore answer (with its note) and replacement answers, highlighted and not, whose labels hold a watched word.
- **Required verification:** A regression test in the binary: drawing restore and replacement answers, highlighted and not, frees no block that still holds the watched word. The probe (both modes) and the candidate harness, adapted to the new code, exit 0.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-SEC001, AUD-015-SEC006
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and reproduced the defect with my own probe. The probe copies, with their format strings, Action::answer, Answer::new, label_width, shortened, draw_entry_rows and paint. It draws the restore answers ('?' typed, highlighted at the first draw; a misspelt word, reached with two Down presses) and the mismatch answers (stepping through all eight). It runs in two modes. In the repository's own AUD-023-SEC001 criterion mode (default GlobalAlloc::realloc, allocations zero-filled so that stale bytes never count), every highlighted check-word answer frees exactly one block from paint(STRONG, label) at choice.rs:394 that still holds the word. The controls (the wiped final buffers) free 0. In pass-through glibc realloc mode, blocks that realloc moved and freed still hold whole password words after the free, for example "rd 3: zookeeper" and "eeper instead of fabric". The candidate's harness also still exits 1. The root cause is confirmed, and it is wider than the candidate says. The line's format! at choice.rs:401-411 grows past the label whenever a note follows it, so every draw of a restore answer, highlighted or not, also frees an unwiped block that holds the restored word. The candidate's 0 for that step holds only for the replacement answers, which have an empty note.
  
  Other corrections:
  - A replacement label cannot read 'zookeeper instead of zookeepr'. Replacements exist only when all six typed words are list words (src/check_word.rs:285-294). A misspelt word gets the restore label 'Word N: zookeeper'.
  - A repair answer is highlighted at the first draw only when the word was typed as '?' (repairs_first, src/check_word.rs:188-193; check_word.rs:147-151). Otherwise it is painted when the person moves to it.
  - The bytes left after the free start at 'eeper', not 'keeper'.
  
  Severity stays low, as for AUD-023-SEC001: reading the residue needs root or kernel access, a swap device or a hibernation image. Not done: a measurement inside the real mhfe process. The binary's modules cannot be linked alone, and the process is non-dumpable, so the probe copies the code line by line. No full-cost Argon2 was needed.

##### AUD-024-SEC009 — Low — When the kernel refuses an isolation boundary a secret command needs (the Landlock write ruleset on a kernel without Landlock, or the seccomp socket filter), the refusal is reported nowhere: mhfe self-test still says 'Isolation enforced' without a '!', the startup checks pass silently, and the command summary leaves the boundary out with no warning

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI on Linux: isolation set-up, read-back and reporting (protect.rs, protect/landlock.rs, protect/seccomp.rs, settings.rs, self_test.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-11, RUST-10, CORE-22
- **Affected files and builds:** src/bin/mhfe/protect/landlock.rs:44-46, :88-89, :95-97 (forbid_writes returns false when Landlock is absent or refuses, with no reason kept); src/bin/mhfe/protect/seccomp.rs:73-81 (forbid_sockets returns only whether prctl succeeded); src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:571-590 (isolate_thread folds 'not needed' and 'refused by the kernel' into the same false of Isolation, so the refusal is lost); :347-373 (probe_claims probes only claimed boundaries); :498-527 (IsolationCheck::outcome: Warning only for a refuted claim, NotAvailable only when nothing at all is confirmed, otherwise Passed); src/bin/mhfe/self_test.rs:226 and :246 (Passed is shown as 'enforced' in GOOD style); src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:380-382 and :419-437 (the summary line lists only what holds) and :389-400 (warns only about refuted claims); src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:42-60 (silent unless a part fails). The definition this contradicts is src/self_check/process.rs:24-29, ISOLATION, 'no network, no writes'. Affects every Linux build (x86-64 and aarch64): commands started directly and the start menu's commands, which run in isolated threads.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with a release binary built at b6fca69 (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target cargo build --release --locked --bin mhfe): python3 -B docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-isolation-refusal-report/refused_isolation.py <tmp target>/release/mhfe. On Linux x86-64 it runs `mhfe self-test` (stdin /dev/null), and `mhfe encrypt --pim 0 --mem 0 --same-length no --new-password own --repair-words 0` at TERM=dumb in a pty up to the first secret prompt. It runs both as they are, and then under a seccomp filter installed before exec that makes one call fail as a kernel without the feature does: landlock_create_ruleset returns ENOSYS; prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP) returns EINVAL; unshare returns EPERM. Nothing is typed and no Argon2 round of the command runs. The static trace: without Landlock, landlock.rs:44-46 returns false, so protect.rs:586 sets no_writes=false, which is never probed (protect.rs:350-352). IsolationCheck::outcome gets confirmed={no_network, empty_network}, refuted={} and unverified={} and returns Passed (protect.rs:525), which self_test.rs:246 shows as 'enforced'.
- **Expected behavior:** RUST-11 (code-rust.instructions.md:85-88): 'Every protection is read back before it is relied on, and reported by the startup checks and by the self-test command, as mhfe's CoreDumpCheck and IsolationCheck do. A protection the system refuses is reported, never assumed.' RUST-10 (code-rust.instructions.md:80-83) names seccomp, the namespace and Landlock as a secret command's protections. src/self_check/process.rs:24 defines the Isolation part as 'The sandbox of a command that handles secrets: no network, no writes.' README.md:457-458: 'a yellow "!" warns about a weaker protection'. README.md:133-134: MHFE 'reports which protections hold'. The library's own LockProbe (src/memory.rs:217-224) shows the expected handling of a system refusal: a Warning, shown as '!' in the self-test and in the summary. CORE-22 (code-core.instructions.md:165-171): 'Every error is handled or passed on; none is swallowed.' Only the user namespace is documented as optional (SECURITY.md:126-129).
- **Observed behavior:** As it is (Linux 7.0 with Landlock): self-test 'Isolation enforced'; summary 'Isolation  isolated network, no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)'. With Landlock refused (ENOSYS): self-test 'Isolation enforced' in GOOD style with no '!'; summary 'Isolation  isolated network, no new sockets (kernel-enforced)'; no warning line before the first secret prompt; the checks at start print nothing. With the seccomp filter refused (EINVAL): self-test 'Isolation enforced'; summary 'Isolation  isolated network, no new file writes (kernel-enforced)'; no warning. With unshare refused (EPERM, documented as optional): summary 'no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)', as SECURITY.md documents. All self-test runs exit 0. The unit tests also tolerate a missing boundary in silence: protect.rs:671 asserts only write == !isolation.no_writes, and :1050 runs only `if claimed.no_writes`. No test gives IsolationCheck::outcome a refused boundary.
- **Impact:** On a Linux kernel without Landlock (before 5.13, or with Landlock left out of the LSM list), secret commands run with no file-write restriction. Without seccomp filters they run with no socket filter. mhfe's self-test still calls isolation 'enforced', with no '!', and the person learns of it only from a missing phrase in one summary line. A person who checks the self-test, or reads SECURITY.md's 'On Linux the kernel enforces this', is told a protection holds when the system refused it. This alone exposes no secret, because the protections only back up the documented offline-host requirement. It is a wrong report of a documented security protection, with bounded practical impact: low.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-isolation-refusal-report/v01-refused-isolation.log (probe from scratch, exit 1) and v02-refused-isolation-harness.log (same probe as the kept harness, exit 1, 2026-10-14T09:04:40Z): in the landlock case, self-test row 'Isolation ... enforced' and summary 'Isolation  isolated network, no new sockets (kernel-enforced)', with lines naming writes or Landlock: []; 'DEFECT REPRODUCED'. The seccomp case gives 'enforced' and 'isolated network, no new file writes (kernel-enforced)'. Release binary sha256 1e29adfd59b7eba6995fc160bfabe273274f03c58a6ee843c4a3c683ffc2e33f, built from the clean tree at b6fca69 (cargo build --release --locked was a no-op). The candidate's own log, docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-infra/g17-isolation-report.log, agrees. Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-isolation-refusal-report/ (README.md, refused_isolation.py).
- **Recommended fix:** Have isolate()/isolate_thread() also return what the command needed and the kernel refused: a needed-but-refused Isolation beside the enforced one, kept in the thread-local beside CLAIMED. Give IsolationCheck::outcome a Warning such as 'weaker: file writes are not restricted (no Landlock in this kernel)' when a needed restriction (seccomp or Landlock) was refused. That gives the '!' in the self-test and lets the summary show it. In settings::show, add a warning that names the refused restriction, as is done for refuted claims and for refused memory locking. Keep the user namespace optional, as SECURITY.md documents. Add unit tests that give IsolationCheck::outcome a refused restriction.
- **Required verification:** docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-isolation-refusal-report/refused_isolation.py exits 0: in the landlock case the self-test row carries '!' with a reason and the encrypt output warns that file writes are not restricted. The seccomp case shows the same for sockets, and the unshare case stays without a warning. New unit tests cover IsolationCheck::outcome and the summary text with a refused Landlock and a refused seccomp filter. cargo test --locked protect:: and settings:: pass.
- **Related findings:** An isolated secret command can still change the file system through extended attributes, file modes and timestamps (and through truncate by path on Linux 5.13 to 6.1), while SECURITY.md, README.md and the command summary state that every file write is refused (kernel-enforced)
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with my own probe, run on the release binary built from the clean tree. The probe adds a seccomp filter that mimics a kernel without Landlock (landlock_create_ruleset returns ENOSYS). Under it, `mhfe self-test` still prints "Isolation ... enforced" in the GOOD style with no "!". The `mhfe encrypt` summary drops "or file writes" from the Isolation line, and nothing warns before the first secret prompt. The same happens when the seccomp socket filter is refused: prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP) returns EINVAL, the self-test still says "enforced", and the summary reads "isolated network, no new file writes" with no warning. The code explains it. isolate_thread keeps only booleans of what succeeded, and probe_claims probes only what was claimed. IsolationCheck::outcome returns Passed whenever something is confirmed and nothing was refuted, and the summary warns only about refuted claims. The memory-lock check, by contrast, reports a system refusal as a Warning. That breaks RUST-11 ("A protection the system refuses is reported, never assumed"). It also contradicts the part's own definition, "no network, no writes", and README's promise of a "!" for a weaker protection. No AUD-023 finding or already-confirmed finding covers this root cause. The confirmed finding on xattr, chmod and utime writes is about gaps in the Landlock ruleset while it is in force; this one is about not reporting a ruleset the kernel refused.

##### AUD-024-SEC010 — Low — The Windows build locks no secret memory and takes no step against crash dumps or other processes reading its memory, and the macOS build does not deny debugger attachment, although both systems offer equivalents

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI process and memory protection (src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs, src/memory.rs, src/engine/ffi.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-09, RUST-13
- **Affected files and builds:** Windows x86-64 release (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, scripts/package-release.sh:128; msvc in CI, .github/workflows/ci.yml:115-133) and macOS aarch64/x86_64 release (.github/workflows/release.yml:55-63); README.md:587-588 lists them as release targets. Linux is not affected. The browser has no equivalent and is out of scope. Windows page locking: src/engine/ffi.rs:316-320 (page_size returns None off Unix) and 339-345 (lock_pages returns false, unlock_pages does nothing); src/memory.rs:292-295 (pages::hold returns false when page_size is None, so no LockedText or LockedBytes is locked); src/memory.rs:1-6 (module doc: 'the browser and Windows builds lock nothing') and 203-214 (LockProbe returns NotAvailable 'this build locks no memory on this system' off Unix); src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:453-455 ('not locked on this system'). Windows crash dumps and same-user memory reading: src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:28-47 (harden_process has only #[cfg(unix)] setrlimit and #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] prctl; nothing for Windows); src/engine/ffi.rs:303-304 (exclude_from_core_dumps does nothing off Linux, so the Argon2 work area is not excluded from WER reports); src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:146-151, 170-173, 188-191 (Windows reads nothing back: 'Windows Error Reporting decides whether a crash is saved'); Cargo.toml:63-67 (windows-sys features lack Win32_System_Memory, Win32_System_ErrorReporting and Win32_Security*). macOS attachment: src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:32-47 (no PT_DENY_ATTACH); no hardened-runtime codesign in scripts/ or .github/workflows/. Documentation of the gap: SECURITY.md:54-58 and 74-77, README.md:137-142, docs/API.md:410, docs/releases/v0.5.0.md:110-113.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69, on Linux, with the pinned toolchain on PATH: `python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-platform-hardening/platform_hardening.py`. It prints the cfg of the release targets (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu: windows, not unix; both apple-darwin targets: unix, target_os="macos") and the branches those targets compile (ffi.rs:316-320 and 339-345, memory.rs:210-214, the whole of harden_process at protect.rs:32-47, protect.rs:147-151, Cargo.toml:63-67). It then searches src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs, scripts/*.sh and the workflows for VirtualLock, WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock/WerAddExcludedApplication/WerSetFlags, SetSecurityInfo/SetKernelObjectSecurity and PT_DENY_ATTACH or `codesign --options runtime`. Result: 4 MISSING, 'FAIL: 4 platform equivalent(s) of RUST-09/RUST-13 missing in the Windows or macOS build', exit 1. The project's own tests confirm the Windows behaviour: memory.rs:371-376, 385, 398, 411, 417, 421 and hidden_input.rs:1021 assert is_locked() == cfg!(unix) and notAvailable off Unix, and CI runs them on windows-2025 (ci.yml:115-133). Not executed on a Windows or macOS host (none available).
- **Expected behavior:** RUST-09 (/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/.github/instructions/code-rust.instructions.md:75-78; Check: review): main sets RLIMIT_CORE to 0 and, on Linux, PR_SET_DUMPABLE to 0, 'which also stops other processes of the same user from reading the process memory (ptrace, /proc/PID/mem). Use the equivalent on other systems where one exists.' RUST-13 (same file, 95-98; Check: review): 'Secret values live in types that wipe them on drop (zeroize), with their pages locked (mlock) where their size allows, and large work areas marked MADV_DONTDUMP.' The guide names mhfe's protect.rs and memory.rs as the model for these rules (lines 70-72). Equivalents exist on both systems:
  - Microsoft Learn, VirtualLock: 'These pages are guaranteed not to be written to the pagefile while they are locked'. The lock limit is the minimum working set minus a small overhead (raised with SetProcessWorkingSetSize), which an 8 KiB typed-line buffer fits.
  - Microsoft Learn, WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock (Windows 10 1703+): 'Marks a memory block ... to be excluded from the Windows Error Reporting (WER) error report'.
  - A restrictive process DACL that includes an OWNER RIGHTS ACE denies PROCESS_VM_READ to other non-admin processes of the user.
  - Apple ptrace(2) PT_DENY_ATTACH 'sets a flag that denies future traces'; the hardened runtime additionally blocks debugger attachment unless get-task-allow is granted.
- **Observed behavior:** Windows: every LockedText and LockedBytes stays unlocked (pages::hold returns false because page_size() is None). The memory-locking check reports notAvailable and the summary says 'not locked on this system'. harden_process does nothing, so the process keeps the default DACL, which grants the user's other processes PROCESS_VM_READ, and the default WER behaviour. The Argon2 work area is not registered for exclusion from WER reports. The core-dumps check reports notAvailable ('Windows Error Reporting decides whether a crash is saved'). macOS: RLIMIT_CORE is set to 0 and read back, but nothing denies debugger attachment: no PT_DENY_ATTACH, and no hardened-runtime signature in the release scripts. SECURITY.md:76-77 says 'nothing is locked in a browser or on Windows'; no ADR or audit decision records the owner accepting this.
- **Impact:** Low. On Windows, typed passwords, seed phrases, BIP39 passphrases, entropy and cipher states can be written to an unencrypted page file, where they can outlast the program. A same-user process can read the process memory (OpenProcess with PROCESS_VM_READ). A crash report collected by WER can contain secret buffers and the Argon2 work area. On macOS, a same-user debugger such as lldb can attach to the process where developer tools are enabled. Bounded because the limitation is documented with mitigations (SECURITY.md:76-82, README.md:137-142: BitLocker or no page file, a trusted offline host). A same-user attacker has other means anyway (such as console input capture). The far larger Argon2 work area cannot be locked on any platform.
- **Evidence:** Logged with docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh into docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-platform-hardening/:
  - v01-platform-hardening-trace.log (+ .command.json): exit 1; cfg of the targets, the cited branches with line numbers, 4 MISSING equivalents.
  - v02-tests-assert-windows-locks-nothing.log: exit 0; HEAD b6fca69; the cfg!(unix) assertions in memory.rs and hidden_input.rs; the windows-2025/macos-15 'cargo test --locked' job (ci.yml:115-133); the release targets (release.yml:18, 59, 61; package-release.sh:128; README.md:587-588).
  The baseline docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/b01-check-fast.log shows memory::tests::* and protect::tests::core_dumps_fail_only_when_a_setting_reads_back_otherwise / the_process_forbids_core_dumps passing on Linux. Harness kept: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-platform-hardening/ (README.md, platform_hardening.py). Public reference pages read only: learn.microsoft.com VirtualLock and WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock; Apple ptrace(2) man page (PT_DENY_ATTACH). AUD-023 recorded the same facts as an informational observation without an ID (docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.json, informationalObservations: 'macOS and Windows builds use no equivalent of PR_SET_DUMPABLE and mlock', CHECK-SEC-001). It is not among the 58 AUD-023 findings. RUST-09 and RUST-13 are Check: review rules, which this audit applies to the whole repository.
- **Recommended fix:** Windows:
  - Implement page_size (GetSystemInfo dwPageSize), lock_pages (VirtualLock) and unlock_pages (VirtualUnlock) in src/engine/ffi.rs, keeping the per-page holder counts of memory.rs. VirtualLock does not count, like mlock. Raise the minimum working set with SetProcessWorkingSetSize when needed.
  - In harden_process, register the locked buffers and the Argon2 work area with WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock (or exclude the process from WER).
  - Set a restrictive process DACL (SetSecurityInfo with an OWNER RIGHTS ACE) so that non-admin processes of the user cannot open the process for PROCESS_VM_READ.
  - Add the windows-sys features these calls need.
  macOS: call ptrace(PT_DENY_ATTACH) in harden_process, and sign the release binary with the hardened runtime (codesign --options runtime, ad hoc if need be).
  Read each protection back in LockProbe and CoreDumpCheck (RUST-11). Change the tests' cfg!(unix) expectations accordingly, and update SECURITY.md:54-58/74-77, README.md:137-142 and docs/API.md:410.
- **Required verification:** docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-platform-hardening/platform_hardening.py exits 0. On the windows-2025 CI job:
  - the LockProbe startup check passes and the memory tests assert is_locked() true;
  - a test shows that a second process of the same user cannot open the mhfe process with PROCESS_VM_READ;
  - CoreDumpCheck reads back the WER exclusion and the DACL.
  On macos-15: a test shows that ptrace(PT_ATTACH) from another process fails (EBUSY), and `codesign -d --verbose` of the release binary shows the runtime flag. scripts/verify-hidden-input-windows.py, scripts/verify-hidden-input.py and the terminal suites still pass; the reproducible Windows build stays byte for byte reproducible.
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced statically at b6fca69 (clean tree). I could not refute it.
  
  1. Windows and macOS are documented release targets: README.md:587-588, .github/workflows/release.yml:18 and 54-63, scripts/package-release.sh:128 (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu). `rustc 1.99.0 --print cfg` gives the Windows target `windows` without `unix`, and both macOS targets `unix` with target_os="macos".
  2. On Windows the cfg(not(unix)) branches compile to stubs:
     - ffi.rs:316-320 page_size returns None, and ffi.rs:339-345 lock_pages returns false and unlock_pages does nothing.
     - memory.rs:292-295 pages::hold returns false, so no LockedText or LockedBytes is ever locked.
     - memory.rs:210-214 makes LockProbe answer NotAvailable, and settings.rs:453-455 prints "not locked on this system".
     - ffi.rs:303-304 leaves the Argon2 work area out of no dump.
     - protect.rs:32-47 holds only a cfg(unix) setrlimit and a cfg(linux) prctl. Windows gets nothing and macOS gets no attach denial.
  3. The project's own tests assert this behaviour on the windows-2025 CI job (ci.yml:115-133): memory.rs:374, 385, 398, 411, 417, 421 and hidden_input.rs:1021 assert is_locked() == cfg!(unix).
  4. A harness searching src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs, scripts and workflows finds no VirtualLock, no WER exclusion, no process DACL, no PT_DENY_ATTACH and no hardened-runtime codesign. It exits 1. Cargo.toml:63-67 enables no windows-sys feature that these calls would need.
  5. The equivalents exist (public reference pages, read-only):
     - Microsoft's VirtualLock page: locked pages "are guaranteed not to be written to the pagefile while they are locked".
     - WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock (Windows 10 1703+) excludes a memory block from WER reports.
     - Apple's ptrace(2) PT_DENY_ATTACH "sets a flag that denies future traces".
  6. SECURITY.md:76-77 only documents the gap. No ADR or audit decision accepts it, and AUDIT_STANDARD forbids inferring acceptance. AUD-023 recorded this only as an informational observation without an ID ("macOS and Windows builds use no equivalent of PR_SET_DUMPABLE and mlock", CHECK-SEC-001). It is not one of the 58 findings, so this is not a repeat.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - RUST-11 is dropped from ruleIds. Every check that runs reports truthfully (LockProbe NotAvailable, CoreDumpCheck NotAvailable with "Windows Error Reporting decides whether a crash is saved"), so nothing is assumed. RUST-11 applies only to the fix.
  - Line ranges are narrowed. The Windows work area not being excluded from WER is added as a variant.
  - The macOS fix also names the hardened runtime. Per Apple's man page, PT_DENY_ATTACH blocks ptrace attachment but not task_for_pid memory reads by an entitled process.
  
  Severity stays low. The gap is defence in depth on supported release targets and is documented with mitigations (BitLocker or no page file; a trusted offline host). It needs an unencrypted page file, a same-user malicious process, or a crash with WER dump collection. No full-cost run is needed: nothing here depends on Argon2.

##### AUD-024-SEC011 — Low — On Linux, a zram swap device whose sysfs entry cannot be read (sysfs not mounted, or no sys/class/block/zramN) is treated as in memory, so mhfe gives no swap warning even though it cannot tell whether the device writes back to a plaintext disk

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI swap inventory (src/bin/mhfe/protect/swap.rs) and the swap warning (src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-11, RUST-13, CORE-22
- **Affected files and builds:** Native mhfe command-line binary on Linux only. Other targets return Available(empty) by design, swap.rs:13-18. The browser/WASM package is not affected.
  
  src/bin/mhfe/protect/swap.rs:
  - 98-118, protected(): lines 102-106 read <root>/sys/class/block/<zram>/backing_dev. The comment at 107 says "No attribute: no writeback". Line 108, `Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Some(true)`, returns "safe" whether the attribute, the device's sysfs directory, /sys/class/block or the whole sysfs mount is missing.
  - 100-101: the comment says the attribute is "absent where writeback is not built in".
  - 94-97: the doc comment promises `None` "when that cannot be told".
  - 47-56: swap_inventory drops an area for which protected() returned Some(true).
  - 9-11 and 1-2: the module and function docs ("followed through /sys").
  - Variant of the same root cause, 117 and 122-142 (encrypted()): without sysfs the dm/uuid and slaves reads fail, the result is false, and the area is listed with unknown: false ("surely unencrypted") at 49-52. This contradicts src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:626-630.
  - Tests 224-254: every zram case creates sys/class/block/zram0 through FakeSystem::device (line 230). No test lists a zram or dm device whose sysfs entry is missing.
  
  src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:
  - 159: choose() calls warn_about_swap().
  - 164-176: warn_about_swap.
  - 178-186: swap_warning returns None for Available(empty).
  
  Reached from every command that runs Argon2 (settings::choose): encrypt.rs:174, decrypt.rs:171, check.rs:261, rekey.rs:150 and 175, wallets.rs:67, new_wallet.rs:117, container_repair.rs:264.
  
  SECURITY.md:78-81.
- **Reproduction:** This is a static trace, confirmed end to end with the real binary.
  
  Build: release mhfe from b6fca69 (cargo build --locked --release with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repository; binary SHA-256 1e29adfd59b7eba6995fc160bfabe273274f03c58a6ee843c4a3c683ffc2e33f).
  
  Probe: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-zram-no-sysfs/e2e.sh. Its source is kept in the v04 log. For each case it runs `bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc <case binds> -- mhfe encrypt --stdin < /dev/null`. settings::choose shows the swap warning before the phrase is read, and the command then stops with exit status 2, "Standard input ended before this answer: Original seed phrase", before any Argon2 round.
  
  Cases (each binds a made-up file over /proc/swaps and an empty file at the /dev node):
  - P: /proc/swaps lists `/dev/sda5 partition`, /dev/sda5 exists, /sys is an empty tmpfs.
  - W: lists /dev/zram0, with /sys/class/block/zram0/backing_dev reading /dev/sda5 and /sys/class/block/sda5/slaves present.
  - A: lists /dev/zram0, with /sys/class/block/zram0 present but no backing_dev.
  - B: lists /dev/zram0, /sys an empty tmpfs (a chroot that mounted /proc and /dev but not sysfs).
  - B2: lists /dev/zram0, with the host's real /sys, which has no zram0 entry.
  - Variant probe e2e-dm.sh, D1: lists /dev/dm-0, with /sys/class/block/dm-0/dm/uuid = CRYPT-PLAIN-cryptswap.
  - Variant probe e2e-dm.sh, D2: lists /dev/dm-0, /sys an empty tmpfs.
  
  Command from the repository root:
  docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-zram-no-sysfs v01-e2e-bwrap /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-zram-no-sysfs/e2e.sh <mhfe>
  Then the same with v03-e2e-dm-variant and e2e-dm.sh.
  
  Static trace for B: device_of_node canonicalizes <root>/dev/zram0 and gets "zram0" (swap.rs:64-68). protected() reads <root>/sys/class/block/zram0/backing_dev, which gives ENOENT because the parent is missing. Line 108 returns Some(true). Line 48 drops the area, giving Available([]). settings.rs:184-186 returns None, so no warning is printed.
  
  The candidate's kept harness gives the same result: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/zram-no-sysfs (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<target> cargo run --offline --release --manifest-path docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/secrets-native/zram-no-sysfs/Cargo.toml -- <scratch>`) exits 1.
- **Expected behavior:** 1. swap.rs:94-97: protected() gives `None` "when that cannot be told, as for a zram writeback device that cannot be resolved (AUD-023-SEC002)". swap_inventory (53-56) then lists the area as unknown, and settings.rs:189-193 warns "MHFE cannot tell whether swap is encrypted".
  2. SECURITY.md:79-81: "the tool therefore warns, before any secret is typed, when a swap area is not encrypted with dm-crypt, directly or under LVM, or when it cannot tell; swap in memory (zram) is safe only without a writeback device".
  3. protect.rs:628-629, SwapArea.unknown: "False when it is surely unencrypted, true when MHFE cannot tell".
  4. RUST-11: "A protection the system refuses is reported, never assumed."
  5. RUST-13: "The program warns when swap is not encrypted."
  6. CORE-22: "'Unknown' stays apart from 'none' ... Every error is handled or passed on; none is swallowed."
  
  A failed read of the device's sysfs entry is "unknown". It is evidence neither of "no writeback device" nor of "not encrypted".
- **Observed behavior:** v01-e2e-bwrap.log, with the real binary:
  - P: "! Swap on this computer is not encrypted: /dev/sda5."
  - W: "! Swap on this computer is not encrypted: /dev/zram0." The AUD-023-SEC002 fix works when sysfs is visible.
  - A: no warning, which is correct.
  - B (sysfs not mounted): no warning.
  - B2 (sysfs mounted, no zram0 entry): no warning.
  - In every case the command then ends with exit status 2 at the empty phrase input.
  
  So a missing sysfs mount or a missing device directory is read as "writeback not built in", which it does not show.
  
  Same root cause, milder variant (v03-e2e-dm-variant.log):
  - D1, dm-crypt with sysfs visible: no warning, which is correct.
  - D2, the same /dev/dm-0 with /sys not mounted: "! Swap on this computer is not encrypted: /dev/dm-0." The warning is still given, but it states as fact that the area is unencrypted (unknown: false) when MHFE cannot tell. It should be "MHFE cannot tell whether swap is encrypted".
  
  The existing tests pass (b01-check-fast.log: protect::swap::tests::zram_is_protected_only_without_a_plaintext_writeback_device ... ok) because none of them removes the device's sysfs entry.
- **Impact:** Low.
  
  The warning is suppressed only when all of these hold:
  - mhfe runs on Linux in an environment where /proc and the /dev/zramN node are visible but sysfs is not. The typical case is a hand-made chroot that mounts only /proc and /dev. Docker, Podman, systemd-nspawn and Flatpak mount /sys. Docker's /dev has no zram node, so there the area is already listed as unknown and warned about.
  - The host's zram swap has CONFIG_ZRAM_WRITEBACK and a plaintext backing_dev set by root.
  - Writeback is triggered while mhfe runs.
  - Someone later reads that disk.
  
  Under these conditions, pages of the Argon2 work area can reach the disk unencrypted. That area is gigabytes in size, cannot be locked, and a password guess can be tested cheaply from its blocks (SECURITY.md:78-79). The person is not given the warning SECURITY.md promises.
  
  The dm-crypt variant only causes a false and alarming "not encrypted" message where "cannot tell" is due. It is fail-safe.
  
  The class and prerequisites are the same as AUD-023-SEC002 and AUD-020-SEC001, both rated Low. Not release-blocking.

- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69: the tracked tree is clean, swap.rs has SHA-256 7e8ee78c... (the same hash the candidate recorded) and the release binary was built from it. I could not refute the candidate. In protected() (swap.rs:98-118), a zram device's writeback is judged only from fs::read_to_string(<root>/sys/class/block/<dev>/backing_dev). The NotFound arm at line 108 returns Some(true), "in memory, safe". That arm fires for several different reasons: the attribute is missing (writeback not built in, which is correct), the device's sysfs directory is missing, /sys/class/block is missing, or sysfs is not mounted at all. Only the first reason supports "no writeback".
  
  I reproduced this end to end with the real release binary, without the candidate's harness. I ran `mhfe encrypt --stdin < /dev/null` inside bubblewrap with a made-up /proc/swaps, /dev and /sys. warn_about_swap runs at settings.rs:159, before the phrase is read, and the command then stops with "Standard input ended before this answer", before any Argon2 round. Results:
  - Plain partition (control): warned.
  - zram0 whose visible backing_dev names a plaintext partition (control): warned. This shows the AUD-023-SEC002 fix works when sysfs is visible.
  - zram0 with a sysfs entry and no backing_dev: correctly not warned.
  - zram0 with /sys empty, i.e. not mounted: NOT warned.
  - zram0 on the host's real sysfs, which has no zram0 entry: NOT warned.
  
  The AUD-023-SEC002 fix (253ca3c) followed that finding's own recommendation ("absent or 'none'") and did not separate an absent attribute from an absent sysfs entry. So this is a remaining gap in that fix, not a duplicate.
  
  The same root cause has a second, milder variant in encrypted(). Without sysfs, a dm-crypt swap is reported as "Swap on this computer is not encrypted: /dev/dm-0." It should be reported as "cannot tell". The warning is still shown, but it states something false. I grouped this variant under the finding.
  
  Severity stays low. The suppressed warning needs all of these together: a chroot-like setup without sysfs but with /dev/zramN visible, root-configured zram writeback to a plaintext device, and an actual writeback while mhfe runs. Docker's /dev has no zram node, so there the area is already warned about as unknown. This matches the class and rating of AUD-023-SEC002. Corrections to the candidate:
  - Line ranges fixed: settings.rs:159, 164-176 and 178-186.
  - All eight settings::choose call sites listed.
  - CORE-22 added.
  - The dm-crypt variant added.
  - A fix proposed that does not depend on a `dev` attribute the FakeSystem helper does not create.

##### AUD-024-SEC012 — Low — On Windows the swap check returns an inspected, empty inventory without inspecting anything, so an unencrypted page file never triggers the swap warning before Argon2 runs

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI swap warning (src/bin/mhfe/protect/swap.rs, protect.rs, settings.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-13, RUST-11
- **Affected files and builds:** Windows x86-64 release build of the mhfe CLI (README.md:587-588 lists Windows x86-64 among the release archives; release.yml builds it). Locations at b6fca69:
  - src/bin/mhfe/protect/swap.rs:9-19: unprotected_swap() returns SwapInventory::Available(Vec::new()) outside Linux. Comment at :16: 'macOS encrypts its swap; Windows keeps its page file without telling'. The doc comment at :10-11 says 'A readable empty inventory is distinct from a failed read'.
  - src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:619-621: mod swap is compiled on every platform.
  - src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:633-638: SwapInventory, documented as 'An inspected swap inventory, or an unavailable Linux inventory that must still warn'.
  - src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:159: choose() calls warn_about_swap.
  - src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:164-176: warn_about_swap.
  - src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:178-186: swap_warning; empty Available gives None; the Unavailable text names Linux.
  - src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:524-534: test pinning Available([]) to no warning.
  - Contracts the Windows build breaks: src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:5-7, src/memory.rs:5-6, src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:442-443 ('the warning about unencrypted swap covers it').
  - Public text that limits the warning to Linux: SECURITY.md:78-82, README.md:139-142.
  macOS builds take the same branch, but macOS encrypts swap unconditionally, so they are not affected in practice.
- **Reproduction:** 1. Static trace at b6fca69. unprotected_swap() tests cfg!(target_os = "linux") (swap.rs:13). In a Windows build that is false, so it returns SwapInventory::Available(Vec::new()) (swap.rs:17) without reading anything. This is the value swap_inventory() returns for a readable /proc/swaps with only its heading (swap.rs:26-60). swap_warning() destructures Available and returns None for an empty list (settings.rs:179-186). warn_about_swap() then returns before style::warn (settings.rs:166-168). choose() runs it before every Argon2 command (settings.rs:142-162), so a Windows run gives no swap warning before the secret prompts.
  2. Executable probe. From the repository root, run: python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-repro/non-linux-swap/non_linux_swap.py <scratch>. It copies unprotected_swap, SwapArea, SwapInventory and swap_warning unchanged into one Rust file and sets the cfg! to false, its value in a Windows build. It then compiles and runs that file. Output: 'control (Unavailable): Some("MHFE cannot read the Linux swap inventory, so its encryption is unknown.")', 'non-Linux build: inventory Available([]), warning None', exit 1.
  3. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<target> cargo test --locked --bin mhfe swap gives 11 passed. settings::tests::unavailable_swap_warns_while_confirmed_empty_does_not asserts swap_warning(&Available(Vec::new())) == None. No test calls unprotected_swap() on the non-Linux branch.
  Not executed: no Windows host in this review.
- **Expected behavior:** - RUST-13 (code-rust.instructions.md:95-98, Check: review, no platform exception): 'The program warns when swap is not encrypted.'
  - RUST-11 (code-rust.instructions.md:85-88): 'A protection the system refuses is reported, never assumed.'
  - The project's rule from AUD-020-SEC001, kept in protect.rs:633 and in swap.rs tests :281-305: a swap state that was not established must not suppress the warning; 'unknown' must not look like 'confirmed empty'.
  - The code's own contracts: protect.rs:5-7 promises 'a warning when swap could write memory to a disk without encryption'. memory.rs:5-6 says 'the program warns instead when swap is not encrypted'. settings.rs:442-443 says the Argon2 work area is covered by 'the warning about unencrypted swap'.
  - Windows encrypts its page file only with BitLocker or device encryption on the volume, or with NtfsEncryptPagingFile=1 (fsutil behavior set encryptpagingfile 1); the default is off.
- **Observed behavior:** In the Windows build, unprotected_swap() returns Available([]). That is the value meaning 'inspected, and no unprotected swap', although nothing was inspected. The code's own comment admits it: 'Windows keeps its page file without telling'. The Argon2 work area, which runs to gigabytes, is not locked; on Windows nothing is locked at all (memory.rs:4). It can be paged to a plaintext pagefile.sys, and the tool prints no warning and no 'cannot tell' notice before the secret prompts. The same conditions on Linux, an unencrypted swap or an inventory that cannot be read, do produce a warning. The startup checks and self-test have no swap line on any platform (evidence secrets-native/s11-self-test.log), so nothing else reports it. The Unavailable warning text itself names Linux only (settings.rs:181).
  The macOS half of the candidate does not hold as a defect. macOS has always encrypted swap since OS X 10.8, with no user setting to turn it off. Every macOS version the Rust darwin targets support is covered, so the comment at swap.rs:16 is accurate. Reading vm.swapusage back would only add defence in depth; this goes to observations.
- **Impact:** Low, per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a missing protective diagnostic with bounded practical impact. A Windows user running an everyday system without BitLocker or device encryption gets no runtime warning. The Argon2 work area can then be written to an unencrypted page file, where it can stay. From its blocks a password guess can be tested cheaply (SECURITY.md:78-79). This needs actual paging under memory pressure and later access to the disk. Bounded because SECURITY.md:81-82 and README.md:141-142 tell Windows users to use BitLocker or no page file, and README.md:136-137 recommends Windows PE, which normally has no page file. No secret extraction was demonstrated.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-repro/v-swap01-non-linux-swap.log and .command.json: exit 1. The probe shows inventory Available([]) and warning None for the non-Linux branch; the control with Unavailable gives Some(...). The harness and its README are in docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-repro/non-linux-swap/. The generated probe source is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-repro/non-linux-swap/non_linux_swap.rs.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-repro/v-swap02-swap-unit-tests.log: cargo test --locked --bin mhfe swap, 11 passed, including settings::tests::unavailable_swap_warns_while_confirmed_empty_does_not, which pins Available([]) to no warning.
  - grep of src, scripts and packaging for 'bitlocker', 'page file', 'pagefile' and 'paging': the only hit is the comment at swap.rs:16, so no Windows-specific check exists.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/secrets-native/s11-self-test.log: the self-test has no swap line.
  - Prior records: AUD-020-SEC001 (Linux-only fix) and AUD-023-SEC002, whose 'Affected' field notes the non-Linux empty inventory without raising it. No owner acceptance is found in docs/audits or AUD-005-decisions.md.
- **Recommended fix:** On Windows, return SwapInventory::Unavailable, or a Windows-specific unknown state, unless the page file's protection can be read back. It can be read back when NtfsEncryptPagingFile is 1 (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem), or when BitLocker protection is on for every volume listed in PagingFiles (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management). No page file at all counts as an empty inventory. Make the Unavailable warning platform-neutral: it currently says 'Linux swap inventory'. Keep macOS as is, or read vm.swapusage as defence in depth. Update the comment at swap.rs:16 and the SwapInventory doc at protect.rs:633. Add unit tests for the non-Linux branch: give the platform test a seam, as unprotected_swap_under does for Linux.
- **Required verification:** - A unit test on the Windows branch: an unreadable or unknown page-file state gives a warning, an encrypted page file or no page file gives none. Run it in the CI portable job on windows-2025.
  - On a Windows host without BitLocker and with a page file, a command that runs Argon2 (for example mhfe encrypt at its first prompt) shows the swap warning before any secret prompt.
  - The harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-repro/non-linux-swap/non_linux_swap.py exits 0, or the fix's own tests replace it if the shape changes.
  - The existing Linux swap tests keep their outcomes.
- **Related findings:** AUD-020-SEC001, AUD-023-SEC002

That is the same value a readable but empty /proc/swaps gives. swap_warning() (settings.rs:178-186) returns None for it, so warn_about_swap() (settings.rs:165-168, called from choose() at settings.rs:159 before every Argon2 command) prints nothing.

A control run with Unavailable does warn. The project's own test settings::tests::unavailable_swap_warns_while_confirmed_empty_does_not passes, and it pins swap_warning(Available([])) to None.
