  On the Windows x86-64 release build, an unencrypted pagefile.sys therefore gets no warning. That breaks RUST-13 ('The program warns when swap is not encrypted', Check: review, no platform exception). It also breaks the code's own contracts in protect.rs:5-7, memory.rs:5-6 and settings.rs:442-443, and the type's own meaning, 'An inspected swap inventory', at protect.rs:633. No owner acceptance is recorded in any audit decision.
  
  The macOS half of the candidate is not a defect. Since OS X 10.8 macOS always encrypts swap and has no setting to turn it off, so the comment matches the system. Not reading vm.swapusage is at most a defence-in-depth observation (not run on a macOS host).
  
  Severity stays low. SECURITY.md:78-82 and README.md:139-142 openly limit the warning to Linux and tell Windows users to use BitLocker or no page file. Exploitation also needs paging of the Argon2 work area and later access to the disk.

##### AUD-024-SEC013 — Low — mhfe new copies the chosen word out of its locked buffer into an ordinary heap string and keeps it there, unlocked, while it waits for the person to type the word never to use

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: secrets in memory (mhfe new chosen word; rekey passphrase copy)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-13
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool on Linux and macOS, the builds where LockedText locks its pages. Present at b6fca69 and in the released v0.6.0 (the same line is in v0.6.0's chosen_words.rs).
  - src/bin/mhfe/chosen_words.rs:158-166, read_chosen. Line 160: input.secret_words(...) returns a LockedText. Line 165: `Ok(vec![(place, Zeroizing::new(word.to_string()))])` copies it into an unlocked heap String. The LockedText is dropped (wiped, unlocked) when the function returns.
  - src/bin/mhfe/chosen_words.rs:105-114, ask. The copy is held in `chosen` while read_never_use (:112, :191-195; it waits at :193) reads the word never to use. It is dropped only at the end of the loop body (:131) or at a return (:125, :130).
  - src/bin/mhfe/new_wallet.rs:111 and :158. mhfe new runs only at a terminal (private_input), so the never-use prompt always waits for a person whenever a word is chosen and --never-use is not given.
  - Minor variant, momentary: src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:349-353 copies the wallet's BIP39 passphrase out of WalletReference's LockedText into a Zeroizing<String> for the 16-bit source check (:354). The copy is dropped at :386 with no wait for the person in between.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with the b6fca69 release binary (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --release --bin mhfe), run:
  
  python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-chosen-word-unlocked/chosen_word_unlocked.py /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/release/mhfe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-chosen-word-unlocked/run
  
  It drives `mhfe new --pim 0 --mem 0 --wallet-check no --repair-words 0` in a pseudo-terminal: no passphrase, choose a word, type the public word "zoo" as "ZoO", Enter for anywhere, then "zooo" (refused) at the never-use prompt, then Ctrl+C. Nothing is drawn and no Argon2 runs beyond the checks at start.
  
  The preloaded shim locked_scan.c records mlock/munlock page by page. Each time the program blocks in read(0), it scans the program's writable memory through process_vm_readv for "ZoO".
  
  Static trace: chosen_words.rs:160 -> :165 -> :105-112 -> :193.
- **Expected behavior:** - RUST-13: "Secret values live in types that wipe them on drop (zeroize), with their pages locked (mlock) where their size allows."
  - SECURITY.md:57-66: "The secrets the program keeps beyond a moment are held in locked memory (mlock) ... a seed phrase as text, whether typed, recovered, new or a hidden wallet's". The list of copies that are wiped but not locked (SECURITY.md:68-74) does not name the chosen word's text.
  - The code itself calls the word secret. chosen_words.rs:156: "typed hidden on a private screen as part of the secret phrase". src/memory.rs:14-17: LockedText is the type for "Text that is secret, or may be".
- **Observed behavior:** Probe log v02-chosen-word-lock-scan, exit 1, reproduced on a second run:
  - S1, chosen-word prompt: no copy.
  - S2, position prompt: one copy in a LOCKED 8 KiB heap chunk, which is the typed line's LockedText (positive control). A second copy sits in the standard library's stdin buffer, an exception SECURITY.md already names.
  - S3, never-use prompt: "[... UNLOCKED chunk-size-word=0x21 region=[heap]] total 1". The only copy of the chosen word is a live 32-byte heap allocation in an unlocked page, while the locked page count falls from 8 to 5.
  - S4, first question again after the refusal: total 0. The copy was wiped by Zeroizing, so it was live and not freed residue.
  
  While the person decides on a word never to use, the chosen word (a word of the new seed phrase) is held only in memory the system may write to swap.
- **Impact:** Limited, the same class the project has rated Low before (AUD-014-SEC002, AUD-023-SEC001).
  - Prerequisites: an unencrypted swap device, the heap page swapped out while the prompt waits, and later privileged or physical access to that swap.
  - What is exposed: one word of the new 24-word phrase. Per chosen_words.rs:200-206 and README "Chosen words", that word lets someone rule out almost every wrong password and tell the wallet from a decoy.
  - SECURITY.md's statement that secrets kept beyond a moment are locked does not hold for this copy.
  - The gain from a fix is bounded. After the never-use answer, the library's WordWishes keeps the word's number unlocked in a plain Vec (src/word_wishes.rs:89-96) through the repair-words question (new_wallet.rs:159) and the draw. SECURITY.md:70-71 lists these "word numbers a phrase ... is drawn from" among wiped-but-unlocked copies.
  - The rekey variant is momentary. It breaches RUST-13's locking requirement but not SECURITY.md's "beyond a moment".
- **Evidence:** Folder: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-chosen-word-unlocked/
  - v01-release-build: cargo build --locked --release --bin mhfe, already up to date at b6fca69.
  - v02-chosen-word-lock-scan: the harness run, exit 1, stages S1-S4 as quoted under observed.
  - v03-code-excerpts: HEAD, SHA-256 of the files, and the cited lines of chosen_words.rs, new_wallet.rs, rekey.rs, memory.rs, word_wishes.rs and SECURITY.md:54-77; also shows the copy in v0.6.0.
  
  File hashes: chosen_words.rs d0c8009b..., rekey.rs eead2ff9..., SECURITY.md 35dfc63b....
  
  Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-chosen-word-unlocked/ (README.md, chosen_word_unlocked.py, locked_scan.c).
  
  Scratch outputs: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-chosen-word-unlocked/run{1,2}/ and run/scan.log.
- **Recommended fix:** - read_chosen: return Vec<(Place, LockedText)> and build the pairs for WordWishes::new by borrowing (`(*place, &**word)`), so the chosen word stays in its locked buffer until the wishes are taken.
  - rekey.rs record_recovery: bind the Reference in a local and pass its passphrase().unwrap_or("") by reference instead of copying it into a Zeroizing<String>.
  - Optionally, lock WordWishes' word numbers as well, or keep SECURITY.md's list of wiped-but-unlocked copies stating that the chosen word's number is among them.
- **Required verification:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-chosen-word-unlocked/chosen_word_unlocked.py exits 0: no unlocked live copy at S3, and the S2 and S4 controls still hold.
  - A unit test that the chosen-word answer is kept as LockedText, checked with is_locked() where locking is permitted.
  - A code check that record_recovery no longer copies the passphrase.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-SEC001, AUD-014-SEC002
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 on the real release binary. A preloaded shim recorded every mlock/munlock and scanned the process's writable memory each time it blocked on standard input. While the never-use prompt waits, the chosen word typed as "ZoO" is held in exactly one place: a live 32-byte heap chunk (size word 0x21) in an UNLOCKED page. One prompt earlier, the same word sits in a LOCKED 8 KiB buffer. After the next answer the copy is gone (wiped by Zeroizing), so it was a live copy, not freed residue. Two runs gave the same result.
  
  The static trace matches. read_chosen (chosen_words.rs:160) receives a LockedText, copies it at :165 with Zeroizing::new(word.to_string()), and keeps the copy in `chosen` through read_never_use (:112, :193). mhfe new runs only at a terminal (new_wallet.rs:111), so that prompt always waits for a person unless --never-use is given.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - RUST-13 is the rule breached. CORE-24 is met, because Zeroizing owns and wipes the copy; only RUST-13's locking part is missing.
  - The rekey passphrase copy (rekey.rs:350-353) is a minor variant. It is momentary: it is dropped at :386 with no wait for the person. It breaches RUST-13 and could be avoided, but it does not contradict SECURITY.md's "beyond a moment".
  - I dropped the wallet_reference.rs:84 variant. The text there is a one-word address, a public value; only a single-word secret typed into the wrong field would be exposed, which I could not establish as a defect.
  
  Context that limits the gain from a fix: once the never-use answer is in, the library's WordWishes keeps the chosen word's number in a plain Vec (word_wishes.rs:89-96) through the repair-words question and the draw. SECURITY.md:70-71 already names this among the copies that are wiped but not locked.
  
  Not a duplicate. The confirmed findings about repair words and memory cover check-word repairs and browser objects, not the chosen word. AUD-014-SEC002 was about wiping, not locking.

##### AUD-024-SEC014 — Low — A random source is checked only by check_source's one-time two-block probe: a source that is then stuck makes uniform_below retry with no limit (a password draw never returns), and a source that is then stuck or fills only part of each buffer gives out a fixed or half-zero 24-word phrase without an error

- **Category:** SEC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** random source / password generator / new phrase draw
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-004
- **Rules:** CORE-50, CHECK-SEC-004
- **Affected files and builds:** src/random.rs:52-64: check_source, two 32-byte probes, the only source check on any draw path.
  src/random.rs:70-88: uniform_below. Its rejection loop at lines 79-87 has no retry limit and no error path besides a failed fill.
  src/random.rs:34-37: the RandomSource contract 'Fills bytes completely, or fails'. The library relies on it and never verifies it.
  src/new_password.rs:136-144: PasswordRecipe::make. check_source runs once at line 139, then uniform_below at line 142 for words and the check word.
  src/new_password.rs:216-232: characters_from, with uniform_below at line 223.
  src/wallet_check.rs:219-251: PhraseDraw::try_draws refuses only an all-zero entropy (lines 231-235).
  src/wallet_check.rs:253-271: PhraseDraw::draw, with check_source once at line 262.
  src/wallet_check/threads.rs:82-99: threaded checked draw, with check_source once per thread at line 85, then try_draws(source, 1) in a loop.
  src/random/health.rs:24-42: check_spread, which refuses both faulty sources. Its only non-test caller is the live part of the Tier::Full self-check at lines 193-200.
  
  Builds affected:
  - Native CLI: mhfe password via src/bin/mhfe/made_password.rs:177, diceware paths at src/bin/mhfe/diceware.rs:212 and :290, and mhfe new via src/bin/mhfe/new_wallet.rs:317.
  - Browser modules: browser-passwords (makePassword, src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:198) and browser-wallet (drawPhrase, src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:248).
  - The public Rust library API: PasswordRecipe::make, PhraseDraw::draw and draw_on_every_core, random::uniform_below.
  
  Shipped sources: src/bin/mhfe/system_random.rs:9-13 (getrandom::fill) and web/worker-runtime.js:108 (self.crypto.getRandomValues). Both fill completely or fail, so a faulty host source is needed to trigger the defect.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with the pinned toolchain and the workspace CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME:
  
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-random-source/run.sh
  
  The probe uses only the public API and synthetic sources:
  - StuckAfterProbe gives two different non-zero 32-byte probes, then one constant byte for ever.
  - HalfFill writes only the first half of each buffer.
  
  What the harness runs:
  (1) PasswordRecipe::characters(16), ::words(5) and ::check_word(), each with .make() and a source stuck on 0xff after its probes, given 5 s on a thread. 0xff is at or above 228, the last full multiple of 57, and 0xffff is at or above 62,208 for 7,776 words, so every value is refused.
  (2) PhraseDraw::unchecked().draw() with sources stuck on 0xff and on 0x5a after their probes.
  (3) PhraseDraw::unchecked().draw() with the half-filling source.
  (4) Controls: check_spread on both faulty sources, and make() with a working LCG source.
  
  The core-crypto harness reproduces (1) and (3) as well: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/core-crypto/run.sh findings, lines stuck-source-is-refused and half-filling-source-is-refused.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-50 (code-core.instructions.md, Check: review): 'Searches, retries, batches, ranges and concurrency have explicit limits that the person sets or the program states. Work that grows with input stops at its limit and says so.' uniform_below's rejection loop is a retry on host input and should stop at a stated limit with RANDOM_FAILED.
  
  CHECK-SEC-004 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md:154-156) requires the injected source's 'repeated/short/oversized responses' to be handled. A source that cannot be random should end the draw with RANDOM_FAILED instead of hanging or giving out a fixed or half-zero phrase. Continuous health tests for this case are the practice of NIST SP 800-90B section 4.4 (repetition count and adaptive proportion tests).
  
  The library's own error contract names this case: RANDOM_FAILED is 'The random source failed or gave bytes that cannot be random' (docs/API.md:704).
- **Observed behavior:** check_source returned Ok(()) for both the stuck-after-probe source and the half-filling source. Then:
  (1) characters-16, words-5 and check-word make() did not return within 5 s: 819,268,618, 735,053,707 and 697,618,043 fills respectively, still drawing, with no error and no limit.
  (2) The unchecked draw gave out Ok("zoo zoo ... zoo vote") (23 x zoo, the all-0xff entropy) for 0xff. For 0x5a it gave a phrase repeating the 8 words 'fog spot notable regret pizza coffee harvest ensure'.
  (3) The half-filling source gave Ok("budget wreck earth daughter stairs entry harsh away rent junk dawn divorce abandon x11 arrive"): only 128 random bits, the other 16 entropy bytes zero.
  (4) Controls passed: check_spread returned RANDOM_FAILED for both faulty sources, and a working source made a 16-character password in 18 fills.
  
  By static trace, a checked draw (mhfe new with a passphrase, src/wallet_check/threads.rs:86-97) with a source stuck after its probe would retry the same entropy until the person stops it. The native CLI's on_draws is a no-op (src/bin/mhfe/new_wallet.rs:317). I did not run this case.
- **Impact:** With a faulty or substituted host random source that passes the start probe, a password draw (CLI mhfe password or browser makePassword) hangs for ever without an error. A new 24-word phrase (mhfe new, browser drawPhrase) can be given out fixed (for example 'zoo ... vote') or with half its entropy zero, and nothing is reported. Funds sent to such a phrase would be guessable. No secret leaks, and the impact is bounded: the shipped sources (getrandom, crypto.getRandomValues) fill completely or fail, and a page cannot inject its own source. Only an OS or browser generator failure after the probe, or a third-party Rust caller's contract-breaking RandomSource, triggers it.
- **Evidence:** All commands were run from the repository root through docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh. Evidence is in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-random-source/:
  
  - v01-faulty-source-after-probe.log and .command.json: scratch probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-random-source/probe, built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.0, cargo build --offline --release. Exit 1, with 3 hangs, 2 fixed phrases and 1 half-zero phrase.
  - v02-static-trace.log: git rev-parse HEAD = b6fca69238344dd2525b06270ee6ff3b055e68c1, the cited lines, every check_source( caller (src/wallet_check.rs:262, src/new_password.rs:139, src/wallet_check/threads.rs:85) and every check_spread( caller (only src/random/health.rs:156-163 and 198, the self-check, plus tests).
  - v03-harness.log and .command.json: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-random-source/run.sh, exit 1. Six FAIL lines, and PASS for the two controls.
  
  The candidate's own evidence agrees: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/core-crypto/c04-probe-uniform-below-hangs.log, c04-probe-short-fill.log and c13-harness-findings.log (stuck-source-is-refused and half-filling-source-is-refused FAIL).
- **Recommended fix:** 1. Bound uniform_below. After a stated number of consecutive refused values, for example a named constant of 64, return MhfeError::RandomFailed. A working source reaches 64 refusals with probability (28/256)^64, about 2^-204, for 57 characters, and (3,328/65,536)^64, about 2^-275, for 7,776 words. Assert that bound in a test, as health.rs does for check_spread.
  2. Add a continuous check on the draw paths. In PhraseDraw::try_draws and the threaded search, refuse an entropy equal to the previous one or to a probe block, a repetition test. At the start of every make() and draw() session, run check_spread over a fresh 1 KiB (cheap), which refuses both a source stuck after the probe and a half-filling one.
  3. Name the limits in the doc comments of uniform_below, check_source and RandomSource, and in docs/API.md next to RANDOM_FAILED.
- **Required verification:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-random-source/run.sh: every line PASS, exit 0.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/core-crypto/run.sh findings: stuck-source-is-refused and half-filling-source-is-refused PASS.
  - New unit tests in src/random.rs (uniform_below with a source stuck after its probe returns RANDOM_FAILED within the limit) and src/wallet_check.rs (stuck-after-probe and half-filling sources refused by draw and by the threaded draw).
  - A test asserting the false-alarm bound of the new retry limit.
  - The existing tests still pass: random::, wallet_check::, new_password:: (cargo test --locked with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside target/), the random-source self-check and the password-generator known answers.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and reproduced the defect with my own probe, built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside target/. No Argon2 runs. The only check on a random source is check_source (src/random.rs:52-64): two 32-byte probes, run once per make() or draw() (src/new_password.rs:139, src/wallet_check.rs:262, src/wallet_check/threads.rs:85). After that probe, nothing bounds or checks what the source returns:
  - uniform_below's rejection loop (src/random.rs:79-87) has no retry limit.
  - try_draws refuses only an all-zero entropy (src/wallet_check.rs:231-235).
  - check_spread runs only on the live source in the full self-check (src/random/health.rs:193-200).
  
  What I observed with a source that passes the probe:
  - A source stuck on 0xff after the probe made 16-character, 5-word and check-word passwords run for 5 s (about 0.7 to 0.8 billion fills) with no error.
  - A half-filling source produced a 24-word phrase whose last 128 bits of entropy are zero.
  - I also found a variant the candidate did not list. A source that repeats one byte after the probe produces a fixed phrase: "zoo" 23 times then "vote" for 0xff, and a repeating 8-word pattern for 0x5a.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - I added the stuck-source phrase variant, which is the clearest unhandled "repeated response" case under CHECK-SEC-004.
  - I removed CORE-46 from ruleIds. The shipped sources are the operating system's and the browser's cryptographic generators handed in from outside, so that rule is met.
  - health.rs:4-8 ("the guard before every draw") is accurate, since check_source does run before each draw call, and the docs state its two-block scope (docs/API.md:380-381, README.md:469-470). The expected behaviour therefore rests on CORE-50 and CHECK-SEC-004, not on a contradiction in the project's own documentation.
  
  Severity stays low under AUDIT_STANDARD.md: only a host source that breaks the RandomSource contract or fails after the probe triggers it. getrandom and crypto.getRandomValues fill completely or fail, and a page cannot supply its own source (docs/API.md:1048-1050).

#### FUN

##### AUD-024-FUN001 — Medium — The missing-word search with a master key fingerprint of the container's own wallet returns the first candidate that matches and never looks for a second. When two missing words of a 12-word container leave another candidate with the same 32-bit fingerprint before the real one, the tool shows that other container as the found container phrase, unqualified, and tells the owner to write its words on the copy.

- **Category:** FUN.
- **Severity:** medium.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Library missing-word search (src/search.rs). Used by the CLI's decrypt, check, rekey, wallets and repair, and by the browser package's MhfeClient.searchDecoy.
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-FUN-001
- **Rules:** CORE-22, DOC-07
- **Affected files and builds:** src/search.rs:15-16: the module doc says a candidate that matches proves 'a fingerprint with 32 bits'.
  src/search.rs:32-34: MAX_MISSING_FOR_DECOY = 2 for every container length, so a 12-word container has 2048^2/16 = 262,144 candidates.
  src/search.rs:64-73: Found holds one container and no count of other matches.
  src/search.rs:127-152: search_decoy. Its doc at :131-132 says 'the first match stops them all', and it returns one Option<Found>.
  src/search.rs:275-367: native compare_candidates. At :297-299 and :313, `stop` ends the taking of candidates after a match. At :319-325 it keeps the lowest index and sets stop. Its result type Option<(usize, CheckOutcome)> cannot express a second match.
  src/search.rs:373-387: wasm32 compare_candidates returns at the first match.
  src/search.rs:161-197: search_wallet also returns its first match, the same pattern. With at most 128 candidates there, it is negligible.
  src/bin/mhfe/container_search.rs:280-327: with_container_wallet. For a fingerprint, reference.show_search prints nothing (src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:131-136).
  src/bin/mhfe/container_search.rs:485-490: found_answers, with 'and write the found words on your copy' at :487.
  src/bin/mhfe/container_search.rs:493-558: use_found prints 'Found container phrase, N words' (:506) and 'Found word …, with the container's own wallet.' (:526).
  src/wasm_api/core/search.rs:107-136 and web/client.js:560-600: searchDecoy resolves to one container.
  Documents: docs/API.md:257-260 ('stopping at the first match'). README.md:625-628 offers the fingerprint for the search with no caveat, whereas README.md:240-241 and src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:594-600 (match_limit) give the 32-bit caveat for a single comparison.
  Builds: every native build and the browser package. The case that matters is a 12-word container, which is always a same-length (suite 4) container with no verifier.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, run: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/aud024-verify-decoy-target docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-decoy-fingerprint-collision/run.sh <mhfe release binary built from b6fca69>. It takes about 25 s and runs no Argon2.
  
  Part 1 is a library probe (probe/src/main.rs). It checks that 'abandon'x10 'able ghost' and 'abandon'x10 'best student' share fingerprint a30a4e0f, and that 'amused buzz' and 'employ giraffe' share 02ba9d7a. It then calls ContainerSearch::new('abandon'x10 '? ?').search_decoy(&Reference::Fingerprint { fingerprint of the later phrase, passphrase: "" }, DECOY_SCAN_GAP, ..).
  
  Part 2 (cli_found.py) drives `mhfe decrypt --pim 0` on a pseudo-terminal with the terminal suite's Session. It types 'abandon'x10 '? ?', then Enter for no repair words. It answers 1 (the container's own wallet), a30a4e0f, and 1 (no passphrase). After 'Use it' it presses Ctrl+C at 'Container password:', so no password is typed.
  
  The complete list of 8 colliding pairs comes from docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/decoy.sh (about 66 CPU minutes).
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-22 (code-core.instructions.md:165-171, Check: review): a search that stopped early is a result of its own, and 'A partial result stays visibly partial', because 'a failure read as an empty result becomes a false conclusion about a wallet'. A search that stops after its first match has not compared the other candidates. So it must not present that match as the one container found. It must report every match, or say that a second match was not looked for.
  
  DOC-07 (docs.instructions.md:41-45): documents, help and messages claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides. search.rs:15-16 says a fingerprint match proves 32 bits. Among 262,144 candidates it proves about 15: the returned candidate is wrong with probability about 2^-15. The CLI's own single-comparison caveat, 'A fingerprint is a quick 32-bit check; an address (--address) is stronger.' (check.rs:599), README.md:240-241 and the specification's rehearsal section ('the BIP32 master key fingerprint as a quicker but weaker 32-bit check', mhfe_spec/README.md) all treat the fingerprint as a 32-bit check. The search, where it is about 2^18 times weaker, says nothing.
- **Observed behavior:** The library probe (library-probe.log) shows that both pairs share their fingerprints (equal: true). search_decoy returned [(11, "able"), (12, "ghost")] for the fingerprint of 'best student', after about 285 of 262,144 candidates. It returned [(11, "amused"), (12, "buzz")] for that of 'employ giraffe', after about 8,100. Both results read 'container is [later]: false', and the Found value has no sign of a second match.
  
  The kept gap-1 harness (harness-decoy.log) finds 8 colliding pairs among the 262,144 candidates. In 8 of 8 searches the earlier candidate is returned.
  
  mhfe decrypt (cli-decrypt-found.log) prints 'Comparing 262144 candidates with the container's own wallet.', then 'Found container phrase, 12 words' with words 11 'able' and 12 'ghost'. It prints '✓ Found word 11: able, word 12: ghost, with the container's own wallet.' and offers '1 Use it — and write the found words on your copy'. It gives no word about another match or about the fingerprint's strength. On 'Use it' it goes to 'Container password:' with that container.

- **Impact:** Prerequisites: two words of a 12-word container are lost, there is no repair card, and the owner gives the master key fingerprint of the container's own wallet. MHFE prints this fingerprint under every container it makes (README.md:165-169). Among 262,144 candidates about 8 pairs share a fingerprint, so the owner's container is the later member of a pair, and is shadowed, about once in 32,768 such searches. For a 24-word container (16,384 candidates) this is about once in 524,000, and with one missing word it is negligible.
  
  When it happens, the tool shows a wrong container as found and tells the owner to write its words on the backup. That corrupts the written copy, which loses the record of which words were missing. decrypt then recovers another valid 12-word phrase with only the warning that every same-length recovery carries: 'Not verified: a 12-word container has no built-in check' (decrypt.rs:289-297). Nothing points at the found words. mhfe repair shows the wrong container with a fingerprint equal to the owner's record. A later mhfe check against the original wallet says 'does not match', which points to the password or settings instead. The outcome is a wrong reconstructed secret in supported behaviour, with no secret disclosed, so the severity is medium.

The rule guards against a stopped or failed search being shown as a negative result. search_decoy never does that. It stops early only after a candidate truly matches the given reference, and it returns that match. Without a match it compares every candidate, and a cancel or error returns Err (search.rs:305-366). A first match is not partial data. Stopping there is the documented contract of the operation:

None of the confirmed AUD-024 findings has this root cause. The Scope::spawn finding is in the same function but has a different root cause.
  
  Why it is not a matter of taste:
  - The help's per-check statement ('a match is very likely right') is true for one comparison. The search, however, raises the false-match chance 262,143-fold, to about 1 in 16,385, and then silently picks the lowest index. No help, README text or API doc states those odds.
  - The project and its specification otherwise refuse to pick one of several matches silently. The spec says several matching lengths 'MUST NOT pick one silently', and the library has Recovery::Ambiguous for a 1-in-4-billion event.
  - Detecting the ambiguity costs no more than a search that finds nothing.
  - The result breaks CORE-22: whether another candidate matches is unknown, yet the result is presented as the container found.

It is left as analysis, not part of the confirmed evidence.
