- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, build with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --bin mhfe. Then run docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dumb-colour pty-dumb-colour python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-dumb-colour/probe.py /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/debug/mhfe packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py. The probe starts each program in a clean environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, plus the listed variables), with stdin, stdout and stderr on one pseudo-terminal of 100x40. It runs five invocations: 'mhfe frobnicate' (usage error), 'mhfe --help', 'mhfe repair-words --count 4' (Ctrl+C at the container prompt), 'mhfe-fast-mode.py --help' and 'mhfe-fast-mode.py /nonexistent/index.html' (refused, nothing served). It counts ESC[...m sequences. No Argon2 runs. Manual equivalent: in any terminal, run 'TERM=dumb CI=false mhfe frobnicate' and see the red '✗ Error:'.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-38 (code-core.instructions.md:289-292): 'NO_COLOR turns colour off, CLICOLOR_FORCE turns it on, TERM=dumb and CLICOLOR=0 turn it off.' Only CLICOLOR_FORCE turns colour on; CI is no colour signal and CLICOLOR=1 does not override TERM=dumb. The project's own text, src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:3-5, says colour codes are dropped 'when the terminal cannot show colours', and TERM=dumb declares a terminal that cannot.
- **Observed behavior:** Log pty-dumb-colour.log, run 2026-10-14T08:56:00Z to 08:56:16Z, exit 1, '20 TERM=dumb cases without CLICOLOR_FORCE carry colour'. At TERM=dumb with no extra variable, every invocation writes 0 SGR sequences. With CI='true', CI='', CI='false' or CLICOLOR='1' at TERM=dumb, mhfe frobnicate writes 7 SGR sequences, starting b'\r\n\x1b[1m\x1b[31m\xe2\x9c\x97 Error:\x1b[0m Unrecognized subcommand ...'. mhfe --help writes 108, mhfe repair-words --count 4 writes 17 before Ctrl+C, mhfe-fast-mode.py --help writes 32 and the launcher's refusal writes 8. With CI=true plus NO_COLOR=1, or plus CLICOLOR=0, they write 0. CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 at TERM=dumb colours, as the rule allows. The cli-ux reviewer's run of the full repair-words card (pty-dumb-ci.log) gives 0 sequences with no variable, 48 with CI=true and 48 with CLICOLOR=1. Its harness check dumb_terminal_has_no_colour_with_ci_or_clicolor FAILs (verify-cli-ux.log line 8).
- **Impact:** Presentation only. Where a dumb terminal (Emacs shell or compilation mode, some IDE or serial consoles) runs with CI set, by a CI-like wrapper or even as CI=false, or with CLICOLOR=1 exported globally, every heading, label, hint, help section and '✗ Error:' line of mhfe and of the Python launcher carries raw escape codes, which show up as garbage. Input handling, results for scripts (pipes stay plain) and secrets are not affected.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dumb-colour/pty-dumb-colour.log with pty-dumb-colour.command.json (verifier probe, exit 1, 20 breaching cases across mhfe and mhfe-fast-mode.py). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/pty-dumb-ci.log (reviewer, exit 0 of the driver, SGR counts 0/48/48). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/verify-cli-ux.log line 8: 'FAIL dumb_terminal_has_no_colour_with_ci_or_clicolor'. Static trace: grep finds no ColorChoice/write_global in src/. anstream-1.0.0/src/auto.rs:205-219 gives the decision order NO_COLOR, then CLICOLOR_FORCE, then CLICOLOR=0, then is_terminal && (TERM not dumb || CLICOLOR set || CI set). anstyle-query-1.1.5/src/lib.rs:134 is std::env::var_os("CI").is_some(). Cargo.lock pins anstream 1.0.0 and anstyle-query 1.1.5. packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:130 and scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py:273,276 encode the same behaviour for the launcher. AUD-023 (CHECK-UI-003) recorded only the CI case, as an observation.
- **Recommended fix:** In main.rs, before the clap parse, so that help and usage errors follow too: when NO_COLOR is empty or unset, CLICOLOR_FORCE is empty or unset, and TERM is 'dumb', call anstream::ColorChoice::Never.write_global(). anstream keeps NO_COLOR first and CLICOLOR_FORCE as the only way to turn colour on. Put the decision in one small function with a unit test over the CORE-38 table: TERM=dumb with CI, CI=false or CLICOLOR=1 gives no colour, and TERM=dumb with CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 gives colour. Make the same change in packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py colours() (line 130: require TERM not 'dumb' before CLICOLOR or CI can turn colour on). Change ANSTREAM_ANSWERS and test_colours_follow_anstream in scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py, since the rule then differs from bare anstream: expect no colour for TERM=dumb with CLICOLOR=1 and for TERM=dumb with CI=true. Update the module doc of style.rs:1-6 to state the rule.
- **Required verification:** Run python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/cli-ux/verify_cli_ux.py <mhfe> and check that dumb_terminal_has_no_colour_with_ci_or_clicolor passes. Rerun the verifier probe (tmp/aud024/verify-dumb-colour/probe.py <mhfe> packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py): it should report 0 breaching cases and exit 0, with TERM=dumb CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 still coloured, TERM=dumb CI=true NO_COLOR=1 still plain, and TERM=xterm-256color still coloured. python3 scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py passes with the updated colour table. The new Rust unit test of the colour decision passes under cargo test --locked.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced it at b6fca69 with my own logged pseudo-terminal probe. I used a debug build in the audit target directory and ran only commands that need no Argon2: a usage error, --help, and repair-words stopped with Ctrl+C at its first prompt, plus the Python launcher's --help and a refusal. At TERM=dumb with no colour variable, mhfe writes 0 SGR sequences. With CI=true, CI='', CI=false or CLICOLOR=1 it writes 7 (usage error), 108 (--help) or 17 (repair-words) SGR sequences. NO_COLOR=1 and CLICOLOR=0 still turn colour off.
  
  The cause is confirmed in the code. mhfe never sets an anstream ColorChoice, so it relies on anstream's automatic choice. In anstream 1.0.0 auto.rs:211-214, colour is on at a terminal when term_supports_color() OR CLICOLOR is set (not 0) OR is_ci(). is_ci() in anstyle-query 1.1.5 lib.rs:134 is var_os("CI").is_some(), so any CI value, even "false" or empty, turns colour on. That breaks CORE-38, which says TERM=dumb turns colour off and gives only CLICOLOR_FORCE the role of turning it on.
  
  The same root cause has a second variant. packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py copies anstream's rule on purpose (colours(), line 130). Its unit test in scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py:273 and :276 asserts colour for TERM=dumb with CLICOLOR=1, and for CI=true. My probe shows the launcher also colours its help and its refusal at TERM=dumb with CI or CLICOLOR=1.
  
  This is not a duplicate. AUD-023 recorded only the CI case, as an observation, under CHECK-UI-003. It was not one of its 58 findings. CORE-38 is a review rule, which this audit applies to the whole repository. None of the already confirmed findings is about colour choice.

##### AUD-024-UI005 — Low — A container or phrase that is valid but that the command cannot use ends the command right after it was typed, instead of being asked again: wallets with a 12- to 21-word container, encrypt --same-length with a 24-word phrase, and a --words length that a same-length container cannot have

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: container and phrase reading
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** CORE-42, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** Native CLI, every platform, terminal input (with --stdin the refusal is correct, since a script cannot be asked again).
  - src/bin/mhfe/wallets.rs:77-83: terminal::read_container, then `container.require_hidden_wallets()?` at :83, outside the read loop. Library refusal: src/container.rs:129-136 (NoHiddenWallets); message at src/error.rs:259-262. The shared prompt src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:573 (CONTAINER_PROMPT, "Container, 24 words or as long as the original seed phrase: ") invites the short container that wallets then refuses.
  - src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:178-180 (read_original, then choose_suite) and :343-344 (`Suite::SameLength.require_original(words)?`). Refusal: src/suite.rs:94-99 (SameLengthNeedsShortPhrase); message at src/error.rs:232-235. The --same-length long help at src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:55-67 ends "A 24-word phrase always gives 24 words." (:64-65).
  - Same root cause, a --words conflict with the typed container: src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:173-180 (`container.require_length(length)?`); src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:263-272 (`container.require_reference(...)?`); src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:218-224 calling phrase_length, whose refusal is at :640 (`container.require_length(given)?`).
  - The retype path these checks bypass: Input::accepted at src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:107-122, used only for ContainerFacts::read (terminal.rs:603-606) and OriginalFacts::read (encrypt.rs:451). Exit-code mapping to 2: src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs:69-73.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with a debug build at b6fca69 (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<workspace>/tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --bin mhfe):
  1. python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-container-ask-again/check_container_ask_again.py <target>/debug/mhfe
     Each terminal case starts mhfe in a pseudo-terminal (TERM=xterm-256color), types one answer and checks whether the command is still running 10 s later. Nothing reaches an Argon2 round: each case ends with a refusal first, or is stopped with Ctrl+C.
  2. By hand: `mhfe wallets --pim 0 --mem 0`, then type the 12-word "abandon x11 about" phrase at "Container, 24 words or as long as the original seed phrase:".
  3. `mhfe encrypt --same-length --pim 0 --mem 0`, then type the 24-word "abandon x23 art" phrase at "Original seed phrase".
  4. `mhfe decrypt|check|rekey --words 15 --pim 0 --mem 0`, then type the 12-word phrase as the container.
  5. Control: `mhfe wallets --pim 0 --mem 0` with 24 x abandon (bad checksum) shows "1 Type it again / 2 Repair it with its repair words". With the valid 24-word phrase it goes on to the passphrase question.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-42 (.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md:310-314, "Check: review"): "A wrong or unusable answer is explained in one line and asked again, keeping earlier answers. A command ends only on the person's Escape or Ctrl+C, or on a critical self-test failure." The rule's reason: "an abrupt end loses everything the person typed, secrets included." At a terminal, Input::can_ask_again() is true (terminal.rs:102-105), so the refusal can be shown and the container or phrase asked again, as the command already does for an invalid container or phrase.
  
  DOC-06 (docs.instructions.md:36-39): code and documents agree. The --same-length help says "A 24-word phrase always gives 24 words" (encrypt.rs:64-65), which reads as the option making no difference for a 24-word phrase, not as a refusal. The wallets prompt asks for a container "24 words or as long as the original seed phrase", although wallets accepts only 24 words (README.md:383, 397).
- **Observed behavior:** - wallets + 12-word container: after "Container 12 words, valid / Format MHFE-BIP39-LP-EXPERIMENTAL-4 (no built-in check)", the command prints "✗ Error: A container of 12 words opens no hidden wallets: they are opened on a 24-word container only, for now" and exits 2.
  - encrypt --same-length + 24-word phrase: after the secret phrase is typed and "Phrase 24 words, valid" is shown, it prints "✗ Error: A 24-word phrase has no same-length container: its container always has 24 words. Encrypt it without choosing the same length" and exits 2.
  - decrypt --words 15 and rekey --words 15 with a 12-word container: "✗ Error: A container of 12 words keeps the length of its original seed phrase, so no length is chosen for it; ...", exit 2.
  - check --words 15 with a 12-word container: "✗ Error: A container of 12 words has no built-in check; ...", exit 2.
  - In no case is "Please type it again" shown, nor any choice to retype.
  - Controls: an invalid container gets the "Type it again" choice, and a usable 24-word container goes on to the next question. With --stdin, encrypt --same-length and a 24-word phrase exits 2 with empty standard output, which is correct for a script.
- **Impact:** At a terminal, a person who types the wrong container, or who passed an option that does not fit their phrase, loses everything typed so far and must start the command again. For encrypt this includes the original seed phrase, a secret typed in full. No secret is exposed and no wrong result is produced: the refusal comes before any Argon2 round and the cause is named. The cost is bounded to retyping, so the severity is low.
- **Evidence:** All under docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-container-ask-again/, each with a .command.json:
  - build-debug.log: cargo build --locked --bin mhfe, exit 0, up to date at b6fca69.
  - harness-container-ask-again.log: the kept harness. Output: PASS control_wallets_with_a_24_word_container; FAIL for the five terminal cases, each "ended by itself with exit code 2" plus its error text; PASS script_encrypt_same_length_24_still_exits_2; "2 of 7 checks pass"; exit 1.
  - pty-container-ask-again.log: probe tmp/aud024/verify-container-ask-again/probe.py (workspace scratch). It shows the full screens: the control ends with exit 130 after Ctrl+C at the "Type it again" choice; the five cases end with exit 2 and asked again False; --stdin exits 2.
  The cli-ux role's logs match: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/pty-wallets-short-container.log, pty-same-length-24.log (both exit 2) and verify-cli-ux.log (FAIL wallets_asks_again_for_a_short_container).
  Static trace: wallets.rs:83 and encrypt.rs:344 return their MhfeError through `?` after the read loops at terminal.rs:599-607 and encrypt.rs:446-453 have ended. The only re-asking wrapper, Input::accepted (terminal.rs:107-122), wraps only the parse.
  Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-container-ask-again/ (README.md, check_container_ask_again.py).
- **Recommended fix:** Check the command's requirement inside the read loop, so that a refusal goes through Input::accepted and the answer is asked again (Escape still ends the command):
  - read_container (and read_original) take an extra requirement closure, e.g. `input.accepted(ContainerFacts::read(w).and_then(|c| require(&c).map(|_| c)), TYPE_AGAIN)`.
  - wallets passes require_hidden_wallets and asks "Container, 24 words:" in its own prompt.
  - encrypt --same-length with a 24-word phrase: either make the 24-word container with a one-line note, which matches the help's "A 24-word phrase always gives 24 words", or explain and ask for the phrase again. Update the --same-length help to say which one.
  - decrypt, check and rekey with a conflicting --words: explain the conflict and ask for the container again (still before the password, as AUD-008-FUN002 requires).
  - Keep the exit-2 refusal for --stdin.
- **Required verification:** python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-container-ask-again/check_container_ask_again.py <mhfe> prints 7 PASS lines and exits 0. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/cli-ux/verify_cli_ux.py passes wallets_asks_again_for_a_short_container. A terminal-suite case types a 12-word container at wallets and a 24-word phrase at encrypt --same-length, and finds the retype message and the prompt again (or the documented 24-word outcome). The --stdin refusals still exit 2.
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with the debug build (cargo build --locked, up to date) in a pseudo-terminal. All five terminal cases end with exit 2 straight after the answer, with no "Please type it again" and no choice to retype: `wallets` with a valid 12-word container, `encrypt --same-length` with a valid 24-word phrase, and decrypt/check/rekey `--words 15` with a 12-word container. A control case shows the retype path exists for a container that is not valid: 24 x abandon gets the "Type it again" choice, and a valid 24-word container moves on to the next question.
  
  The cause, traced statically: the container and phrase readers wrap only ContainerFacts::read and OriginalFacts::read in Input::accepted, which explains the refusal and asks again (terminal.rs:603-606, encrypt.rs:451). The command's own requirement on the answer is checked after the read loop, where `?` turns its refusal into an exit-2 Failure (exit.rs:69-73). Both commands run at a terminal, where can_ask_again() is true (wallets accepts only a terminal), so asking again was possible. CORE-42 says a command ends only on Escape, Ctrl+C or a critical self-test failure.
  
  The --stdin case still ends with exit 2, which is correct for a script. This is not a duplicate: the confirmed line-reader finding (non-UTF-8 or long lines) and AUD-023-UI002 (rekey refuses an invalid --new-pim only after recovery) have other root causes. Severity is low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: the person loses typed input and must retype it, and no secret is exposed.

##### AUD-024-UI006 — Low — At a terminal that cannot redraw (TERM=dumb), encrypt skips the container-length and repair-word questions, and rekey skips the repair-word question. They silently take 24 words and no repair card, although the helps and README.md say a person at a terminal is asked and Input::choose has a numbered form for such terminals.

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: questions of encrypt and rekey
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** Native CLI on every platform, at a terminal where hidden_input::can_redraw() is false (TERM=dumb, or a console without control sequences); standard input and standard error are terminals.
  
  Code:
  - src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:352-355: choose_suite returns Suite::TwentyFourWords when !hidden_input::can_redraw(). It records no 'Container' choice, unlike the --same-length paths at :331-350 and the asked question.
  - src/bin/mhfe/container_repair.rs:651-656: ask_when_creating returns None (no repair words, no 'Repair' record) when !hidden_input::can_redraw(). It is reached through RepairWordsOption::choose (:627-633) from encrypt.rs:183 and rekey.rs:184.
  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:187-190, 199-205: Input::choose falls back to numbered answers for 'a terminal that cannot redraw lines'. container_repair.rs:594 (ask_count) already uses it, and container_repair.rs:537 (mhfe repair-words) asks the same question numbered at TERM=dumb.
  - src/bin/mhfe/length_choice.rs:15-46 uses choice::choose directly, so the length question has no numbered fallback today.
  
  Documents that disagree:
  - encrypt.rs:61, the --same-length long help: 'Without it, a person at a terminal is asked, and 24 words is the default'.
  - container_repair.rs:645, the --repair-words long help of encrypt and rekey: 'Asked at a terminal when not given; a script that does not give it gets none'.
  - encrypt.rs:133-157, the encrypt --help 'What it asks for' section: Container length 'for 12 to 21 words: 24 words (default) or the same length'; Repair words 'at a terminal: none, or 2, 4, 6 or 8'.
  - README.md:214-216: 'For 12 to 21 words, choose the container length'.
  - README.md:400-402: 'encrypt, new and rekey offer them'.
  
  Test that fixes the skip as intended:
  - scripts/terminal_suite/menus.py:141-160 (check_encrypt_numbered). Its docstring (:142-145) says neither question 'can be a list there', although Input::choose would number the repair question.
  
  Not affected: mhfe new, which refuses TERM=dumb before any question (new_wallet.rs:111, terminal::private_input).
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, on a debug build of b6fca69 (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --bin mhfe):
  1. python3 /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-dumb-length-question/probe.py /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/debug/mhfe. The probe runs `mhfe encrypt` in a pseudo-terminal at TERM=dumb and then at TERM=xterm-256color. It answers the settings question with Enter and types the public phrase 'abandon x11 about'. At TERM=xterm-256color it answers the length list with Enter. It records which questions appear before the password prompt and ends with Ctrl+C at the password prompt or at the repair list, before any Argon2 round. Result: exit 1, 'TERM=dumb asks: []', 'TERM=xterm-256color asks: [length, repair]'.
  2. python3 /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-dumb-length-question/repair_words_dumb.py /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/debug/mhfe. This runs `mhfe repair-words` at TERM=dumb with the 24-word public phrase 'abandon x23 art'. Result: exit 0; 'Repair words for the container phrase?' is shown with numbered answers 1-4 and 'Choice [1]:'.
  3. For rekey, a static trace: rekey.rs:184 calls the same RepairWordsOption::choose and ask_when_creating guard. Reaching it dynamically needs a full-cost recovery of the old container, which the audit rules forbid; the code path is identical.
- **Expected behavior:** Per DOC-06 (code and documents agree; a mismatch is named and settled, never left silently), the documents and the code should say the same thing. The --same-length help (encrypt.rs:61), the --repair-words help (container_repair.rs:645), the encrypt --help 'What it asks for' section (encrypt.rs:133-157) and README.md:214-216 and :400-402 all say that a person at a terminal is asked the container length (12- to 21-word phrases) and the repair words. They name scripts as the only case that is not asked. Input::choose (terminal.rs:187-190) documents the numbered form as the way a terminal that cannot redraw gets such questions. The settings question of encrypt and the repair question of mhfe repair-words are asked that way at TERM=dumb.
- **Observed behavior:** At TERM=dumb, `mhfe encrypt` asks the settings question in numbered form. After a 12-word phrase it prints 'Phrase 12 words, valid', then 'Letter case and spaces count.' and 'Container password (hidden):'. It asks neither the container length nor the repair words, and it records no 'Container' or 'Repair' line. At TERM=xterm-256color the same input is asked 'Your phrase has 12 words. How long should the encrypted phrase be?' and then 'Repair words for the container phrase?'. `mhfe rekey` at TERM=dumb skips its repair-word question through the same guard. No help text, README section or other user document says that these questions are skipped at such a terminal. The skip is stated only in a code comment (encrypt.rs:352) and in the terminal suite's docstring.
- **Impact:** A person at a terminal without control sequences silently gets a 24-word container with no repair card. They are never told that a same-length container or repair words exist, unless they read the option help, which says they would have been asked. The defaults are the safe ones (24 words is the recommended suite 3, as the specification's 'Choosing the suite' requires), so no secret is exposed and no wrong container is made. The defect is limited to presentation and documentation.
- **Evidence:** Logs in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dumb-length-question/, each with a .command.json beside it:
  - build-debug.log: cargo build --locked --bin mhfe, exit 0; the build was up to date with the clean tree.
  - pty-dumb-vs-xterm-encrypt.log: probe.py, exit 1. TERM=dumb asks [] between the phrase and the password; TERM=xterm-256color asks [length, repair]. Both runs exit with code 130 after Ctrl+C.
  - pty-dumb-repair-words.log: repair_words_dumb.py, exit 0. The same ask_count question appears numbered at TERM=dumb.
  - encrypt-help.log and rekey-help.log: the --same-length and --repair-words long helps and the 'What it asks for' section as printed by the binary.
  - static-trace.log: the git rev-parse HEAD result (b6fca69238344dd2525b06270ee6ff3b055e68c1) and grep -n of every cited line.
  
  The candidate's own logs agree: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/pty-dumb-encrypt.log, pty-xterm-encrypt.log and pty-dumb-repair-words.log. The baseline docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/b11-terminal-suite-fast.log:44 shows the terminal suite asserting the skip ('encrypt, TERM=dumb: the hidden password right after the hidden phrase'). History: the skip predates AUD-023 (choice::can_run() at 253ca3c^). AUD-010 (docs/audits/AUD-010-2026-10-07.md:875) recorded it only as an observation, noting 'README does not say what is skipped'; no document was changed since. Probes: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-dumb-length-question/probe.py and repair_words_dumb.py.
- **Recommended fix:** Settle the mismatch in one direction, in one change.
  (a) Preferred: ask both questions at every terminal through Input::choose. Its numbered form already serves TERM=dumb. Remove the !can_redraw() guards in encrypt.rs:353 and container_repair.rs:652. The terminal suite's check_encrypt_numbered is updated to match. The rekey repair-word path is checked the same way, statically or by a full-cost run if one is authorized. The encrypt and rekey --help texts and README.md:214-216 and :400-402 agree with the code.

At TERM=dumb, mhfe encrypt asks the settings question in the numbered form ('Choice [1]:'). After the public 12-word phrase it goes straight to 'Container password (hidden):', with no container-length question and no repair-word question. The same run at TERM=xterm-256color asks both. The probe exits 1 ('TERM=dumb skips [length, repair]'). The numbered form exists for exactly this repair question: mhfe repair-words at TERM=dumb asks the same container_repair::ask_count question numbered, and my probe exits 0. Only the guards at encrypt.rs:353 and container_repair.rs:652 skip the questions. The --same-length and --repair-words helps, the encrypt --help 'What it asks for' section and README.md say a person at a terminal is asked, and they name no exception except scripts. AUD-010 recorded the skip only as an observation; no document was changed, so code and documents still disagree (DOC-06). Corrections to the candidate: rekey has no length question (it keeps the container's suite), so only its repair-word question is affected. mhfe new is not affected, because it refuses TERM=dumb before any question (new_wallet.rs:111). CORE-39 is dropped: it requires only plain sequential output at TERM=dumb, and the tool keeps to that. Not a duplicate of any confirmed finding or of AUD-023-UI004, which is about control sequences in word hints.

##### AUD-024-UI007 — Low — mhfe rekey --confirm show is refused only after the container, its length and the old password have been typed. Where no private screen can open (TERM=dumb, standard output redirected, a Windows console without VT), this is known at start, and --new-password words is refused at start in the same condition.

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: rekey
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** CORE-42
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool, `mhfe rekey`, every platform, wherever `terminal::can_show_privately` is false: TERM=dumb, standard output or standard error redirected or on another terminal, standard input not a terminal, or a Windows console without VT sequences.
  - src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:244-249: `choose_confirmation` refuses `(Some(Kind::Owner), _) if !terminal::can_show_privately(input)` with Failure::invalid_input (exit 2). It is called at rekey.rs:166, only after `read_old_container` at rekey.rs:165. That function reads the container (:218-222), the phrase length (:224, asked unless --words is given or the container fixes it) and the old password (:227-230).
  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal/private_screen.rs:110-116: `can_show_privately` depends only on the standard streams and the terminal (hidden_input.rs:287-292). Its doc says a command that must show a phrase only privately "refuses otherwise, before anything secret is asked".
  - Contrast rekey.rs:146 `options.new_password.check(&input)`, which calls made_password.rs:98-121 (`refuse_kind`: "Refuses at the start, before anything secret is asked or computed"), and rekey.rs:156-158 (`refuse_confirm` for a given --words, the AUD-023-UI002 fix). Also `terminal::private_input` in new_wallet.rs:111 and wallets.rs:60.
  - README.md:305-306 ("It is unavailable without a private screen.") says nothing of when the refusal comes.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with the debug binary built by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<tmp>/aud024/target cargo build --locked --bin mhfe` at b6fca69, run the probe in a pseudo-terminal with public data only. The probe is kept in tmp as verify-rekey-confirm-show-late/probe.py.
  1. TERM=dumb: `mhfe rekey --confirm show --pim 0 --mem 0`. Type the public 24-word phrase (23 x abandon + art), then '5' (24 words), then any synthetic old password. Result: 'Container 24 words, valid', the length question, 'Old container password (hidden)', 'Password typed', and then '✗ Error: --confirm show needs a terminal that can show the phrase on a private screen.' with exit 2.
  2. The same with TERM=xterm-256color and standard output redirected to a file: the same late refusal, exit 2.
  3. Control in both conditions: `mhfe rekey --new-password words --pim 0 --mem 0` is refused at once with '✗ Error: A password made by MHFE is shown only on a private screen ...', exit 2, before the container prompt.
  The kept cli-ux harness check `confirm_show_is_refused_before_the_container` (docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/cli-ux/verify_cli_ux.py) fails for the same reason.
- **Expected behavior:** The project's own rule, at the function the guard calls (src/bin/mhfe/terminal/private_screen.rs:110-113): "A command that must show a phrase only privately refuses otherwise, before anything secret is asked (AUD-007-SEC001)." The tool follows it for --new-password (made_password.rs:98-99) and for mhfe new and mhfe wallets (`private_input`).
  AUD-023-UI002's expected behaviour: a given --confirm is judged "before the container and the old password are asked".
  CORE-42 (code-core.instructions.md:310-314): a command ends only on Escape or Ctrl+C, so that an abrupt end does not lose what the person typed, secrets included.
  The outcome of `can_show_privately` is fixed at process start. The given --confirm show should therefore be refused at the start of rekey::run, beside new_password.check, before the container is asked.
- **Observed behavior:** The refusal comes from choose_confirmation (rekey.rs:244-249), after the container, the length answer and the old password have been entered (rekey.rs:165, 218-232). The command then ends with exit 2, and the person must start again and type the container and the old password a second time. No memory reservation or Argon2 round precedes the refusal: `recover` is called at rekey.rs:169, after it. The match arm refuses `Some(Kind::Owner)` for any value of `rekey.confirmation_needed()`, so nothing typed can change the outcome.
  The AUD-023-UI002 fix (253ca3c) added early refusals only for a --confirm way the length does not allow (rekey.rs:156-158 and 225). Before that fix the private-screen refusal was already in the same place, after the password (253ca3c^:src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs, match after Rekey::new).
- **Impact:** A person who runs `mhfe rekey --confirm show` at a terminal that cannot show a private screen types the old container phrase, answers the length question and types the old password, and only then learns that the option cannot work there. Everything typed is lost, and the run must be repeated with another --confirm or at another terminal. No wrong result and no disclosure: no secret leaves the terminal, and no Argon2 work is wasted.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-rekey-confirm-show-late/probe.log and probe.command.json (exit 0 = the claimed order was observed). RESULT lines:
    - 'confirm-show TERM=dumb redirected=False: after-password, exit 2'
    - 'new-password-words TERM=dumb redirected=False: start, exit 2'
    - 'confirm-show TERM=xterm-256color redirected=True: after-password, exit 2'
    - 'new-password-words TERM=xterm-256color redirected=True: start, exit 2'
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/pty-rekey-confirm-show-dumb.log: the same TERM=dumb transcript, exit 2 after 'Password typed'.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/verify-cli-ux.log: 'FAIL confirm_show_is_refused_before_the_container'.
  - Static trace at b6fca69: rekey.rs:145-146 (start, new_password.check), :165 read_old_container (:218-232), :166 choose_confirmation (:244-249), :169 recover (reserve_memory at :268); private_screen.rs:110-116; hidden_input.rs:287-292.
  - `git show 253ca3c^:src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs` shows the same refusal after Rekey::new before the AUD-023 fix.
- **Recommended fix:** In rekey::run, right after `options.new_password.check(&input)?` (rekey.rs:146), refuse a given `--confirm show` when `!terminal::can_show_privately(&input)`, with the same message. Use one shared helper so that the message has one source (CORE-10), and leave the arm at rekey.rs:245 unreachable or remove it. Optionally, word the --confirm help to say that show is refused at start where no private screen can open.
- **Required verification:** - verify_cli_ux.py `confirm_show_is_refused_before_the_container` passes.
  - New terminal-suite cases: `mhfe rekey --confirm show` at TERM=dumb and with standard output in a pipe or file each end with exit 2 before 'Container, 24 words' is shown.
  - With a private screen available, `--confirm show` still reaches the container prompt.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-UI002, AUD-007-SEC001
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 with my own pseudo-terminal probe against a current debug build. `cargo build --locked` was a no-op on the tmp target, so the build matches the commit.
  
  **What the probe shows**
  - `mhfe rekey --confirm show --pim 0 --mem 0` reaches its refusal only after three entries: the public 24-word container, the length answer "5" and an old password. It then ends with exit 2 and "--confirm show needs a terminal that can show the phrase on a private screen."
  - This happens both at TERM=dumb and with standard output redirected to a file.
  - In both conditions the control `--new-password words` is refused at once, with exit 2, before the container prompt.
  - No memory reservation or Argon2 round is reached. The refusal is in `choose_confirmation` (rekey.rs:166), which runs before `recover`/`reserve_memory` (rekey.rs:169, 268).
  
  **Why the check is known at start**
  - The guard is `terminal::can_show_privately(input)` (private_screen.rs:114-116). It reads only whether stdin, stdout and stderr are terminals, TERM and VT support (hidden_input.rs:287-292). It depends on nothing the person types, so the result is the same at start.
  - The match arm at rekey.rs:245 refuses `Some(Kind::Owner)` regardless of `rekey.confirmation_needed()`. Nothing typed can change the outcome.
  
  **Expected behaviour, from the project's own sources**
  - The doc of `can_show_privately` (private_screen.rs:110-113): "A command that must show a phrase only privately refuses otherwise, before anything secret is asked (AUD-007-SEC001)." `mhfe new` (new_wallet.rs:111) and `mhfe wallets` (wallets.rs:60) follow it through `private_input`, as does `--new-password` (made_password.rs:98-121).
  - AUD-023-UI002 expected "a given --confirm ... judged before the container and the old password are asked". Its fix (253ca3c) moved only the length-based refusal earlier (rekey.rs:156-158 and 225). The private-screen refusal of `--confirm show` stays after the password, where it already was before that fix.
  
  **Rule basis**
  - CORE-42 applies: the command ends after typed answers, the old password among them, instead of asking again. Its stated reason is that an abrupt end loses what the person typed, secrets included.
  - I dropped CORE-41. The refusal message is clear, and CORE-41 does not say when the refusal must come.
  
  **Duplicates and severity**
  - No already confirmed finding covers this.
  - Severity is low under AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a limited presentation or flow defect with bounded impact. The result is never wrong and no secret leaves the terminal.

##### AUD-024-UI008 — Low — The secret prompts explain the secret only when their own private screen is active. So at TERM=dumb, and in the missing-word search with standard output redirected, the container password, new password and BIP39 passphrase prompts do not say what the secret does or that it is not the other secret.

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: secret prompts
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** CORE-39
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool, every platform, at b6fca69. Single root cause: each explanation is guarded by `if screen.is_active()`.
  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:535-569 read_password. The explanation `what` (:537-546: "The password the container was encrypted with; it is NOT a BIP39 passphrase." / for rekey "The password the container has now; the new one comes later.") and check_word::FORGOTTEN_WORD_HINT are printed only inside `if screen.is_active()` (:549-553). The prompt itself, "Container password" or "Old container password" (:554), is always shown. Callers: decrypt.rs:184, check.rs:276, rekey.rs:229, container_search.rs:391.
  - src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:515-545 read_typed_password. `what` (:518-539) is printed only at :542-544. "Letter case and spaces count." (:545) is printed unconditionally. Used by encrypt (encrypt.rs:508; at TERM=dumb kind is always Own, :500), the rekey's new password (Operation::Rekey/RekeyNew) and wallets.rs:134. wallets is refused at TERM=dumb, so that caller cannot be reached there.
  - src/bin/mhfe/check/passphrase.rs:32-41 passphrase_screen. "Part of {whose}, as a 25th word; it is NOT the container password." is printed only at :34-39. Every BIP39 passphrase prompt goes through it: read_passphrase_until :51 (read_check_passphrase, called from check.rs:340; read_passphrase_named, called from check/wallet_reference.rs:202, rekey.rs:395, container_search.rs:352 and :137/:152), read_passphrase_of :182, and new_wallet.rs:267.
  - Why the screen is inactive while a person answers. src/bin/mhfe/terminal/private_screen.rs:46-53 (enter) leads to :61-91 (enter_if).
    (a) Terminal cannot redraw. terminal_screen_possible (:137-139) uses hidden_input::can_redraw (hidden_input.rs:287-292), which is false at TERM=dumb and where control_sequences() fails, e.g. a Windows console refusing VT. The latter was not run.
    (b) Nested screen. A screen opened while another private screen is active is never active (:73-77). The search prompts are opened inside read_container's screen (terminal.rs:590-609, then container_repair.rs:392, then container_search.rs:352/:391). This happens whenever the command's steps are not shown: flow.rs:72-85 calls enter_steps (private_screen.rs:173-180), which needs standard output on the terminal, so the steps are skipped whenever standard output is redirected to a file or /dev/null.
  - Same gate, not CORE-39 itself: the forgotten-word hint (terminal.rs:552) and the container's `?` hint UNREADABLE_HINT (terminal.rs:592-597) are also hidden in these cases.
  - Contrast within the tool: container_repair.rs:379-387 prints its card hints whenever `!input.is_script()`, and made_password.rs:188-189 prints TYPE_BACK_HINT unconditionally.
  - Commands affected. At TERM=dumb: decrypt, check, rekey (old and new password; the new one comes after the old recovery), encrypt, and the BIP39 passphrase questions of check, decrypt, rekey and repair. With standard output redirected: the missing-word search of decrypt, check, rekey and repair.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with a built mhfe (I used CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target, release/mhfe):

     - TERM=dumb `mhfe check --words auto --passphrase-used yes --pim 0 --mem 0`: types the 24-word "abandon ... art" container, waits for "Container password", types the fixture password "public test password", waits for "BIP39 passphrase of", then sends Ctrl+C.

     - Types the container with word 4 as `?`, Enter at "Repair words:", chooses 3 "The original seed phrase's passphrase", types "TREZOR" (BIP39 test-vector passphrase), chooses 1 at "Start the search?", then sends Ctrl+C at "Container password".
  No run reaches settings::reserve_memory (check.rs:369, container_search.rs:455) or any Argon2 round. Static trace only for the rekey's new password at TERM=dumb, because it follows the old recovery's Argon2.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-39 (.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md:294-297): "Every password or passphrase prompt says which secret it is and what it does ('the container password encrypts the 24 words; it is not the BIP39 passphrase')." The same rule says that script mode, a redirected output and TERM=dumb "keep plain sequential output". It exempts them from the screen handling only, not from the explanation. The project's release note docs/releases/v0.5.0.md:99-100 also says: "Each password prompt says which password it asks for, and \"NOT\" in capitals marks where a container password and a BIP39 passphrase differ."
- **Observed behavior:** TERM=dumb, check. The lines before the prompt are the container echo, "Container 24 words, valid" and "Format MHFE-BIP39-256-EXPERIMENTAL-3", then "Container password (hidden): " alone. After the password, "Password typed" is followed by the BIP39 passphrase prompt alone, with no "it is NOT the container password".
  TERM=dumb, encrypt. Only "Letter case and spaces count." appears before "Container password (hidden): ".
  TERM=xterm-256color, same check run. "The password the container was encrypted with; it is NOT a BIP39 passphrase." and "If you forgot a word of a password with a check word, type ? in its place." appear before the password prompt. "Part of the original seed phrase, as a 25th word; it is NOT the container password." appears before the passphrase prompt.
  Missing-word search at xterm. With standard output on the terminal, both prompts are explained. With standard output on /dev/null, neither the passphrase prompt nor the password prompt is explained.
  All runs exit 130 after Ctrl+C.
- **Impact:** Where a person answers at a terminal without an active screen of the prompt's own, nothing tells them that the container password is not the BIP39 passphrase, or that the passphrase is not the container password. That covers Emacs shell-mode, some IDE or serial consoles with TERM=dumb, and a recovery whose result goes to a file and needs the missing-word search. This is exactly the confusion CORE-39 exists to prevent. A swapped secret costs a full-cost recovery that fails, or a passphrase check that does not match. No secret is exposed. The defect is limited to presentation.

Only the screen handling, such as the blank line after a clear, should stay tied to is_active(). - **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: settings questions and mhfe new word wishes

The project's own statement at src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:85-86 says 'Settings that are asked are checked when they are answered.' The fix recommended in AUD-015-UI002 says 'A refused answer is asked again so that it can be corrected'. So a wrong PIM should be refused when typed and asked again alone, a wrong or unusable level should be asked again with the PIM kept, and a wrong position or never-use word should be asked again with the chosen word kept.
- **Observed behavior:** Log pty-ask-again-baseline-release.log:
  (a) After 'Memory level: 22': '! The memory level must be a whole number from 0 to 21, not 22. Please choose again.' Then 'PIM, 0 to 1023 ... PIM:': the valid PIM 0 is thrown away.
  (b) After level 4: '! This memory level needs 8 GiB of memory, but only 7.1 GiB is available; close other programs or choose a lower memory level. The highest memory level this computer can use now is 3. Please choose again.' Then 'PIM:' again.
  (c) PIM 5000 is taken with no refusal and 'Memory level:' is asked. After level 0: '! The PIM must be a whole number from 0 to 1023, not 5000. Please choose again.' Then 'PIM:': the valid level 0 is thrown away.
  (d) Position 0 is taken and 'Word never to use, or Enter for none:' is asked. After Enter: '! The wishes for the new phrase cannot be used: the chosen word needs a position from 1 to 24. Choose again.' Then 'Do you want to choose a word of the new phrase?', then the chosen word again. With --choose-word yes it goes straight back to 'Chosen word, or Enter for none:'.
  (e) After 'xyzzy': '! The wishes for the new phrase cannot be used: the word never to use is not an English BIP39 word. Choose again.' Then 'Chosen word, or Enter for none:': the valid secret chosen word and position are asked again.
- **Impact:** A person who mistypes one answer must retype answers that were accepted. That means a non-default PIM, or the secret chosen word of the new phrase, typed again on the private screen. A PIM out of range is reported only after another question, so the refusal comes away from the answer it concerns. No wrong result is produced, nothing is saved, and no secret leaves the private screen. The impact is bounded to extra typing and confusion: low.

##### AUD-024-UI010 — Low — In a several-readings recovery, mhfe decrypt does not say that a stated short length fails. With 24 words stated beside two passing short lengths, it names one checked length and says "Both readings follow" over three readings.

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Command-line tool, mhfe decrypt (terminal and --stdin), all platforms
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06, CHECK-FUN-006
- **Affected files and builds:** src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:357-397 (show_ambiguous):
  - :366 read_as_stated looks only at whether the last reading has the stated length.
  - :367-370 take only the first candidate's words() and stated_words().
  - :371-375 print check_finds(first, stated) and the fixed text "Both readings follow, the checked one first".
  - :376-379 print the generic "Several lengths passed their check" message, which ignores stated_words.
  - show_ambiguous never uses tell_stated_length (:339-355) or the readings' stated_words beyond the first.
  
  Promise it breaks: the --words help at src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:57-62 ("a built-in check that passes takes precedence, and the tool says so").
  
  Library facts, which are correct:
  - src/detection.rs:69-85, under_length_rules. The catch-all at :83 gives Several([12, 21, 24]) for Some(15), Some(18) or Some(24) beside short [12, 21].
  - src/mhfe.rs:221-229, compared_with. :222 sets stated_words on every reading whose length differs from the stated one.
  - src/mhfe.rs:481-495, recover.
  
  Helper: src/bin/mhfe/phrase_length.rs:112-114, check_finds.
  
  Not affected:
  - mhfe check: src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:500-510 prints "The built-in check of N words fails." and every passing length.
  - The browser package: src/wasm_api/core.rs:483 gives each candidate its statedWords, and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:153-156 asks pages to say it.
  
  Affects every native build of the mhfe binary.
- **Reproduction:** Static trace at b6fca69. For the state X of the published vector ambiguous-12-21:
  - LengthDetection::of gives short = [12, 21] (src/detection.rs:174-184 test).
  - under_length_rules(Some(15) | Some(18) | Some(24)) falls to :83 and gives Several([12, 21, 24]).
  - compared_with (src/mhfe.rs:222) sets stated_words:
    - 15 or 18 stated: on all three readings.
    - 24 stated: on the 12- and 21-word readings only.
  - show_ambiguous then takes the branch at decrypt.rs:376-379 for 15 or 18, because the last reading has 24 words, not 15.
  - For 24 it takes the branch at :371-375, with found = 12.
  
  Dynamic probe, run by me without Argon2:
  1. git archive b6fca69 into tmp/aud024/verify-decrypt-several/mhfe-copy.
  2. In the copy only:
     - make src/mhfe.rs recover pub and re-export it as mhfe::probe_recover;
     - add a cfg(test) module to src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs. It feeds X = 4d48464520616d62000000004dda455a85b22f09e43e0ae5de9322dce19210ad (the fixture's packing.state_hex) with Detect and each of --words 12/15/18/21/24 into the unchanged show_single/show_ambiguous, in --stdin (script) mode.
  3. Run: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<tmp>/aud024/target NO_COLOR=1 cargo test --locked --manifest-path <copy>/Cargo.toml --bin mhfe aud024_probe -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
  
  Output with --words 15, and the same with 18:
  - the library lines "candidate: words 12/21/24 ... stated_words Some(15)";
  - then only "! Several lengths passed their check, a rare accident." and "! Compare each with your wallet, or run again with --words N.";
  - then the 12-, 21- and 24-word readings.
  
  Output with --words 24:
  - "! The built-in check finds 12 words, not the 24 you gave.";
  - "! Both readings follow, the checked one first: a receiving address of your wallet tells them apart.";
  - then THREE readings: 12 and 21 words "passed its check", 24 "not verified".
  
  For contrast, the same probe with --words 12 or 21 resolves to one reading and names the other passing length (tell_stated_length).
- **Expected behavior:** mhfe_spec README.md:414-423 (Recovering a mnemonic, "With a stated length"):
  - "a short length was stated, it does not match, and other lengths do: say so and continue as with no stated length";
  - "24 words were stated and a short length matches: show the short readings first and also offer the 24-word reading, labelled as not verified".
  
  The tool's own --words help, src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:57-58: "a built-in check that passes takes precedence, and the tool says so".
  
  The tool already does this elsewhere:
  - with a single passing short length (show_single via tell_stated_length, decrypt.rs:339-348);
  - in mhfe check (check.rs:503).
  
  DOC-06 requires the code to agree with the specification and its own help.
- **Observed behavior:** Several short lengths pass beside a stated length that is not among them.
  - 15 or 18 stated: decrypt prints only the generic accident message. It never says that the stated length's built-in check fails, or that the passing checks took precedence.
  - 24 stated: it says that the check finds 12 words, omitting the 21 that also passes. It says "Both readings follow" while three readings follow.
- **Impact:** The case is rare: a packed short phrase passes a second short check about once in 2^32, and the user must also state a length outside the passing ones.
  
  Nothing is hidden: every reading is printed with its word count and status, and the source check runs on the 24-word reading.
  
  The owner is still misinformed:
  - When the stated length fails, the tool does not tell them it failed.
  - With 24 stated, they are told about one of two checked lengths, and the count of readings in the message is wrong.
  
  That can make the owner trust or skip the wrong reading when comparing with the wallet. This is a presentation defect with bounded impact (AUDIT_STANDARD.md: low).
- **Evidence:** Evidence is under docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-decrypt-several/; each log has a .command.json beside it. Every command was run through run-logged.sh from the repository root.
  - render-ambiguous-probe.log (exit 0): the library's readings and the rendered decrypt messages for Detect and --words 12/15/18/21/24 over the ambiguous-12-21 state. It reproduces both cases verbatim.
  - probe-patch.log: the exact diff of the scratch copy against src/mhfe.rs, src/lib.rs and src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs at b6fca69, plus git rev-parse HEAD = b6fca69 and a clean tracked tree.
  - lib-ambiguity-test.log (exit 0): on the real tree, cargo test --locked --lib ambiguity_lists_every_candidate_and_the_24_word_reading passes. It asserts at src/mhfe.rs:963-983 that a failing stated short length gives all three readings, each with stated_words == Some(stated). The library therefore hands the binary the facts the binary does not show.
  
  The original static trace is in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/spec-parity/decrypt-several.log.
  
  No terminal-suite case covers decrypt's ambiguous rendering: grep finds no "ambiguous", "Several lengths" or "Both readings" in scripts/terminal_suite, and decrypt.rs has no unit tests.
- **Recommended fix:** In show_ambiguous (src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:357-380), work from the whole candidate list:
  - Take the stated length from any reading's stated_words.
  - When no reading has the stated length (a short length that fails), say first "The built-in check of N words fails", as check.rs:503 does. Then name every passing short length and continue as with no stated length.
  - When 24 was stated, name every checked length, not only the first.
  - Word the follow-up by the number of readings ("Both" only for two).
  
  Add a unit test of the rendered lines for ambiguous-12-21 with 15 and with 24 stated. Construct the readings through the library's length rules or a reduced engine, not by hand. Also add a terminal-suite case if a reduced-cost path exists.
- **Required verification:** Unit test of the rendered lines for ambiguous-12-21 under --words 15, 18 and 24. Each must:
  - name the failing stated length;
  - name 12 and 21;
  - give the right reading count.
  
  The scratch probe above (render-ambiguous-probe) can be re-run against the fixed tree.
  
  Optionally, a full-cost terminal-suite case: mhfe decrypt --stdin with the published ambiguous-12-21 container and password and --words 15 / --words 24, checking standard error. It needs 2 GiB Argon2 and was not run in this audit.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced both cases at b6fca69. The library's length rules were run on the published state X of ambiguous-12-21 (packing.state_hex in tests/fixtures/suite3-vectors/ambiguous-12-21.json), and the result went through the unchanged show_ambiguous/show_single of src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs. This was done in a scratch copy of the tree, and no Argon2 ran.
  
  - With --words 15 or 18, every reading carries stated_words = Some(15) or Some(18). The tool still prints only "Several lengths passed their check, a rare accident." Nothing says that the stated length fails.
  - With --words 24, the 12- and 21-word readings carry Some(24). The tool prints "The built-in check finds 12 words, not the 24 you gave." and "Both readings follow, the checked one first". Three readings follow, and the passing 21-word check is not named.
  
  This contradicts the specification's stated-length rule ("say so"), the tool's own --words help ("the tool says so") and what mhfe check prints in the same state. It is not an AUD-023 finding: none of the 58 covers decrypt's ambiguous rendering.
  
  Severity is low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: it is a presentation defect, and every reading is still shown and labelled.

##### AUD-024-UI011 — Low — For a same-length (suite 4) container, the command-line tool never says that a mistyped setting goes undetected, and says that the container reveals the phrase's word count only behind `?` and in --help, not in the line shown after the choice

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Command-line tool: mhfe encrypt (container-length list, --same-length at a terminal and with --stdin, --help) and mhfe rekey of a same-length container; the browser integration guide (same missing clause)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** CHECK-DOC-001, CHECK-FUN-006, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool, every platform. Reproduced on a release build of b6fca69.
  
  1. Consequence line after the choice: src/bin/mhfe/length_choice.rs:115-125 (show_consequences). Its only text is at line 120: "A wrong password will not be detected: it opens another {words}-word wallet." It is called after the list choice (length_choice.rs:42-45) and for --same-length at a terminal and in a script (src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:343-351, call at 349).
  
  2. Before the choice: the list answers carry empty notes (length_choice.rs:19-22). The comparison is shown only when `?` is pressed (length_choice.rs:34-37; choice.rs:162-169). explain_same_length (length_choice.rs:90-113) states the wrong password (93) and the word count (105-108) but no wrong setting.
  
  3. Long help of --same-length (encrypt.rs:54-67, text at 61-65): wrong password and length, no setting.
  
  4. Summary after creation (encrypt.rs:196-212): Format, Keep, Next and More only.
  
  5. Documents that claim otherwise: the module doc at length_choice.rs:1-3 ("its consequences are shown before and after the choice") and SECURITY.md:184-193 ("the tool ... show[s] the consequences before the choice", including "A wrong password, PIM or memory level gives another valid phrase" at 189 and the word count at 192).
  
  6. Variant, mhfe rekey of a same-length container: the replacement keeps suite 4 (src/rekey.rs:326-336). The tool shows only "Format MHFE-BIP39-LP-EXPERIMENTAL-4 (no built-in check)" when the old container is read (src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:615-622) and the Format/Keep/Old backup/Next summary after sealing (src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:175-196, 430-449).
  
  7. Variant, browser guidance: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:835-840 and docs/API.md:56-60 list the wrong password and the shown length, but not the undetected wrong setting.
- **Reproduction:** Run from the mhfe repository root:
  
  python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-same-length-consequences/probe.py /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/release/mhfe
  
  The binary is a release build of b6fca69 with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target. Public data only: the zero-12 phrase, and the same-length-zero-12 container from tests/fixtures/suite4-vectors. Nothing reaches Argon2.

  - B: the same, but presses `?` at the list.
  - C: `mhfe encrypt --pim 0 --same-length` at a terminal.
  - D: `mhfe rekey --pim 0` with the suite 4 container, cancelled at the password prompt.
  - E: reads `mhfe encrypt --help`.

- **Expected behavior:** mhfe_spec/README.md:669-671 (at mhfe_spec 79c69d5): "Applications MUST tell the user that a mistyped password or setting is not detected and recovers a different valid wallet, and that the container reveals the source's word count."
  
  :605-606: "It MUST show the consequences of the choice".
  
  The project's own SECURITY.md:184-193 says the tool shows the consequences before the choice, among them "A wrong password, PIM or memory level gives another valid phrase" and "It shows the original seed phrase's word count". The module doc at length_choice.rs:2-3 says they are shown before and after the choice.
  
  DOC-06 (Check: review) requires code and documents, mhfe and mhfe_spec, to agree. CORE-40 allows a short hint needed to answer.

  After key 2, or with --same-length (terminal or --stdin), the tool shows only "! A wrong password will not be detected: it opens another 12-word wallet." and the More link.
  
  Pressing `?` adds "Recovery cannot check the password: a wrong one opens another wallet." and "It shows that your phrase has 12 words." It says nothing on settings. --help says "nothing detects a wrong password ... The container also shows the phrase's length" and nothing on settings.

- **Impact:** An owner who makes, or remakes, a same-length backup is never told by the tool that a mistyped PIM or memory level at recovery silently opens another valid wallet. The README's suite 4 row (README.md:57) does not say it either.
  
  The statement that the container discloses the original's word count also appears only on request. The owner can infer it from the answer label.

  - a README link is shown;
  - every suite 4 recovery is labelled not verified, with a pointer to mhfe check (decrypt.rs:290-298);
  - a rehearsal against an address or fingerprint would expose a wrong setting.

- **Required verification:** 1. Rerun docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-same-length-consequences/probe.py on the fixed build. It should exit 0; if the decision keeps the consequences behind `?` before the choice, relax A1 and record why.
  2. Add a unit test of show_consequences' text, both statements with the word count.
  3. Add a terminal-suite case: encrypt list, key 2, the lines shown, Ctrl+C before Argon2.
  4. Check that SECURITY.md, the length_choice module doc, BROWSER-PACKAGE.md and API.md say what the tool and pages show.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 with my own probe and found no Argon2 work needed. The probe drove `mhfe encrypt` in a pseudo-terminal: list, then key 2, then `?`, then `--same-length`. It also ran `encrypt --stdin --same-length` with two different passwords, read `encrypt --help`, and started `rekey` on the published same-length-zero-12 container, cancelling at the password prompt. It exits 1 with 12 failed checks.
  
  After the choice, the tool shows only one line: "A wrong password will not be detected: it opens another 12-word wallet." and a More link. That holds for the list, for --same-length and for a script. The word-count disclosure appears only under `?` and in `--help`. No text anywhere in the tool says that a wrong PIM or memory level also goes undetected for a same-length container, including `?` and `--help`. The project's own SECURITY.md:184-193 lists exactly that ("A wrong password, PIM or memory level gives another valid phrase") as a consequence the tool shows before the choice. So this breaks the specification's MUST (mhfe_spec README.md:669-671) and also DOC-06 (Check: review).
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - src/rekey.rs:349-352 is `wallet_passphrase`; the suite is kept at src/rekey.rs:326-327.
  - The browser guide (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:835-840) and docs/API.md:56-60 also leave out the wrong-setting clause. The browser is therefore not held to the full MUST; I grouped this as a variant of the same missing statement.
  - The list label "12 words, the same length as yours" implies the length disclosure, so the word-count half is a missing explicit statement, not a total absence.
  
  AUD-023 recorded the same gap only as informational observation 68 ("Several CLI texts meet spec SHOULD/MUST wording only in part"). It was not a finding, so no remediation was due, and this is not a duplicate.
  
  Possibly a separate issue, not part of this finding: rekey keeps suite 4 for the new container without a choice (spec 604-605: "only when the user has chosen it for that container").

##### AUD-024-UI012 — Low — The two fast-mode launchers end their documented stops differently. On Ctrl+C, mhfe serve shows '! Cancelled. Nothing was saved.' and exits 130, while the Python launcher shows 'Stopped.' and exits 0. On SIGTERM or a closed window (SIGHUP), mhfe serve exits 130 with that line, while the Python launcher is killed by the signal with no line. Yet the Python launcher says it does what mhfe serve does and uses mhfe's exit codes.

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Fast-mode launchers (mhfe serve, packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06, CORE-10

  - :6-7: the docstring says 'It does what `mhfe serve` does, with the same limits'.
  - :73-76: '# Exit codes, as the mhfe program uses them.' defines SUCCESS, INTERNAL_ERROR and INVALID_INPUT, but no cancelled code.
  - :548-551: 'Fast mode is running. Close this window or press Ctrl+C to stop.'
  - :552-556: `try: serve(...) except KeyboardInterrupt: say(["", "Stopped."]); return SUCCESS`.
  - No handler exists for SIGTERM or SIGHUP, so the process dies of the signal with no message.

  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:362-376: exit_cancelled calls show_cancelled and then std::process::exit(exit::CANCELLED).
  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:378-381: show_cancelled calls style::warn("Cancelled. Nothing was saved.", "").
  - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:255-262: the 'Close this window or press Ctrl+C to stop.' line, then serve(), which never returns, then an unreachable Ok(SUCCESS).
  - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:99-100: --no-browser help, 'The server stops when you press Ctrl+C.'
  - src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs:22-24: CANCELLED = 130 for Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and a closed terminal.
  
  Documents:
  - README.md:577: 130 for Ctrl+C, SIGTERM or a closed terminal.
  - SECURITY.md:203-205: the Python launcher is 'the same launcher'.
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:752-754: the Python launcher 'does the same'.

  1. Write the public page '<!doctype html><title>public test page</title>' as tool.html in a temporary folder, next to the sha256sum line 'mhfe-fast-mode.sha256'.
  2. Start each launcher with NO_COLOR=1 and the SIGINT disposition reset to default: `mhfe serve --no-browser <work>/tool.html`, then `python3 packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py --no-browser <work>/tool.html`.
  3. Wait for 'Fast mode is running', then one second more, then send SIGINT.
  
  Result: mhfe serve exits 130 with the last line '! Cancelled. Nothing was saved.'. mhfe-fast-mode.py exits 0 with the last line 'Stopped.'. The probe exits 1 because the two differ.

- **Expected behavior:** One end for the same documented stop, as the launchers' own statements promise:

  - packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:73: 'Exit codes, as the mhfe program uses them'. That program exits 130 on Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and a closed terminal (src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs:22-24; README.md:577).

- **Impact:** Low. A person sees a cancellation warning at the ordinary end of serving in one launcher and a plain line in the other. No secret, served byte or security header is affected.

  - mhfe-fast-mode.py:6-7, :73-76 and :548-556.
  - verify-fast-mode-script.py:623 and :649.
  
  AUD-023 (docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.md:1281) recorded the Ctrl+C difference only as an informational observation, not as a finding.
- **Recommended fix:** Settle the intended end (DOC-06) and give both launchers that end.

##### AUD-024-UI013 — Low — Valid single-key address forms of supported coins are refused with a reason that is false for them: a Bitcoin Cash token-aware 'z…' address is called not single-key, a Zcash ZIP-320 TEX 'tex1…' address is said to have a wrong checksum or format, and a Dash Core testnet 'y…' address is called 'not an address of Dash'

- **Category:** UI.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Library address parser (src/wallet/encodings.rs, src/wallet.rs), whose refusal text the CLI (mhfe check/rekey --address, missing-word search) and the browser package (describeAddress, address references) show unchanged
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-UI-001
- **Rules:** CORE-48, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** All builds (native CLI and browser package; the message comes from the library). src/wallet/encodings.rs:294-295: the doc comment says only version byte 0 ('q…') is single-key. :327-338: every version other than 0 gets 'only single-key addresses (bitcoincash:q…) can be checked' (:335-337). :11-26 with :51 and :185-189: parse() diverts only shielded Zcash prefixes, so a Bech32m 'tex1…' goes to parse_base58, fails Base58 decoding and gets malformed_address() 'its checksum or format is wrong' (:34-37). :190-193 with :167: Dash's Base58 versions list only 0x4c, so a testnet 0x8c address gets not_of(): 'it is not an address of Dash (X… or dash1k…)' (:39-46). Meanwhile :19 and :72-75 accept the Dash Platform testnet 'tdash1…', searched under coin type 1 (src/wallet.rs:247-249, :292-297). src/wallet.rs:142-156: address_forms ('X… or dash1k…' for Dash at :154, 't1…' for Zcash, 'bitcoincash:q… or 1…') states neither the accepted tdash1k… nor anything about the refused forms. src/wallet.rs:255-256: the Address::parse rustdoc says only multisignature and script addresses, shielded Zcash and other coins' addresses are refused. Shown by src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:183-198 (read_given) and :93-104 (missing-word search), and by the browser's describeAddress through AddressSearch::describe (src/wallet.rs:478-497). README.md:242-246 lists Dash as Core X… and Platform dash1k… only.
- **Reproduction:** 1. Independent decode, no mhfe code: python3 /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-address-forms/decode.py. bitcoincash:zqyx49mu0kkn9ftfj6hje6g2wfer34yfnqnpwfwhlf has a valid checksum, version 0x10 (type 2, size 0) and HASH160 086a977c…8998, the same as the accepted bitcoincash:qqyx49mu0kkn9ftfj6hje6g2wfer34yfnq5tahq3q6. tex1j4jdnlkjg7vxk9dz747skwcr9m4js3mvsg2wra is valid Bech32m, HRP 'tex', and its 20 bytes equal the hash of t1XVXWCvpMgBvUaed4XDqWtgQgJSu1Ghz7F. yRd4FhXfVGHXpsuZXPNkMrfD9GVj46pnjt is valid Base58Check with version 0x8c (140). The script exits 0 when all three forms are valid.
  2. Library probe: the crate /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-address-forms/probe (path dependency on the repository). Built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/verify-address-forms cargo build --offline --manifest-path …/probe/Cargo.toml and run. Address::parse and AddressSearch::describe both refuse the three forms with INVALID_ADDRESS and the false reasons, and accept the controls q…, t1…, X… and tdash1k…. It exits 1.
  3. CLI: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-address-forms/cli.sh pipes the public zero-24 container (tests/fixtures/suite3-vectors/zero-24.json), a dummy password and the address into `mhfe check --stdin --address --coin {bitcoin-cash|zcash|dash}`, at TERM=dumb, with ulimit -v 1 GiB and a 60 s timeout. The address is read before any round (src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:278-283). Each run exits 2 at once with the false reason.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-48: input that does not fit is 'refused with a clear message'. A reason that states something false about the input is not clear. The code's own contract (DOC-06: code and its documents agree): src/wallet.rs:255-256 'Reads text as a single-key receiving address of coin. Multisignature and script addresses, Zcash shielded addresses and those of other coins are refused', and src/wallet/encodings.rs:1-3 'the refusals of anything that is not a single-key receiving address of the coin'. Published standards define the three inputs as single-key HASH160 addresses of supported coins. CashTokens CHIP 'CashAddress Token Support': type 2, version byte 0x10 and prefix 'z', is token-aware P2PKH with the same hash as the 'q' form. ZIP-320: TEX is a Bech32m re-encoding of a transparent P2PKH key hash. Dash Core chain parameters: testnet P2PKH version 140, the 'y' prefix, pinned for the abandon…about phrase as 'Dash Core testnet / BIP44' in multi-chain-wallet-tools packages/verification/src/derivation-self-test-dash.ts:44-45. Each form should therefore either be read, or be refused as a recognised form of that coin that mhfe does not check, naming the form to use instead. The listed forms should also match what is accepted.
- **Observed behavior:** Library, describeAddress and CLI give INVALID_ADDRESS 'The address cannot be used for the check: …' with three different reasons. For the z-form: 'only single-key addresses (bitcoincash:q…) can be checked', which implies the address is not single-key, and the comment at encodings.rs:294-295 states that outright. For the TEX address: 'its checksum or format is wrong', which implies a typing error, although the Bech32m checksum is valid. For the y-address: 'it is not an address of Dash (X… or dash1k…)', although Coin::Dash accepts Dash testnet in its Platform form tdash1k… (searched under coin type 1). Coin::address_forms and README.md list neither testnet form. At a terminal the same reason is shown and the person is asked again. With --stdin and in the browser, the call ends with that reason.
- **Impact:** An owner who gives a correct receiving address of the right wallet is told that it is mistyped, not single-key, or not of the coin. They may retype it, doubt their records, or fall back to the weaker fingerprint or built-in check. Nothing is accepted wrongly and no secret is exposed. The CashTokens z-form is the receiving address that token-aware Bitcoin Cash wallets show, so that variant is the one most likely to be met. Limited presentation defect: low.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-address-forms/decode-forms.log (independent decode, exit 0, all forms valid). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-address-forms/library-parse.log (Address::parse and AddressSearch::describe, exit 1, 3 forms refused, 4 controls accepted). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-address-forms/cli-refusals.log (mhfe check --stdin, exit 2 for each form, refused before any round under a 1 GiB address-space cap). Each log has its .command.json beside it, and all were run through docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh. The candidate's own logs agree: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/address-forms.log, address-forms-encodings.log and harness-run.log ('address forms' FAIL). Probe sources: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-address-forms/{decode.py, probe/src/main.rs, cli.sh}. Standards read: zips.z.cash/zip-0320 (TEX: Bech32m HRP 'tex'/'textest' over the 20-byte P2PKH validating key hash) and github.com/cashtokens/cashtokens (type 2 'Token-Aware P2PKH', prefix 'z', same payload as 'q'). grep finds no mention of CashTokens, token-aware, ZIP-320 or TEX in src/, docs/, README.md or SECURITY.md, and no unit test pins these reasons. The only BCH refusal tested is the P2SH 'p…' form (src/wallet.rs:1152-1156), and it asserts is_err only.
- **Recommended fix:** Recognise the three forms in src/wallet/encodings.rs. Either read them (CashAddr version 0x10 and ZIP-320 TEX/TEXTEST as P2PKH of the same hash; Dash testnet version 0x8c, with 0x13 refused as P2SH, under coin type 1 as for Bitcoin and Dash Platform testnet), or refuse each with a reason that names the form and the alternative, such as 'a token-aware address: give the bitcoincash:q… address of the same key' or 'a TEX address: give its t1… form'. Correct the comment at encodings.rs:294-295 and keep the Address::parse rustdoc true. Make Coin::address_forms and README.md list exactly the accepted forms, tdash1k… included. Add unit tests that assert the reason or the parsed hash for each form.
- **Required verification:** Unit tests in src/wallet.rs for bitcoincash:z…, tex1…/textest1… and Dash 'y…' (and P2SH 0x13) that assert either the parsed type and hash (equal to the q…, t1… or BIP44 testnet hash) or the specific new reason. The probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-address-forms/probe (or the candidate role's 'address forms' check in docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/run.sh) passes. `mhfe check --stdin --address` gives the new reason or reads the address. The CLI/browser parity script compares one such refusal.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[14] (BCH token-aware and Zcash TEX refused with an inaccurate reason), AUD-023 informationalObservations[15] (Dash testnet: tdash1k accepted, y refused, neither listed), AUD-024 [ARC] A coin's address rules are not held by Coin (structure, different root cause)
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced all three variants at b6fca69, both in the library and through the CLI. An independent decoder (no mhfe code) shows each input is a valid single-key form of a supported coin. bitcoincash:z… is CashAddr version 0x10 (CashTokens type 2, token-aware P2PKH) with a valid checksum and the same HASH160 as the accepted q… form. tex1… is valid Bech32m, HRP 'tex', with a 20-byte payload equal to the t1… hash (ZIP-320). yRd4… is Base58Check version 0x8c (140), which is Dash Core testnet P2PKH. multi-chain-wallet-tools pins it as the 'Dash Core testnet / BIP44' address of the public test phrase.
  
  My own probe calls Address::parse and AddressSearch::describe, which is the browser's describeAddress. It gets INVALID_ADDRESS with the three claimed reasons, and the controls (q…, t1…, X…, tdash1k…) are accepted. `mhfe check --stdin --address --coin …` exits 2 with the same reasons before any round. That run was capped at 1 GiB of address space, so no Argon2 ran.
  
  The reasons contradict the code's own contract. Address::parse's rustdoc (wallet.rs:255-256) and encodings.rs:1-3 say only non-single-key, script, shielded and other-coin addresses are refused. encodings.rs:294-295 says only version byte 0 is single-key, which the CashTokens CHIP contradicts. Coin::Dash accepts the testnet tdash1k… under coin type 1 and then calls a Dash Core testnet address 'not an address of Dash'.
  
  No unit test pins these reasons, and no document records the refusals as intended. AUD-023 recorded these as informational observations [14] and [15], not as findings, so this is not a repeat. No confirmed AUD-024 finding has this root cause; the 'Coin does not hold its address rules' finding is structural.
  
  Corrections to the candidate: DOC-07 is about overstated guarantees and does not fit, so I replaced it with DOC-06 (code against its rustdoc and listed forms).
