##### AUD-024-ARC002 — Low — Every worker operation table serves a packageVersion operation that no class, script or test sends

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package / worker operation tables
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-002
- **Rules:** CORE-16, CORE-52
- **Affected files and builds:** web/core-worker.js:77, web/repair-worker.js:18, web/passwords-worker.js:21, web/wallet-worker.js:22 (each `packageVersion: () => mhfe.packageVersion(),`, present since d52dff8, 0.5.1). scripts/build-wasm.sh:64-66 joins them into the shipped dist/runtime/worker.js (lines 2533, 3014, 3043, 3077 of the built file). Affects every build of the browser package. The CLI and the library are not affected.
- **Reproduction:** From the mhfe root: node /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-dead-packageversion/probe.mjs. The probe loads web/worker-runtime.js, web/argon2-engine.js and the four *-worker.js tables in a node:vm context and lists each table's keys. It collects every `operation: "..."` and `phraseRequest("..."` name sent by web/client.js, repair.js, passwords.js, wallet.js and runtime.js, and reports the table entries without a sender. Output: core 17 entries, repair 6, passwords 7, wallet 9, and in each table the only entry never sent is packageVersion. The probe then serves the repair table over stand-in bindings (initSync no-op, packageVersion returning a stand-in version) and posts {module:"repair", operation:"packageVersion"}. The worker answers [{type:"ready"},{type:"result",result:"0.6.1-standin"}], so the entry is a live entry point of the worker's message surface. `git grep -nE "operation: *.packageVersion." -- . ":!docs/audits"` finds nothing.
- **Expected behavior:** FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md CHECK-ARC-002 lists orphan entry points and obsolete worker surface for review. Code that no consumer uses must take part in the active path or be removed, after checking generated sources, dynamic composition and public type contracts for consumers. CORE-16 (Check: review) asks for the simplest construction that does the job. CORE-52 (speculative generality, a judgement call) says to inline hooks that no current need uses. The worker's own contract, web/worker-runtime.js:175, says "The page's class of this build sends each operation the request that its table names", and the typedefs at web/repair-worker.js:6, passwords-worker.js:7 and wallet-worker.js:7 describe each table as the requests its class sends.
- **Observed behavior:** Four table entries that no class, page runtime function, package check, browser check or sibling-repository consumer sends. The worker protocol is not a public contract: runtime.d.ts declares no ModuleWorker or WorkerJob and says a page uses the classes. The version already reaches the page through every parameters() (`version` from src/wasm_api/core.rs:70, repair.rs:31, passwords.rs:38, wallet.rs:43) and through every self-check report, which reads bindings.packageVersion() directly (web/worker-runtime.js:118). The package checks call the WebAssembly export packageVersion() (scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs:53, module-bindings.mjs:38), not the worker operation.
- **Impact:** Maintenance only. The worker's message surface, which AUD-010 hardened against unknown operation names, carries four extra entry points that serve no caller and that no test covers as a worker operation. A reader of a table cannot tell which entries are part of the class contract. The answer is the public release version, so nothing secret is exposed.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dead-packageversion/probe-unsent-operations.log (exit 1 as intended: FAIL entries no class sends: core.packageVersion, repair.packageVersion, passwords.packageVersion, wallet.packageVersion. It also shows the live worker answer). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dead-packageversion/shipped-and-senders.log (build-wasm.sh concatenation, four entries in dist/runtime/worker.js, no sender in tracked files, introduced by d52dff8). Earlier role evidence: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-browser/gb11-dead-packageversion-op.log and gb18-kept-harness.log (kept harness check 8 FAILS).
- **Recommended fix:** Remove the four `packageVersion` entries from CORE_OPERATIONS, REPAIR_OPERATIONS, PASSWORD_OPERATIONS and WALLET_OPERATIONS. Keep the WebAssembly export packageVersion(), which the worker runtime's self-check report and the package checks use. Optionally, add to the package check a comparison of each table's keys with the operations its class sends, so that an orphan entry fails the check.
- **Required verification:** The probe (or kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-browser check 8) reports no table entry without a sender. pnpm typecheck of web/ and the package checks (scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs via scripts/check.sh) still pass. The self-check reports still carry `version`.
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. Loading the real worker scripts in a VM and listing each operation table's keys shows that packageVersion is the only entry of the four tables (core 17 entries, repair 6, passwords 7, wallet 9) that no class or shared runtime function sends. Every other entry, including wordHints (via wordHintsOf) and walletCheck/fingerprint (via phraseRequest), has a sender. git grep over every tracked file outside docs/audits finds no `operation: "packageVersion"`, and a search of the sibling repositories finds no outside consumer. The worker message protocol is internal: runtime.d.ts exposes no ModuleWorker or WorkerJob, and worker-runtime.js:175 says the page's class of the same build sends the requests its table names. The entry is still live. A worker over stand-in bindings answers {module:"repair", operation:"packageVersion"} with a result. It has shipped in dist/runtime/worker.js since d52dff8, and no sender has ever existed in history. The version already reaches the page through each parameters() (`version` in src/wasm_api/{core,repair,passwords,wallet}.rs) and each self-check report (worker-runtime.js:118). The defect is real but has maintenance impact only. Note that CORE-52 calls itself a judgement call. The firmer sources are CHECK-ARC-002, which lists orphan entry points, and CORE-16, which asks for the simplest construction.

##### AUD-024-ARC003 — Low — The browser package keeps secret bytes in plain request objects wiped by free functions over a list of field names, with no owner type that has wipe() and [Symbol.dispose](), as TS-07 requires.

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package runtime, classes and worker parts (secret ownership)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-002
- **Rules:** TS-07, CORE-24, CORE-03
- **Affected files and builds:** web/runtime.js:601-617 (SECRET_FIELDS), 619-633 (wipeSecrets over Record<string, unknown>, the message and one level of .value only), 635-645 (secretBuffers, top level only), 674-701 (encodeSecret returns a bare Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>), 218-305 (WorkerJob.run/send call wipeSecrets on the request record at 282, 294 and 300), 943-961 (ModuleWorker.run/start build the transfer list by field name), 745-748 (wordHintsOf: typed); web/worker-runtime.js:60-76 (second SECRET_FIELDS list), 178-182 (finally wipeSecrets(message)), 255-265 (worker wipeSecrets); web/client.js:330-336 (readPhrase), 855-868 (session open), 994-1044 (#start), 1368-1378 (answerOwner), 1390-1411 (answerNoLength), 1448-1456 (answerConfirmAgain); web/wallet.js:166-178 (describeDraw chosenWords), 250-276 (#draw: three fill(0) calls by hand at 272-274), 290-344 (#startDraws copies secrets by field name at 320 and wipes them at 331), 403-414 (phraseRequest); web/passwords.js:93-107 (review), 131-137 (strength), 158-164 (make: rolls); web/core-worker.js:162-166, 297-301, 350-352, 398-411 (wipeSecrets on page answers). Shipped unchanged in dist/runtime/runtime.js (SECRET_FIELDS at line 605, wipeSecrets at 626, secretBuffers at 641), in dist/runtime/worker.js (SECRET_FIELDS at 2237, wipe at 2434) and in the class files of dist/core, dist/passwords and dist/wallet. dist/runtime/worker.js:125, 213 and 483 do set [Symbol.dispose] = free, but only on the wasm-bindgen glue of the Rust sessions, not on any JavaScript copy of a secret.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: node docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-secret-owners/probe.mjs (README beside it). The harness lists every wipe() and [Symbol.dispose] in web/ (result: none) and every class in web/ (12, none owning secret bytes). It compares the two SECRET_FIELDS lists (equal, 11 names) and checks that every field receiving encodeSecret() bytes is listed (0 unlisted). It then imports web/runtime.js in Node and runs secretBuffers() and wipeSecrets() on the same encodeSecret() bytes placed in five ways: under the listed field 'passphrase' they are transferred and wiped; under an unlisted field 'seed' neither; at .value.passphrase they are wiped but not transferred; at .value.value.passphrase neither; inside an array neither. encodeSecret() returns a plain Uint8Array with no wipe and no Symbol.dispose. The harness exits 1 because the owner type is missing. Static trace: grep -n -E 'wipe\(\)|Symbol\.dispose' web/*.js web/*.d.ts prints nothing; grep -n -E 'wipeSecrets|fill\(0\)|SECRET_FIELDS' web/*.js lists the free-function wipes cited under affected.
- **Expected behavior:** TS-07 (code-typescript.instructions.md:49-54, applyTo **/web/**/*.js, Check: review) says: 'A secret lives in a Uint8Array held by its owner type. The owner's method that erases it is called wipe(), and [Symbol.dispose]() calls wipe(); callers wipe in finally.' CORE-24 (code-core:180-183) says a secret lives in a type that owns it and wipes it when its work ends. CORE-03 (code-core:40-43) says to use a class for a lifetime, an object that owns a secret wiping it when it goes away. WEB-04 points to TS-07 for page secrets. code-core:13 requires any exception to be written where it applies, with its reason. The audit brief applies review rules to the whole repository.
- **Observed behavior:** web/ has no owner type for secret bytes: no wipe() method and no [Symbol.dispose] in any web/*.js or web/*.d.ts. The secrets (phrase, password, passwordRepeat, passphrase, passphraseRepeat, chosenWords, newPassword, newPasswordRepeat, mainPassphrase, rolls, typed) are bare Uint8Arrays from encodeSecret(), stored as fields of untyped WorkerRequest records (Record<string, unknown>). Whether a buffer is transferred to the worker and wiped depends on its field name being in SECRET_FIELDS, which is kept twice (page web/runtime.js:605 and worker web/worker-runtime.js:64, compared by scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs:63-71). It also depends on each call site calling secretBuffers() and wipeSecrets(), or fill(0) by hand as in web/wallet.js:272-274. wipeSecrets() looks only at the record and its .value; secretBuffers() looks only at the top level. Some callers wipe in catch rather than finally: client.js:1039-1043, wallet.js:329-333 and 409-412, passwords.js:102-106. No comment records an exception to TS-07. Every current secret field is covered: the probe found 0 unlisted fields, and no leak was found.
- **Impact:** This is a maintainability defect in the secret lifecycle of the browser package, not a demonstrated leak. A secret added under a new field name, nested deeper than .value, put in an array, or held in a new local variable is silently neither transferred nor wiped, the probe shows this for each case, and no type or check catches it. The wipe logic is spread over about 20 call sites in six files instead of one owner.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-secret-owners/v1-secret-owners.log (probe run from tmp, exit 1) and v2-secret-owners-harness.log (same probe run from the kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-secret-owners/probe.mjs, exit 1), each with its .command.json. The original role's log is docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/browser-isolation/p14-secret-owners.log (grep listing, exit 0). Rule texts read at .github/instructions/code-typescript.instructions.md:1-3 (applyTo) and 49-54, code-core.instructions.md:13, 40-43 and 180-183, and code-browser.instructions.md:26-29. tmp/aud024/aud023-findings.json has no finding citing TS-07, CORE-24, SECRET_FIELDS or wipeSecrets.
- **Recommended fix:** Add one owner class in web/runtime.js, for example SecretBytes, that holds the Uint8Array privately and exposes the bytes, its transfer buffer, wipe() and [Symbol.dispose]() calling wipe(). Define [Symbol.dispose] only when the browser has Symbol.dispose, as the wasm-bindgen glue does, and add esnext.disposable to the tsconfig lib if using/Disposable types are wanted, since lib is es2024 today. Have encodeSecret() return it. Give requests a type that owns their secrets and yields both the transfer list and wipe(), so that WorkerJob, ModuleWorker, the classes (client, wallet, passwords) and the page answers (answerOwner, answerNoLength, answerConfirmAgain) wipe through it in finally or with using, and drop the field-name lookups. On the worker side, which imports nothing, define the same small owner in worker-runtime.js. Mark it 'deliberate copy' with its reason and keep it in step with the page's copy through the existing check in scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs. Replace the hand-written fill(0) calls in web/wallet.js:272-274 with wipe().
- **Required verification:** Review web/ against TS-07: each secret is held by an owner with wipe() and [Symbol.dispose](), and callers wipe in finally. node docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-secret-owners/probe.mjs must then exit 0, and part 5 must be adapted to the owner API. scripts/package-check/phrase-wipes.mjs, the residue block of scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs and the browser suite in Chromium and Firefox must still show every copy wiped and transferred.
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with both a static trace and a runtime probe. TS-07 (Check: review; it applies to web/**/*.js through the applyTo of code-typescript.instructions.md) requires an owner type for each secret, whose wipe() erases it and whose [Symbol.dispose]() calls wipe(). No such type exists. web/ has no wipe() method and no [Symbol.dispose] member. The 12 classes in web/ include none that owns secret bytes. encodeSecret() returns a bare Uint8Array. The page wipes and transfers secrets only through the free functions wipeSecrets() and secretBuffers(), which look up an 11-name SECRET_FIELDS list. That list is copied in the worker, which wipes through its own wipeSecrets(). wallet.js also has three fill(0) calls written by hand. No place in the code records an exception to TS-07, which CORE "Exceptions" (code-core line 13) would require. I imported web/runtime.js in Node to check the claimed mechanism. Bytes under an unlisted field name, two levels down, or inside an array are neither transferred nor wiped. Every field that currently receives encodeSecret() bytes is listed, so this is a maintainability defect with no leak, and low severity is right. The defect is not an AUD-023 finding, and no earlier audit reports TS-07.

CORE-10 also says (line 89) that a front end that refuses early reads the library's values (parameters()), so constants copied for an early refusal count as the fast-path exception. - **Recommended fix:** Add 'Deliberate copy:' with the reason to each listed comment, worded like web/client.js:1460-1461. For example, at web/worker-runtime.js:60-63 and 221-226: 'Deliberate copy of SECRET_FIELDS/packageMismatch in web/runtime.js: a worker script imports nothing; scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs keeps both equal'. Where an early refusal is not needed, remove the copy instead, for example by reading the limit from the WebAssembly's parameters() once the worker is ready. - **Required verification:** Review: grep -rn -i 'deliberate copy' web/ finds a marker beside each location listed under affected. The probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/v-arc-deliberate-copy/probe-markers.mjs exits 0. node scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs and the browser package checks (scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs) still pass.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC011
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69. All twelve copies are where the candidate puts them. Each has a comment giving its reason and pointing to the test that keeps it in step, but none of those comments says "deliberate copy". In web/, only web/client.js:1460 and web/passwords.js:43 carry the marker. Those two are copies of the same kind (a library refusal checked early in a class), so the convention exists and is applied unevenly. The package checks confirm the "a test keeps both in step" half of the rule: scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs:61-75 covers SECRET_FIELDS and the PACKAGE_MISMATCH advice, and scripts/package-check/page-classes.mjs:76-95 compares the client.js constants with parameters(). ##### AUD-024-ARC005 — Low — Type assertions stand in for checks in the browser package. rekey() casts an owner callback that may be undefined to a function, and page-worker messages are cast to their protocol types with no shape check. A worker message the page should not get therefore ends as the page's CALLBACK_FAILED or as a plain TypeError instead of PACKAGE_MISMATCH

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package: typed JavaScript and the page-worker protocol (web/)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-002
- **Rules:** TS-04, TS-02, TS-03
- **Affected files and builds:** All builds of the browser package (dist/core, dist/runtime, dist/wallet and runtime/worker.js built from web/). (1) web/client.js:766-769: the rekey handler `ownerCheck: (check) => answerOwner(/** @type {PageOwner} */ (owner), check)`. `owner` is `PageOwner | undefined` (DescribedConfirmation, client.js:97-103), and describeConfirmation returns undefined for the built-in check (client.js:1502) and for an address or fingerprint (client.js:1540). The handler is installed for every confirmation kind, and the comment at :767 states an invariant of the worker, not a check. This is a non-null assertion written as a JSDoc cast, which oxlint's typescript/no-non-null-assertion cannot see. (2) Worker results typed Promise<unknown> (WorkerJob.run, runtime.js:226; RunSet, runtime.js:825) are cast with no shape check, and the comments name the producer: web/client.js:1085-1086 (SetReport & { parameters }, then requireSameLimits at :1100 reads parameters.maxPim) and web/runtime.js:1149-1150 (SetReport, then ran.version at :1158). (3) Worker message values passed to page handlers, and an error code: web/runtime.js:417 and :445 (WorkerHandler cast to ArrivedHandler; isReadableReply at :593-599 checks only the type, a ready's buildId and an error's text fields, and its comment says results and values 'go to the page as they are'), and web/runtime.js:367 (a string cast to MhfeErrorCode without a membership check). (4) The worker side, which trusts the page runtime's messages: web/worker-runtime.js:155 (`any` event.data declared as PageMessage, no validator), :175-176 (Operation<never> cast to Operation<PageMessage>), and web/core-worker.js:157-158, :290-291, :328-330, :353 and :393-394 (host.ask's unknown answer cast to ReferenceFields, the owner's answer, HiddenWalletRequest and ConfirmationFields). The shapes are built and checked in web/client.js (answerNoLength, answerOwner, openHiddenWallets, answerConfirmAgain). The worker function checks nothing, and its comment names the sender. (5) web/runtime.js:98-100: Uint8Array cast to BufferSource. The cast is not needed by tsc 7.0.2, and its comment says WebAssembly.compile rejects bytes over a SharedArrayBuffer, which Node.js 26, Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 do not do. (6) web/wallet.js:303-304: `unknown` cast to `object` for a spread, with no runtime effect. Not part of the finding, because the shape is proven or the cast is `as const`: client.js:209, :1305, :1496, :1515; runtime.js:360, :1185; worker-runtime.js:282. Also excluded: worker-runtime.js:122 widens null to a nullable type and asserts nothing false.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with dist/ and target/wasm-bindgen/ as the AUD-024 baseline built them at b6fca69: (a) `node --no-warnings docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-type-assertions/check-unchecked-casts.mjs`. It loads the classes and the stand-in Worker of scripts/package-check/ and runs five cases. A rekey with confirmation { owner } is the control: the owner is asked and the rekey resolves. A rekey with { fingerprint: "00000000" } and walletHasPassphrase false, and one with { builtInCheck: true }, get a worker that replies { type: "ask", question: "ownerCheck" }. MhfeClient.startupCheck() gets a core report without `parameters`. MhfeRepair.startupCheck() gets a null result. (b) `node --no-warnings docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-type-assertions/check-shared-bytes-compile.mjs` calls WebAssembly.compile on the 8-byte module header in a view over a shared WebAssembly.Memory buffer, in Node.js and in Playwright's Chromium and Firefox. (c) `bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-type-assertions/uncast-tsc.sh` copies web/ to ../tmp/aud024/verifier-type-assertions/web-uncast, removes the casts at client.js:769 and :1086, runtime.js:100 and :1150 and wallet.js:304, and runs tsc -p on the copy. (d) A static inventory of every JSDoc cast in web/*.js (vta04). No Argon2 rounds, no network, and only the package check's test strings.
- **Expected behavior:** TS-04 (code-typescript.instructions.md, 'Check: review'; TS-13 extends the TS rules to the plain JavaScript of web/): 'A type assertion is `as const`, or sits inside a function that parses outside input after it has checked the shape, with a comment that names the check.' TS-02: 'Input whose shape is not known yet is `unknown`, and a validator narrows it to a type.' TS-03: replace a non-null assertion 'with a check that narrows'. The package's own contract: runtime.js:437-441 says 'A question must be answered: one the page has no handler for is a fault of the package' and stops with PACKAGE_MISMATCH. docs/API.md:989-992 defines PACKAGE_MISMATCH as covering 'a message of the worker that the page does not know or cannot read'. docs/API.md:993-995 limits CALLBACK_FAILED to 'a callback of the page threw ... the page's error is the cause'. docs/API.md:979-980 and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:524 say that every error other than a wrongly typed argument is an MhfeError.
- **Observed behavior:** vta01, exit 1. The control resolves. The fingerprint and built-in-check rekeys whose worker asks ownerCheck both end with 'MhfeError CALLBACK_FAILED: The page's ownerCheck callback failed.; cause TypeError: owner is not a function'. The page gave no owner callback, and the worker is terminated without an answer. With a core report lacking `parameters`, startupCheck() rejects with 'TypeError (no code): Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'maxPim')'. With a null module self-check result it rejects with 'TypeError (no code): Cannot read properties of null (reading 'version')'. Neither is an MhfeError or PACKAGE_MISMATCH. vta03, exit 1. With the casts removed, tsc 7.0.2 reports TS2345 'PageOwner | undefined' is not assignable to 'PageOwner' at client.js:769, TS2339 and TS2700 at client.js:1086, TS18046 and TS2345 at runtime.js:1158-1159, and TS2698 at wallet.js:304. The casts are what keeps the type check (gb09: page and worker tsc exit 0) quiet. tsc reports nothing at runtime.js:100, so that cast is redundant. vta02, exit 1: Node.js v26.10.0, Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Firefox 157.0 all compile bytes over a SharedArrayBuffer, so the check named in the comment at runtime.js:98-99 does not happen. vta04 lists 23 casts, 7 of them proven or `as const`. The remaining casts assert types that the containing function never checked, and their comments name a sender or a build ('The worker of this build gives ...', 'The page answers with ... (answerX in web/client.js)'). Correction to the candidate: the page's answers are checked in web/client.js before they are posted. On the worker side, the copy is cast with no check of its own.
- **Impact:** Type checking is switched off at the page-worker boundary and wherever a value is known to be defined only by convention, so the next protocol change can go wrong without tsc noticing. Only a faulty package reaches the misreports today: a worker of another build is refused at its 'ready'. When it happens, an unexpected ownerCheck question is blamed on the page's callback (CALLBACK_FAILED with a TypeError cause), although the page has no such callback. A malformed self-check result rejects with an untyped TypeError that a page following BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:958-959 (on PACKAGE_MISMATCH, offer nothing of that class) cannot recognize. One cast's comment names a browser check that does not exist. There is no secret exposure and no wrong cryptographic result. The impact is limited to diagnosis and maintenance.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-type-assertions/vta01-unchecked-casts.log (exit 1), vta02-shared-bytes-compile.log (exit 1), vta03-uncast-tsc.log (exit 1) and vta04-cast-inventory.log (exit 0), each with a .command.json. Kept harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-type-assertions/ (README.md, check-unchecked-casts.mjs, check-shared-bytes-compile.mjs, uncast-tsc.sh). Earlier: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-browser/gb15-type-assertions.log, whose grep missed client.js:1515, runtime.js:367 and worker-runtime.js:122, and gb09-tsc-web.log (tsc passes). dist/core/client.js and dist/runtime/runtime.js differ from web/ only in the stamped build IDs (checked with diff).
- **Recommended fix:** In rekey(), install the ownerCheck handler only when the confirmation in force is the owner's, or narrow it: `if (owner === undefined) throw packageMismatch("The worker asked the owner for a confirmation that is not the owner's")`. Make sure #answer passes that MhfeError on as it is, not as CALLBACK_FAILED. Give the page-worker protocol one small validator per message type, inside the parse step of WorkerJob#receive and #answer and in the worker's onmessage, with `unknown` in and the typed value out: a SetReport check (version string or null, components array, ids string array), the core's parameters, the error code against the MhfeErrorCode list, and on the worker side each answer type of host.ask. Refuse a mismatch with PACKAGE_MISMATCH. Then remove the casts or leave them inside those validators with a comment naming the check. Delete the redundant BufferSource cast at runtime.js:100 and its false comment, or check `wasm.buffer instanceof ArrayBuffer` in CompiledModule's constructor if shared bytes are to be refused. Replace the `object` cast at wallet.js:304 with a checked result type.
- **Required verification:** tsc -p web/tsconfig.json and -p web/tsconfig.worker.json and the lint gate pass with the casts listed above removed or moved into validators. check-unchecked-casts.mjs exits 0: an ownerCheck question without an owner confirmation and a malformed or null self-check result reject with PACKAGE_MISMATCH. A package check (scripts/package-check/) keeps those cases, plus a worker error whose code is not in MhfeErrorCode. check-shared-bytes-compile.mjs is retired together with the comment at runtime.js:98-99, or the constructor refuses shared bytes and a package check covers it.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and reproduced the defect without Argon2, through the package check's stand-in worker loaded from the baseline's dist/. Four cases fail. A rekey confirmed by a fingerprint or by the built-in check, whose worker asks "ownerCheck", rejects with CALLBACK_FAILED "The page's ownerCheck callback failed." and the cause "TypeError: owner is not a function", although the page gave no owner callback. A core self-check report without `parameters` makes startupCheck() reject with a plain TypeError (reading 'maxPim'), and so does a null module self-check result (reading 'version'). docs/API.md says every error other than a wrongly typed argument is an MhfeError, and that a worker message the page does not know is PACKAGE_MISMATCH. A scratch copy of web/ with five casts removed fails tsc 7.0.2 at client.js:769, :1086, runtime.js:1158-1159 and wallet.js:304, so the casts are what keeps the type check quiet. The cast at runtime.js:100 is not needed by tsc, and its comment names a check that does not exist: Node.js 26, Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 all compile bytes over a SharedArrayBuffer. I corrected the candidate in two places. First, the page's answers are checked in client.js before they are posted, so the defect on the worker side is that it casts the runtime's message with no check of its own. Second, I added casts that the evidence grep missed: runtime.js:367, and the `any` event.data typed as PageMessage at worker-runtime.js:155. No duplicate among the confirmed findings and no AUD-023 counterpart. Severity stays low: only a faulty package reaches these paths, and the effect is on diagnosis and maintenance.

##### AUD-024-ARC006 — Low — The real-browser suite runs its fast mode on a stand-in server of its own, which retypes two of the launchers' seven security headers with no marker or test, so no check ever opens mhfe serve or the Python launcher in a browser

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser regression suite (scripts/verify-browsers.mjs) and the fast-mode launchers (mhfe serve, packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-10, CHECK-ARC-003, CORE-33, CHECK-BLD-002
- **Affected files and builds:** - scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:15-17: the header comment says each browser opens the page "from a loopback server with the isolation headers (fast mode), as `mhfe serve` gives them".
  - scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:239-248: the comment at :239, then `createServer` at :240-247 and its listen call at :248. The server answers every request with the page, whatever its method, path or Host. It needs no mhfe-fast-mode.sha256. It sends three headers: Content-Type, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp. The other five of SECURITY_HEADERS are missing: Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control.
  - scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:250-253: the fast-mode address is this stand-in's port. The file never names serve.rs, SECURITY_HEADERS or mhfe-fast-mode, and never starts a child process.
  - The source of the values is src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:62-72 (SECURITY_HEADERS). The Python copy is packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:53-63.
  - The launcher tests open no browser: scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py (check.sh:66), scripts/terminal_suite/serve.py, and serve.rs's unit tests (e.g. :478-487, which iterate over the constant they check).
  - The only browser gate is .github/workflows/ci.yml:91-102, which runs `node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs`. The only browser script in package.json is `check:browsers`, which runs the same file. scripts/check.sh runs no browser.
  - verify-browsers.mjs has no 'deliberate copy' marker, and scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs names neither the headers nor verify-browsers.mjs.
  - Builds affected: none at run time. This is a gap in test fidelity in CI and in the release checks (release.yml runs the same checks).
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-suite-fast-mode-server suite-fast-mode-server-probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-suite-fast-mode-server/probe.sh. The probe prints the following.
  (1) verify-browsers.mjs:12-17 and :238-253.
  (2) verify-browsers.mjs contains none of serve.rs, SECURITY_HEADERS, mhfe-fast-mode, spawn, execFile or child_process.
  (3)-(4) Of all tracked non-audit files that mention playwright, chromium or firefox, the only ones that also start a launcher are docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md and docs/releases/v0.6.0.md, both documents.
  (5) Each file that starts a launcher names a browser 0 times: packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py, scripts/build-wasm.sh, scripts/terminal_suite/serve.py and scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py.
  (6)-(7) check.sh and the workflows run only verify-fast-mode-script.py and verify-browsers.mjs. package.json has only check:browsers.
  (8) There is no deliberate-copy marker, and the copy gate does not cover the headers.
  (10) A simulated change of COEP to 'require-crop' in serve.rs alone makes the Python launcher test FAIL. The same change in both launchers makes it PASS. verify-browsers.mjs still sends require-corp, so its fast mode would go on testing headers that no launcher sends, and every gate would pass.
- **Expected behavior:** - CORE-10 (Check: copies, review): every constant and data shape has exactly one source. An unavoidable copy says 'deliberate copy' next to it, with its reason, and a test keeps both copies in step. AUD-023-ARC018 treated the same suite's own CSP copy as such a finding.
  - CHECK-ARC-003 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md): a test-only seam must not give a false impression that the production path was exercised. The suite's comment (:16-17) presents its server as giving what mhfe serve gives.
  - CORE-33 (Check: review): a feature has its case in the browser regression suite in both browsers, plus launcher checks where the change calls for them. Users reach the fast mode only through the two launchers (README.md:503-507, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:752-766). The browser-facing contract of those launchers is that the page becomes cross-origin isolated under their headers plus its meta policy, and that the Host the browser sends is accepted. That contract has no browser case.
- **Observed behavior:** The suite's fast mode runs on a third server. It shares only the two isolation header values with the launchers, typed again with no marker and no test, and keeps none of the launchers' rules: no exact Host check, no checksum gate, none of the five other headers. Neither launcher meets a real browser in any gate (check.sh, CI or release). The unit tests keep the Python launcher's header values equal to serve.rs's, but they only check each launcher against itself or against the other, never against a browser and never against the suite. AUD-023 recorded the same gap as completenessGaps[2] and as an informational observation. It is unchanged at b6fca69.
- **Impact:** Low. This is a regression risk in test fidelity only. At b6fca69 the route works through both launchers in Chromium and Firefox (g03 of the gap-1 role). A mistyped value in one launcher alone is caught by verify-fast-mode-script.py. The following would still pass every check while breaking or changing the route users take:
  - the same COOP or COEP change made in both launchers (the suite keeps sending require-corp);
  - a header added to both launchers that conflicts with the page, such as a stricter Content-Security-Policy that blocks the page's inline module;
  - a Host rule or response-format change that refuses or breaks what a real browser sends.
  The suite also tests the page under different response headers from the ones users get.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-suite-fast-mode-server/suite-fast-mode-server-probe.log (exit 0, SHA-256 c50f5e367f79c4d75cc2516bd2fcddce1493ebf1aec87177ea5a14c729d257af, with .command.json beside it).
  - Corroborating logs:
    - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser/g10-suite-fast-mode-server.log (exit 0, SHA-256 bd07cb73de7148f2b66237e54419d90a72a9d348458253415404fdfec58abf75, re-hashed and matching);
    - g03-fast-mode-route.log (exit 0, SHA-256 dec9d8baf75c84f6c0224fe978c865736971e1d1d5b13995a1d09b9263adb65c, RESULT: PASS). It shows that a loopback run of both launchers in both browsers takes about two minutes (10:57:52 to 10:59:43 UTC).
  - AUD-023-2026-10-13.json completenessGaps[2] and the informationalObservations entry 'No automated check opens a page served by either documented fast-mode launcher in a browser' (priorId null). This was not an AUD-023 finding.
- **Recommended fix:** Serve the suite's fast-mode page through the launchers. Write mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 beside target/browser-check/reduced-cost.html. Run the fast-mode page once under `mhfe serve --no-browser` and once under `python3 packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py --no-browser`, taking the address each prints. Then remove the stand-in server and its copied header values. If a stand-in must stay, mark it 'deliberate copy' with its reason, and test its values against SECURITY_HEADERS in serve.rs, as verify-fast-mode-script.py already does for the Python copy. Correct the comment at :16-17 either way. As a minimum, add a launcher smoke check in both browsers to scripts/check.sh or the CI browser step, as the AUD-024 harness fast-mode-route.mjs does. It should check that the browser's request gets a 200 answer with the seven headers, that crossOriginIsolated is true, that client.mode() is 'fast' and that the threaded build's startup check passes.
- **Required verification:** A gate that check.sh, CI and the release workflow run opens the page through mhfe serve and through mhfe-fast-mode.py in Chromium and Firefox. Changing COEP in both launchers, or adding a Content-Security-Policy script-src header to both, makes that gate fail. No unmarked copy of the header values remains outside serve.rs and the marked, tested Python copy, which a grep for require-corp in tracked non-audit files shows.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 completenessGaps[2] and its informational observation (fast-mode serving path never run with a real browser), AUD-023-ARC018 (the suite's own copy of the page CSP; its fix did not cover the header copy), AUD-024: The Python fast-mode launcher copies mhfe serve's limits, security headers, checksum format values, exit codes, title and messages with no 'deliberate copy' marker
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 with a static trace and a logged probe. In fast mode the browser suite opens a node:http stand-in server (scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:239-248), not either launcher. That server sends Content-Type and only two of the seven security headers. It answers every path and Host and needs no checksum file. Two values, COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp, are typed again with no 'deliberate copy' marker, and no test keeps them equal to serve.rs:64-72. No gate opens mhfe serve or packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py in a browser. Every tracked non-audit file that drives a browser and also starts a launcher is a document (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, releases/v0.6.0.md). Every file that starts a launcher names no browser. check.sh:66 runs only the Python unit tests, and ci.yml:97-102 runs only verify-browsers.mjs. AUD-023 recorded this as an informational observation and a completeness gap, not as a finding, so this is not a repeat. Its sibling AUD-023-ARC018, the suite's CSP copy, was a finding, and its fix did not cover the header copy. The candidate overstates one point, and I corrected it below. A mistyped COOP or COEP value in only one launcher is caught: verify-fast-mode-script.py's test_the_security_headers_match_the_rust_launcher fails (probe step 10). What passes every gate is the same change made in both launchers, a header added to both, or a Host or response change that only a real browser exposes, while the suite goes on testing its own headers. I found no duplicate in the confirmed list. The 'Python launcher copies mhfe serve's ... security headers' finding covers the launcher's copy, not the suite's stand-in or the missing browser case.

##### AUD-024-ARC007 — Low — The real-browser suite never runs a searchWallet that searches: its only call is a refusal of two missing words, so the search with the password, its per-candidate progress and its result run in no browser, and the worker's searchWallet operation runs in no check at all

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser suite coverage / MhfeClient.searchWallet and the core worker's searchWallet operation
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-33
- **Affected files and builds:** All browsers (Chromium, Firefox) and both modes (standard, fast), commit b6fca69. Untested product code: web/client.js:601-643 (searchWallet JSDoc and method; message operation "searchWallet" built at :632); web/client.d.ts:629-644 (declaration, onProgress: MhfeSearchProgress at :632); web/core-worker.js:190-216 (worker operation; candidate counter at :206-210 and the combined candidate+round progress post at :212-213). The suite: scripts/browser-check/client-checks.mjs:188-238 (checkCandidateSearch), where the only searchWallet call, at :229-237, is expectRejection(..., "TOO_MANY_MISSING_WORDS", "searchWallet refuses two missing words before any round"). The suite's own claim: scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:17-19 ('The page calls every method of the four classes with each of its options and compares the results, or the refusals, with known values'). Its list of what reduced cost cannot show, :31-37, does not name the search. The documented progress contract: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:499 and :502-503. Coverage that exists outside a browser: scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs:419-450 calls the WebAssembly binding directly at reduced cost with its own callbacks, not the worker. scripts/package-check/core-client.mjs:176-185 and client-refusals.mjs:301-310 run the class against a stand-in worker that replies { found: false } or { found: [] } and sends no progress.
- **Reproduction:** From the mhfe root at b6fca69: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-search-wallet-browser search-wallet-coverage python3 /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-search-wallet-browser/probe.py. The probe lists every `.searchWallet(` call in scripts/browser-check/*.mjs and classifies it as a refusal when expectRejection/rejectionOf opens within the 3 lines before it. It looks in scripts/**/*.mjs for any message with operation: "searchWallet" that a check builds for the real worker. It counts the baseline b20-browsers.log lines that name searchWallet. Output: 'scripts/browser-check/client-checks.mjs:230: refusal'; 'messages with operation "searchWallet" built by a check script: none'; worker operation at web/core-worker.js:190, its candidate+round progress at :213; '4' baseline lines, all 'ok searchWallet refuses two missing words before any round -> TOO_MANY_MISSING_WORDS ...'; 'FAIL: no browser-suite case runs a searchWallet that searches (1 call(s), all refusals)'; exit 1. Static trace: client.searchWallet (client.js:616) sends the message to the worker. The worker's searchWallet (core-worker.js:190) calls argon2For and then mhfe.searchWallet. The binding refuses the two-? container before any round, so the onCandidate and onRound callbacks (core-worker.js:206-213) never run. git log -S'searchWallet(' shows that the same lone refusal was already there in 3a705db (v0.6.0).
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-33 (code-core.instructions.md:260-263, Check: review): 'A feature has its case in the browser regression suite ... in both editions and both browsers where the feature exists'. In mhfe that suite is scripts/verify-browsers.mjs, and the AGENTS.md:16 browser-package line says it runs the package in Chromium and Firefox. The suite's own header (verify-browsers.mjs:17-19) says the page calls every method of the four classes with each of its options and compares the results with known values. Its list of what the reduced cost cannot show (:31-37) names only a PIM above 0 and the published vectors' verdict, not the search. docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:499 and :502-503 document searchWallet's progress as 12 rounds a candidate, '{ stage: "search", candidate, candidates }' with 'round and rounds of the candidate's recovery as each of its rounds starts'. A search is feasible in the suite: the reduced-cost wrapper (verify-browsers.mjs:118-161) serves any suite 3 request, and Node already searches REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER with its last word as ? (core-operations.mjs:419-450; baseline b14-browser-package exit 0).
- **Observed behavior:** The browser suite has one searchWallet call (client-checks.mjs:229-237). It expects TOO_MANY_MISSING_WORDS for two missing words and is refused before any round. The suite never passes searchWallet an { address, coin, path? }, { fingerprint } or { walletCheck: true } reference, a passphrase, passwordRepair, pim, memoryLevel or onProgress. It never sees a candidate recovered, a progress report or a { found, container, containerFingerprint, words, path, candidates } result. No Node check sends the operation to the real worker script either: in-process-worker.mjs exercises other operations only, and core-client.mjs and client-refusals.mjs use a stand-in worker that sends no progress. So the worker's searchWallet operation (core-worker.js:190-216), including the progress record it combines from the two binding callbacks, is exercised by no check except up to the refusal. The baseline run (b20-browsers.log:44, :559, :1075, :1590) shows just that refusal in each browser and mode.
- **Impact:** Coverage only, no wrong result is shown. A regression in the page-worker path of the search with the owner's wallet would pass every gate in both browsers and modes. Examples: the worker posting progress without candidate or round, a wrong candidate count, the result JSON shape, cancelling a search mid-candidate, or the transfer and wipe of the password through this operation. The documented progress contract of BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:502-503 is asserted nowhere.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-search-wallet-browser/search-wallet-coverage.log with search-wallet-coverage.command.json (exit 1, 2026-10-14T11:33:22Z; probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-search-wallet-browser/probe.py). Baseline docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/b20-browsers.log (node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs, exit 0, 06:54:02Z-06:58:40Z): lines 44, 559, 1075 and 1590 are the only searchWallet labels. Baseline b14-browser-package.log (node scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs, exit 0) shows that the reduced-cost binding search passes under Node. The reporter's docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-unapplied-review-rules/option-cases.log (lines 36-43) and verify-review-rules.log line 7 ('FAIL the_browser_suite_runs_a_search_wallet_that_finds_the_word: 1 searchWallet calls, 1 of them refusals') agree. History: git log -S'searchWallet(' -- scripts/verify-browsers.mjs scripts/browser-check/ gives 3a705db (v0.6.0) and 19e1cd5 (the split into browser-check/), both with the same single refusal.
- **Recommended fix:** In scripts/browser-check/client-checks.mjs (checkCandidateSearch), add cases that run client.searchWallet on REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER with its last word typed as ? and PASSWORD. Use { fingerprint } of the phrase, { address, coin } and { builtInCheck: true }, plus { walletCheck: true } with a passphrase if a suitable container exists. Each case should check the found word and container, the result's fields, an onProgress sequence that names candidate, candidates, round and rounds (12 rounds a candidate), and a cancel() during a candidate's recovery. Also send the 'searchWallet' operation once through the in-process worker in scripts/package-check/in-process-worker.mjs, so that the worker's progress composition is checked under Node too.
- **Required verification:** The new cases pass in Chromium and Firefox in standard and fast mode (node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs). Each fails when web/core-worker.js's searchWallet operation is broken: for example, drop candidate from the progress post at :213 or return the raw string instead of the parsed result. The probe above then exits 0.
- **Related findings:** AUD-024 (confirmed): MhfeClient.keepOldContainer(), added for AUD-023-ARC016, is called by no check: the browser suite never calls it although it says the page calls every method, AUD-024 (confirmed): Twelve of the browser suite's 1,986 reported checks cannot fail
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced it at b6fca69. scripts/browser-check/ has one MhfeClient.searchWallet() call, at client-checks.mjs:229-237. It sits inside expectRejection and is refused with TOO_MANY_MISSING_WORDS before any round. The baseline b20-browsers.log shows only that label, at lines 44, 559, 1075 and 1590 (Chromium and Firefox, standard and fast). No check of any kind sends the worker's "searchWallet" operation through the real worker script (web/core-worker.js:190-216): the in-process worker check never sends it, and core-client.mjs replaces the worker with a stand-in. So the documented per-candidate progress { stage, candidate, candidates, round, rounds }, which that operation builds at :212-213, is checked nowhere. The search is feasible at the suite's reduced cost: Node already runs the binding's search on REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER (core-operations.mjs:419-450, and b14 exited 0). The suite's list of what reduced cost cannot show does not include searchWallet. The gap goes back to v0.6.0 (3a705db), so it is not an AUD-023 regression. No earlier record reports it. It is a different root cause from the confirmed keepOldContainer finding: a different method, and here the method is called but only in its refusal.

##### AUD-024-ARC013 — Low — Every library module returns the one crate-wide MhfeError, and no independent module (repair words, password tools, wallet check, encryption core) has an error enum of its own

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** error types of the library modules
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-004
- **Rules:** RUST-04, CORE-04
- **Affected files and builds:** src/error.rs:12 (pub enum MhfeError, 52 variants, the only error enum in src/; no From impl into it anywhere in src/). Its Display depends on other modules: src/error.rs:230 and :248 (crate::phrase::word_counts_text / counts_text), :289 (crate::phrase::grouped, crate::wallet_check::WALLET_CHECK_ODDS), :308 (crate::phrase::LIST_SIZE), :394 and :400 (crate::suite::memory_text), :445 (crate::self_check::failure_message, defined at src/self_check.rs:224; src/self_check.rs:20 declares pub mod sets, whose src/self_check/sets.rs:88-169 pulls in crate::mhfe, repair, search, wallet, wallet_check and new_password). Modules that import MhfeError instead of an error of their own (import line): repair words src/repair.rs:34 (pub fns at :265, :281, :408); password tools src/password.rs:13 (:38, :77), src/new_password.rs:11 (:53, :72, :138, :148, :278), src/check_word.rs:19 (:201, :226, :236, :245), src/eff.rs:10, src/word_wishes.rs:25 (:111), src/word_hints.rs:15 (:82); random source src/random.rs:7 (:52, :70); wallet check src/wallet_check.rs:45 (:73, :88, :124, :133, :142, :155, :185); encryption core src/mhfe.rs:18 with its parts src/feistel.rs:27, src/packing.rs:14, src/suite.rs:8; wallet src/wallet.rs:30. All builds (native library, CLI, WASM package).
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69: `grep -rnE "enum [A-Za-z]*Error\b" src --include=*.rs` prints only src/error.rs:12. `grep -rnE "impl From<[^>]*> for (crate::)?MhfeError" src` prints nothing. `grep -noE "crate::[a-z_]+::[A-Za-z_]+" src/error.rs` shows that the non-test Display code calls into phrase, suite, wallet_check and self_check. `grep -nE "pub fn .*Result<" src/repair.rs src/password.rs src/new_password.rs src/check_word.rs src/wallet_check.rs src/word_wishes.rs src/word_hints.rs src/random.rs` lists 25 public functions, and every one returns Result<_, MhfeError>. The whole probe is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-error-types/probe.sh.
- **Expected behavior:** RUST-04 (code-rust.instructions.md, 'An error type per module', Check: review): each independent module (CORE-04) has its own error enum, so that another program can take the module without the rest; where a crate-wide error is useful, it wraps the module errors through From. CORE-04 (code-core.instructions.md) names mhfe's repair words, password tools, wallet checks and encryption core as such modules, which should be importable alone because MnemoCode, the Deriver and future tools take single parts.
- **Observed behavior:** There is no module error enum anywhere in src/. The repair words, password, generator, check word, word wishes, word hints, random source, wallet check and encryption core all return the single 52-variant MhfeError. That enum carries the variants and messages of every other module, and nothing wraps a module error through From. MhfeError's Display calls into phrase, suite, wallet_check and self_check (error.rs:230-445), and self_check declares the sets submodule, which references mhfe, repair, search, wallet, wallet_check and new_password. So a program cannot take src/repair.rs (or any other named module) without also taking the whole crate.
- **Impact:** Maintainability and reuse only. Another program such as MnemoCode or the Deriver cannot take one module, for example the repair words, without the crate-wide error type, and through its Display the rest of the library. Every module's error surface also grows with every other module's variants. Behaviour, secrets and error codes are not affected.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-error-types/v01-error-types-static.log with .command.json, exit 0, 2026-10-14T07:55:29Z, run through run-logged.sh with bash /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-error-types/probe.sh. The log shows: HEAD b6fca69; the only error enum at src/error.rs:12; 52 variants; no From impl into MhfeError; error.rs references at lines 7, 230, 248, 289, 308, 394 and 445 into phrase, suite, wallet_check and self_check; the import line of MhfeError in each module; 25 public functions of the CORE-04 modules returning MhfeError; no RUST-04 exception in src/ or docs/. Manual reads: src/self_check.rs:20 (pub mod sets), src/self_check.rs:224 (failure_message), src/self_check/sets.rs:88-169 (module dependencies). The original evidence is docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/core-crypto/c09-error-types.log.
- **Recommended fix:** Give each independent module an error enum of its own (for example RepairError, PasswordError, WalletCheckError, a core cipher error), each with Display, std::error::Error and its own message text, and with no dependency on unrelated modules: move what self_check::failure_message and the phrase and suite helpers do for those messages into the module that owns them, or into a small shared text module. Keep MhfeError as the crate-wide error that wraps them through From, and keep code() returning the same stable codes, so the CLI exit mapping and the browser error codes do not change. This is a crate-wide change; agree its scope and order with the owner.
- **Required verification:** Each named module compiles and is tested with its own error type, and its error module depends on no unrelated module (no crate::self_check or crate::wallet_check reference from the repair or password error). MhfeError::code() returns the same code for every former variant (a table test). The CLI exit codes and messages, and the browser package's error-code check and CLI/browser parity run, still pass unchanged.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 (HEAD checked) and the claim holds. src/ has exactly one error enum, src/error.rs:12 `pub enum MhfeError`. Nothing in src/ has an `impl From<..> for MhfeError`, so no module error is wrapped. The repository writes down no exception to RUST-04. The public entry points of every module that CORE-04 names (repair words, password tools, wallet check, encryption core) return MhfeError directly. My logged static probe (v01-error-types-static) reproduces this.
  
  I also found that the coupling is real, not only a naming matter. The Display of MhfeError reaches into crate::phrase, crate::suite, crate::wallet_check and crate::self_check (error.rs:230, 248, 289, 308, 394, 445). crate::self_check declares `pub mod sets;` (self_check.rs:20), and that module builds checks from crate::mhfe, repair, search, wallet, wallet_check and new_password. So a program that takes src/repair.rs has to take the whole crate.
  
  Corrections to the candidate: MhfeError has 52 variants, not 80. The encryption core itself (src/mhfe.rs:18) and src/wallet.rs:30 belong in the affected list. eff, feistel, packing and suite are parts of the password tools and the encryption core, not independent modules on their own.
  
  Severity stays low under AUDIT_STANDARD.md, because this is a maintainability defect with bounded practical impact. RUST-04 is "Check: review", and the task applies such rules to the whole repository. AUD-023 has no finding about error types.

##### AUD-024-ARC014 — Low — MhfeError's Display is not the one place its messages are written: 14 variants carry free text written at 102 non-test sites, the CLI and the browser bindings write or rewrite messages of library codes, and the split already gives broken sentences such as "unknown coin the coins are bitcoin, …"

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Errors / message source (library, CLI, browser bindings)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** RUST-04, CORE-23
- **Affected files and builds:** Every build and front end (native CLI, browser package).
  
  Claim:
  - src/error.rs:9-10 "Each variant has a stable code ... and one message, written by its `Display`".
  - src/error.rs:211-214 expect reason "the one place the messages are written (CORE-23)".
  
  Display arms that write only or mostly the caller's text:
  - src/error.rs:413 `Self::InvalidPasswordSize(reason) => write!(f, "{reason}")`.
  - src/error.rs:443 `unknown coin {reason}`.
  
  The 14 free-text variants: InvalidPhrase, InvalidContainer, InvalidRepairWords, InvalidWordWish, InvalidAddress, InvalidDerivationPath, InvalidFingerprint, Argon2, InvalidRequest, InvalidPasswordSize, RandomFailed, InvalidCoin, Internal, SelfCheckFailed (src/error.rs:14-199).
  
  Library composition sites (77 construction sites in 28 files; full list in the v04-scan log), among them:
  - src/phrase.rs:40-71 (parse returns String reasons; :43-45 "it has {word_count} words")
  - src/new_password.rs:55-57 and :74-76 (the whole InvalidPasswordSize message), :150-152, :171-173
  - src/wallet.rs:189 ("the coins are …"), :329, :389, :549
  - src/repair.rs:267-270; :419-425 (rewrites the refusal's text by string formatting)
  - src/mhfe.rs:429-438
  - src/word_wishes.rs:113-145 and :260 through wish() at :263-265
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:30-43
  - src/rekey.rs:96-101, :256, :356-370
  - src/search.rs:81, :431
  - src/random.rs:59-61; src/random/health.rs:37-39
  - src/word_hints.rs:86-88
  
  CLI:
  - src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:73, :77 and :186-191 (rewrites a library InvalidAddress reason into a new sentence)
  - src/bin/mhfe/made_password.rs:174
  - src/bin/mhfe/system_random.rs:11 (getrandom's error text)
  
  Browser bindings:
  - src/wasm_api.rs:267-276: whole_number writes "{code}: {name} must be a whole number, not {value}" for INVALID_WORD_COUNT, INVALID_REPAIR_WORDS, INVALID_PIM, INVALID_MEMORY_LEVEL, INVALID_PASSWORD_SIZE and INVALID_REQUEST.
  - Error values built only to read code(): src/wasm_api.rs:332; src/wasm_api/core.rs:599, :609, :625, :630; src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:495; src/wasm_api/core/search.rs:121; src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:184; src/wasm_api/repair.rs:53; src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:175.
  - Library reasons written in the binding: src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:84; src/wasm_api.rs:260, :291-297 (the page's thrown Error message), :337; src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:184-193; src/wasm_api/core.rs:514, :522, :563; src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:121, :503-526; src/wasm_api/word_hints.rs:40.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69, with a debug build (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<audit target> cargo build --locked --bin mhfe). Each command below is refused before any Argon2 round.
  
  1. `NO_COLOR=1 mhfe password --words 33 </dev/null` prints "✗ Error: Choose between 1 and 32 words" and exits 2. The whole sentence comes from src/new_password.rs:55-57, and Display (src/error.rs:413) adds nothing.
  2. `NO_COLOR=1 mhfe password --chars 65 </dev/null` prints "✗ Error: Choose between 1 and 64 characters" (src/new_password.rs:74-76).
  3. `NO_COLOR=1 mhfe check --address --coin zzz </dev/null` prints "... unknown coin the coins are bitcoin, bitcoin-cash, …". The sentence is half in Display (src/error.rs:443) and half at src/wallet.rs:189.
  4. `printf 'abandon\n' | NO_COLOR=1 mhfe encrypt --stdin` prints "The seed phrase is not a valid English BIP39 phrase: it has 1 words, but a phrase has 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24" and exits 2. The variable part comes from src/phrase.rs:43-45.
  5. Static check: `python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-error-text-sites/scan.py`. It lists:
     - the payload-only Display arm (src/error.rs:413);
     - 102 non-test construction sites of free-text variants in 37 files (77 in 28 library files);
     - 11 places in the bindings that write a code's message themselves or build an error only to read its code().
     It exits 1.
- **Expected behavior:** RUST-04 (code-rust.instructions.md, Check: review): every error type's Display is the one place its messages are written (CORE-23). CORE-23 (code-core.instructions.md, Check: review): every error has a stable code, and the text a person reads is built in one place per front end from that code. Its wording follows DOC-05 and DOC-07. The project claims the same of MhfeError at src/error.rs:9-10 ("one message, written by its Display") and :211-214 ("the one place the messages are written (CORE-23)").
- **Observed behavior:** - Fourteen MhfeError variants carry a free String. Their message text is written where the error is built: 102 non-test sites in 37 files, about 77 in the library.
  - For InvalidPasswordSize, Display writes only `{reason}`, so the whole message lives in new_password.rs. One code, INVALID_PASSWORD_SIZE, has two unrelated texts.
  - The split gives sentences that no single place reviews: "unknown coin the coins are bitcoin, …" and "it has 1 words".
  - Messages are rewritten after construction: by the library (repair.rs:419-425) and by the CLI (wallet_reference.rs:186-191).
  - The browser bindings write their own message for six library codes (whole_number, src/wasm_api.rs:267-276). For INVALID_PIM this sits beside Display's own "... must be a whole number from 0 to 1023, not {pim}".
  - The bindings reach a code only by constructing a dummy error, such as InvalidRepairWords(String::new()) or InvalidPim { pim: 0, .. }.
  - Dependency or page text can reach the person: getrandom's error (system_random.rs:11), the page's thrown Error message (wasm_api.rs:291-297), and the Argon2 reference message (engine/ffi.rs:191, documented at error.rs:159).
  - The bip39 texts at phrase.rs:69 and :143 can reach a person only if an earlier check fails, since word count, word list and entropy length are validated first.
  - No reason found repeats text a person typed.
- **Impact:** This is maintainability and presentation only.
  - The wording of one code is spread over many callers and front ends, so it cannot be reviewed against DOC-05/DOC-07 in one place.
  - It already gives at least two ungrammatical refusals ("unknown coin the coins are …", "it has 1 words").
  - A front end cannot render its own text from a code and its typed data, and the same code is worded differently by the library and the browser bindings.
  - No secret is exposed and no result changes.
- **Evidence:** Evidence folder docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-error-text-sites/, each log with a .command.json:
  - v01-password-words-33.log: exit 2, "✗ Error: Choose between 1 and 32 words".
  - v02-password-chars-65.log: exit 2, "✗ Error: Choose between 1 and 64 characters".
  - v03-check-coin-refusal.log: exit 2, "... unknown coin the coins are bitcoin, bitcoin-cash, cosmos, ...".
  - v04-scan.log: harness output, exit 1. It shows:
    - check 1: src/error.rs:413;
    - check 2: 102 sites in 37 files, 77 in 28 library files (Internal 34, InvalidRequest 27, InvalidPhrase 9, RandomFailed 6, InvalidContainer 6, InvalidAddress 5, Argon2 3, others fewer);
    - check 3: 11 binding places, including src/wasm_api.rs:273.
  - v05-cited-lines.log: git HEAD b6fca69 and the cited source lines.
  - v06-encrypt-one-word.log: exit 2, "... it has 1 words, but a phrase has 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24".
  
  The original reviewer's static list is guide-lib-core/s01-error-text-sites.log.
  
  The harness is docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-error-text-sites/ (scan.py plus README.md). It exits non-zero while Display is not the one message source.
  
  The binary was a debug build at b6fca69 in the audit target directory. No full-cost Argon2 was run.
- **Recommended fix:** - Replace the String payloads with typed reasons: per-variant enums or fields such as a word position, a count, a limit or a list of allowed values. Display writes their text, and a front end can render its own text from the code and those fields.
  - Make InvalidPasswordSize carry the kind and the limit.
  - Make InvalidCoin carry nothing or the list, and write the whole sentence in Display.
  - Stop rewriting reasons after construction (repair.rs:419-425, wallet_reference.rs:186-191). Add the hint as a typed field instead.
  - Expose each code without constructing an error, for example an associated const or a code enum per variant.
  - Let the bindings' whole_number refusal be a library error variant, such as NotAWholeNumber { field }, whose message Display writes.
  - Map dependency and page errors (getrandom, a page's random source) to typed reasons. Keep at most the Argon2 reference message as a documented exception.
  - This can be done together with the per-module error enums of the confirmed RUST-04 finding, but it is a separate change: those enums need typed reasons too.
- **Required verification:** - `python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-error-text-sites/scan.py` exits 0, after removing from its list only the variants documented as exceptions, with the reason.
  - A unit test renders every MhfeError variant's message from Display alone and checks every one against the wording rules. At least it checks that "unknown coin" and the word-count refusals read as whole sentences, and that singular counts are handled.
  - The browser bindings read codes without constructing errors and write no `{code}:` message outside js_error.
  - `mhfe password --words 33`, `mhfe check --address --coin zzz` and a one-word phrase with `mhfe encrypt --stdin` print messages written in src/error.rs.
- **Related findings:** AUD-024 confirmed: [ARC] Every library module returns the one crate-wide MhfeError, and no independent module has an error enum of its own (RUST-04), AUD-023-ARC011 (its fix replaced literal codes in the bindings with MhfeError::X(String::new()).code()), AUD-023-UI001 (browser early refusals worded apart from the library's sentences), AUD-023 informational observation: shared refusal texts read badly ("unknown coin the coins are …", "it has 1 words")
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. src/error.rs:9-10 and the expect reason at :211-214 say Display is "the one place the messages are written (CORE-23)", and that is not true.
  
  - Display writes none of some messages. `Self::InvalidPasswordSize(reason) => write!(f, "{reason}")` (:413) takes the whole sentence from the caller. `mhfe password --words 33` prints "Choose between 1 and 32 words", written at src/new_password.rs:55-57 (log v01). `--chars 65` prints a text from :74-76 (log v02).
  - Other messages are split between Display and the caller, and the split shows to the user. Display writes `unknown coin {reason}` and src/wallet.rs:189 supplies "the coins are …". `mhfe check --address --coin zzz` prints "unknown coin the coins are bitcoin, …" (log v03). src/phrase.rs:43-45 gives "it has 1 words, but a phrase has …" (log v06, refused before any Argon2 round).
  - Code outside Display rewrites existing reasons: the library at src/repair.rs:419-425 and the CLI at src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:186-191.
  - The browser bindings write messages for library codes themselves. whole_number builds "{code}: {name} must be a whole number, not {value}" (src/wasm_api.rs:267-276). Ten bindings construct a dummy error, such as InvalidRepairWords(String::new()) or InvalidPim { pim: 0, .. }, only to read its code().
  
  The harness scan finds 102 non-test construction sites of the 14 free-text variants in 37 files, 77 of them in 28 library files.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - The bip39 texts it cites, src/phrase.rs:69 and :143, cannot reach a person in practice. Word count, word list and entropy length are checked before. Dependency or page text that can reach a person: getrandom's error (src/bin/mhfe/system_random.rs:11), the page's thrown Error message (src/wasm_api.rs:291-297), and the Argon2 reference message (src/engine/ffi.rs:191, documented at src/error.rs:159).
  - CORE-10 is dropped from the rules: no single message was shown to be copied.
  - The site count is now 102 by an exact scan; the candidate said about 90.
  
  This is not a duplicate of the confirmed RUST-04 finding. That finding is about the missing per-module error enums. Per-module enums could still carry free String reasons and binding-written messages, so fixing it does not fix this. AUD-023 recorded the "unknown coin the coins are" text only as an informational observation. Its ARC006, ARC011 and UI001 findings were about copied literals, not about where messages are composed.
  
  Severity is low: a maintainability and presentation defect with one visibly broken sentence. No secret is exposed.

With connection.settimeout(None) in the Python answer(), the mutation that AUD-023-ARC017's required verification names, scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py never ends. serve.rs's test of write_until never ends either when set_write_timeout(None) is used or the call is deleted.

The mutation set's removed timeout is `connection.settimeout(None)` in answer() (AUD-023-ARC017, reproduction step 2).

- **Observed behavior:** At b6fca69, harness-response-deadline-guard.log (exit 1) shows:

  - 'Python answer() with settimeout(None): NOT GUARDED (the test is still running after 60 s)'

  - settimeout(8): fails after 8.2 s.
  
  So a lost timeout that leaves some finite timeout is caught. A timeout of None, or a very long one, makes the test block in sendall for ever, with no failure named.
  
  The Rust test has the same structure. A blocking TcpStream write with no write timeout never returns once the socket buffers are full (rust-response-deadline-mutant.log: exit 124 after 60 s). Deleting serve.rs:339 leaves the accepted stream's default, which is also no timeout. Neither unittest nor libtest has a per-test time limit; libtest only warns after 60 s.
  
  AUD-023's addendum row for ARC017 (AUD-023-2026-10-13.md:1231) says "Its own required verification was not run again".
- **Impact:** A regression that drops either launcher's response deadline is not reported as a failing test. It shows as a run that never ends. That is the slow-reader bound SECURITY.md promises: a client that never reads would otherwise hold a thread and a connection slot.
  - Locally, scripts/check.sh, scripts/check-fast.sh and scripts/build-reproducible.sh hang with no limit.
  - In CI, the Python case stalls the release-check job until GitHub's default 360-minute job limit. It stalls the canonical Docker build until the release job's 90-minute limit, or 60 minutes for ci.yml's canonical-build job.
  - The Rust case stalls every push's and pull request's check job up to 360 minutes.
  
  None of these runs names the cause. No release can pass with the defect, so the effect is bounded to lost time and an unclear diagnosis.
- **Evidence:** All logs are in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-arc017-deadline-hang/:
  - harness-response-deadline-guard.log: exit 1, started 2026-10-14T11:39:10Z, sha256 442a1f9649340c18…, command docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-arc017-deadline-hang/response_deadline_guard.sh <scratch> 60.
  - response-deadline-mutants.log: started 11:34:17Z, sha256 697ac85ac220a062…, probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verifier-arc017-deadline-hang/probe.sh.
  - rust-response-deadline-mutant.log: started 11:36:46Z, sha256 40149c8968c21097…, probe rust_probe.sh in the same scratch folder.
  
  The candidate's own logs agree, in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-required-verification-and-remediation-diff/:
  - harness-arc017-response-deadline.log ('exit 124 after 60 s').
  - arc017-python-mutations.log ('P2 Python answer() without a response timeout: HANGS (killed after 120 s)'; every other limit mutation fails test_the_limits_match_the_rust_launcher).
  
  The baseline b17-fast-mode-script.log shows 'Ran 31 tests in 2.594s OK'. b01-check-fast.log shows the Rust test 'ok'.
  
  Static trace: verify-fast-mode-script.py:239-240, mhfe-fast-mode.py:354 and :369-370, serve.rs:339-340 and :608. ci.yml:29-34 (RELEASE_CHECKS), :36-90 (no timeout-minutes), :121. release.yml:21.
- **Recommended fix:** Bound both tests from outside the code they test.
  
  Python: run fast_mode.answer() in a daemon thread and join it with a timeout of about 3 s. Assert that the thread has ended. Close the client socket in cleanup so a blocked sendall returns.
  
  Rust: run write_until in a spawned thread that sends its result over a channel. Use recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(3)) and fail the test on a timeout; dropping the client side unblocks the thread.
  
  Then a lost deadline fails with the test's own message instead of hanging. Optionally give the CI check job a timeout-minutes.
- **Required verification:** 1. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-arc017-deadline-hang/response_deadline_guard.sh <scratch> 60 exits 0: the control passes, and both mutants fail within the limit.
  2. python3 scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py and cargo test --locked serve:: pass on the unchanged tree in about the same time as now (about 3 s for the Python script).
  3. The AUD-023-ARC017 mutation set fails at least one test for every mutation, with none hanging.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC017, AUD-003-SEC001
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69. On the unchanged tree, the Python response-deadline test passes in 0.6 s and the whole script passes in 2.8 s. AUD-023-ARC017's reproduction names one mutation: connection.settimeout(None) in answer(). With that mutation the single test and the whole script were both still running when timeout killed them at 20 s and at 60 s (exit 124). No test fails, and nothing reports a failure.
  
  The test cannot catch it because it calls fast_mode.answer() in its own thread with no outer bound. It reads the elapsed time only after answer() returns, which never happens once sendall blocks with no timeout. AUD-023's addendum row for ARC017 says its own required verification was not run again.
  
  Two refinements:
  - Deleting line 369 outright is caught. The read deadline's settimeout(remaining), about 5 s, stays in force, so the test fails after 5.2 s. A finite timeout such as settimeout(8) also fails, after 8.2 s. Only a timeout of None, or a very long one, hangs.
  - The Rust counterpart, serve.rs's a_client_that_does_not_read_is_dropped_at_the_response_deadline, which the Python test copies, has the same root cause. It calls write_until synchronously. With set_write_timeout(None) at serve.rs:339 it was still running at 60 s (exit 124). Deleting that line leaves the default, which is no timeout. I added it as a variant.
  
  I also corrected the impact. The Python script runs only in scripts/check.sh, which CI runs only for release tags and by hand, in a check job with no timeout-minutes (GitHub's 360-minute default), and in the canonical Docker build, which the release job bounds at 90 minutes. The Rust test runs in check-fast.sh on every push and pull request. This is not a duplicate of any confirmed finding.

CORE-10 (code-core.instructions.md): a copy that cannot be avoided is kept in step with its source by a test. DOC-07: documents claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides. The AUD-023-ARC013 record in AUD-023-2026-10-13.json is marked fixed in da4618d with the evidence that the gate "keeps ... copies equal to their sources".
- **Recommended fix:** Add ["THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md", "commit `{}`"] to the copies of the Argon2 commit pin. Add ["THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md", "wasm-bindgen command-line tool {}", "`wasm-bindgen-cli-support` {}"] to the copies of the wasm-bindgen pin; a space in a text already matches any white space, which covers the line break at :354-355 if the text moves. Three changed copies in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md each still give exit 0 and "Every copy of a pinned value equals its source.": the Argon2 commit at line 13, the wasm-bindgen tool version at line 350 and the wasm-bindgen-cli-support version at line 355. Two listed copies changed the same way are refused with exit 1: the Emscripten version in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at line 33, and the Argon2 commit in src/vectors.rs at line 57. The notices file is therefore in the gate's scope for Emscripten but not for the other two values. No other check covers these lines. third-party-licenses.py --check keeps the hand-written part above the marker as written. Its check_toolchain compares only the standard library section.
