A future result written past one of these cuts, or with write!/writeln! on stdout, would bring back the AUD-023-FUN001 behaviour: exit 0 on a closed pipe, or a panic and abort on a full disk. The regression test would stay green. Bounded maintainability defect: low.
- **Evidence:** Verifier evidence in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-stdout-guard-reach/:
  - v01-guard-mutants.log: first manual probe. The baseline passes. The draw_entries println! passes. The added decrypt.rs write_all passes. The added menu.rs control fails at main.rs:435 with 'menu.rs writes to standard output with println!('.
  - v02-guard-reach.log: reach.py lists the unread spans and their functions per file: choice.rs 301-439, self_test.rs 21-342, startup.rs 121-166, style.rs 331-697, cell_widths.rs 10-518. Total 1,383 lines.
  - v03-guard-reach-harness.log: the kept harness, one mutation at a time. Three MISSED, the control caught, 'mutations the guard missed: 3', exit 1.
  - v04-static-writers.log: main.rs:409-442, style.rs:19-28, the stdout writers menu.rs:104 and main.rs:289, the only println! being main.rs:434 (the test's own search list) and made_password.rs:298 (inside mod tests), the cut points, and the clap_builder 4.6.7 sources for Error::exit (src/error/mod.rs:245-249, `let _ = self.print();`) and print_long_help (src/builder/command.rs:968-978).
  - v05-help-to-full-device.log: target/release/mhfe from the baseline build. --help > /dev/full and --version > /dev/full both exit 0.
  
  Reviewer's evidence, consistent with the above: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-infra/g05-stdout-guard-mutation.log and g08-stdout-scan-reach.log.
  
  Cargo.toml [lints.clippy] and clippy.toml enable no print_stdout lint, so this test is the only gate.
- **Recommended fix:** 1. Cut each file only at the #[cfg(test)] line directly followed by `mod tests`, the end-of-file test module that RUST-08 prescribes. Alternatively, drop every #[cfg(test)] item rather than everything after the first one.
  2. Widen the search to every standard-output writer: println!/print!, write!/writeln!/write_all on io::stdout() or anstream::stdout() (allowing style::out alone), and clap's print_help, print_long_help and Error::exit.
  3. Route menu.rs:104 through style::out (render_long_help, then style::out). Alternatively, name menu.rs:104 and main.rs:289 in the test as allowed exceptions, each with its reason, and correct the doc at main.rs:409-411.
  4. Per CORE-28, give the scanner a case it must refuse: a fixture text with a println! after a mid-file #[cfg(test)] item must be flagged.
- **Required verification:** With CARGO_TARGET_DIR set to a scratch target, docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-stdout-guard-reach/guard_reach.sh <scratch> <fix commit> prints 'caught:' for all four mutations and exits 0. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-cli-infra/stdout_guard_mutation.py also exits 0. The unchanged tree still passes the guard test.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-FUN001
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. I exported the commit into a scratch tree and changed one file at a time. A println! in choice::draw_entries and a println! in style::error_lines both leave the guard test green, because each sits after a mid-file #[cfg(test)] item where the test cuts the file. A std::io::Write::write_all on io::stdout() in decrypt::print_result, a file the test reads whole, also leaves it green. The control, a println! in menu.rs before its only #[cfg(test)], makes it fail. The static trace agrees: main.rs:432 keeps only the text before the first "#[cfg(test)]", and :434 searches only for "println!(" and "print!(".
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - The unread span is 1,383 lines, not 1,389. Of these, 509 are the generated cell-width table and 874 are hand-written code.
  - The test's doc claim is already false today. Two writers print to standard output outside style::out: menu.rs:104 (clap print_long_help) and main.rs:289 (clap Error::exit, used for --help and --version).
  - CORE-33 is replaced by CHECK-ARC-003. The guard would have failed before the AUD-023-FUN001 fix, so CORE-33's seen-failing rule was met.
  
  This is not a duplicate. The confirmed standard-error finding is about eprint!/eprintln! panicking at run time; this one is about how far the regression gate reaches. Observation outside this finding: `mhfe --help` and `--version` to /dev/full exit 0 (clap swallows the write error). Help is not a result under AUD-023-FUN001, so I did not make it a finding.

##### AUD-024-ARC028 — Low — The longest answer and its refusal are written twice, with different values. The --stdin and visible-prompt reader (terminal.rs read_bounded_line) counts the line break inside LINE_CAPACITY, takes at most 8,191 bytes (8,190 with CRLF) and says 'longer than 8191 bytes'. The line editor of hidden and hinted prompts (hidden_input.rs LineEditor::push) takes 8,192 bytes and says 'longer than 8192 bytes'.

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: answer readers (src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs, src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-10, CORE-48
- **Affected files and builds:** All builds of the native command-line tool, at commit b6fca69. (1) src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:40 defines LINE_CAPACITY = mhfe::memory::TYPED_LINE_BYTES (src/memory.rs:168, 8192), described as 'Longest line accepted, line break included'. (2) src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:440-458, read_bounded_line: :444 reads with take(LINE_CAPACITY) including the line break; :445 refuses when no LF falls within LINE_CAPACITY bytes; :448-451 builds the refusal with LINE_CAPACITY - 1; :453 then strips LF or CRLF (strip_line_ending :461-468). It serves --stdin scripts (read_script_line :422-431) and Input::visible at a terminal (:159-171, call at :164). (3) src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:525-531, LineEditor::push: :527 refuses only when 8,192 bytes are already held, the line break excluded (edit_line :431-454 stores no CR or LF, :509). :528-530 builds a second copy of the same sentence with LINE_CAPACITY. It serves hidden secret prompts and hinted visible word prompts (read_line :91). (4) The literal end-of-input refusal 'No answer was typed.' appears twice, at src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:166 and :183. (5) The unit tests pin the two different limits: terminal.rs:676-702 (a_line_up_to_the_limit_keeps_its_buffer takes LINE_CAPACITY - 1, a_longer_line_is_refused) and hidden_input.rs:997-1008 (a_line_over_the_capacity_or_invalid_utf8_is_refused takes LINE_CAPACITY).
- **Reproduction:** Run from the repository root, with the release binary built from b6fca69 (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --release --bin mhfe): docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-line-limit p01-line-limit-probe python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-line-limit/probe.py /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target/release/mhfe. The probe feeds 'mhfe encrypt --stdin --pim 0 --mem 0 --same-length no --new-password own --repair-words 0' these lines: 8,191 bytes + LF, 8,192 bytes + LF, 8,190 bytes + CRLF, 8,191 bytes + CRLF. It then types 8,192 bytes + CR and 8,193 bytes + CR at the hidden 'Original seed phrase' prompt of the same command in a pseudo-terminal. No case reaches Argon2 or the memory reservation: every line is refused as a phrase or for its length, and encrypt reserves memory only after the phrase and password (encrypt.rs:178, :229). Unit level: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... cargo test --locked --bin mhfe a_line (log p02), plus terminal::tests::a_longer_line_is_refused in baseline b01.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-10 (code-core.instructions.md:84-95): every limit and message has exactly one source. A value with a meaning, such as a limit, is a named constant defined once, a value that follows from another is derived from it, and the same message is built in one place. CORE-48 (code-core.instructions.md:195-198): input is validated where it enters, with explicit limits on size, and refused with a clear message when it does not fit. The project states one limit: memory.rs:164-168 (TYPED_LINE_BYTES, 'The buffer a front end reads one typed line into ... 8 KiB') and SECURITY.md:48-49 ('Answers read from standard input are limited to 8192 bytes').
- **Observed behavior:** From log p01. --stdin with 8,191 bytes + LF: exit 2, refused as a phrase, not for length. --stdin with 8,192 bytes + LF: exit 2, 'Error: An answer is longer than 8191 bytes; no valid answer is that long.' Hidden prompt with 8,192 bytes + CR: taken as a line, no length refusal. Hidden prompt with 8,193 bytes + CR: refused as 'longer than 8192 bytes'. So the same 8,192-byte answer is accepted by one reader and refused by the other, and the stated limits differ (8191 and 8192). Variant with the same cause: because read_bounded_line counts the break inside LINE_CAPACITY before strip_line_ending, a CRLF script line can hold only 8,190 bytes. --stdin with 8,190 bytes + CRLF is not refused for length, but 8,191 bytes + CRLF gets exit 2 and 'An answer is longer than 8191 bytes', which is false for an 8,191-byte answer. From log p02, both readers' unit tests pass with their different limits (LINE_CAPACITY - 1 and LINE_CAPACITY). Static: the refusal sentence is built twice (terminal.rs:448-451, hidden_input.rs:528-530), and 'No answer was typed.' is written twice (terminal.rs:166, :183). Correction to the candidate: Input::visible at a real Linux terminal reads in canonical mode, which caps a line at 4,095 bytes in the tty driver. So the visible-versus-hidden difference cannot be seen at a terminal. It can be seen between --stdin (or a pipe read by Input::visible) and the line editor.
- **Impact:** Maintainability, with a small presentation defect. Every valid answer is far shorter: a password is at most 4,096 typed bytes (memory.rs:165-167). So no valid input is refused and no secret is exposed. Still, whether one answer is accepted or refused, and the limit the refusal states, depend on which reader takes it. A CRLF script line gets a refusal whose stated limit is wrong. The two copies of the rule and the sentence can drift further, and the tests pin each copy separately. Low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md (a maintainability or presentation defect with bounded practical impact).
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-line-limit/p01-line-limit-probe.log with .command.json (exit 1, DEFECT REPRODUCED; the probe source is under the scratch folder tmp/aud024/verify-line-limit/probe.py). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-line-limit/p02-reader-unit-tests.log (cargo test --locked --bin mhfe a_line: terminal::tests::a_line_up_to_the_limit_keeps_its_buffer and hidden_input::tests::a_line_over_the_capacity_or_invalid_utf8_is_refused pass). Baseline docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/b01-check-fast.log (terminal::tests::a_longer_line_is_refused ok). The original reporter's logs: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-infra/g04-cli-infra-probes.log (P3, same result) and g06-static-evidence.log (S5).
- **Recommended fix:** Define the longest answer once, as the number of answer bytes with the line break counted apart, derived from TYPED_LINE_BYTES. Make read_bounded_line strip LF or CRLF before it applies that limit, for example by reading up to the limit plus two bytes into the reserved buffer, or by reserving the buffer at the limit plus two. Then LF and CRLF lines and the line editor all take the same longest answer. Build the refusal in one function (for example terminal::too_long()) that both readers call, and give 'No answer was typed.' a single source. Change the tests of both readers to use the one constant and the one message, and add a CRLF case at the limit.
- **Required verification:** Rerun probe.py (log p01): both readers take the same longest answer, refuse one byte more, and state the same limit, and an answer at the limit followed by CRLF is accepted. guide-cli-infra P3 passes. The unit tests of terminal.rs and hidden_input.rs check the one constant and the one refusal function, and there is a CRLF-at-the-limit test. grep shows the refusal sentence and 'No answer was typed.' once each in src/bin/mhfe.
- **Related findings:** Confirmed AUD-024 finding: A typed line that is not UTF-8 or longer than 8,192 bytes ends the command instead of being asked again (same readers, different root cause)
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with a release binary built from that commit and with the unit tests. The two line readers share one constant, LINE_CAPACITY (terminal.rs:40, which is mhfe::memory::TYPED_LINE_BYTES = 8192), but they apply it differently and each builds its own refusal. read_bounded_line counts the line break inside the 8,192 bytes and says "longer than 8191 bytes" (terminal.rs:443-451). LineEditor::push leaves the break out, so it takes 8,192 bytes and says "longer than 8192 bytes" (hidden_input.rs:526-530). My probe got exactly that: --stdin refuses 8,192 bytes plus LF as "longer than 8191", while the hidden prompt in a pseudo-terminal takes 8,192 bytes and refuses 8,193 as "longer than 8192". It also found a variant with the same cause. Because the break counts toward the limit, a --stdin line ending in CRLF can hold only 8,190 bytes, and an 8,191-byte answer with CRLF is refused with the false statement that it is longer than 8191 bytes. "No answer was typed." is written as a literal twice (terminal.rs:166 and :183). One correction: at a real Linux terminal, Input::visible reads in canonical mode, where the tty driver caps a line at 4,095 bytes, so you cannot see the visible-prompt difference there. You can see it between --stdin (or a pipe read by Input::visible) and the line editor. This is not a duplicate of the confirmed finding that a too-long or non-UTF-8 line ends the command. That one is about what happens after a refusal; this one is about the limit and its message having two sources. CORE-10 is a review-only rule, so no gate enforces it.

##### AUD-024-ARC029 — Low — mhfe check decides from its own Choice enum which reference proves the wallet, instead of asking Reference::identifies_wallet, and that table's wallet-check row is dead: it describes a match the library has not given since the AUD-023-FUN002 fix

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: mhfe check result
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-14, CORE-10, CHECK-ARC-002, CHECK-ARC-003
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool, `mhfe check`, all platforms, at b6fca69. The library and the browser package are not affected.
  
  CLI, src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:
  - :184-195: enum Choice, a CLI copy of the reference kinds without their data. The library's ReferenceTarget (src/rehearsal.rs:211-226) has the same kinds.
  - :540-541: passed_lines' doc comment restates the library rule: "Only an address or a fingerprint identifies the wallet".
  - :555-563: passed_lines adds a line "... of the wallet" only for Choice::Address and Choice::Fingerprint.
  - :595-606: match_limit, a per-Choice table of what a match does not prove. Its only caller is report's Matches arm (:427, :454).
    - :601-603 says the built-in check and the own checks do not prove the wallet.
    - :604 is the Choice::WalletCheck arm, "It does not prove the wallet; an address (--address) does." It is unreachable.
  - :513-519: not_verified_reason's WalletCheck text repeats the same rule in prose ("only a receiving address (--address) or the fingerprint proves the wallet"). This arm is reachable.
  - :763-784: the test only_a_wallet_reference_claims_the_wallet tests the CLI's own table, not the library's predicate.
  
  Library:
  - src/rehearsal.rs:326-333: Reference::identifies_wallet. It is used only in rehearsal/reencryption.rs:34 and :60 and in search.rs:430.
  - src/rehearsal.rs:414-416: RecoveredForCheck::compare.
  - src/rehearsal.rs:458-462: refuse_impossible refuses WalletCheck on a same-length container and without a passphrase.
  - src/rehearsal.rs:520-527: compare_state's WalletCheck arm gives only NotVerified or DoesNotMatch.
  - src/suite.rs:103-105: holds_full_state is true for suite 3 only.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69, with no Argon2 at suite cost:
  
  1. `grep -rn identifies_wallet src/bin/mhfe` finds nothing (log v01). The only callers are in the library: rehearsal/reencryption.rs:34 and :60, and search.rs:430.
  
  2. Static trace of the wallet-check path (log v02):
     - check.rs:642: ask_for_choice is the only source of Choice::WalletCheck.
     - :339-340 and :353: GivenReference turns it into Reference::WalletCheck { passphrase }.
     - :284, :393 and :665: compare() calls Compared::with, which calls recovered.compare(reference). The OwnChecks re-ask at :394 does not apply.
     - rehearsal.rs:415: refuse_impossible refuses a non-suite-3 container (:458-460) and an empty passphrase (:462).
     - rehearsal.rs:416 and :484: evidence_of calls compare_state. Its WalletCheck arm at :522-527 returns NotVerified or DoesNotMatch.
     - check.rs:427 and :454: match_limit is reached only for CheckOutcome::Matches. So the arm at :604 never runs.
  
  3. `git show 253ca3c^:src/bin/mhfe/check.rs` and `git show 253ca3c^:src/rehearsal.rs` (log v03):
     - Before the AUD-023 fix, compare_state's WalletCheck arm was `CheckOutcome::of(detection.passes_wallet_check(passphrase)?)`, so a wallet-check match was possible.
     - matched_lines had a `Choice::WalletCheck => Some(wallet_check_line())` arm (old :444). The fix removed it.
     - match_limit (old :468-479) is unchanged at b6fca69 (:595-606).
  
  4. Reduced-cost tests:
     - `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target cargo test --locked --lib a_wallet_check_leaves_a_phrase_made_with_it_not_verified_and_never_confirms_a_rekey` passes (log v04). It asserts NotVerified for the right password and DoesNotMatch otherwise.
     - `cargo test --locked --bin mhfe check::tests` passes (log v05). The CLI's table is tested only against itself.
- **Expected behavior:** - CORE-14 (code-core.instructions.md:112-115, Check: review): "Each question is answered by the type that owns the data: ... a reference says whether it identifies a wallet ... Callers ask them instead of deciding again."
  - CORE-10 (:84-95): every rule and message has exactly one source, and everything else calls it.
  - Workspace AGENTS.md:42: all logic in library modules, which every front end calls.
  - FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE CHECK-ARC-002: "A helper formerly needed must either participate in the active path or be removed if its behavior is now owned elsewhere."
  - FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE CHECK-ARC-003: review impossible states.
- **Observed behavior:** - The CLI decides from its Choice enum which references prove the wallet: passed_lines :555-563 and its doc :540-541, match_limit :595-606, and the prose of not_verified_reason :513-519. It never asks Reference::identifies_wallet.
  - That table already lags the library. Since the AUD-023-FUN002 fix the library never gives a match for a wallet-check reference (rehearsal.rs:520-527), but match_limit keeps an unreachable Choice::WalletCheck arm (:604) describing such a match.
  - The CLI test (:763-784) checks the CLI's table only, so nothing ties it to the library's predicate.
- **Impact:** - No wrong output today. Every reachable claim line and limit agrees with the library.
  - A new reference kind, or a change to what identifies the wallet or what a reference can match, must be made both in the library and in the CLI's Choice tables. Nothing fails when they differ. The library's FUN002 change has already left the CLI with a stale, unreachable row.
  - A future divergence could make `mhfe check` print "the receiving address of the wallet" or "the master key fingerprint of the wallet" for a reference the library does not treat as identifying, or leave out a match's limit.
  - This is maintainability and drift risk only: low under AUDIT_STANDARD.md.
- **Evidence:** Logs in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/mhfe/docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-check-reference-table/, each with a .command.json beside it:
  - v01-grep-identifies-wallet.log: no identifies_wallet in src/bin/mhfe. Lists the Choice::WalletCheck sites and match_limit's only caller (check.rs:454).
  - v02-static-trace.log: numbered excerpts of check.rs:183-195, 276-284, 384-400, 410-457, 536-606, 624-643, 652-671; rehearsal.rs:326-333, 410-417, 440-470, 473-487, 507-531; suite.rs:101-105.
  - v03-fun002-fix-history.log:
    - match_limit before 253ca3c (old :468-479) and at b6fca69 (:595-606), identical;
    - the old matched_lines WalletCheck arm (old :444, removed by the fix);
    - the old compare_state WalletCheck arm, CheckOutcome::of(pass) at old rehearsal.rs:377-380.
  - v04-lib-wallet-check-never-matches.log: the library test passes (1 passed), with reduced cost.
  - v05-cli-claim-table-test.log: the 3 check::tests of the CLI pass.
  
  The proposer's log: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-commands/g08-code-excerpts.log.
  
  The baseline b01-check-fast.log runs the full test suite.
- **Recommended fix:** - Carry the reference's verdict into the result. Give Compared the reference's identifies_wallet(), or let the library's CheckEvidence expose which reference matched and whether it identifies the wallet. Have passed_lines add the "... of the wallet" line only when that is true; the kind decides only the label.
  - Move "what a match does not prove" into the library beside own_checks_passed, as an evidence fact that both front ends render. Otherwise derive it from identifies_wallet().
  - Remove the unreachable Choice::WalletCheck arm of match_limit, or make match_limit take an outcome that cannot express a wallet-check match.
  - Consider replacing Choice with the library's ReferenceTarget kinds, so the CLI keeps no copy of the reference kinds.
- **Required verification:** - A CLI unit test that, for every Reference kind, binds the "of the wallet" claim line and the match limit to Reference::identifies_wallet() and to the outcomes the library can give.
  - `grep -rn "Choice::WalletCheck => Some(\"It does not prove" src/bin/mhfe` finds nothing.
  - The library test a_wallet_check_leaves_a_phrase_made_with_it_not_verified_and_never_confirms_a_rekey still passes.
  - `cargo test --locked --bin mhfe check::tests` passes.
  - The terminal suite's check cases, fast mode, give the same output.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-FUN002, AUD-023-ARC016
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 by a static trace, the commit history and reduced-cost tests.
  
  1. Nothing in src/bin/mhfe calls Reference::identifies_wallet (v01). passed_lines (check.rs:542-579) and match_limit (:595-606) decide from the CLI's own Choice enum which reference proves the wallet. The doc comment at :540-541 restates the library's rule. CORE-14 uses this exact question as its example: a reference says whether it identifies a wallet.
  
  2. match_limit's Choice::WalletCheck arm (:604) can never run:
     - Choice::WalletCheck comes only from ask_for_choice (:642). It becomes Reference::WalletCheck (:339-340, :353).
     - Compared::with (:665) calls RecoveredForCheck::compare (rehearsal.rs:414-416). That calls refuse_impossible, which refuses a same-length container (:458-460, holds_full_state is suite 3 only), and then compare_state.
     - compare_state's WalletCheck arm (rehearsal.rs:520-527) returns only NotVerified or DoesNotMatch.
     - match_limit is called only in report's Matches arm (:427, :454).
  
  3. History (v03): before 253ca3c, compare_state returned CheckOutcome::of(pass), so a wallet-check match was possible. The AUD-023-FUN002 fix removed the WalletCheck arm from matched_lines but left the one in match_limit. The CLI table therefore did not follow the library's rule change.
  
  Library and CLI tests pass (v04, v05), so today's output is correct and the impact is maintainability only, which is low under AUDIT_STANDARD.
  
  The CORE-14 half alone would be borderline, because the labels for an address and a fingerprint differ by kind anyway. The dead arm shows that drift has already happened.
  
  This is not a duplicate. The AUD-023-ARC016 secondary instance covered which own checks to list, now fixed by own_checks_passed. No already confirmed AUD-024 finding covers the Choice-keyed wallet-proof table.
  
  Not covered: the browser package's rendering of check evidence. The finding is limited to the native CLI.

##### AUD-024-ARC030 — Low — Two output helpers of the command-line tool exist twice. style::fact_wrapped has the same body as style::fact (through fact_as), and its doc still says fact does not wrap. Two write_control functions write the same raw control sequence: choice::write_control returns write errors, and terminal/private_screen.rs has its own copy that discards them.

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: output layer (src/bin/mhfe/style.rs, choice.rs, terminal/private_screen.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-10, CORE-22, CORE-19, CHECK-ARC-002
- **Affected files and builds:** Fact helpers:
  - src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:108-111: fact calls fact_as(Kind::Fact, label, value).
  - style.rs:113-121: fact_as runs fact_lines(label, &value.to_string()), then flow::keep(kind, &lines), then write_lines(&lines). Its wrap comment at :116 cites AUD-023-UI007.
  - style.rs:142-149: fact_wrapped runs the same three statements for a &str. Its doc at :142-143 is stale: "[`fact`] for a value that may be longer than a line: wrapped to the text width under its own column."
  - style.rs:151: the doc of fact_lines is stale: "The lines of [`fact_wrapped`]".
  - 10 call sites of style::fact_wrapped in 6 files: container_repair.rs:514 and :550, encrypt.rs:203 and :205, new_wallet.rs:187 and :188, rekey.rs:437 and :447, self_test.rs:337, wallets.rs:120.
  
  write_control copies:
  - src/bin/mhfe/choice.rs:432-438: pub fn write_control(sequence: &str) -> Result<(), Failure> passes the error on with `?`. It is used by choice.rs:165, :172, :177, :180, menu.rs:97, :209, :227, settings.rs:297 and terminal.rs:332.
  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal/private_screen.rs:200-204: fn write_control(sequence: &str) runs `let _ = terminal.write_all(...)` and `let _ = terminal.flush()`. It is used at :82 (enter_if), :105 (clear), :164 (Drop), :177 (enter_steps), :190 (clear_screen) and :196 (leave_private_screen).
  - At :82-83 and :177-178, PRIVATE_SCREEN_ACTIVE is set whether or not the switch was written.
  - The parent module src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs already imports crate::choice (:18) and calls choice::write_control (:332).
  - Neither copy has a 'deliberate copy' marker.
  
  Affects the native mhfe binary on every platform. The WASM package is not affected.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, run the kept harness: bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-dup-output-helpers/dup_output_helpers.sh. It reads the commit with git show. It prints the cited lines and the 10 call sites, then PRESENT for D1 to D5:
  - D1: fact (fact_as with Kind::Fact) and fact_wrapped run the same statements once normalised.
  - D2: 253ca3c added the AUD-023-UI007 wrap to fact_as and left the body of fact_wrapped byte-identical.
  - D3: the doc of fact_wrapped still presents it as the wrapping variant of fact.
  - D4: there are two `fn write_control(sequence: &str)`. The private-screen copy has two `let _ = terminal` lines, and terminal.rs calls choice::write_control.
  - D5: no 'deliberate copy' marker.
  It ends with '5 of 5 parts present', 'DEFECT REPRODUCED' and exit 1.
  
  The earlier role's harness shows the same: bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-cli-infra/static_evidence.sh, section S3.
- **Expected behavior:** - CORE-10 (code-core.instructions.md:84-95, Check: copies, review): every rule, check, conversion or message has one source. 'Before writing one, search the repository for an existing one ... and use it, extending it where needed.' 'Two blocks that differ only in a value become one function with a parameter.' A copy is allowed only with a 'deliberate copy' comment, a reason, and a test that keeps both copies in step.
  - CHECK-ARC-002 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md): inconsistent helper implementations. 'A helper formerly needed must either participate in the active path or be removed if its behavior is now owned elsewhere.'
  - CORE-22 (code-core.instructions.md:165-171, Check: review): 'Every error is handled or passed on; none is swallowed.'
  - CORE-19 (code-core.instructions.md:148-151, Check: review): 'Update or remove a comment when the code it describes changes.'
- **Observed behavior:** - Since the AUD-023-UI007 fix (253ca3c), style::fact and style::fact_wrapped give the same output for the same text: same wrapping, same flow::keep(Kind::Fact) and same write_lines. Ten call sites still use fact_wrapped, whose doc presents it as the variant of fact that wraps. The docs of fact_wrapped and fact_lines describe the code as it was before the fix.
  - The raw write of a cursor-control sequence to standard error is implemented twice. The private-screen copy, which enters, clears and leaves the alternate screen, discards both io errors with `let _`, with no comment giving a reason. The terminal module that contains it already calls choice::write_control, which passes the error on.
  - enter_if (:82-83) and enter_steps (:177-178) set PRIVATE_SCREEN_ACTIVE after the write whether or not it succeeded. After a failed switch the tool goes on as if the alternate screen were active, and the failure is never reported.
  - The copies gate (scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs) does not report either copy, at its default 50 tokens or at 20 tokens: both are below its threshold, so only review catches them.
- **Impact:** Mainly a maintenance risk. Callers choose between helpers that differ only in name (fact or fact_wrapped) or in error handling (the two write_control functions). A later fix to one copy can miss the other, as happened when the AUD-023-UI007 wrap went into fact_as only and left fact_wrapped behind. A failed alternate-screen switch is swallowed: enter_if and enter_steps still record the private screen as active, and the failure is never reported. In practice a failing standard error usually also makes the next anstream eprintln! panic (a separate, already confirmed finding), so the observable effect is bounded. Low severity (AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a limited maintainability defect with bounded practical impact).
- **Evidence:** All paths are relative to the repository root.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dup-output-helpers/v03-dup-output-helpers.log (+ .command.json, exit 1): the kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-dup-output-helpers/dup_output_helpers.sh at b6fca69. D1 to D5 PRESENT, '5 of 5 parts present', 'DEFECT REPRODUCED'. The normalised bodies of fact_as and fact_wrapped are both 'letlines=fact_lines(label,VALUE);if!flow::keep(KIND,&lines){write_lines(&lines);}}'.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dup-output-helpers/v01-dup-helpers.log (exit 0): an earlier scratch run of the same checks. It also shows that node scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs passes (exit 0) and reports neither copy, and that a 20-token run reports neither copy either.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-infra/g06-static-evidence.log, S3: 'PRESENT: S3 fact_wrapped has fact's body'.
  - git show 253ca3c -- src/bin/mhfe/style.rs: fact_as gains the fact_lines and write_lines wrap with the AUD-023-UI007 comment, and fact_wrapped is not touched. Its body is the same in 253ca3c^ and b6fca69.
  - Checked and set aside: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dup-output-helpers/v02-search-fact-width.log. A third fact writer, style::fact_before_work (style.rs:124-130), does not wrap, and a refusal probe stopped before any Argon2 round shows an 88-column 'Search' line. style::wrap never breaks a word, though, so style::fact would print that path at 88 columns too. No output divergence is shown, and v02 is not evidence of this finding.
- **Recommended fix:** - Remove style::fact_wrapped and call style::fact at its 10 call sites. Update the doc of fact_lines, which now serves fact.
  - Keep one write_control: choice::write_control, or a single terminal-level helper that returns the error. Make private_screen.rs call it.
  - In PrivateScreen::enter_if, clear and enter_steps, either pass the error on (refuse to show a secret when the switch to the alternate screen failed) or report it.
  - In Drop and leave_private_screen, which cannot pass an error on, ignore it explicitly, with a comment that says why (CORE-19, CORE-22).
  - Set PRIVATE_SCREEN_ACTIVE only after the switch has been written.
- **Required verification:** 1. bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-dup-output-helpers/dup_output_helpers.sh with COMMIT set to the fix commit prints DEFECT NOT REPRODUCED and exits 0.
  2. git grep shows no fact_wrapped, and a single `fn write_control` in src/bin/mhfe.
  3. The clippy, code-rules and copies gates pass (scripts/check-fast.sh).
  4. The terminal suite's fast cases still pass with unchanged fact output.
  5. Optional: a unit test in which a failing writer makes the private-screen switch report its error and leave PRIVATE_SCREEN_ACTIVE unset.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-UI007
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and reproduced the defect with a static trace, git show of the AUD-023 fix commit, and a kept harness (exit 1, 5 of 5 parts present).
  
  (1) style::fact (style.rs:109-111) calls fact_as(Kind::Fact, ...) (115-121). That runs fact_lines, then flow::keep, then write_lines. style::fact_wrapped (144-149) runs the same three statements for a &str. Commit 253ca3c (the AUD-023-UI007 fix) added the wrap to fact_as and left fact_wrapped unchanged, so the two now have the same body. The doc of fact_wrapped (142-143) still says it is the wrapping variant of fact. The doc of fact_lines (151) still calls it 'The lines of [`fact_wrapped`]'.
  
  (2) There are two `fn write_control(sequence: &str)`. choice.rs:433-438 returns the io error. terminal/private_screen.rs:200-204 discards both the write_all and the flush error with `let _`. Its parent module terminal.rs already imports choice (line 18) and calls choice::write_control (line 332). Neither copy has a 'deliberate copy' marker. The copies gate reports neither copy, at its default 50 tokens or at 20 tokens.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  - fact_wrapped has 10 call sites in 6 files, not 11.
  - The claim that secrets are then 'shown on whatever screen is current' is stronger than the evidence. What holds is narrower: enter_if (82-83) and enter_steps (177-178) set PRIVATE_SCREEN_ACTIVE whether or not the switch was written, and the failure is never reported. A failed write to standard error would usually also make the next anstream eprintln! panic (a separate, already confirmed finding).
  
  I also checked the third fact writer, style::fact_before_work (124-130). It does not wrap. A refusal probe gave an 88-column 'Search' line before any Argon2 round (v02). But style::wrap never breaks a word, so style::fact would print that 75-character path at 88 columns too. That probe shows no output divergence, so it is not part of this finding.
  
  None of the confirmed findings covers duplicate output helpers, and no AUD-023 finding covers these copies, so this is not a duplicate. Severity stays low: a maintainability defect with bounded practical impact (AUDIT_STANDARD.md).

##### AUD-024-ARC031 — Low — The progress bar names each stage from round numbers instead of the Stage the library reports: mhfe encrypt drops the library's Stage, and the rekey and the self-test renumber their rounds to fit the bar's arithmetic

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: progress bar (src/bin/mhfe/terminal/progress.rs) and its callers
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-10, CORE-14, CORE-01
- **Affected files and builds:** Native CLI build (all targets). src/bin/mhfe/terminal/progress.rs:129-137 (fn stage: (ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS, round) if round <= ROUNDS => "Encrypting"; (ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS, _) => "Checking"; _ => single), called at :58 from round_starts (:57). The rule is restated in the doc comments at :13-14, :55-56 and :129-130. Callers that receive the library's Stage and drop it or renumber for that arithmetic: src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:261 (`&mut |_, round, rounds|` in show_sealing, used by mhfe encrypt, mhfe new and mhfe rekey); src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:420-422 (`progress(stage, round - ROUNDS, ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS)`, renumbering the library's rounds 13-36 of 36); src/bin/mhfe/self_test.rs:302-312 (Stage::Recover rounds 13-24 of 24 renumbered to `round - ROUNDS` of ROUNDS at :309, because passing them as reported would draw a "Checking" bar). Library sources of the rule and of the Stage: src/operation.rs:1-4 (module doc: each round is reported with its stage 'so that a front end can show a bar for each stage'), :14-27 (enum Stage), :40-48 (StageCallback), :233-259 (Encryption::run: Stage::Encrypt for rounds 1-12, Stage::Check for 13-24); src/mhfe.rs:341 and :370 (round numbering of encrypt and check); src/self_test.rs:100-123 and :474-475 (Encrypt 1-12 then Recover 13-24 of 24); src/rekey.rs:313-336 (seal counted after round 12 of 36).
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-cli-derived-facts/run.sh b6fca69238344dd2525b06270ee6ff3b055e68c1 <work dir>. The harness copies fn stage verbatim from progress.rs at the commit into a small Rust program, with ROUNDS read from src/suite.rs and ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS = 2 * ROUNDS (src/mhfe.rs:32). It feeds the program the rounds exactly as the library reports them with their Stage and counts the rounds whose bar name differs from the reported stage. It then checks the caller lines encrypt.rs:261, rekey.rs:422 and self_test.rs:309 at the commit. No Argon2 and no cargo build are run.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-10 (code-core.instructions.md): 'Every rule, check, validation, limit, constant, conversion, message, list of answers and data shape has exactly one source, and everything else calls or imports it'. CORE-14: 'Each question is answered by the type that owns the data ... Callers ask them instead of deciding again from word counts or literals.' CORE-01: front ends 'only translate input and output, and call the library'. The library already answers which stage a round belongs to: src/operation.rs:1-4 and :40-48 report a Stage before every round 'so that a front end can show a bar for each stage'. The bar should therefore name its stage from that Stage, or from a stage the caller names for the 12-round operations whose ProgressCallback carries none. It should not re-derive the stage from round arithmetic.
- **Observed behavior:** progress.rs:131-137 decides the stage from (rounds, round) alone. Fed the library's reports as they are (log v01-derived-facts): Encryption::run (Encrypt 1-12, Check 13-24 of 24) names all 24 rounds as the library does. SelfTest::replay names 12 of 24 rounds differently (library Recover round 13 of 24 becomes bar "Checking"). Rekey::seal names 24 of 24 differently (library Encrypt round 13 of 36 becomes bar "Recovering"). That is 36 mismatching rounds in total. The bars on screen are right only because: encrypt.rs:261 discards the Stage it is given; rekey.rs:422 renumbers the seal's rounds to 1-24 of 24; self_test.rs:309 renumbers the recovery to 1-12 of 12. No unit test covers fn stage, and the terminal suite only waits for the text "Encrypting" (scripts/terminal_suite/passwords.py:235).
- **Impact:** Maintenance only; no wrong output today. The rule that an encryption encrypts in rounds 1-12 and checks in rounds 13-24 has a second copy in the CLI, and every caller must know it and renumber for it. Suppose the library changes how a long operation is split into stages, for example a 24-round operation that is not encrypt plus check (as the self-test already is), or a rekey shown as one 36-round operation. Then the bar shows the wrong stage name, and no test fails. Low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a maintainability defect with bounded practical impact.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-cli-derived-facts/v01-derived-facts.log with v01-derived-facts.command.json (exit 1). The log shows 'SelfTest::replay as reported: 12 of 24 rounds named differently, first: library Recover round 13 of 24 -> bar "Checking"', 'Rekey::seal as reported: 24 of 24 rounds named differently, first: library Encrypt round 13 of 36 -> bar "Recovering"' and PRESENT for encrypt.rs:261, rekey.rs:422 and self_test.rs:309. Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-cli-derived-facts/run.sh and README.md; probe sources were built in tmp/aud024/verify-cli-derived-facts/. The first reviewer's log is docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-infra/g06-static-evidence.log (S6 PRESENT). Static reads at b6fca69: progress.rs:13-16, :55-58, :129-137; encrypt.rs:241-264; rekey.rs:262-282 and :406-426; self_test.rs:285-315; src/operation.rs:1-75, :233-260; src/self_test.rs:95-123, :465-478; src/rekey.rs:205-336; src/mhfe.rs:29-32, :335-372. Callers without a Stage (ProgressCallback): decrypt.rs:193-199, check.rs:370-376, wallets.rs:95-97, container_search.rs:456-466.
- **Recommended fix:** Let Progress::round_starts take the stage to show. Encrypt, rekey and self-test pass the library's Stage, mapped to a bar name in one place, for example a match on Stage::Encrypt/Check/Recover. The 12-round operations whose ProgressCallback carries no Stage (decrypt, check, wallets, container search) pass Stage::Recover or their own single name. Then remove fn stage and the renumbering in rekey.rs:420-422 and self_test.rs:302-312, keeping only a per-stage round counter in the bar if a 1-12 count per stage is wanted. Add a unit test that drives the bar with the library's reported (Stage, round, rounds) sequences for an encryption, a rekey seal and the self-test.
- **Required verification:** progress.rs holds no arithmetic that maps round numbers to stage names. encrypt.rs, rekey.rs and self_test.rs pass the library's Stage and do not renumber rounds to choose a stage. The harness's Part 1 reports no mismatching rounds (or is replaced by a unit test over the library's reported sequences). The terminal suite still shows Encrypting, Checking and Recovering bars for encrypt, rekey and self-test --vectors; the last needs a full-cost run that the coordinator must schedule.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC009
- **Verification:** confirmed: I confirmed the core defect with a static trace and a probe, narrowed it to one root cause and corrected its fields.
  
  Part 1, the progress bar stage, is reproduced. At b6fca69 the private fn stage in src/bin/mhfe/terminal/progress.rs:129-137 names a stage from round arithmetic:
  - rounds == ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS and round <= ROUNDS gives "Encrypting";
  - rounds == ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS otherwise gives "Checking";
  - anything else gives the caller's single name.
  
  This restates the library's rule (src/operation.rs:233-259, src/mhfe.rs:341 and :370). It ignores the Stage the library reports through StageCallback, which src/operation.rs:1-4 and :40-48 say exists so a front end can show a bar for each stage.
  
  I copied fn stage verbatim from the commit into a probe and fed it the rounds exactly as the library reports them. Encryption::run is named correctly. SelfTest::replay comes out wrong for 12 of 24 rounds: library Recover round 13 of 24 becomes bar "Checking". Rekey::seal comes out wrong for 24 of 24 rounds: library Encrypt round 13 of 36 becomes "Recovering". The bars on screen are right today only because:
  - encrypt.rs:261 drops the Stage;
  - rekey.rs:422 renumbers to round - ROUNDS of ENCRYPTION_ROUNDS;
  - self_test.rs:309 renumbers the recovery to round - ROUNDS of ROUNDS.
  
  No unit test covers fn stage. The terminal suite only waits for "Encrypting" (scripts/terminal_suite/passwords.py:235).
  
  Correction: the candidate said the library reports a Stage for every round. That is not true. Mhfe::decrypt, recover_for_check, the hidden-wallet open and the container search report through ProgressCallback (round, rounds) with no Stage (src/mhfe.rs:29). So the fix cannot only forward the library's Stage: those 12-round callers must name their stage themselves.
  
  Part 2, the benchmark's argon2_engine (src/bin/mhfe/test_tools.rs:350-361), is reproduced but is a separate root cause. Its fix and module differ, and FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE section 14 says to keep independent root causes separate. I removed it from this finding. It should be filed on its own, low ARC under CORE-10. The function runs its own is_x86_feature_detected!("ssse3") at :354, copying the engine's processor_has_ssse3 (src/engine/native.rs:32-39). That function is pub(super), so the binary cannot reach it. The function also restates build.rs's choice of ref.c on targets other than x86-64 (build.rs:116-117) and types "4 threads" three times (:355, :357, :360) beside LANES (src/engine.rs:11). The comment at :350-351 says the copy is chosen as the engine chooses, but there is no "deliberate copy" marker and no test keeping the two in step (CORE-10 exceptions). The same harness checks it (S2, 4 of 4 present).
  
  Part 3, src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:617-621, is moved to observations. It matches the Suite variant to choose the " (no built-in check)" display text. That translates a variant into text, as length_choice.rs:53-64 does. It does not decide again from word counts or literals, which is what CORE-14 names, so it is not a clear breach. The harness still records the code fact (S3).
  
  Not a duplicate: none of the confirmed findings or the AUD-023 findings covers the progress stages or the engine name. AUD-023-ARC009, about the fingerprint, is a related pattern only.

##### AUD-024-ARC032 — Low — The missing-word search decides whether a scan gap applies, and which gaps are valid, by restating the library's rules instead of asking ContainerSearch

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: search for missing container words
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-14, CORE-10, CHECK-ARC-001, CHECK-ARC-002
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool at b6fca69. The search runs in decrypt, check, rekey and wallets (RepairOption at decrypt.rs:26, check.rs:48, rekey.rs:41, wallets.rs:30) and in repair, when container words are typed as ? and the container's own wallet (address or fingerprint) is chosen.
  
  Primary: whether the gap applies is decided from a word count.
  - src/bin/mhfe/container_search.rs:288 `let two_missing = search.missing().len() > MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET;` decides at lines 289-293 whether the gap question is asked (ask_scan_gap) or DECOY_SCAN_GAP is used.
  - It repeats the private condition of ContainerSearch::decoy_address_limits at src/search.rs:119-125 (line 120: `if self.missing.len() > MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET`).
  - It is the negation of the public ContainerSearch::offers_wallet_search() at src/search.rs:201-203, which the same CLI file already calls for the same 'two words are missing' fact at container_search.rs:115.
  - The CLI uses MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET, the constant of the owner's-wallet search (src/search.rs:52), for a decoy-search decision.
  
  Secondary: the valid-gap range is restated.
  - src/bin/mhfe/container_repair.rs:209-211, scan_gap_parser: `range(1..=i64::from(SearchLimits::MOST))`.
  - src/bin/mhfe/container_search.rs:245 and 248-260, read_own_gap: `(1..=MOST_SCAN_GAP).contains(&gap)` at line 252.
  - Both repeat SearchLimits::new at src/wallet.rs:382-394 (line 383: `(1..=Self::MOST).contains(&count)`), which SearchLimits::first_account (wallet.rs:399) calls.
  - The library checks it again anyway at container_search.rs:294-300 through search.decoy_address_limits(scan_gap).
  - Neither copy carries a 'deliberate copy' marker or has a test that keeps it in step with the library.
- **Reproduction:** From the mhfe repository root at b6fca69:
  1. `python3 tmp/aud024/verify-scan-gap-arc/trace.py`: a static trace (path relative to the workspace /home/user/.../bip_tools). It prints src/search.rs:50-52, 113-125 and 198-203, src/wallet.rs:380-401, container_search.rs:109-119, 244-260 and 280-300, and container_repair.rs:205-211, and it finds each condition by pattern. It exits 1 and reports:
     - container_search.rs:288 restates search.rs:120;
     - container_search.rs:252 and container_repair.rs:210 restate the range at wallet.rs:383;
     - no 'deliberate copy' marker in either CLI file.
  2. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch>/target cargo test --locked --lib the_decoy_address_scope_narrows_for_two_missing_words` shows the library's own rule (one missing word gives SearchLimits::default(), two give first_account(gap), gap 0 is refused). It passes.
  3. Static fact: for every ContainerSearch, `search.missing().len() > MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET` equals `!search.offers_wallet_search()`, because missing() maps self.missing one to one (search.rs:104-106). The CLI could ask the type, and in the same file at line 115 it does.
- **Expected behavior:** - CORE-14 (code-core.instructions.md:112-115, Check: review): 'Each question is answered by the type that owns the data ... Callers ask them instead of deciding again from word counts or literals.' ContainerSearch owns the missing positions and the decoy narrowing, so the CLI should ask it whether a scan gap applies.
  - CORE-10 (code-core.instructions.md:84-95): 'Every rule, check, validation, limit ... has exactly one source, and everything else calls or imports it.' A front end that refuses early 'calls the library's rule or reads the library's values'. Any copy says 'deliberate copy' with its reason and has a test that keeps both in step.
  - CHECK-ARC-002 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md): duplicated logic and inconsistent helpers.
- **Observed behavior:** - The rule 'a scan gap narrows the decoy address search when more words are missing than the owner's-wallet search takes' is written twice: the library (search.rs:120) and the CLI (container_search.rs:288). The CLI's copy is a word-count comparison, although the library offers offers_wallet_search() and the CLI calls it 173 lines earlier in the same file.
  - The rule 'a gap is 1 to 2^31' is written three times: SearchLimits::new (wallet.rs:383), the --scan-gap clap parser (container_repair.rs:210) and read_own_gap (container_search.rs:252). Only the upper bound is imported from the library.
  - No copy is marked 'deliberate copy', and no test ties them to the library.
  - Behaviour is consistent at b6fca69. The terminal suite (scripts/terminal_suite/repair.py:240-263) checks that the gap is asked for two missing words, not that the CLI and library conditions agree.
- **Impact:** Maintainability only, with no current behavioural defect. If the library changes when it narrows the decoy search (for example, by tying it to MAX_MISSING_FOR_DECOY or another count), the CLI either asks a gap the library then ignores, or silently uses the default gap of 20 for a search that does take one, and no test notices. If the library changes the valid gap range, the CLI refuses or accepts gaps differently from the library and the browser package.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-scan-gap-arc/v01-static-trace.log (with .command.json): `python3 tmp/aud024/verify-scan-gap-arc/trace.py` gave exit 1, lists the three restatements and finds no 'deliberate copy' marker.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-scan-gap-arc/v02-library-narrowing-test.log (with .command.json): `cargo test --locked --lib the_decoy_address_scope_narrows_for_two_missing_words`, CARGO_TARGET_DIR set to the AUD-024 scratch target, gave exit 0 with 1 passed.
  - Reviewer's log: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-cli-commands/g08-code-excerpts.log, section 'F: container search restates the scan-gap rules'.
  - Not covered by AUD-023: its CHECK-ARC-001 entry (docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.md:180) passed the scan gap as library-owned, and no AUD-023 finding names decoy_address_limits, MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET or the CLI gap reader.
- **Recommended fix:** - Give ContainerSearch one public answer, for example `takes_scan_gap()` (true when the decoy address search narrows to the first account). Use it inside decoy_address_limits, and in with_container_wallet in place of `search.missing().len() > MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET`. Drop the CLI's import of MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET there. As a minimum, ask `!search.offers_wallet_search()` as line 115 already does.
  - Validate a gap only through the library. Make the --scan-gap value parser a custom parser that calls SearchLimits::first_account(gap) and maps its error to the clap message. In read_own_gap, call the same function (or search.decoy_address_limits) and retry on its error. Drop the restated `1..=MOST` ranges and MOST_SCAN_GAP's own check.
- **Required verification:** - A library unit test of the new answer: false for one missing word, true for two. Assert it agrees with decoy_address_limits (SearchLimits::default() vs first_account).
  - A CLI unit test that the --scan-gap parser refuses 0 and 2^31+1 and accepts 1 and 2^31, with the library's refusal.
  - The terminal-suite repair cases in scripts/terminal_suite/repair.py: two missing words ask 'How far does the wallet go?', a typed 0 is asked again, 30 states '0-1/0-29, 60 addresses', and one missing word asks no gap.
  - A re-run of the static trace showing no restated condition.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and they match. The CLI decides whether the decoy scan gap applies with its own word-count condition. At src/bin/mhfe/container_search.rs:288 it writes `search.missing().len() > MAX_MISSING_FOR_WALLET`, which repeats the private condition of ContainerSearch::decoy_address_limits (src/search.rs:120). It is also exactly the negation of the library's public ContainerSearch::offers_wallet_search() (src/search.rs:201-203), and the same file already calls that method for the same 'two words are missing' fact at line 115. So one CLI file asks the owning type in one place and decides again from a word count in another. CORE-14 rules this out in so many words ('Callers ask them instead of deciding again from word counts or literals'). It is also a second source of one rule under CORE-10.
  
  The gap range is a weaker, secondary variant. The --scan-gap parser (container_repair.rs:210) and read_own_gap (container_search.rs:252) both repeat the inclusive check `1..=MOST` of SearchLimits::new (src/wallet.rs:383). They import the library's MOST, but the lower bound and the check are written again, with no 'deliberate copy' marker and no test that keeps them in step.
  
  My static trace exits 1 and lists all three repeats (log v01). The library's own narrowing rule passes its reduced-cost unit test (log v02). Behaviour today is consistent, so the finding stays low: a maintainability defect with bounded impact (AUDIT_STANDARD.md, low). AUD-023's CHECK-ARC-001 passed the scan gap as owned by the library, and no AUD-023 finding covers this. It duplicates none of the confirmed findings listed.

##### AUD-024-ARC033 — Low — The closing summary of a new container (Format, Keep, Next) is written out again in mhfe new, where it differs from mhfe encrypt's only in two values

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Native CLI: summaries after a container is made
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-10, CHECK-ARC-002
- **Affected files and builds:** Native command-line tool, all builds, at b6fca69.
  - src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:195-212 (in the encrypt command's run) and src/bin/mhfe/new_wallet.rs:183-195 (in mhfe new) hold the same sequence:
    - flow.finish();
    - style::fact("Format", paint(MUTED, new.suite().id())), at encrypt.rs:197 and new_wallet.rs:184. The comment at encrypt.rs:196 says the specification asks for this line after a container is created.
    - let keep = new.keep(work, ...), at encrypt.rs:201 and new_wallet.rs:186;
    - style::fact_wrapped("Keep", &what_to_keep(&keep)), at encrypt.rs:203 and new_wallet.rs:187;
    - style::fact_wrapped("Next", &format!("rehearse with {} from the backup you wrote", paint(ACCENT, "mhfe check"))), at encrypt.rs:205-211 and new_wallet.rs:188-194;
    - style::more(readme::...), at encrypt.rs:212 and new_wallet.rs:195.
  - The only code differences are two values:
    - WalletPassphrase::Unknown (encrypt.rs:201) against WalletPassphrase::from(!passphrase.is_empty()) (new_wallet.rs:186);
    - readme::ENCRYPT (encrypt.rs:212) against readme::NEW (new_wallet.rs:195).
    The rest that differs is comments and the encrypt:: path qualifier.
  - src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:436-440 (print_summary, 430-449) writes the Format and Keep lines a third time, before its own Old backup and Next lines.
  - No 'deliberate copy' comment stands next to any of them.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69:
  1. node scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs --tokens 30
     This is read-only and below the gate's default of 50 tokens. Among others it reports:
     - "src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:194-201 = src/bin/mhfe/new_wallet.rs:182-186 (42 tokens)"
     - "src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:203-212 = src/bin/mhfe/new_wallet.rs:187-195 (38 tokens)"
     They are one block, split only by the differing keep line (encrypt.rs:201 / new_wallet.rs:186).
  2. node scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs (the default 50 tokens, as the copies gate runs it) prints "No copies of 50 tokens or more in 191 files of src/, web/, tests/, scripts/.", so the gate does not catch this copy.
  3. grep -rn '"Format"\|"Keep"\|from the backup you wrote\|deliberate copy' src/bin/mhfe/ shows the Format fact at encrypt.rs:197, new_wallet.rs:184 and rekey.rs:436, and the Keep fact at encrypt.rs:203, new_wallet.rs:187 and rekey.rs:438. The Next message literal is at encrypt.rs:208 and new_wallet.rs:191. No 'deliberate copy' comment is in the CLI.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-10 (.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md:84-95, Check: copies, review) says:
  - "Two blocks that differ only in a value become one function with a parameter; ... the same question, list of answers or message is built in one place."
  - An allowed copy says "deliberate copy" in a comment, gives the reason, and has a test that keeps both copies in step.

##### AUD-024-ARC036 — Low — What may follow a refused rekey confirmation, or a check whose detection found no verified length, is ruled by the WebAssembly binding, the page client and the command line, each in its own code. The library's Rekey::set_length and RecoveredForCheck::compare accept what every front end refuses, and after LENGTH_DIFFERS the library takes an owner confirmation at lengths the binding refuses.

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Ownership of rules / check and rekey sessions (library, WebAssembly binding, page client, CLI)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-002
- **Rules:** CORE-01, CORE-10, CORE-14
- **Affected files and builds:** Rekey variant. Library: src/rekey.rs:145-153. Rekey::set_length checks only that the container can have the length (container.require_length). src/rekey.rs:167-191: owner_lengths_after documents the rule ('After AmbiguousLength the owner states one of them; after LengthDiffers it is the stated length') but nothing holds a caller to it. src/rehearsal/reencryption.rs:148-191: RecoveredForRekey::confirm with Confirmation::Owner needs only one reading at the length. Binding: src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:296-315 (confirm_again) and :488-517 (owner_length). This is the only enforcement of the rule that the owner's length is one of owner_lengths and that it is 0 for every other kind. Its message prints the list with {:?}, as '[15]'. Client: web/client.js:1423-1447 (answerConfirmAgain) checks membership again, with its own default and message ('words must name the reading the owner compares: 15.'). CLI: src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:325-333 asks only among the lengths and defaults to the only one; the comment at :307-308 says this is the library's to say (AUD-017-ARC002). Check variant. Library: src/rehearsal.rs:411-417 (RecoveredForCheck::compare takes any reference). Binding: src/wasm_api/core/check.rs CheckSession.compare passes any reference through. Worker: web/core-worker.js:154-166 (when to ask: outcome notVerified and asksLength). Client: web/client.js:1380-1411 (NO_LENGTH_ANSWERS; answerNoLength refuses detection again at :1394-1396 and the wallet check at :1399-1401). CLI: src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:393-404 (its own trigger) and :686-718 (its own list of answers: 12 to 21 words is the built-in check, 24 words is an address or a fingerprint). Builds affected: the library API, the browser core module (dist/runtime/worker.js and mhfe.wasm, used without client.js), and every front end that would be written on them.
- **Reproduction:** All commands run from the repository root at b6fca69, reduced-cost Argon2 only (256 KiB, one pass; the 1 MiB known answer runs on the real build). (1) Binding: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-follow-up-rules v02-binding-follow-ups node --no-warnings ../tmp/aud024/verify-follow-up-rules/p-binding-follow-ups.mjs. It loads dist/runtime/worker.js (the baseline build, SHA-256 matching dist-SHA256SUMS) and calls the bindings directly. CheckSession is made with the public reduced-cost abandon container, a wrong password and { words: 0 }; after notVerified it accepts detection again and the wallet check. RekeySession is made with 15 stated words: recover('builtInCheck') gives LENGTH_DIFFERS, ownerLengths() is [15], confirmAgain('owner', words 18) is refused with INVALID_REQUEST and the rekey ends, and words 15 is accepted. (2) Library: make a scratch copy with git archive b6fca69 into ../tmp/aud024/verify-follow-up-rules/copy. Append the test shown in v00-probe-test-diff.log to the tests module of src/rekey.rs in that copy. Then, from the copy, run CARGO_TARGET_DIR=../tmp/aud024/target cargo test --locked --lib aud024_probe -- --nocapture. With ABANDON_12 and 15 stated, the refusal is LengthDiffers { stated: 15, found: 12 } and owner_lengths_after is Some([15]). set_length(12), set_length(18) and set_length(21) are Ok, and an owner confirmation then returns the 12-word reading awaiting the owner; only 24 is refused. With AMBIGUOUS_12_21 and 12 stated, the named lengths are [12, 21], and a stated 21 followed by the right fingerprint is a ReferenceMismatch. (3) Static trace of every cited line: v03-static-trace.log.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-01 (code-core.instructions.md): every rule, check and computation lives in a library module, and the command line, the WebAssembly bindings and the page only translate and call the library. CORE-10: the same question, list of answers or message is built in one place. A front end that refuses early calls the library's rule or reads its values. CORE-14: the type that owns the data answers the question. The library itself states the rekey rule in Rekey::owner_lengths_after's documentation (src/rekey.rs:167-175): after LENGTH_DIFFERS the owner states the stated length. The command line says at src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:307-308: 'Whether another confirmation may follow, and at which lengths the owner may give it, is the library's to say (AUD-017-ARC002)'. docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:207-216 and docs/API.md:1030-1034 document what may follow detection and confirmAgain's rule for words.
- **Observed behavior:** Rekey: the library documents the owner-length rule but does not enforce it. After LENGTH_DIFFERS (15 stated, 12 found), owner_lengths_after names [15], yet set_length plus an owner confirmation accepts 12, 18 and 21 (v01). The binding refuses 18 with INVALID_REQUEST 'the owner confirms a reading of [15] words here, not 18' and ends the rekey (v02). The client refuses it with its own TypeError, 'words must name the reading the owner compares: 15.', and its own only-length default. The CLI asks only among the list, with the same only-length default. The binding alone requires words to be 0 for non-owner kinds. In the library a stated length may come before a wallet reference and narrow its readings: AMBIGUOUS_12_21 with 21 set and the right 12-word fingerprint gives ReferenceMismatch, which ends a rekey (v01). Check: CheckSession.compare and RecoveredForCheck::compare accept detection again and the wallet check as the second comparison (v02, as in gb05). Only web/client.js refuses them. The CLI builds the same list of answers (a 12- to 21-word length with its built-in check, or 24 words with an address or a fingerprint) and its own trigger in check.rs. The worker has a separate trigger in core-worker.js.
- **Impact:** No wrong outcome or exposure of secrets: the library's confirm still shows the owner only a single reading, and the check comparisons return the library's correct evidence. The cost is maintainability, plus a difference in behaviour between the library and the binding. A program built on the library or on the core module alone (CORE-04), or a new front end, gets none of these refusals and has to write the rules again. The copies already differ: the library accepts owner lengths that the binding, client and CLI refuse, and the binding and the client word the same refusal differently ('[15]' versus '15').
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-follow-up-rules/v01-library-owner-lengths.log (reduced-cost library test, exit 0, PROBE lines), v00-probe-test-diff.log (the exact test added to the scratch copy; no other source differs), v02-binding-follow-ups.log (binding probe, exit 0), v03-static-trace.log (every cited range with line numbers at b6fca69). The probe script is at /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-follow-up-rules/p-binding-follow-ups.mjs. The candidate's own logs agree: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-browser/gb05-check-session-follow-up.log and gb14-follow-up-rule-locations.log. The baseline dist build is current: b12 and b14 exited 0, and the worker.js and mhfe.wasm SHA-256 values match dist-SHA256SUMS.
- **Recommended fix:** Move the rules into the library. For a rekey, add a Rekey method that states the owner's length after a refusal, for example Rekey::owner_states(recovered, refusal, Option<WordCount>). It refuses a length outside owner_lengths_after with a library error and message, gives the only length by default, and is the only way to change the length after recovery. set_length then becomes crate-private or is limited to before recovery, so that no stated length can come before a wallet reference after a refusal. For a check, give RecoveredForCheck a follow-up after detection, for example compare_after_detection(reference) or a CheckEvidence::asks_length() plus a typed answer. It refuses detection again and the wallet check, maps a 12- to 21-word length to its built-in check, and takes an address or a fingerprint for 24 words. The binding (owner_length, CheckSession), the worker trigger, client.js (answerNoLength, answerConfirmAgain) and the CLI (check.rs ask_length_after_detection, rekey.rs) then call these, and keep at most early refusals that read the library's values, each marked as a deliberate copy with a test.
- **Required verification:** Library unit tests: after LENGTH_DIFFERS (15 stated) an owner at 12, 18 or 21 is refused; outside owner_lengths_after a length is refused and the only length is the default; a stated length cannot come before a wallet reference after a refusal; a follow-up after detection refuses detection again and the wallet check and accepts a 12- to 21-word length, an address and a fingerprint. Rerun the binding probe p-binding-follow-ups.mjs: CheckSession refuses detection again and the wallet check, and RekeySession keeps refusing 18 with the library's error. Existing CLI terminal-suite cases and browser-suite cases for onNoLength and onConfirmAgain must pass unchanged.
- **Related findings:** AUD-017-ARC002, AUD-023-ARC010
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with reduced-cost probes. First, a library test in a scratch copy of the commit. The library's own documentation says that after LENGTH_DIFFERS the owner states the stated length (src/rekey.rs:167-175). In the test, Rekey::owner_lengths_after returns [15] after LENGTH_DIFFERS (15 stated, 12 found), yet Rekey::set_length followed by an owner confirmation still accepts 12, 18 and 21. The library also lets a stated length come before a wallet reference. Second, the binding: RekeySession.confirmAgain refuses owner length 18 with INVALID_REQUEST "the owner confirms a reading of [15] words here, not 18" and ends the rekey. web/client.js refuses it again in its own words, and the command line asks only among the listed lengths. So the binding is the only place that holds the rule, and it already behaves differently from the library. Third, CheckSession.compare accepts detection again and the wallet check after a detection that found no verified length. Only web/client.js:1394-1401 refuses them, and the command line builds the same list of answers in its own code (check.rs:686-718). No wrong outcome or secret exposure results, so this is a low-severity maintainability breach of CORE-01, CORE-10 and CORE-14. None of the already confirmed findings has this root cause. The deliberate-copy-marker finding covers other copies, and the dropped-passphrase finding is a different defect.
