Every file has docstring lines over 72, for example verify-hidden-input.py (114). The per-file table is in the log. Builds affected: none. This is source style only; packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py ships unchanged in the browser package. Nothing in the repository sets a Python line length: no pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, .flake8, tox.ini or .editorconfig, and the workspace's docs/adr has no Python decision. CORE-21 (/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md:158-161) sets 100 columns only for Prettier and cargo fmt. scripts/verify-code-rules.mjs checks only file length (CORE-15) for .py files.
- **Reproduction:** From the mhfe repository root, run `python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-pep8-lines/pep8-line-lengths.py b6fca69238344dd2525b06270ee6ff3b055e68c1`. The harness reads each tracked .py file outside docs/audits/ from the commit with git show, so the working tree does not affect it. It counts characters per line, finds comments with the tokenizer and docstrings with ast. It prints `TOTAL | 5898 | 1528 | 58 | 27 | 273 | 537 | 1 | 4` and exits 1. To spot-check one line, run `git show b6fca69:scripts/independent-suite3.py | sed -n 48p`. It is a 122-character sys.exit line.
- **Expected behavior:** TOOL-04 (/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/.github/instructions/code-tooling.instructions.md:24-27) says "Python follows PEP 8. Check: review." PEP 8's Maximum Line Length section limits all lines to 79 characters and comments and docstrings to 72. A team that agrees on it may raise the limit to at most 99, provided comments and docstrings are still wrapped at 72. The project's guide points to PEP 8 and sets no other Python width.
- **Observed behavior:** At b6fca69, of the 5,898 lines in the 20 Python files: 1,528 are over 79 characters, 58 over 99 and 27 over 100 (31 lines are exactly 100 characters). 273 comment-only lines and 537 docstring lines are over 72. Only 4 of the lines over 79 contain a URL. The code is wrapped at the repository's 100-column Prettier width, and a few lines go beyond it, up to 122. That breaks both PEP 8's default limit and its team maximum of 99, and no comment or docstring limit is kept.
- **Impact:** Style and maintainability only, with no runtime or security effect. It is a clear, repository-wide breach of a review-only rule that no gate checks, so new Python code will keep breaching it.
- **Evidence:** 1. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-pep8-lines/pep8-line-lengths-harness.log (sha256 6f72f0fd669382310cddc6cf7ba547f9ef00fbd116aa4bc34e60cc5b7daed025, exit 1) with its .command.json. It is the kept harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verifier-pep8-lines/ (pep8-line-lengths.py and README.md) run on commit b6fca69 and gives the per-file table and the totals above.
  2. docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-pep8-lines/pep8-lengths-at-b6fca69.log: the same probe run from the scratch copy, with the same totals.
  3. The candidate's own log, docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-tooling-other/pep8-line-lengths.log (sha256 70a4babe...), agrees on 1,528 and 58 and on the list of lines over 99.
  4. Spot checks with git show b6fca69:<file> | sed -n <n>p: independent-suite3.py:48 is 122 characters, :260 is 119; independent-suite4.py:174 is 117; verify-hidden-input-windows.py:10 is 116 (docstring), while :38 is 91; generate-published-rounds.py:104 is 106; mhfe-fast-mode.py:488 is 105; third-party-licenses.py:1 is 101.
  5. git ls-files shows no Python style configuration. grep finds no Python width in the coding guide, AGENTS.md or docs/adr. pycodestyle is not installed, so the count comes from the harness.
- **Recommended fix:** Either reformat the 20 Python files to 79 columns with comments and docstrings at 72, or have the owner record an agreed Python limit of at most 99 columns, with comments and docstrings at 72, in TOOL-04 and reformat to it. List the reformatting commit in .git-blame-ignore-revs (CORE-21). Then add a Python line-length check to scripts/verify-code-rules.mjs, with a self-test case like its CORE-15 one, so the rule is checked by a gate and not only in review.
- **Required verification:** The kept harness, or an equivalent, run at the fix commit reports no line over the agreed limit and no comment-only or docstring line over 72, and exits 0. verify-code-rules.mjs fails on a test .py file that has a line over the limit.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this on its own. I read the 20 tracked Python files outside docs/audits/ straight from commit b6fca69 with git show, so the working tree played no part. 1,528 of the 5,898 lines are over 79 characters and 58 are over 99, the same counts as the candidate. 27 lines are over 100, so the 100 columns Prettier uses elsewhere would not cover them either. 273 comment-only lines and 537 docstring lines are over 72. Only 4 of the lines over 79 contain a URL.
  
  TOOL-04 says "Python follows PEP 8. Check: review." PEP 8 limits lines to 79 characters. A team may agree on up to 99, but comments and docstrings must then still wrap at 72. The code breaks even that looser limit. No project rule overrides PEP 8 for Python. CORE-21's 100 columns applies only to Prettier and cargo fmt. There is no Python formatter configuration in the repository (no pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, .flake8 or .editorconfig), and the workspace ADRs record no Python decision. verify-code-rules.mjs checks only file length (CORE-15) for .py files.
  
  The task treats a clear breach of a review-only rule as a finding. This is one root cause: the Python is formatted to about 100 columns. It is not a duplicate of any confirmed finding or of any AUD-023 finding.
  
  I corrected the candidate in four places:
  - verify-hidden-input-windows.py: the 116-character line is :10, a docstring line. Line :38 is 91 characters.
  - The 72-character count: PEP 8's 72 covers comments and docstrings, so the right figures are 273 comment-only lines plus 537 docstring lines. The candidate's 276 counted comment tokens, inline ones included, and no docstrings.
  - Scope: the repository tracks 189 .py files. The 169 historical audit harnesses under docs/audits/ are excluded from the count.
  - Evidence: the probe is now kept as a harness that reads the commit, not the working tree.

##### AUD-024-ARC038 — Low — No test checks that a rehearsal check keeps a pass of the 16-bit check made with the empty passphrase, a case that AUD-023-FUN002's required verification names: a library whose evidence_of drops that pass passes every library, command-line and integration test

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Rehearsal check evidence (src/rehearsal.rs evidence_of / CheckEvidence::own_checks_passed) and its unit, self-check and browser tests
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-32, CORE-33
- **Affected files and builds:** Product code that is right but has no guard. src/rehearsal.rs:470-505 is evidence_of, with the 16-bit check at :495-499. Line :498 `other => Some(detection.source_check(other.passphrase().unwrap_or(""))?)` takes the empty passphrase for OwnChecks { passphrase: None } and for an address or fingerprint with "". src/rehearsal.rs:50-61 own_checks_passed lists PassedCheck::WalletCheck only for Some(true) (:57-59).
  
  Front ends that show this evidence:
  - src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:542-583 passed_lines (the 'phrase + passphrase check' line through own_checks_passed) and :698-701 ask_length_after_detection ('The 24-word reading passes the 16-bit check.').
  - src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:136-145: the browser check() evidence.passed and evidence.walletCheck.
  
  Tests that miss the case:
  - src/rehearsal.rs:623-656: an empty passphrase is asserted only as Some(false), at :653.
  - :659-713 and :721-783: Some(true) only with "TREZOR", at :675 and :755.
  - :786-823: wallet_check not asserted.
  - :828-849: hand-built evidence.
  - src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:57-63, :68-118 and :120-139: LENGTH_CASES compare outcome, built_in_check and matching_lengths, never wallet_check.
  - src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:818 and :833-840: hand-built evidence.
  - scripts/browser-check/rehearsal-checks.mjs:184-203 and :213-283: walletCheck is true only with TREZOR (:215-233) and false at :280.
  - scripts/browser-check/decrypt-checks.mjs:240-258: made.emptyChecked, built at encrypt-checks.mjs:230-237, is used only for decrypt(), not check().
  - The test phrase exists (src/test_support.rs:78-81 EMPTY_COUNTER; scripts/browser-check/page-values.mjs:28-29 EMPTY_CHECKED_PHRASE) but is used only at the detection and wallet_check level (src/detection.rs:219, src/wallet_check.rs:411).
  
  Builds affected: the library, the native command line (mhfe check), and the WebAssembly browser package (check() in both modes).
- **Reproduction:** Run from the repository root, all at reduced Argon2 cost (256 KiB, 1 pass); no full-size run is needed.
  
  1. The verifier's probe is a scratch script. It extracts b6fca69 with git archive and, depending on its mode, adds one test to src/rehearsal.rs's test module and/or the mutant. The test is probe_aud024_empty_passphrase_pass_keeps_its_evidence. It seals counted(EMPTY_COUNTER) ('abandon' x21 'absorb another spoil') in a 24-word container. It checks the container with Reference::OwnChecks { passphrase: None } and asserts NotVerified, wallet_check == Some(true) and own_checks_passed() == [WalletCheck]. It then checks with a fingerprint of the phrase and passphrase "", and asserts a match with wallet_check == Some(true). The mutant changes :498 to `Some(!passphrase.is_empty() && detection.source_check(..)?)`.
     - On the unchanged tree: `cargo test --locked --lib probe_aud024_` passes.
     - On the mutant: the same test fails.
     - On the mutant without the probe test: `cargo test --locked --lib`, `cargo test --locked --bin mhfe`, and `cargo test --locked --test suite3_vectors --test suite4_vectors` all pass. CARGO_TARGET_DIR is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/target.
  2. The kept harness reproduces step 1's mutant run: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/gap-1-aud023-required-verification-and-remediation-diff/fun002_empty_passphrase_evidence.sh <scratch> <cargo target> (prints NOT GUARDED and exits 1 at b6fca69).
- **Expected behavior:** AUD-023-FUN002 requiredVerification (docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.json), unit tests in src/rehearsal.rs: "The empty-passphrase 16-bit pass keeps its evidence." Its recommendedFix also says: "Keep the evidence line for the empty-passphrase 16-bit pass."
  
  The guarded behaviour is a specification MUST:
  - mhfe_spec/README.md:425-430 (at 3c97b66): every 24-word reading goes through the wallet check "with the BIP39 passphrase the user enters or the empty one", and "A pass is reported as 'passes the 16-bit check'".
  - :477-481: the rehearsal check reports "a pass of the 16-bit wallet check for a 24-word reading".
  
  Rules:
  - CORE-32 (Check: review): library unit tests cover "the edge cases a reviewer would ask about". A reviewer asked for this one by name.
  - CORE-33 (Check: review): a feature has its case in the browser regression suite, and a fix's test is seen failing before it.
- **Observed behavior:** At b6fca69 the library behaves correctly. The probe test passes on the unchanged tree (guard-clean.log: '1 passed').
  
  No existing test detects the loss of that behaviour. On the mutant the probe fails ('assertion `left == right` failed: detected length, no passphrase; left: Some(false), right: Some(true)'), but every existing test passes:
  - 'test result: ok. 360 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored' (lib)
  - 'test result: ok. 141 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored' (bin mhfe)
  - 'test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored' for each of tests/suite3_vectors.rs and tests/suite4_vectors.rs
  
  The five ignored tests are full-size runs, and the rehearsal self-check's LENGTH_CASES do not compare wallet_check. No browser or package check calls check() on a phrase that passes with the empty passphrase: the empty-checked container is used only for decrypt(), which reads the 16-bit check through RecoveredPhrase::passes_wallet_check, not evidence_of.
- **Impact:** A regression that hides a passing 16-bit check of a wallet made without a BIP39 passphrase would ship unnoticed in three places:
  - mhfe check's list of checks that passed, and the explanation over the length question after detection.

##### AUD-024-ARC039 — Low — Two release-tooling comments no longer describe their code: package-release.sh's comment on the files every archive carries sits 24 lines above add_common_files(), and remap-builder-paths.sh still says scripts/build-wasm.sh sources it, although since 253ca3c only scripts/bind-wasm.sh does

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Release and build scripts (comments)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-003
- **Rules:** CORE-19, CHECK-ARC-003
- **Affected files and builds:** - scripts/package-release.sh:39-41 (all builds that package-release.sh packs: the macOS release jobs and the canonical container build). The comment "Documents and licence texts that every archive carries. An archive that brings its own README.md ... gets the project overview as README-mhfe.md" describes add_common_files(). That function starts only at :65, and nothing documents it there. Between the comment and the function are the source-commit comment and code (:42-51, inserted by b6e65fb on 2026-10-01) and the provenance comment and code (:53-63, inserted by da4618d). So the block at :39-43 now reads as one comment about source_commit/source_state. In cc91b0b and b6e65fb~1 the comment sat directly above add_common_files().
  - packaging/remap-builder-paths.sh:1-4. The header says the helper is "Sourced, not run, by every build ...: packaging/Dockerfile.reproducible, scripts/package-release.sh, scripts/check.sh and scripts/build-wasm.sh". At b6fca69 scripts/build-wasm.sh does not source it: build-wasm.sh:40 runs `scripts/bind-wasm.sh wasm "$bindgen_dir"`. scripts/bind-wasm.sh:41 sources it, and bind-wasm.sh is not named. Commit 253ca3c (AUD-023 remediation) moved the sourcing from build-wasm.sh:60 to bind-wasm.sh and did not update the header. e949b01 then added header text at :23-24 whose truth depends on that list ("the scripts that source it set their own options") and also left the list as it was.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69:
  1. `awk 'NR>=36 && NR<=66' scripts/package-release.sh` shows the comment at :39-41, two other blocks, and `add_common_files() {` at :65.
  2. `git show b6e65fb~1:scripts/package-release.sh | sed -n 29,32p` shows the same comment directly above add_common_files() before the insertions.
  3. `grep -rn '\. packaging/remap-builder-paths.sh' scripts packaging` lists check-release-artifacts.sh:35, bind-wasm.sh:41, package-release.sh:26, check.sh:17, check-fast.sh:15 and Dockerfile.reproducible:103. build-wasm.sh is not in the list.
  4. `grep -n 'remap\|bind-wasm' scripts/build-wasm.sh` prints only line 40, which runs bind-wasm.sh.
  5. `git show 253ca3c~1:scripts/build-wasm.sh | grep -n remap` shows that build-wasm.sh sourced the helper at :60 before 253ca3c.
  6. `git show --stat 253ca3c -- packaging/remap-builder-paths.sh` shows that 253ca3c left the helper unchanged.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-19 (code-core.instructions.md, "Check: review"): "Update or remove a comment when the code it describes changes." CHECK-ARC-003 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md) asks the audit to review stale comments. A comment that explains a function sits on that function, and a list of the scripts that source a helper names the ones that do.
- **Observed behavior:** The archive-files comment describes a function 24 lines below it, past two unrelated blocks, and add_common_files() has no comment. The remap helper names build-wasm.sh as a script that sources it and leaves out bind-wasm.sh, the one script that sources it for the WebAssembly build.
- **Impact:** Maintainability only, with no runtime effect. A reader takes the README-mhfe.md rule as part of the source-commit logic, and finds no explanation at add_common_files(). Someone changing remap-builder-paths.sh, for example checking that every script that sources it sets its own shell options or runs under bash or dash as the header says, is sent to build-wasm.sh, which no longer sources it, and does not learn that bind-wasm.sh (used by build-wasm.sh and verify-single-modules.mjs) does.
- **Evidence:** Static probes, run through docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh from the repository root:
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-tooling-comments/static-probe.log (exit 0; probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-tooling-comments/probe.sh). It records HEAD b6fca69238344dd2525b06270ee6ff3b055e68c1, package-release.sh:36-66 with add_common_files() at :65, `git log -L39,43` (comment created in cc91b0b, the source-commit lines added below it in b6e65fb), the list of scripts that source the helper (bind-wasm.sh:41, not build-wasm.sh), and build-wasm.sh:40 running bind-wasm.sh.

It shows the comment directly above add_common_files() in cc91b0b (:28-31) and b6e65fb~1 (:29-32), separated by the source-commit block in b6e65fb and by the provenance block in da4618d. It also shows build-wasm.sh sourcing the helper at :60 in 253ca3c~1 and only calling bind-wasm.sh in 253ca3c, with 253ca3c touching bind-wasm.sh, build-wasm.sh and check-release-artifacts.sh but not the helper.
- **Recommended fix:** - Move the comment at scripts/package-release.sh:39-41 to sit directly above add_common_files() at :65, leaving the source-commit comment at :42-43 on its own block.
  - In packaging/remap-builder-paths.sh:1-4, replace scripts/build-wasm.sh with scripts/bind-wasm.sh (the WebAssembly build of build-wasm.sh and of verify-single-modules.mjs). Optionally also name scripts/check-fast.sh, or say the list covers only release and release-checked builds.

- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC003, Three Rust doc comments begin with a sentence that describes another, undocumented item (the AUD-023-ARC003 pattern, missed by that audit), and no check detects such joined doc blocks
- **Verification:** confirmed: I confirmed the candidate only in part and narrowed it to its one CORE-19 root cause: comments that were not updated when the code they describe changed.
  
  What I reproduced at b6fca69 (static-probe.log and history-probe.log):
  (1) The comment at scripts/package-release.sh:39-41 sat directly above add_common_files() in cc91b0b and in b6e65fb~1. b6e65fb inserted the source-commit block, and da4618d inserted the provenance block, between them. add_common_files() now starts at :65 and has no comment of its own.
  (2) Until 253ca3c~1, scripts/build-wasm.sh:60 sourced packaging/remap-builder-paths.sh. 253ca3c moved the sourcing to the new scripts/bind-wasm.sh:41, and build-wasm.sh:40 now only runs that script. The helper's header at :1-4 was not updated: it still names build-wasm.sh and does not name bind-wasm.sh. e949b01 later added text to that same header that depends on the list ("the scripts that source it set their own options") and still did not correct it.

  - The .gitignore:8 comment is incomplete, not wrong. It names one producer of bytecode for a general `__pycache__/` pattern, and independent-suite3.py does produce bytecode. That is an observation.
  - The Cargo.toml:106 and clippy.toml:5-6 part is a separate root cause and not a CORE-19 breach. At b6fca69 (committed 05:40 UTC) those comments matched the guide's own RUST-01 example, "threshold 100, CORE-15". The workspace guide changed CORE-15 and RUST-01 to 150 only in f09d363 at 06:51 UTC. handovers/README.md records the move as pending: "A repository already set to 100 moves to 150". The candidate's version of this part is also incomplete and partly wrong. It leaves out .oxlintrc.json:18-22, whose max-lines-per-function is also 100. Its arms for these codes are at 470 (HIDDEN_WALLET_PASSES_CHECK), 477-481 (EMPTY_PASSWORD, PASSWORD_TOO_LONG, INVALID_PASSWORD_UTF8, CONTROL_CHARACTER_IN_PASSWORD, UNASSIGNED_CHARACTER), 499 (PASSWORD_REPAIR_NOT_OFFERED), 502 (PASSWORDS_DIFFER) and 504 (PASSWORD_ALREADY_USED). The only checks of the list are a third hand-typed list in scripts/browser-check/client-checks.mjs:53-63, the behaviour checks of eight codes in scripts/browser-check/hidden-wallet-checks.mjs:58-147 (both run only by verify-browsers.mjs), and a two-code subset in scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs:96-97. Affected builds: the library in every build, and the browser package (feature browser-core) through its worker.

  (1) `sed -n 61,75p src/hidden.rs` shows nine string literals. `grep -n` over the code() arms in src/error.rs shows the same nine strings as match arms. `grep -rn KEEPS_SESSION_OPEN src` finds only the definition (hidden.rs:65) and its use at wasm_api/core.rs:81, with no test. `grep -ci 'deliberate copy' src/hidden.rs` gives 0. Logged as s01-literals-and-codes.
  (2) The copy is avoidable. A scratch crate depending on mhfe-experimental defines `const DERIVED: [&str; 9] = [MhfeError::PasswordAlreadyUsed.code(), MhfeError::HiddenWalletPassesCheck.code(), MhfeError::PasswordsDiffer.code(), MhfeError::PasswordRepairNotOffered.code(), MhfeError::EmptyPassword.code(), MhfeError::PasswordTooLong(0).code(), MhfeError::InvalidPasswordUtf8.code(), MhfeError::ControlCharacterInPassword.code(), MhfeError::UnassignedCharacter.code()]` and asserts that it equals HiddenWallets::KEEPS_SESSION_OPEN. Run it with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch>/target cargo test --offline --manifest-path <scratch>/verify-session-codes/Cargo.toml`: it compiles and passes, so there is no drift today (p01-derive-from-code).
  (3) No Rust test notices drift. Make a copy with `git archive b6fca69`, change hidden.rs:66 to "PASSWORD_ALREADY_USE" and hidden.rs:70 to "EMPTY_PASWORD", then run `cargo test --locked --offline --lib`. The result is 360 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (p03-mutant-all-lib-tests). The `hidden` filter alone gives 5 passed (p02).
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-10 (.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md:84-95, 'Check: copies, review') says: 'A value with a meaning (24 words, a list of lengths, a limit, an error code) is a named constant defined once; a value that follows from another is derived from it' (line 90). The only exceptions are 'a deliberate fast path, or a copy a build cannot avoid', and each must say "deliberate copy" in a comment with the reason and have 'a test [that] keeps both copies in step' (line 93). code() is a const fn, so the list can be derived from the variants at compile time (shown by probe p01). The v0.6.0 release note (docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:356-361) also presents KEEPS_SESSION_OPEN as part of 'Every rule has one source ... instead of their own copies'.
- **Observed behavior:** The nine codes are typed a second time as string literals in the library itself (src/hidden.rs:66-74). They have no deliberate-copy marker and no Rust test against MhfeError::code(). With two entries misspelt, every one of the 360 lib unit tests still passes. Drift would be caught only outside Rust:
  - The real-browser suite (verify-browsers.mjs) deepEquals the parameters with a third hand-typed list (client-checks.mjs:53-63).
  - The same suite triggers eight of the codes in a live session and then opens another wallet (hidden-wallet-checks.mjs:58-147). EMPTY_PASSWORD is never triggered in a session.
  - verify-browser-package checks only that PASSWORD_ALREADY_USED and HIDDEN_WALLET_PASSES_CHECK are included (core-operations.mjs:96-97).
  The baseline b20-browsers.log shows those browser checks passing at lines 27, 326 and 335-339. The doc comment at hidden.rs:62-64 also calls these 'the error codes of Self::open', but seven of them come from new_password_from in the binding (src/wasm_api/core/hidden.rs:62) before open runs.
- **Impact:** This is a maintainability defect with bounded impact, and there is no drift at b6fca69. Suppose an entry is misspelt, or a code is renamed in error.rs (the fixtures would flag the rename itself) and the list is not updated. Every Rust test and the fast checks pass. Only the real-browser suite, a run of about five minutes in CI and check.sh, catches it, and it does so through another hand-typed copy. If that suite is skipped, the worker ends the whole hidden-wallet session (web/core-worker.js:348) on a refusal that the documents say leaves it open (web/client.js:796-797; src/wasm_api/core/hidden.rs:47-50). Its Argon2 work area and passwords are freed, and the user must open the session again and type the main passphrase again. No secret is exposed and no wrong wallet is given. The candidate's claim that 'no test fail[s] for most of the nine codes' holds only for the Rust and package checks, not for the browser suite.
- **Evidence:** All under docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-session-codes/, each with its .command.json:
  - s01-literals-and-codes.log (exit 0): hidden.rs:61-75, the code() arms, the only uses of KEEPS_SESSION_OPEN, and the deliberate-copy marker count of 0.
  - s02-js-readers.log (exit 0): every reader of hiddenWalletRefusals and the client-checks.mjs hand copy.
  - p01-derive-from-code.log (exit 0): the const list derived from code() compiles and equals the literals.
  - p02-mutant-hidden-tests.log (exit 0): 5 passed with two misspelt entries.
  - p03-mutant-all-lib-tests.log (exit 0): 360 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored on the same mutant.
  The probe source is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-session-codes/src/lib.rs and the mutant tree is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-session-codes-mutant (git archive b6fca69 with hidden.rs:66 and :70 edited). The api-contracts harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/api-contracts/check-contracts.mjs:292-298 reports 'FAIL session-refusal-codes-from-the-library' (h01-check-contracts.log). The baseline b20-browsers.log, lines 27 and 326-339, shows the browser-side checks that do keep the list in step. The AUD-023 refutation of the same observation (AUD-023 JSON refutedCandidates[1]) was weighed: CORE-10 now names error codes explicitly as values that must be derived.
- **Recommended fix:** Derive the list from the variants, for example `pub const KEEPS_SESSION_OPEN: [&'static str; 9] = [MhfeError::PasswordAlreadyUsed.code(), ...]` (shown to compile). Better still, give MhfeError or HiddenWallets a classifier such as `fn keeps_hidden_session_open(&self) -> bool`, derive the list from it, and add a unit test that each listed code equals code() of its variant. Correct the doc comment so that it says the codes come from HiddenWallets::open and from building the password in the binding. Optionally extend the AUD-023-ARC011 check in scripts/package-check/manifest.mjs so that no file in src/ outside error.rs and the test modules types a code of MhfeError::code() as a literal.
- **Required verification:** 1. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch>/target cargo test --locked hidden` passes and includes the new test.
  2. The mutant from p03 (an entry misspelt or mapped to the wrong variant) fails at compile time or in a Rust test.
  3. check-contracts.mjs check session-refusal-codes-from-the-library passes.
  4. In verify-browsers.mjs, 'parameters gives every fixed value of the core' and the 'leaves the session open' checks pass.
  5. verify-browser-package.mjs passes.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC011
- **Verification:** confirmed: I confirm the CORE-10 breach at b6fca69, but the candidate overstates its impact, and I have corrected that below.
  
  **The breach.**
  - src/hidden.rs:65-75 types nine MhfeError codes again as string literals. Their one source is the arms of MhfeError::code() at src/error.rs:456-511 (lines 470, 477-481, 499, 502 and 504).
  - No "deliberate copy" marker is present: grep -ci finds 0 in src/hidden.rs.
  - No Rust code reads the list except src/wasm_api/core.rs:81, so no Rust test keeps it in step.
  - The copy is avoidable. My probe crate builds the same [&str; 9] in a const item from MhfeError::X.code(). It compiles, and it equals the literals today (p01).
  - A mutant copy of b6fca69 misspells two entries (PASSWORD_ALREADY_USE and EMPTY_PASWORD). All 360 reduced-cost lib unit tests still pass on it (p03).
  
  **What the candidate got wrong.** It says no test fails for most of the nine codes. That is not true of the whole repository:

  - It also triggers eight of the codes in a live session and then opens another wallet (scripts/browser-check/hidden-wallet-checks.mjs:58-147). Only EMPTY_PASSWORD is not triggered there. The baseline b20-browsers.log shows these checks passing at lines 27, 326 and 335-339.
  - verify-browser-package checks two of the codes (core-operations.mjs:96-97).
  - The codes themselves are pinned to code() by the fixtures and the known answers.
  
  So drift would be caught by the slow browser suite in CI, through a hand copy, and never by Rust or the fast checks. The practical impact is bounded, which makes this a low maintainability defect.
  
  **Why it is a finding now.** AUD-023 refuted the same observation as info, under AGENTS.md wording. AUD-024 applies CORE-10, which is marked "Check: copies, review". Its line 90 names "an error code" explicitly and says a value that follows from another is derived from it. Line 93 requires a marker and a test for any deliberate copy, and allows a copy only where a build cannot avoid it. That makes this a clear breach of a review rule, and the copies gate does not see it.
  
  **Not a duplicate.** The confirmed deliberate-copy finding covers only copies in web/ (v-arc-deliberate-copy/markers.log), not src/hidden.rs. AUD-023-ARC011's fix added a check that bindings type no codes (scripts/package-check/manifest.mjs:78-89), but that check reads only src/wasm_api and only whole_number calls.

##### AUD-024-ARC042 — Low — The public memory API builds a LockedText from any lock guard, so a LockedText can report is_locked() for a buffer whose pages are not locked

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Secrets in memory / memory module API
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-11, RUST-06, CORE-03, RUST-13, CHECK-ARC-001, CHECK-ARC-002
- **Affected files and builds:** Native Unix library builds. The browser (wasm32) and Windows builds lock nothing, so their is_locked() is always false. src/lib.rs:43 `pub mod memory`. src/memory.rs:24-29: pub fn LockedText::from_locked(text, locked) stores any guard. Its contract ('locked must cover the buffer of text itself, not of a copy, and text must not grow') is written in its doc but never checked. src/memory.rs:62-65: LockedText::is_locked() returns only the guard's flag. src/memory.rs:228-264: pub struct LockedPages with pub fn of_vec (240-242) and pub fn of_string (245-247). The only users are inside src/memory.rs: from_locked at :134 (LockedBytes::into_text), of_string at :40 and of_vec at :101 (build), plus the module's own tests. No user in the CLI, tests/ or any other module.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repository: (a) docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-lib-core/run.sh locked-text (exit 1). (b) Verifier probe /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-locked-text-from-locked/probe, whose source is kept as docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-locked-text-from-locked/v04-run-probe.source.rs. It depends on the crate by path and calls only public items: mhfe::memory::{LockedPages, LockedText}. Control: LockedText::copy_of of 8,400 public bytes. Case 1: a 3-page Zeroizing<String> with LockedText::from_locked(text, LockedPages::of_vec(&other_64_byte_vec)). Case 2: LockedPages::of_string(&text) on a 16-byte String, then push 12,600 bytes so the buffer moves, then from_locked(text, guard). For every page of the text's own capacity it compares is_locked() with the mapping's VmFlags 'lo' in /proc/self/smaps.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-11: 'Fields and helpers are private by default and are made visible only when a caller needs them.' RUST-06: 'Items are private; pub(crate) comes before pub, and pub is for the library's API.' CORE-03: a class is used for 'state whose rules must hold'. LockedText's own documentation (src/memory.rs:14-17) says its buffer is locked before the text is written and stays locked until it is wiped, and is_locked() (src/memory.rs:62) says whether 'the operating system keeps the text out of swap'. RUST-13 and SECURITY.md (secrets 'held in locked memory (mlock)') rely on that lock.
- **Observed behavior:** v04 (exit 1): 'control LockedText::copy_of (8400 bytes): is_locked() = true, pages of its own buffer locked by the kernel = 3 of 3'. 'case 1 from_locked(text, LockedPages::of_vec(&other)): is_locked() = true, pages of its own buffer locked by the kernel = 1 of 4', where the one locked page is shared with the other buffer. 'case 2 buffer moved: true'. 'case 2 from_locked(grown text, LockedPages::of_string(&text)): is_locked() = true, pages of its own buffer locked by the kernel = 0 of 4'. Both cases print FAIL. The candidate harness (v05, exit 1) prints 'LockedText::is_locked() = true' and 'kernel keeps a page of the text's own buffer locked = false'. The two constructors needed for this, from_locked and LockedPages::of_vec/of_string, are public although nothing outside src/memory.rs uses them.
- **Impact:** No current caller misuses the API, so no secret reaches swap today. A program that takes the memory module as a library (CORE-04, and the RUST guide names src/memory.rs as the model to reuse) can build a LockedText, through safe public calls with no error, whose is_locked() is true while its secret's pages can be swapped. The CLI's note_unlocked (src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:456, hidden_input.rs:444) and the library's unit tests (feistel.rs:383-392, mhfe.rs:639-650, password.rs:293-296 and others) trust is_locked(), so a new caller that went through from_locked would get a false 'locked' report, or a passing test, for a protection that does not exist.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-locked-text-from-locked/v01-build-probe.log and v03-build-probe.log (probe builds, exit 0). v04-run-probe.log with .source.rs and .Cargo.toml beside it (exit 1, output above). v05-candidate-harness.log (the candidate's run.sh locked-text, exit 1). v06-static-trace.log (HEAD b6fca69, every use of from_locked, LockedPages, of_vec and of_string in src/ and tests/, all in src/memory.rs, and `pub mod memory` in src/lib.rs). Earlier: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-lib-core/h-locked-text.log, s07-locked-text-api.log, and h-unused-api.log, which lists LockedText::from_locked and LockedPages with no outside user.
- **Recommended fix:** Make LockedText::from_locked, LockedPages, LockedPages::of_vec and LockedPages::of_string private to src/memory.rs (or pub(crate) at most). Their only users are LockedText::build, LockedBytes::build and LockedBytes::into_text. If a public constructor is ever needed, have it check that the guard's start and length cover text.as_ptr() for text.capacity() and refuse otherwise.
- **Required verification:** The two probes no longer compile because the items are private; then drop the probes and confirm with the unused-api scan that no public item is left without a user. Or, if a checked public constructor is kept: run.sh locked-text and the verifier probe exit 0, because the foreign guard and the moved buffer are refused, and the memory module's unit tests still pass (cargo test --locked memory:: with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repository).
- **Related findings:** AUD-024 guide-lib-core: public items without any caller (CORE-11/RUST-06); h-unused-api lists LockedText::from_locked and LockedPages, so merge if that finding is confirmed with these items, AUD-024 confirmed: Library and front-end code panics on wrong input or broken invariants (LockedText::build / LockedBytes::build assert_eq!)
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. The candidate's harness still fails (exit 1, v05). My own probe also fails (exit 1, v04). It first checks that the kernel lock reading (smaps "lo") agrees with LockedText::copy_of, at 3 of 3 pages. It then shows that two public, safe call sequences give a LockedText whose is_locked() is true while its own buffer is not wholly locked. (1) from_locked with a LockedPages::of_vec guard of another buffer leaves 1 of 4 pages locked, and only because that page is shared with the other buffer. (2) from_locked with an of_string guard, after the String grew and moved, leaves 0 of 4 pages locked. The code matches the cited lines: from_locked (src/memory.rs:27-29) stores any guard, is_locked() (63-65) reads only the guard, and LockedPages, of_vec and of_string (231-247) are pub in `pub mod memory` (src/lib.rs:43). No code outside src/memory.rs uses from_locked or LockedPages (v06). CORE-11 and RUST-06 say helpers stay private unless a caller needs them, so this clearly breaks a review-only rule, and it has a concrete effect on LockedText's documented invariant. It is not a duplicate of any confirmed finding: the build/assert finding has a different root cause. A guide-lib-core finding on public items no caller needs (h-unused-api lists LockedText::from_locked and LockedPages) is not in the confirmed list. If the coordinator confirms that finding with these items in it, merge the two, because the same change fixes both. Severity is low: no caller misuses the API today, nothing reaches swap, and the wasm and Windows builds report false anyway.

##### AUD-024-ARC043 — Low — The startup and full self-checks do not cover four library answers that the front ends show, all added or changed by the AUD-023 remediation: the 16-bit wallet-check evidence of a rehearsal check, its list of the phrase's own checks that passed, a rekey's old-container keep list and the reference of the replacement's rehearsal

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** self-checks: rehearsal, keep advice, rekey
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-26, CORE-27, CORE-28, CORE-30, CHECK-ARC-003
- **Affected files and builds:** Every build that has the core: the native CLI (sets::native, src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:36) and the browser core module (sets::core through selfCheckCore, src/wasm_api/core/self_test.rs:92-104).
  
  1. Rehearsal evidence.
  - src/rehearsal.rs:473-506: evidence_of. The wallet_check value is computed at :494-499, separately from the outcome.
  - src/rehearsal.rs:46-62: CheckEvidence::own_checks_passed.
  - Shown by src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:565-577 (passed_lines), src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:698-701 ('The 24-word reading passes the 16-bit check.' when wallet_check == Some(true)) and src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:134-147 (evidence.passed and walletCheck in the JSON).
  - Not checked: src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:58-64 (LengthCase has no wallet_check field) and :119-139 (LengthCase::run compares only outcome, built_in_check and matching_lengths). No self-check calls own_checks_passed.
  
  2. Old-container keep list.
  - src/operation.rs:189-198: Keep::old_container. It is the list behind the specification's MUST warning before every rekey (mhfe_spec/README.md:530-536).
  - Shown by src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:519-528 (keep_until_funds_moved) and src/wasm_api/core.rs:246-255 (keepOldContainer).
  - Not checked: src/operation/known_answers.rs:27-141 (KeepCheck checks only Sealed::keep of new containers).
  
  3. Replacement rehearsal.
  - src/rekey.rs:79-106: ConfirmedPhrase::replacement_rehearsal, which carries the MUST of mhfe_spec/README.md:522-529.
  - Used by src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:390-400 and src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:345 and :414.
  - Not checked: src/rekey/known_answers.rs:1-255 never calls it.
  
  Tier: RehearsalCheck::run (src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:206), KeepCheck::run (src/operation/known_answers.rs:153) and RekeyCheck::run (src/rekey/known_answers.rs:233) all ignore it, so the full self-test checks nothing more.
- **Reproduction:** Run from the repository root:
  
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=../tmp/aud024/target python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-selfcheck-answers/run.py ../tmp/aud024/verify-selfcheck-answers/work
  
  The script copies the crate to the work directory, runs the unchanged copy, then applies each fault alone:
  - V1: evidence_of inverts the 16-bit evidence, `Some(!detection.source_check(..)?)`.
  - V2: own_checks_passed drops `PassedCheck::BuiltInCheck` for the verified reading.
  - V3: Keep::old_container drops changed_settings, so the PIM and memory level are lost.
  - V4: replacement_rehearsal no longer returns ConfirmingReference for a phrase confirmed by an address or a fingerprint, and falls through to a fingerprint.
  
  For each fault it runs self_check::sets::tests::every_set_passes_at_startup and the part's known_answers tests, then the covering unit test as a control.
  
  The reviewer's harness gives the same result with other mutants: python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-lib-wallet/run.py mutants.
  
  Static check: grep for own_checks_passed, old_container, replacement_rehearsal and .wallet_check in the known_answers and self_check files finds nothing.
- **Expected behavior:** Project documentation:
  - src/self_check/sets.rs:1-3: a set holds the checks of the parts its front end computes.
  - src/self_check/sets.rs:6-8: core() holds 'everything the encryption, recovery, rehearsal, rekey and hidden-wallet operations compute'.
  
  Coding guide:
  - CORE-27: known answers run at every start, before the feature's controls open.
  - CORE-26: a new feature brings its checks in the same change.
  - CORE-30: each new feature's checks are added to the full self-test.
  - CORE-28: a known answer compares exact output.
  
  Earlier audit:
  - AUD-023-ARC015 (observed) recorded that the CheckEvidence fields the front ends show, built_in_check and wallet_check, have no self-check.
  - AUD-023-ARC010 and AUD-023-ARC016 moved the replacement-rehearsal rule and the old-container warning into the library for every front end.
- **Observed behavior:** The ARC015 fix added LENGTH_CASES, which compare built_in_check and matching_lengths but not wallet_check. A build that reports the 24-word reading as passing the 16-bit check, or as failing it, still passes the rehearsal self-check.
  
  own_checks_passed, Keep::old_container and replacement_rehearsal, added by the AUD-023 remediation, have unit tests only.
  
  All four faults V1 to V4 leave every startup set passing, and with them the full tier, whose checks ignore the tier. In each case the covering unit test fails:
  - rehearsal::tests::a_check_lists_the_checks_of_the_phrase_itself
  - rehearsal::tests::the_passed_own_checks_are_listed_in_order
  - operation::tests::the_old_container_is_kept_with_settings_that_are_not_the_defaults
  - rekey::tests::the_replacement_is_rehearsed_with_what_confirms_it
- **Impact:** A build or platform fault in these answers is not caught by the startup or full self-check that the CLI and the browser run before secrets are typed. Only the developer's unit tests would catch it. Examples of such faults:
  - a 16-bit pass shown beside 'not verified' for a phrase that fails, or a pass left out;
  - a list of passed own checks that omits the verified built-in check;
  - a rekey warning that leaves out the old passwords or a non-default PIM or memory level, so the owner may not keep what opens the derived wallets;
  - a replacement rehearsed against the wrong reference.
  
  No wrong result is shown in the unmodified build. The defect is in the coverage of the run-time checks, so the impact is bounded (low).

Last line: '4 of 4 faults survive the self-checks or have no failing control'. Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-selfcheck-answers/ (run.py and README.md).

- **Recommended fix:** 1. Add an expected wallet_check, and the expected own_checks_passed list, to LengthCase, and compare the whole CheckEvidence. Cases from published containers:
  - zero-24 with the length detected (Some(false));
  - zero-24 with WalletCheck("TREZOR") (Some(false));
  - ambiguous-12-21 with the length detected (BuiltInChecks [12, 21]; the wallet_check value is recomputed independently);

  3. Add RekeyCheck assertions of replacement_rehearsal: BuiltInCheck for the zero-12 rekey, ConfirmingReference for the detected rekey confirmed by its fingerprint, and the owner-confirmed fingerprint with and without a passphrase where a published vector allows it.
  4. Give each new case a damaged-value test, as a_length_rule_that_differs_fails does.
- **Required verification:** With the fix applied, run both harnesses from the repository root:
  - python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-selfcheck-answers/run.py must exit 0, with every fault killed and every control failing.
  - python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-lib-wallet/run.py mutants must kill M1 to M4.
  
  Then run cargo test --locked --lib rehearsal::known_answers operation::known_answers rekey::known_answers self_check::sets, with the startup set still within its time budget (the_startup_set_stays_within_its_budget, release build).
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC015, AUD-023-ARC010, AUD-023-ARC016
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 with four faults of my own, different from the reviewer's M1 to M4. Each one breaks an answer the front ends show: V1 inverts CheckEvidence::wallet_check, V2 drops the verified built-in check from own_checks_passed, V3 drops the PIM and memory level from Keep::old_container, and V4 makes replacement_rehearsal answer with a fingerprint for a reference-confirmed phrase. Each fault alone leaves self_check::sets::tests::every_set_passes_at_startup and the known-answer tests of its part passing, while the covering unit test fails. A static trace agrees. LengthCase::run (src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:119-139) compares only outcome, built_in_check and matching_lengths. KeepCheck checks only Sealed::keep. RekeyCheck never calls replacement_rehearsal. No self-check file uses own_checks_passed, old_container, replacement_rehearsal or the wallet_check field. All three checks ignore the Tier, so the full self-test adds no case. AUD-023-ARC015 had named the missing self-check of the wallet_check evidence; its fix covered built_in_check but not wallet_check, so the remaining part is reported as new. It is not a duplicate of any confirmed finding.

- **Category:** ARC.

- **Subsystem:** self-checks: rekey and Argon2 engine known answers
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-28, CORE-32, CHECK-ARC-003
- **Affected files and builds:** Library unit tests, and the startup self-check `rekey` (src/self_check/sets.rs:102) and `argon2` of every native build with the core.
  - src/rekey/known_answers.rs:276-286 a_rekey_is_compared_with_its_target_vector. Its comment at :279-280 says 'A vector of another phrase fails'. The third case (:284, zero-12 to nonzero-12) is asserted only with `assert!(check.run(Tier::Startup).is_failure())` at :285.
  - src/rekey/known_answers.rs:118-120: RekeyCheck holds only `cases`. :60-86: REFUSALS is a const, read directly by run() at :252. :88-115: Refusal::run. :161-199: confirmed_again, called at :251. :202-221: sealed_as, with the comparison at :217-220. :233-254: run, with the same-password refusal as an inline closure at :236-250. No test can run one refusal alone or reach a failing comparison.
  - src/engine/known_answers.rs:427-444 a_wrong_lane_count_fails. Its doc comment at :427-428 says the MHFE-shaped call with another lane count gives another tag. two_lanes (:431-440) replaces the call for both vectors, and the assertion at :443 is only is_failure(). NativeArgon2::small (:231-253) runs the RFC 9106 vector first in the loop at :237-250, so the check fails there.
  - For comparison, the AUD-023-ARC019 fix: CipherRoundsCheck { vectors, refusals } at src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:142-145, with exact-detail meta-tests at :892-982.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=../tmp/aud024/target:
  1. python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-rekey-ka-tests/run.py probes (exit 1). It appends two probes to a scratch copy and prints:
  - 'AUD024 V1 RekeyCheck(zero-12 -> nonzero-12): Failed("rekey 1 of 1 stops with INTERNAL_ERROR")'
  - 'AUD024 V2 seal under nonzero-12's password: Err(INTERNAL_ERROR: internal error: no published round has this password and salt) before any comparison'
  - control: 'AUD024 V3 sealed_as(unicode-password with another container): Err("the sealed container differs from the published one")'
  - 'AUD024 L1 the test's own two-lane call: Failed("the SSE2 core gives another tag for the RFC 9106 vector")'
  - control: 'AUD024 L2 two lanes for the MHFE-shaped call only: Failed("the SSE2 core gives another tag for the 1 MiB vector")'
  Both probes then fail: each asserts the failure that its test's comment names.
  2. python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-rekey-ka-tests/run.py mutants (exit 1). Each mutant is applied alone to src/rekey/known_answers.rs: M5 replaces `sealed.container() == to.container` with `true`, M6 makes every refusal pass, M7 makes confirmed_again return Ok at once. Each survives `cargo test --locked --lib --bins --tests`: 360 + 141 + 3 + 3 = 507 tests pass, 0 fail.
  3. Static trace: nonzero-12's password is 'audit probe password 2026' (tests/fixtures/suite3-vectors/nonzero-12.json), and only the legal/letter phrases have vectors under it. Sealing the abandon phrase under it asks PublishedRoundKeys::derive (src/mhfe/known_answers/published.rs:130-138) for an unrecorded salt, so seal fails before sealed_as compares anything.
- **Expected behavior:** - CORE-28 (code-core.instructions.md:229-232): checks must be able to fail, a known answer compares exact output, and a verifier is also given a case it must refuse.
  - CORE-32: a test asserts behaviour and prefers a small exact assertion.
  - FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md CHECK-ARC-003: broad 'any error' assertions require explicit scrutiny, and tests must not give a false impression of what was exercised.
  - The tests' own comments: src/rekey/known_answers.rs:279-280 says a vector of another phrase fails the comparison with its target; src/engine/known_answers.rs:427-428 says the MHFE-shaped call with another lane count gives another tag.
  - AUD-023-ARC019 set the remedy for the same pattern in CipherRoundsCheck: refusals as data of the check, and exact-detail meta-tests.
- **Observed behavior:** - The rekey test's failing case stops with INTERNAL_ERROR in the seal, because the replay engine has no round key for that password and salt. It never reaches the container comparison, yet is_failure() passes.
  - The lane test fails on the RFC 9106 vector and never reaches the MHFE-shaped 1 MiB call it describes. A wrong lane count only in that call would be caught by the check (control L2), but no test shows it.
  - RekeyCheck takes neither its refusals nor its second-confirmation scenario as data, and the same-password refusal is an inline closure, so no test can make one of them fail.
  - With the comparison made always true, every refusal made to pass, or confirmed_again made to return Ok, all 507 non-ignored tests of the crate still pass.
- **Impact:** A regression that left the rekey startup self-check unable to detect a wrong sealed container, an accepted refusal or a broken second confirmation would ship with every test green. The self-check would then silently lose cases that CORE-28 requires, before any secret is typed. Impact is bounded. Today the production check compares exact output and passes. The library's own rekey refusals have unit tests (src/rekey.rs:416, :543, :753, :802, :867, :943), and the Argon2 1 MiB comparison is pinned by a_corrupted_tag_fails (src/engine/known_answers.rs:409-418). No wrong result for users is shown.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-rekey-ka-tests/harness-probes.log (exit 1; outcomes V1-V3 and L1-L2; both probes FAILED with left: Failed("rekey 1 of 1 stops with INTERNAL_ERROR") against right: Failed("rekey 1 of 1 the sealed container differs from the published one")).
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-rekey-ka-tests/harness-mutants.log (exit 1; M5, M6 and M7 each SURVIVE, 507 tests passed in 4 test binaries).
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-rekey-ka-tests/static-trace.log (HEAD b6fca69; the cited lines; the passwords of zero-12 and nonzero-12; the baseline b01-check-fast.log:76, :218, :239 showing the three tests pass unmodified).
  - Each log has its .command.json. Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-rekey-ka-tests/ (run.py, probes/, README.md).
  - The original reviewer's logs (guide-lib-wallet/probes-copy.log, harness-probes.log, harness-mutants.log, mutant-self-checks.log) agree.
- **Recommended fix:** - Make RekeyCheck's refusals (including the same-password refusal) and its published table fields of the check, as CipherRoundsCheck { vectors, refusals } does. A test can then run one refusal alone, and replay a target vector whose container is changed but whose password and settings have recorded round keys (for example unicode-password with another container).
  - Assert the exact detail 'rekey 1 of 1 the sealed container differs from the published one'. Add exact-detail meta-tests for each refusal ('refusal 1 of 1 is accepted instead of refused with ...') and for confirmed_again, and correct the comment at :279-280.
  - In a_wrong_lane_count_fails, change only the MHFE-shaped call (for example only when inputs.secret is empty), or assert the exact detail ending 'for the 1 MiB vector'.
- **Required verification:** python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-rekey-ka-tests/run.py all exits 0: both probes pass and M5-M7 are killed. cargo test --locked rekey::known_answers engine::known_answers passes. self_check::sets::tests::every_set_passes_at_startup still passes.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC019
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced it at b6fca69 with my own probes and mutants, run on a scratch copy of the crate. All of it was reduced cost: replayed round keys and the 1 MiB Argon2 call.
  (1) The third case of a_rekey_is_compared_with_its_target_vector (zero-12 to nonzero-12) ends in Failed("rekey 1 of 1 stops with INTERNAL_ERROR"). The seal under nonzero-12's password 'audit probe password 2026' asks PublishedRoundKeys for a password and salt pair that no vector records. It is refused with "no published round has this password and salt", so sealed_as never reaches its comparison at :217-220. A control shows the comparison does fail when it is reached: unicode-password's settings with another container give Err("the sealed container differs from the published one").
  (2) a_wrong_lane_count_fails ends in Failed("the SSE2 core gives another tag for the RFC 9106 vector"). Giving two lanes only to the MHFE-shaped call (empty secret) gives "... for the 1 MiB vector". So the test passes before it reaches the call its doc comment is about.
  (3) M5 (comparison always true), M6 (every refusal passes) and M7 (confirmed_again always passes), each applied alone, survive every non-ignored test of the crate: 507 tests in the library, binary and integration tests. REFUSALS (:60) is a const that run() reads directly (:252). RekeyCheck (:118-120) holds only `cases`, so no test can feed it a refusal, and the same-password refusal at :236-250 is an inline closure. This is the pattern AUD-023-ARC019 fixed in CipherRoundsCheck only. CipherRoundsCheck now has a `refusals` field (src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:142-145).
  Changes from the candidate:
  - I dropped the merged variant src/new_password.rs:355-358. That assertion sits in a test named dice_rolls_must_fit_the_word_count, and the failure it gets is the word-count mismatch the name describes. Removing the refusal at :149-153 would also be caught by scripts/browser-check/password-checks.mjs:262-267, which pins INVALID_REQUEST and its message.
  - I dropped CORE-34 from ruleIds as only weakly applicable.
  Severity stays low, as for AUD-023-ARC019. The production checks compare exact output, and the library's own rekey refusals have unit tests (src/rekey.rs:416, :543, :753, :802, :867, :943). The defect is that the self-check's ability to fail is never tested.
  This is not a duplicate: none of the confirmed findings covers it, and no earlier audit names these tests.
- **Merged variants:** The test a_wrong_lane_count_fails passes on the RFC 9106 vector and never reaches the MHFE-shaped call it is about (Library unit tests: src/engine/known_answers.rs:427-444 (test and doc: 'The MHFE-shaped call is the engine's own: a call with another lane count, as a broken parameter assembly would make, gives anoth)

  The nine sentence-named cases show that the suite already knows the convention: check_rekey_warns_about_other_wallets, check_rekey_asks_about_the_passphrase, check_never_use_is_refused_at_start, check_quit_keys_leave_the_private_screen, check_wallet_check_needs_a_passphrase, check_rekey_refuses_given_settings_at_start, check_dumb_terminal_has_no_hints, check_typed_ahead_keys_answer_nothing and check_search_reference_is_recorded_once_read.
  
  For the browser labels, read self-checks.mjs:97 and :165 and client-checks.mjs:246 and :254. They are printed in b20-browsers.log at lines 3, 379, 894 and 161-162. expectRejection (scripts/browser-check/harness.mjs:87-100) appends ' -> CODE: message' to the label.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-34 (.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md:265-268, Check: review): 'A test's name says the behaviour it proves, as a sentence: `refuses what @scure/bip39 refuses`, `one_missing_word_is_restored_at_any_place`.' code-core applies to every file (applyTo '**'). The guide also says a touched function is brought to the rules in the same change. The terminal-suite cases were moved into new modules by d5940de, after the guide added CORE-34 in 1491885.
- **Observed behavior:** 28 of the 37 case functions the terminal suite runs are named after a topic: check_menu, check_check_word, check_encrypt_lists, check_self_test, check_serve_output and so on. They do not name a behaviour, and several prove four to six behaviours each; check_menu prints four results.
  
  The suite's printed result lines and most docstrings do state the behaviour, for example 'menu: a lone Escape quits, exit code 0, terminal restored'. So the gap lies in the case names that appear in code and in a failure's traceback ('in check_menu'), not in most reported lines. A few printed lines are noun lists too, for example 'menu: password regeneration, Escape/q return, private screens cleared, terminal restored'.
  
  In the browser suite, the labels at self-checks.mjs:97 and :165 are noun phrases that do not say what is expected. The labels at client-checks.mjs:246 and :254 are bare imperatives ('cancel before the first round'). Most of the other 487 unique labels are sentences.
- **Impact:** Maintainability only. A reader of the suite, or of a failure's traceback, cannot tell from a case's name which behaviour it proves. A name like check_menu or check_script_messages gives no hint that the case covers exit codes, terminal restoration or wrapping. The assertion messages and printed lines partly make up for this. No product behaviour is affected.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/skeptic-test-names/terminal-case-names.log (with .command.json, exit 0). It holds the static probe python3 tmp/aud024/skeptic-test-names/case_names.py run from the mhfe root at b6fca69, listing each case with file:line, its classification, the first docstring line and its printed labels, and it ends with 'cases run: 37; named as a sentence: 9; named as a topic: 28'.

  - The candidate's docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-unapplied-review-rules/test-names.log.
  - git show d5940de, which moved the cases into scripts/terminal_suite/ in a remediation commit.
  - git log -S'CORE-34' on the workspace guide: 1491885 of 2026-10-14 01:15 UTC.
- **Recommended fix:** Rename each terminal-suite case function after the behaviour it proves, as a sentence. Split the cases that prove several behaviours, for example check_menu into a_lone_escape_quits_and_restores_the_terminal, ctrl_c_ends_the_menu_with_exit_code_130 and the_password_entry_makes_words_or_characters. Reword the printed noun-list lines, such as 'menu: password regeneration, ...' and 'self-test: every part with its pass mark, ...', as sentences. In the browser suite, reword self-checks.mjs:97 and :165 and client-checks.mjs:246 and :254 to state the behaviour, for example 'MhfeWallet: the startup check reports every part passed', 'cancel() before the first round rejects with CANCELLED'.
- **Required verification:** Rerun the probe: every case that main() and FULL_SIZE_CHECKS run is named as a sentence that states a behaviour. The fast terminal suite still runs every case in the same order, with each printed line a sentence. The browser suite prints sentence labels at the four places named, and its check count changes only where a case was split.
- **Related findings:** AUD-024 (confirmed): Source comments, a test-failure message and test identifiers cite 'G10 of the self-check plan' (it covers the g10_isolated_command identifier, left out of this finding), AUD-024 (confirmed): Twelve of the browser suite's 1,986 reported checks cannot fail (self-checks.mjs:139 and :167, labels next to the ones named here)
- **Verification:** confirmed: The core claim reproduces at b6fca69. A static probe of scripts/verify-hidden-input.py main() (lines 174-216) and FULL_SIZE_CHECKS finds that 28 of the 37 terminal-suite cases are named after a topic (check_menu, check_self_test, check_serve_output and so on). Only 9 say the behaviour they prove. CORE-34 (Check: review) requires a test's name to state that behaviour as a sentence. These functions were moved into the new scripts/terminal_suite/ modules by d5940de, a remediation commit made after CORE-34 entered the guide (1491885), so they also count as touched code.
  
  I narrowed the candidate in three places:
  - The printed labels are not topics. Almost every line has the form 'area: behaviour', for example 'menu: a lone Escape quits, exit code 0, terminal restored', and failures carry assertion messages that say what broke. The title now concerns the names.

Neither is a clear breach.

So the given-gap branch (container_search.rs:290), the forced card (container_repair.rs:185), the given-passphrase answer in decrypt and rekey (decrypt.rs:209, rekey.rs:258) and check's path use (check.rs:333, :403) run in no test.

A check --path case would have caught it. Likewise the CLI's restated scan-gap rules (another confirmed AUD-024 finding) are never exercised through --scan-gap. This is limited to test coverage and maintainability, with no secret exposure, so the severity is low.

##### AUD-024-ARC047 — Low — MhfeClient.keepOldContainer(), added for AUD-023-ARC016, is called by no check: the browser suite never calls it although it says the page calls every method, and the package check calls only the raw WebAssembly binding, so the class method and its worker operation are untested

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Test fidelity / browser package rekey advice (MhfeClient.keepOldContainer)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-33, CORE-26, CHECK-ARC-003
- **Affected files and builds:** Public API: web/client.d.ts:690 (declaration), web/client.js:538-551 (doc comment and method: requireSettings at :548, #quick operation "keepOldContainer" at :550); worker operation web/core-worker.js:172-173, in the table CORE_OPERATIONS typed Record<string, Operation<CoreRequest>> (:72-74), shipped in dist/runtime/worker.js; binding src/wasm_api/core.rs:250-256.
