Claims: scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:17-19 and docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:401-403. Host duty: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:923-925 (shipped as dist/README.md). Builds: the browser package core module (dist/core/client.js, dist/runtime/worker.js).
- **Reproduction:** From the mhfe root at b6fca69, with the package built by the baseline: (1) `node docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/guide-tooling-js/browser-suite-methods.mjs` lists each method declared by MhfeClient, MhfeRepair, MhfePasswords, MhfeWallet and MhfeModuleClass, counts its calls in scripts/browser-check, and exits 1 when one is missing. (2) `node /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-keep-old-container/probe.mjs` lists every line of scripts/ and tests/ that names keepOldContainer. It confirms that core-rekey.mjs's `core` is the bindings. It sends operation keepOldContainer (pim 3 and memoryLevel 2, then pim 1024) to the package's own dist/runtime/worker.js in process, using in-process-worker.mjs's helper. Then it sends the same call to that script with the table entry `keepOldContainer: (request) =>` renamed in memory.
- **Expected behavior:** scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:17-19: 'The page calls every method of the four classes with each of its options and compares the results, or the refusals, with known values'. docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:401-403 says the same of scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs and scripts/verify-browsers.mjs. CORE-33 (Check: review): 'A feature has its case in the browser regression suite ... in both editions and both browsers where the feature exists'. mhfe's suite is scripts/verify-browsers.mjs (mhfe/AGENTS.md:16). CORE-26: 'A new ... feature in any program brings its checks in the same change.' CHECK-ARC-003: 'Test-only seams must not give a false impression that production dispatch was exercised.' AUD-023-ARC016's required verification: 'a browser package test gets the same items from the new client method or field'.
- **Observed behavior:** browser-suite-methods.log, exit 1: 34 of the 35 declared methods are 'ok'. The exception is 'FAIL MhfeClient.keepOldContainer() (web/client.d.ts): 0 calls in the browser suite, 1 calls of that name in the package check'. That one call is the raw binding. The probe's log, exit 0, holds every claim. The only line naming keepOldContainer in scripts/ or tests/ is scripts/package-check/core-rekey.mjs:197, `assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(core.keepOldContainer(pim, level)), ...)`. The browser suite never names it. Today the worker answers {"type":"result","result":[{"item":"oldContainer"},{"item":"oldPasswords"},{"item":"pim","value":3},{"item":"memoryLevel","value":2}]}. For pim 1024 it answers {"type":"error","error":{"code":"INVALID_PIM",...}}. With the table entry renamed, the client's operation gets {"type":"error","error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"unknown operation core.keepOldContainer"}}. No check sends that operation, and the table is typed Record<string, ...>, so such a rename fails no gate. The guide-tooling-js role's tsc-declarations.log shows a related case: removing keepOldContainer() from client.js while client.d.ts still declares it also passes tsc (exit 0). The class's own client-side refusal (requireSettings at client.js:548) is also untested for this method.
- **Impact:** Before every rekey a page must show what to keep of the old container (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:923-925). This is the advice the specification makes a MUST (mhfe_spec README, as cited by AUD-023-ARC016). A break in the class method, its argument handling or its worker entry would ship with every check passing, and pages would lose the structured list the library now provides. The suite's claim to call every method is false for this one. This is a coverage defect, not wrong behaviour: today's results are correct.
- **Evidence:** Logs in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-keep-old-container/. browser-suite-methods.log, exit 1, log SHA-256 66dd023039b91dc8b802553622d8eec375ca00f08fb56f08739b31a66b104688. This is identical to the guide-tooling-js run, so the result is reproducible. keep-old-container-probe.log, exit 0, log SHA-256 9d1ca90de635fd62c342566c2424e15305a05a9e134d697f551e4bfff78e285f. Both are run through docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh, and each has a .command.json beside it. The probe source is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-keep-old-container/probe.mjs. Related evidence from another role: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-tooling-js/tsc-declarations.log ('FAIL client.js loses its keepOldContainer() method, which client.d.ts declares: tsc exit 0') and keep-old-container-worker.log. Static reads: core-rekey.mjs:34 and :181-198; core-worker.js:72-74 and :172-173; client.js:547-551; module-classes.mjs:143-147 (the only dynamic method loop, over fingerprint and walletCheck); verify-browsers.mjs:17-19; docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:401-403; AUD-023-2026-10-13.md:1230 (ARC016 fixed in 253ca3c; 'Its own required verification was not run again'). A search of the workspace finds no other caller, so no multi-chain-wallet-tools page or regression test covers the method either.
- **Recommended fix:** Add a browser-suite case, for example in scripts/browser-check/rekey-checks.mjs, that calls client.keepOldContainer() with no options, {} and pim/memoryLevel 3/0, 0/2 and 3/2, and compares the exact item lists. Add a refused setting too, pim 1024 → INVALID_PIM with the library's sentence. Add the class call to the Node package check (core-client.mjs or client-rekey.mjs) through the stand-in or in-process worker, so that the worker operation and requireSettings are exercised. Keep browser-suite-methods.mjs, or an equivalent, in scripts/check.sh, so that a declared class method with no browser-suite call fails.
- **Required verification:** browser-suite-methods.mjs exits 0. scripts/verify-browsers.mjs and scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs pass with the new cases. With the web/core-worker.js:172 entry renamed, or client.js's keepOldContainer removed, the new cases are seen failing and then passing once restored.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC016, AUD-024 guide-tooling-js candidate: tsc passes a client.js that lacks a method client.d.ts declares (tsc-declarations.log)
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced the gap at b6fca69, and none of the evidence refutes it. Across scripts/ and tests/, keepOldContainer is named on one line only: scripts/package-check/core-rekey.mjs:197. That line calls `core.keepOldContainer(pim, level)`, and core-rekey.mjs:34 binds `core` to the raw WebAssembly bindings (`const core = bindings;`), not to MhfeClient. The page code of the browser suite (scripts/browser-check/*.mjs) never names the method. It also has no dynamic dispatch that could reach it: the only `walletClient[method]` loop, in module-classes.mjs:143-147, covers fingerprint and walletCheck. The in-process worker checks never send the operation "keepOldContainer". client-refusals.mjs has no keepOldContainer case. verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs does not cover the old-container warning. Of the 35 methods the classes declare, it is the only one with no call in the browser suite. scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:17-19 and docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:401-403 both say the suites call every method of the four classes. CORE-33 asks for each feature to have its case in the browser regression suite. The operation works today: my probe ran the package's own dist/runtime/worker.js in process, the table renamed in memory turns the same call into an unknown-operation refusal, and the type check cannot catch such a rename. This is a coverage defect, not wrong behaviour, so low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md. It is not a duplicate. The confirmed browser-API documentation finding is about docs/API.md and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md leaving the method out, which is a different root cause. AUD-023-ARC016 asked that "a browser package test gets the same items from the new client method or field". The fix's test calls only the raw binding, and AUD-023 records that this verification was not run again. The remaining defect is therefore reported as new, with ARC016 as the related finding. CORE-32 is dropped from the rule IDs because the library item Keep::old_container has unit tests (src/operation.rs:335).

##### AUD-024-ARC048 — Low — Twelve of the browser suite's 1,986 reported checks cannot fail: checkFullChecks records `expect(true, …)` for the full self-check time of each module class, and the MhfeClient line names a time while it checks something else

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Test fidelity / browser suite (scripts/browser-check, scripts/verify-browsers.mjs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-28, CORE-34, CHECK-ARC-003
- **Affected files and builds:** scripts/browser-check/self-checks.mjs:117-140, the loop over MhfeRepair, MhfePasswords and MhfeWallet: line 139 is `expect(true, `${name}: the full self-check took ${time} ms`);` and line 138 already checks report.passed, the tier and the labels. self-checks.mjs:145-150 and :167 are `expect(report.passed && labelled(report), `MhfeClient: the full self-check took ${time} ms`)`; this is the only assertion of the client full check's report.passed and labels, and it is named after a time. scripts/browser-check/harness.mjs:79-84: expect() records every call as an 'ok   ' or 'FAIL ' result, and the harness has no line that only reports information. The page runs once per browser and mode, four pages per run of scripts/verify-browsers.mjs (Chromium and Firefox, standard and fast). The line comes from commit 19e1cd5, which moved it from scripts/verify-browsers.mjs (old lines 3370 and 3398). The count is cited in docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.md:1178 and docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.json:3664. Scope: the real-browser test suite only, with no effect on any shipped build.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: node /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verifier-cannot-fail-checks/probe.mjs. The probe extracts expect() from scripts/browser-check/harness.mjs and calls it as self-checks.mjs:139 and :167 do. Line 139 with a failed report and a time of 9,999,999 ms records 'ok' for all three classes. Line 167 records 'ok' for a 9,999,999 ms time with a passing, labelled report. It records 'FAIL MhfeClient: the full self-check took 1 ms' for a failing report, a failure whose name shows only a time. The probe then counts docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/b20-browsers.log: 4 pages, 1,986 'ok' and 0 'FAIL' lines, and 16 timing lines, of which 12 come from expect(true) and 4 are MhfeClient lines. Static check: grep -n 'expect(true' scripts/browser-check/*.mjs finds only self-checks.mjs:139.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-28 'Checks able to fail' (code-core.instructions.md:229): a check the suite records must be able to fail. CORE-34 (code-core.instructions.md:265): 'A test's name says the behaviour it proves'. CHECK-ARC-003 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md:363-367): tests must not give a false impression of what was exercised. In the same file the startup checks show the expected form: their time line has a bound that can fail (self-checks.mjs:106 `expect(time < 2000, `${name}: the startup check took ${time} ms, under 2 s`)`).
- **Observed behavior:** Each run records 12 'ok' results that no state of the page can turn into FAIL (3 classes × 4 pages). b20-browsers.log lines 372, 375, 378; 887, 890, 893; 1403, 1406, 1409; 1918, 1921, 1924. The 4 MhfeClient lines (b20-browsers.log:380, 895, 1411, 1926) name only a time. They pass or fail on report.passed and the library's labels, and the time plays no part. A failure of the client full check's verdict or labels would therefore appear as 'FAIL MhfeClient: the full self-check took N ms'. The AUD-023 remediation record reports '1986 checks, none failed' for this suite, a total that includes the 12 lines that cannot fail.
- **Impact:** The reported number of passed browser checks is inflated by 12 that test nothing (0.6 %). A reader may take the 16 timing lines for time limits, and a real failure of the client full check's verdict or labels would be reported under a misleading name. There is no effect on the library, the CLI or the browser package.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-cannot-fail-checks/timing-lines-probe.log, exit 0, log SHA-256 6c483efb54d5ddce703aed8d6114d86e88f13715f643b6a7b0eba2a4e8f891e0. It prints harness expect(), self-checks.mjs:134-139, 150 and 167, the recorded ok/FAIL results for worst-case inputs, and the counts in b20-browsers.log. Also docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-tooling-js/checks-that-cannot-fail.log (SHA-256 8b39c5451a0ea761…). Baseline docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/b20-browsers.log (node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs, exit 0) has its timing lines at 372-380, 887-895, 1403-1411 and 1918-1926. git log -L139,139 dates the current line to 19e1cd5 (2026-10-14), which moved it from the old scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:3370.
- **Recommended fix:** Add an information line to harness.mjs, for example a note() that pushes a line verify-browsers.mjs prints but does not count as a result. Report the four full self-check times through it, or give them a bound that can fail, as the startup checks have. Name the MhfeClient check after what it proves, for example 'MhfeClient: the full self-check passes, with the library's labels', and give the time as information.
- **Required verification:** grep -n 'expect(true' scripts/browser-check/*.mjs finds nothing. A run of node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs in both browsers and both modes shows 12 fewer 'ok' lines than before (1,974 against 1,986 at b6fca69, other changes aside) and no FAIL. The times appear as information lines or as bounded checks, and the MhfeClient line names the verdict and labels it checks.
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69. In scripts/browser-check/self-checks.mjs, line 139 calls `expect(true, `${name}: the full self-check took ${time} ms`)` for MhfeRepair, MhfePasswords and MhfeWallet. The harness's expect() (harness.mjs:80-84) records "ok" whenever its condition is truthy, so these lines can never be FAIL. My probe ran the harness's own expect() with a time of 9,999,999 ms and still recorded "ok". The baseline log b20-browsers.log has 4 pages and 1,986 "ok" lines. Sixteen of those lines are timing lines: 12 come from expect(true) and the other 4 are MhfeClient lines. self-checks.mjs:167 names the MhfeClient line after a time, but it fails only on `report.passed && labelled(report)`. The probe shows a 1 ms run recorded as FAIL under a line that names only the time. That breaks CORE-34, whose rule is that a test's name says the behaviour it proves. It also goes against the principle in CORE-28's title, 'Checks able to fail'. The AUD-023 remediation record cites the inflated total ("1986 checks, none failed"). One correction to the candidate: CHECK-ARC-003 does not literally ask auditors to identify checks that cannot fail. It asks for test fidelity, meaning tests must not give a false impression of what they exercised. Not a duplicate: none of the confirmed findings or AUD-023 findings covers test fidelity in the browser suite. Severity stays low. This is a defect in test evidence and naming with no product effect.

##### AUD-024-ARC049 — Low — Check and generator scripts outside the gates do not refuse a command line outside their usage: a misspelled --full makes verify-browser-package.mjs skip its full-size encryption and exit 0, a misspelled --check makes generate-cell-widths.py rewrite the tracked table instead of comparing, and the independent checkers given no file exit 0 having checked nothing

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.

- **Subsystem:** Tooling / command lines of the check, build and generator scripts

(1) scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs: the usage at :3-4 documents --full. :54 `if (process.argv.includes("--full")) await checkFullSizeEncryption();` is the only read of argv in the script and in scripts/package-check/. :94 ends with an unconditional `process.exit(0)`. The only sign of a skipped full-size run is the missing line 'A full-size encryption with the threaded build gives the native container.' (scripts/package-check/core-operations.mjs:722). AGENTS.md:19 documents `node scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs --full` as the full-size run. (2) scripts/generate-cell-widths.py: the usage at :25-26 is `[--check]` ('With --check the script writes nothing'). :117 tests only `"--check" in sys.argv[1:]`, and any other argument reaches :122 `OUTPUT.write_text(...)`, which writes the tracked src/bin/mhfe/cell_widths.rs. Its sibling scripts/generate-published-rounds.py:150-157 refuses anything but [] or ["--check"]. (3) scripts/independent-suite3.py: the usage at :10-13 requires `<file.json> ...` for vector and a file for passwords. At :481-484 `passwords` loops over an empty list and returns; at :487-488 `vector` passes [] to check_files (:387-407); without a command, :476 ends in an IndexError traceback. scripts/independent-suite4.py: usage :9-12; validation :221-224, vector :227-228 and :216 behave the same way. (4) scripts/check-release-artifacts.sh: :60 and :71 compare $1 exactly with --builder-paths and --archives, and the default mode (:115-152) reads no argument. A misspelled `--archive <file>` or `--builder-path <file>` therefore runs the default release-binary/WebAssembly check and ignores the files named (static trace; the script is release-level and not run). (5) These scripts read no argv and ignore any argument: scripts/verify-argon2-wasm.mjs (whole file), scripts/verify-single-modules.mjs (usage :7 has no options) and scripts/build-browser-check.mjs. (6) Build steps run by build-wasm.sh with the fixed argument dist: scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:11 reads argv[2] unchecked. A missing folder ends in TypeError ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE from path.join at :16 with a stack trace, and extra arguments are ignored. scripts/stamp-build-id.mjs:45-49 refuses a missing folder with its usage (exit 1) but ignores extra arguments. (7) Context: .github/workflows/vectors.yml:46-47 and :51-52 pass `$(cut -d' ' -f3 SHA256SUMS)`. A failing cut would hand the checkers no file and the step would pass, but ci.yml's fast test (tests/vector_share/replay.rs:92-99 and :238-241, run by `cargo test --locked` at ci.yml:133) requires SHA256SUMS on the same commit. Contrast, where arguments are refused: scripts/gate-command-line.mjs:10-20, scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs:49-63, scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:90-110, scripts/third-party-licenses.py:609-617, scripts/remove-network-code.mjs:76-79.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69, with dist/ built by the baseline (b12) and PYTHONPATH naming the unicodedata2/cryptography install: (a) `node scripts/verify-argon2-wasm.mjs --full` exits 0. Its output equals that of the run without arguments (cmp: identical; both logs SHA-256 1c1efc8c24b9db19…). (b) verify-browser-package.mjs was not run because it writes target/build-id-check/. The tracked file is untouched (git diff clean). (e) Contrast runs: `python3 scripts/generate-published-rounds.py --chek` exits 1 with its usage; `node scripts/verify-code-rules.mjs --full` and `node scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs --full` exit 2 with their usage. (f) `node scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs` (no folder) exits 1 with a TypeError stack trace and writes nothing. (g) The kept harness, `PYTHONPATH=<packages> docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-script-arguments/run.sh`, prints FAIL on all 7 cases and exits 1.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-48 (Check: review; code-core applies to every file): every input from outside is validated where it enters and refused with a clear message when it does not fit, and 'two inputs that look different never map silently to the same meaning'. CORE-22: wrong input fails. The repository applies this to its own scripts. scripts/gate-command-line.mjs:1-2 says that 'anything else is refused with the usage and exit code 2'. scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs:49-53 refuses arguments 'so that a mistyped threshold never passes a check that looked at nothing (AUD-012-ARC002)'; AUD-012-ARC002 was a low finding of this kind and was fixed. The sibling generator generate-published-rounds.py refuses any argument other than --check. Each script's own usage line (verify-browser-package.mjs:3-4, generate-cell-widths.py:25, independent-suite3.py:10-13, independent-suite4.py:9-12, check-release-artifacts.sh:4-26) names the only accepted command lines.
- **Observed behavior:** An argument outside the usage is ignored, or read as the default mode, and the script exits 0. A misspelled --full runs only the fast parts of verify-browser-package.mjs. A misspelled --check makes generate-cell-widths.py overwrite the table it was asked to compare, removing the difference it should have reported. A command with no file makes either independent checker check nothing, print nothing and exit 0. Static trace: a misspelled --archives or --builder-paths makes check-release-artifacts.sh run a different check and ignore the files it was given. Scripts without options accept any argument silently. A missing folder for write-package-manifest.mjs ends in an internal TypeError instead of a usage message.
- **Impact:** A mistyped manual or release-level run looks like a pass. The full-size browser encryption, which AGENTS.md lists as a full-size run the maintainer starts, does not run. A cell-width table check rewrites the file instead of reporting a difference. An independent vector check covers zero files. An archive check checks the release binaries instead of the named archives. The only sign is a missing or different output line. The impact is bounded: CI and scripts/check.sh call these scripts with correct, fixed arguments (check.sh:60-61 and :67, vectors.yml:41-52, package-release.sh:108, :137 and :158), and the vectors.yml no-file path is covered by ci.yml's fast test on the same commit. No secret, shipped build or cryptographic output is affected.

##### AUD-024-ARC051 — Low — scripts/generate-published-rounds.py is written in Python although it reimplements nothing and needs no library only Python has, and two release-check shell scripts carry multi-line Python programs instead of being thin wrappers

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Tooling language choice (scripts/)

- **Rules:** TOOL-01
- **Affected files and builds:** Main variant, a standalone script in the wrong language:

  - scripts/verify-archive-packing.sh:52-73: a 20-line Python heredoc that reads tar and zip permission bits. scripts/check.sh:69 runs it.
  - Borderline: scripts/build-reproducible.sh:8-12 is a 3-line heredoc that reads the version with tomllib. release.yml:46 and ci.yml:161 run that script.

##### AUD-024-ARC052 — Low — A coin's address rules are not held by Coin: they are spread over Coin's four matches and its hand-kept ALL list, Address::type_description and five coin matches in encodings.rs. A new coin therefore grows cases in up to eleven places, and the compiler points at only five of them. Each Bech32 human-readable part and the 20-byte address program length are typed several times.

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** wallet (coins and address encodings)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-06, CORE-11, CORE-14, CORE-10
- **Affected files and builds:** Library, all builds (native CLI and every browser build with the wallet: browser-core, browser-wallet, wasm).
  - src/wallet.rs:90-103: Coin::ALL, a hand-kept [Self; 12] array. The compiler does not tie it to the variants, and the tests at :961-981 only iterate it.
  - src/wallet.rs:106-121 (name), :124-139 (id), :142-156 (address_forms), :161-175 (coin_types): one match per fact.
  - src/wallet.rs:274-289: Address::type_description matches on self.coin again, with `_ => None` at :287.
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:11-28: parse, with guarded arms per coin and their Bech32 prefixes: 'bc1', 'tb1' (:13), 'ltc1' (:14), 'dash1', 'tdash1' (:19); 'cosmos' and 'inj' (:17-18); the CashAddr and Zcash guards (:15, :20); fallback `_ => parse_base58` (:25).
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:72-76: 'dash' and 'tdash' again, as hrps.
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:127-131: parse_segwit, with 'bc', 'tb' and 'ltc' again, as hrps.
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:133-139: a Bitcoin-only Taproot arm and the coin-specific message 'bc1q with 42 characters, bc1p or ltc1q'.
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:151-176: base58_versions, an exhaustive match on the coin.
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:181-184: parse_base58's alphabet per coin, with `_ =>` fallback.
  - The 20-byte address program length: literal at encodings.rs:79, :134, :195, :249 (the Ethereum/Keccak address) and :329; local const ACCOUNT_BYTES = 20 at :214.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target:
  
  1. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-coin-rules/new-coin-touches.sh b6fca69. The harness extracts the tracked tree with git archive into a scratch folder, adds only `Probe,` to `enum Coin` and runs `cargo check --locked --lib`. Result: E0004 'Coin::Probe not covered' at src/wallet.rs:109, :127, :145, :164 and src/wallet/encodings.rs:153. It then prints FAIL ('a new coin must grow a case in 5 places') and exits 1. Nothing else fails to compile. Coin::ALL (wallet.rs:90), type_description (:276/:287), parse's guarded arms (encodings.rs:13-25), parse_segwit's hrp and Taproot arms (:128-129, :135) and parse_base58's alphabet (:182-183) all accept the new coin silently.
  
  2. Static trace of the repeated literals: the prefixes at encodings.rs:13, :14, :19 against the hrps at :73-74, :128-129; the 20-byte length at :79, :134, :195, :214, :249, :329.
  
  3. Divergence trace: the guard prefix list at :13 decides whether parse_segwit runs, and the hrp table at :127-131 decides the network.
  - A prefix kept in the guard but missing from the table is refused by not_of(coin) at :130 ('it is not an address of Bitcoin (1…, 3…, bc1q… or bc1p…)').
  - An hrp kept in the table but missing from the guard falls to parse_base58 and is refused as 'its checksum or format is wrong' (:189).
  - A variant missing from Coin::ALL still compiles and passes the unit tests. It is never parsed by FromStr (wallet.rs:184-190) or offered by the CLI (src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:83, :102; src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:237-247) or the browser (src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:44).
- **Expected behavior:** Coding guide (/home/user/.../.github/instructions/code-core.instructions.md), all three rules marked 'Check: review':
  - CORE-06: 'A new coin, reference kind or check is one new variant, and code that dispatches over the variants asks the variant instead of growing a case in many places.'
  - CORE-11: 'What is expected to change (formats, profiles, the rules of a coin) sits behind one type, so that a change touches one place.'
  - CORE-14: each question is answered by the type that owns the data. Here: whether a coin has several address types, and the length of an address type's program.
  
  CORE-10 ('Check: copies, review'): 'A value with a meaning ... is a named constant defined once; a value that follows from another is derived from it'. Before typing a literal, the rule says to search for an existing source. The pinned bitcoin_hashes 0.14.101 has hash160::Hash::LEN (src/lib.rs:185), and the pinned bech32 0.12.0 has hrp::BC and hrp::TB (src/primitives/hrp.rs:46, :50). A Bech32 prefix such as 'bc1' follows from its hrp and the separator '1'.
- **Observed behavior:** A coin's facts are split across two files. Name, id, address-forms text and coin types are four matches in impl Coin. The offered list is a separate hand-kept array, Coin::ALL. The description of its address types is a match in Address::type_description. The Base58 versions are an exhaustive match in encodings.rs. Its Bech32 prefixes, hrps, Taproot support and Base58 alphabet are guarded or fallback arms in parse, parse_segwit, parse_dash_platform and parse_base58.
  
  Adding one variant makes the compiler point at five matches. Up to six more coin-specific sites must be found by hand: ALL, type_description, parse's guard, parse_segwit's hrp arm, its Taproot arm, and parse_base58's alphabet. Every Bech32 hrp of Bitcoin, Litecoin and Dash is written twice, once as a prefix ('bc1', 'tb1', 'ltc1', 'dash1', 'tdash1') and once as an hrp ('bc', 'tb', 'ltc', 'dash', 'tdash'). The 20-byte length of the P2PKH, P2WPKH, Keccak, Cosmos-account, CashAddr and Dash Platform programs is typed at five places and as one function-local constant, instead of being asked of AddressType or named once.
- **Impact:** Maintenance only. There is no wrong output at b6fca69: the existing unit tests and the addresses self-check pass in the baseline. A new coin, or a changed or added prefix (for example a regtest 'bcrt' hrp), must be edited consistently in many places, and most of them are not compiler-checked. A partial edit refuses valid addresses with a misleading reason ('not an address of Bitcoin' or 'checksum or format is wrong'). A variant left out of Coin::ALL silently disappears from the CLI menu, from identifier parsing and from the browser's coin list.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-coin-rules/harness-new-coin-touches.log (+ .command.json): exit 1, the five E0004 sites and the unforced sites.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-coin-rules/probe-new-coin.log (+ .command.json): the same probe with the one-line diff it applies and the static greps for the prefixes, hrps and 20s. Probe script: tmp/aud024/verify-coin-rules/probe-new-coin.sh, in the workspace scratch folder.
  - The candidate's own log, docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/guide-lib-wallet/core10-unicode-and-coins.log.
  - Kept harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-coin-rules/ (new-coin-touches.sh and README.md).
  - Library constants checked in the pinned registry sources: bitcoin_hashes-0.14.101/src/lib.rs:185 'const LEN: usize'; bech32-0.12.0/src/primitives/hrp.rs:46, :50 'pub const BC', 'pub const TB'.
- **Recommended fix:** 1. Describe each coin once, as data its variant returns (one match, or one static table): name, id, SLIP-44 coin types, Base58 versions and alphabet, Bech32 hrps with their testnet flag, the account hrp for Cosmos SDK chains, whether Taproot or Dash Platform applies, and whether it has several address types. Derive the address-forms text and type_description from that description.
  2. Let encodings.rs read that description instead of matching on the coin. Build the Bech32 prefix check from the hrps plus the separator '1', so each hrp is written once.
  3. Make Coin::ALL impossible to fall out of step with the enum, for example with a test that maps every ALL entry through an exhaustive match and checks the count, or with a generated list.
  4. Ask the address program length of AddressType, or name it once (for example from hash160::Hash::LEN, with the Keccak address length named beside it), and use that name at encodings.rs:79, :134, :195, :214, :249 and :329.
- **Required verification:** With CARGO_TARGET_DIR set outside target/:
  - cargo test --locked wallet:: passes unchanged, and so do the wallet known answers and the addresses/address-search self-checks.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-coin-rules/new-coin-touches.sh <fix commit> exits 0: one place grows a case for a new coin, and the informational list no longer shows coin-specific arms in encodings.rs or type_description.
  - grep finds no literal 20 for a program length in src/wallet/encodings.rs, and finds each hrp written once.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC008
- **Verification:** confirmed: Re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and reproduced the defect. The candidate holds, apart from small counting and wording errors, which are corrected below. A scratch copy of the tracked tree with one added Coin variant ('Probe') fails cargo check at exactly five exhaustive matches: src/wallet.rs:109, :127, :145, :164 and src/wallet/encodings.rs:153. The other coin-specific sites compile unchanged and have to be found by hand: the fixed-size Coin::ALL, Address::type_description's match with `_ => None`, the guarded arms of encodings::parse with their prefix lists, parse_segwit's human-readable-part and Taproot arms, and parse_base58's alphabet choice. CORE-06 names exactly this case: "A new coin ... is one new variant, and code that dispatches over the variants asks the variant instead of growing a case in many places". CORE-11 names "the rules of a coin" as what sits behind one type. Both are "Check: review" rules, so this is a clear breach and not a matter of taste. The Bech32 human-readable parts are typed twice: once as prefixes in parse, again as hrps in parse_segwit and parse_dash_platform. The 20-byte program length is a literal at five places plus one local constant, although the pinned bitcoin_hashes has hash160::Hash::LEN and bech32 0.12 has hrp::BC/TB. That breaches CORE-10's named-constant rule. Both repetitions follow from the same root cause, because the parsers decide coin and address-type facts themselves instead of asking Coin/AddressType (CORE-14). This is not a duplicate of any confirmed AUD-024 finding. AUD-023-ARC008 covered other repeated values (time units, the 33-byte word-bits size, the field size, the millibit divisor), not these. Corrections: Coin has four matches plus the hand-kept ALL array, not five matches. The 20 at encodings.rs:249 is the Ethereum address length (the last 20 bytes of Keccak-256), not HASH160, so the shared fact is the 20-byte address program length. A disagreement between parse and parse_segwit is refused as 'not an address of Bitcoin', or as a malformed checksum, not as another coin's address. Severity low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md, because this is a maintainability defect with no current wrong output.

##### AUD-024-ARC053 — Low — The runtime self-checks never test the search roots of 9 of the 12 coins, the nested SegWit (49) and Taproot (86) purposes, or the DIP17 hardened chains of the search loop: a wrong coin type for Litecoin, Ethereum/Injective or XRP passes the startup sets and the addresses and address-search checks at both tiers

- **Category:** ARC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Wallet self-checks (src/wallet/known_answers.rs, src/wallet/known_answers/addresses.rs) over the address search of src/wallet.rs
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-ARC-001
- **Rules:** CORE-27, CORE-30
- **Affected files and builds:** Code under check, src/wallet.rs:
  - :158-176, Coin::coin_types.
  - :227-237, AddressType::purpose: 49 and 86.
  - :291-309, Address::search_roots.
  - :437-469, AddressSearch::new: the stated pattern and the hardened_chains text.
  - :589-631, find_address_until: the chain mapping at :605-609, the root loop at :610.
  
  Runtime self-checks:
  - src/wallet/known_answers/addresses.rs:360-371: each table row is derived at its stated path, never through search_roots.
  - addresses.rs:340-342 and :416-428: the full tier's only two searches, row 29 (Bitcoin Cash under coin type 0) and row 9 (Bitcoin BIP84 m/84'/0'/3'/1/7).
  - src/wallet/known_answers.rs:418-474, SEARCHES_STATED: patterns only for Bitcoin BIP84 mainnet and testnet, Bitcoin Cash {145,0} and Dash Platform.
  - Sets that run them: src/self_check/sets.rs:113 (wallet_keys), :164 (wallet), :210 (native).
  
  The search parameters reach the user through:
  - src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:251-267, show_search: the 'Type' and 'Search' facts.
  - src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:175-193, describeAddress.
  
  The only check that searches every row is the unit test src/wallet.rs:713-733 (addresses_are_found_where_their_wallets_put_them).
  
  Uncovered coin types: Ethereum, Injective, XRP, Tron, Zcash, Dogecoin, Litecoin, Ethereum Classic (61 and 60) and Cosmos. Dash is covered through its Platform case.
  
  Affects all native builds and the browser wallet and core modules.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root:
  
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<build folder outside target/> docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-coin-type-selfcheck/mutations.sh
  
  The script git-archives HEAD into a temporary folder and applies, one at a time, these mutations to src/wallet.rs:
  - Litecoin's coin type &[2] -> &[3]
  - Ethereum and Injective's &[60] -> &[61]
  - XRP's &[144] -> &[145]
  - P2shP2wpkh => 49 -> 48
  - P2tr => 86 -> 85
  - CHAINS.map(|chain| chain | HARDENED) -> CHAINS.map(|chain| chain)
  - the control: Dash's &[5] -> &[6]
  
  For each mutation it runs cargo test --locked --offline --lib every_set_passes_at_startup, wallet::known_answers::addresses::tests::the_address_check_passes and the_address_search_is_stated_as_known. It then runs addresses_are_found_where_their_wallets_put_them as the control, which must fail.
  
  The same runs one mutation at a time with fuller test output: /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-coin-type-selfcheck/mutate.sh <litecoin|ethereum|chains|purpose49|purpose86|dash|none>.
- **Expected behavior:** CORE-27: 'Known answers run at every start, before the feature's controls open; a failure keeps them closed and says so.'
  
  CORE-30: the self-test command and the page's full self-test run 'every startup check plus the slower ones'.
  
  The address check of a coin is a feature control. The roots it searches are coin-specific values of that feature: the SLIP-44 coin type, the BIP44/49/84/86 purpose and the DIP17 hardened key classes. The front ends show them before the work starts, as the 'Type' and 'Search' facts and the describeAddress result.
  
  The project's own address-search check exists to give a known answer for 'what an address check states it will search' (known_answers.rs:1-8 and :508-509; docs/API.md:571-578). So a wrong root should fail a self-check for every coin and address type the check supports.
- **Observed behavior:** Each of these mutations passes the startup sets, the addresses check (Startup and Full) and the address-search check (Startup and Full):
  - Litecoin's coin type set to 3, Ethereum/Injective's to 61, XRP's to 145;
  - the nested SegWit purpose set to 48, the Taproot purpose to 85;
  - DIP17 chains left unhardened in the search loop.
  
  The startup set also stays within its budget. Only the unit test fails each time, for example:
  - 'LUWPbpM43E2p7ZSh8cyTBEkvpHmr3cB8Ez by the search, left: None' (Litecoin)
  - '0x9858EfFD…aEda94 by the search' (Ethereum)
  - '37VucYSaXLCAsxYyAPfbSi9eh4iEcbShgf by the search' (purpose 49)
  - 'bc1p5cyx…kedrcr by the search' (purpose 86)
  - 'dash1krma5z…e9n5rs by the search' (chains)
  
  By the same static trace, Tron, Zcash, Dogecoin, Ethereum Classic and Cosmos are uncovered too: none appears in SEARCHES or SEARCHES_STATED.
  
  Control: a wrong Dash coin type is noticed at startup ('address-search: search 5 of 5 is stated otherwise'). Dash Core, which the original candidate listed, is therefore not affected.
- **Impact:** A miscompiled or corrupted coin-type table, purpose mapping or chain mapping passes every runtime self-check, at startup and in mhfe self-test or the page's fullCheck.
  
  The address check of that coin or address type then searches the wrong paths. mhfe check and rekey with --coin X --address, and the browser's searchWallet, report 'does not match' (a rekey: REFERENCE_MISMATCH) for the right password. They also state a wrong Search or Type fact before the work.
  
  No secret is exposed and no container is changed. The practical effect is a misleading verdict on a build that self-checks were meant to catch, so the impact is bounded (low).
- **Evidence:** Logs under docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-coin-type-selfcheck/, each with a .command.json:
  - harness-mutations.log: exit 1, six FAIL lines and the PASS line of the Dash control.
  - mutate-none.log: control, all pass.
  - mutate-litecoin.log, mutate-ethereum.log, mutate-purpose49.log, mutate-purpose86.log, mutate-chains.log: the self-checks pass and the unit test fails.
  - mutate-dash.log: every_set_passes_at_startup, the_startup_set_stays_within_its_budget and the_address_search_is_stated_as_known fail with 'search 5 of 5 is stated otherwise'.
  
  Kept harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-coin-type-selfcheck/mutations.sh with its README.md.
  
  The original role's evidence, which agrees for Litecoin: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/coin-type-mutation.log.
  
  Static trace: grep for find_address, search_roots and AddressSearch in src/*/known_answers.rs. The only other address self-check case is rehearsal/known_answers.rs:220-230, a Bitcoin address at a stated path.
- **Recommended fix:** In SEARCHES_STATED (src/wallet/known_answers.rs), add one stated-search case per coin and per Bitcoin and Litecoin address type, taken from the existing ADDRESSES table: legacy, nested SegWit, native SegWit, Taproot, Keccak, Cosmos and Injective Bech32, XRP, Tron, Zcash, Dogecoin, Ethereum Classic {61,60}. AddressSearch::describe derives no key, so these cases cost microseconds and can run at startup. They cover every coin type and purpose.
  
  To cover the DIP17 chain mapping and the root loop themselves, add one full-tier find_address search of a Dash Platform row and of one row per coin type, with small SearchLimits.
  
  Alternatively, derive the stated cases from Coin::ALL with a test that fails when a coin has no stated-search case.
- **Required verification:** With the fix, docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-coin-type-selfcheck/mutations.sh exits 0, every line reading PASS. Repeat with mutations of the remaining coin types: Tron 195, Zcash 133, Dogecoin 3, Ethereum Classic 61, Cosmos 118, and Bitcoin Cash's and Ethereum Classic's second roots. The new cases must be shown failing, as a_search_stated_otherwise_or_accepted_fails does for the existing ones.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[18] (runtime self-tests verify search roots for only Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash and Dash Platform), AUD-024 [ARC] The startup and full self-checks do not cover four library answers that the front ends show (other answers, same kind of gap), AUD-024 [ARC] A coin's address rules are not held by Coin (where the coin rules live)
- **Verification:** confirmed: The defect reproduces at b6fca69, and I corrected two details.
  
  How I checked it: I re-read every cited location in full (src/wallet.rs, src/wallet/known_answers.rs, src/wallet/known_answers/addresses.rs, src/self_check/sets.rs). I checked statically that no other self-check part goes through Address::search_roots. The only other address case is rehearsal/known_answers.rs:220-230, a Bitcoin address at a stated path. I then mutated a git-archive copy of the crate and ran the reduced-cost self-check tests. No Argon2 runs.
  
  What the runs show:
  - An unmutated control passes every test.
  - Wrong coin types for Litecoin, Ethereum/Injective and XRP pass all of these: every_set_passes_at_startup, the_startup_set_stays_within_its_budget, the_address_check_passes (both tiers), the_address_search_is_stated_as_known (both tiers) and the_wallet_checks_pass.
  - The same holds for the nested SegWit purpose 49->48, the Taproot purpose 86->85, and DIP17 chains left unhardened in the find_address_until loop.
  - In every case only the unit test addresses_are_found_where_their_wallets_put_them fails.
  
  Corrections to the candidate:
  1. Dash Core is not affected. A wrong Dash coin type (5->6) is caught at startup: 'address-search: search 5 of 5 is stated otherwise' (mutate-dash.log). Dash Core's root m/44'/5' is never stated or searched, but both of its steps are checked: 44 through the Bitcoin Cash case, 5 through the Dash Platform case. So Dash Core comes out of the title and of the variants.
  2. The address-type purposes of the search are a variant the candidate missed. Nested SegWit 49 and Taproot 86 are checked by no self-check. They decide both the searched root and the 'Type' text that the CLI and describeAddress show.
  
  Rules and severity: I dropped CORE-26. Every coin came with runtime known answers for its encodings at a stated path, and with the unit test that searches every row, so no 'feature without checks' is shown. The finding rests on CORE-27 and CORE-30: the coin-specific search parameters that the address check states and uses have no known answer at startup or in the full self-test.
  
  Duplicates: this is not a duplicate. The closest confirmed finding, 'The startup and full self-checks do not cover four library answers…', is about rehearsal and rekey answers. The finding 'A coin's address rules are not held by Coin…' is about where the rules live, not whether they are checked. Both are related.
  
  Confidence is medium, not high. The reproduction is exact, but the expected behaviour reads CORE-27 as covering each coin's search root, which the rule does not state word for word. AUDIT_STANDARD keeps pure coverage gaps out of findings unless a concrete defect is described. AUD-023 recorded this as informationalObservations[18]. I confirm it under this audit's rule that a clear breach of a review rule is a finding, consistent with the confirmed 'four library answers' finding.

##### AUD-024-DOC001 — Low — AUD-023 records two defects that its skeptics established only as reasons under 'Refuted candidates', and records neither as a finding or a disposition. ##### AUD-024-DOC008 — Low — The browser API documentation was not updated with the AUD-023 changes to check() and rekey(): docs/API.md and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md (shipped as dist/README.md) still document check() as resolving to { matches, path, evidence: { builtInCheck, walletCheck } }, docs/API.md still gives the old matching rule for a stated length, and docs/API.md leaves out keepOldContainer() and the rekey result's `rehearsal`

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package documentation (docs/API.md browser section, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, shipped as dist/README.md)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06, CHECK-DOC-001, CHECK-DOC-002
- **Affected files and builds:** At b6fca69.
  
  docs/API.md:
  - :774: `onNoLength, // only with { words: 0 }: asked when detection finds no length`. Detection that finds several lengths also asks, and onNoLength receives the evidence (web/core-worker.js:155-160, web/client.d.ts:587-594).
  - :775: `}); // { matches, path, evidence: { builtInCheck, walletCheck } }`.
  - :776-781: the evidence is described without `matchingLengths` or `passed`.
  - :783-785: "A stated length { words: n } matches when the built-in check of any 12- to 21-word length passes, the stated one or another".
  - :830: `}); // a sealed container, as from encrypt, and walletCheck`, with no `rehearsal`.
  - :723-849: the MhfeClient listing has no `keepOldContainer()`.
  - :1002-1009: the WebAssembly exports paragraph has no `keepOldContainer`.
  
  docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:
  - :117: `const { matches, path, evidence } = await client.check({`.
  - :122: "matches is true".
  - :124: `evidence: { builtInCheck, walletCheck }`.
  - These lines contradict the same document's own :177-199, which already describe `outcome` and the four evidence fields.
  
  dist/README.md:117-124: the same three lines, in the coordinator's baseline build at b6fca69 (build de06b919b42eae2f). scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:54 writes dist/README.md from BROWSER-PACKAGE.md.
  
  What the package actually does:
  - web/client.d.ts:308 (MhfeCheckOutcome), :322-336 (MhfeCheckEvidence with matchingLengths and passed), :597-607 (`outcome`, no `matches`), :676-685 (`rehearsal`), :686-690 (`keepOldContainer`).
  - web/client.js:458-526 (check) and :538-551 (keepOldContainer).
  - src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:115-147 (`{"outcome", "path", "evidence"}`).
  - src/wasm_api/core.rs:250-256 (the keepOldContainer export).
  - src/rehearsal.rs:96-105 (CheckOutcome::of_length_rules) and src/detection.rs:69-94 (under_length_rules, verified_length).
  
  The stale lines were last changed in 3a705db6 and d52dff8b. 253ca3c changed the API and edited both documents (+70 and +133 lines) but did not update these lines.
- **Reproduction:** Run each command from the mhfe repository root.
  
  1. python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-doc-check-shape/check-doc-check-shape.py
     It prints 6 ok lines and 7 FAIL lines, and exits 1:
     - API.md line 775 documents a `matches` field.
     - BROWSER-PACKAGE.md lines 117, 122 and 124 document a `matches` field.
     - dist/README.md lines 117, 122 and 124 document a `matches` field.
     - The API.md MhfeClient listing (723-849) names neither keepOldContainer nor rehearsal (2 lines).
     - The API.md exports paragraph (line 1002) has no keepOldContainer.
     - API.md line 784 states the "any length passes" rule.
  
  2. python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/spec-parity/check-spec-parity.py
     It prints 66 ok lines and 3 FAIL lines (API.md [775], BROWSER-PACKAGE.md [117, 122], no client.keepOldContainer( in API.md), and exits 1.
  
  3. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<tmp>/aud024/target cargo test --locked --lib rehearsal::tests::several_matching_lengths_are_reported_and_not_verified -- --exact
     The test runs at reduced cost and passes. For the published ambiguous 12/21 phrase, a stated { words: 15 } or { words: 18 } gives CheckOutcome::NotVerified, with built_in_check None and matching_lengths [12, 21] (src/rehearsal.rs:800-805). API.md:783-785 says such a check matches.
  
  4. Static trace: with under_length_rules(Some(15)) over short [12, 21], none of the arms at src/detection.rs:73-80 applies, so it returns Readings::Several. verified_length then gives None (:89-93), and of_length_rules returns NotVerified (src/rehearsal.rs:99-104).
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-06 (docs.instructions.md, Check: review): a change that alters behaviour on purpose updates its documents in the same change.
  
  CHECK-DOC-002: examples are verified against the real API. CHECK-DOC-001: the user-facing documents match actual behaviour.
  
  The remediation's own release note, docs/releases/unreleased.md:15-18, says that in the browser package `check()` resolves to `outcome` ("matches", "notVerified" or "doesNotMatch") in place of `matches`, that `evidence.matchingLengths` lists the lengths, and that `onNoLength` receives the evidence.
  
  The specification, mhfe_spec README.md section Application requirements, Rehearsal check (:486-491), says the check reports "matches" only for exactly one verified reading under the length rules. If several lengths match and none of them was stated, it reports those lengths, and when it gives only unverified readings it reports "not verified".
  
  The specification's Preserving derived wallets MUST (:530-536) and Checking the replacement (:522-526) reach the browser through keepOldContainer() and the rekey result's `rehearsal` (client.d.ts:682-690). docs/API.md is the integrator API guide and lists every MhfeClient method and WebAssembly export, so it should name both.
- **Observed behavior:** The integrator guide, docs/API.md, and the README shipped in the package, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md copied to dist/README.md, still describe check() with the result shape from before AUD-023-FUN002: `{ matches, path, evidence: { builtInCheck, walletCheck } }`.
  
  The shipped example destructures `matches`, a field the package never returns, and says it "is true" for a container of the test phrase. The same README describes `outcome` correctly sixty lines later (:177-199), so it contradicts itself.
  
  API.md also states the old rule that a stated length matches whenever any short length passes. The code and the specification give "not verified" when several lengths pass and none of them was stated. API.md says onNoLength is asked only when no length is found.
  
  API.md's MhfeClient listing and its WebAssembly exports paragraph omit keepOldContainer(), and its rekey comment omits the result's `rehearsal`.
- **Impact:** A plain-JavaScript page that copies the shipped example gets `matches === undefined`. It would report every rehearsal as failed, a right password included. That can lead an owner to distrust a correct backup or to encrypt it again.
  
  An integrator who follows API.md expects a match where the code and the specification give "not verified" (a stated length among several lengths that pass).
  
  Such an integrator also does not learn from API.md of the two APIs that carry the specification's rekey MUSTs: the warning about derived wallets and the replacement rehearsal. BROWSER-PACKAGE.md does name both.
  
  The impact is bounded:
  - TypeScript users are protected by client.d.ts.
  - The code behaves correctly.
  - No secret is exposed.
- **Evidence:** Logs in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-doc-check-shape/, each with its .command.json:
  - doc-shape-probe.log and doc-shape-harness.log: exit 1, 7 FAIL lines as listed in the reproduction.
  - spec-parity-rerun.log: exit 1, 66 ok and 3 FAIL.

##### AUD-024-DOC009 — Low — The browser guide, shipped as the browser package's README.md, says the page's mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 protects against deliberate tampering, which SECURITY.md says it does not

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package documentation (fast mode)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-07, DOC-06, CHECK-DOC-001
- **Affected files and builds:** docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:740-742 ('What a browser cannot check', the bullet 'Deliberate tampering', unchanged since d52dff8 of 2026-10-07). Its shipped copy, dist/README.md:740-742, is in every browser package built from b6fca69, because scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:54 copies docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md whole into it. The sentence: 'Tampering is for `SHA256SUMS` and its OpenPGP signature, the build attestations and, in fast mode, the page's `mhfe-fast-mode.sha256`.' It contradicts SECURITY.md:222-226 and differs from SECURITY.md:290-293 and docs/API.md:1068-1069, which name only SHA256SUMS and its signature for tampering. The code this concerns: src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:181-209 (load_checked_page) and packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:472-498 (load_checked_page) compare the page only with the checksum file next to it. No release archive ships a page checksum file: scripts/package-release.sh does not name mhfe-fast-mode.sha256.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with an mhfe binary built from b6fca69 (no Argon2 runs; serve is stopped by timeout after 3 s):
  1. Read docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:740-742 next to SECURITY.md:222-226.
  2. In an empty folder, write tool.html and run `sha256sum tool.html > mhfe-fast-mode.sha256`.
  3. Replace tool.html with other content. `mhfe serve --no-browser tool.html` and `python3 packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py --no-browser tool.html` both refuse with exit 2: 'The page has changed or is not the one released'.
  4. Rewrite the checksum file too (`sha256sum tool.html > mhfe-fast-mode.sha256`) and run both launchers again. Both print 'SHA-256 of tool.html verified' and 'Fast mode is running' and serve the replaced page.
  Harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-fastmode-tamper-doc/check.sh <mhfe binary> <work folder>. It exits 1 at b6fca69.
- **Expected behavior:** SECURITY.md:222-226: the checksum file 'catches a damaged, swapped or partly updated page. It does not replace checking the release: someone who can change the page can change the checksum file next to it too, so compare the release files with the published `SHA256SUMS` once, after downloading.' SECURITY.md:290-293 and docs/API.md:1068-1069 likewise name only SHA256SUMS and its OpenPGP signature for deliberate tampering. DOC-07 (Promise only what is done, Check: review): documents claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides. DOC-06 (Code and documents agree, Check: review): disagreeing statements are named and settled.
- **Observed behavior:** The browser guide's list 'What a browser cannot check' names the page's mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 among the protections against deliberate tampering, beside SHA256SUMS with its signature and the build attestations. Both launchers verify and serve a replaced page whose checksum file was rewritten beside it, so this file catches accidental damage only. The guide's other passage about the file (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:756-765) does not repeat SECURITY.md's caveat either.
- **Impact:** Low. No code is wrong. A host-page author or user who reads the package README may take the fast-mode checksum for tamper protection. They may then skip checking the page and the launcher against SHA256SUMS and its OpenPGP signature, the one check that catches a deliberate replacement. DOC-07 counts an overstated guarantee as a security defect in itself, but the release does provide the correct check, and SECURITY.md describes it.
- **Evidence:** - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-fastmode-tamper-doc/v01-tampered-page-with-rewritten-checksum.log (exit 0, log SHA-256 470c6038096f3ccddb0d85c826c77c51541a994c3bc807880056e3b54f35989b). A replaced page beside the released checksum is refused by both launchers (exit 2). The same page with a rewritten checksum is verified and served by both (exit 124 from timeout while running). The log ends with the two document passages.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-fastmode-tamper-doc/v02-harness.log (exit 1, log SHA-256 72b84ca50e258a88d3668db5a81208368c335cd0cfc7d0c8bfa90822165a44f3): the kept harness reports both launchers serving the replaced page, prints the bullet, then FAIL.
  - docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser/g07-launcher-refusals.log (exit 0, log SHA-256 5a0c641f6db90df8d7959e6fb3f23cc1842e54e7e2704694f56e18d9ac24ad15): the 'matching' case, where a freshly written page and checksum are served by both launchers.
  - `cmp docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md dist/README.md`: identical up to line 1040, where dist adds its SHA-256 list (scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:54).
  - `git log -S"in fast" -- docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md` and `git blame -L 740,742` give d52dff8 (2026-10-07).
  - `grep -n mhfe-fast-mode scripts/package-release.sh` finds nothing.
- **Recommended fix:** Replace the sentence with SECURITY.md's wording. The page's mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 catches a damaged, swapped or partly updated page, not deliberate tampering, because whoever can change the page can change the checksum file too. Tampering is covered by SHA256SUMS with its OpenPGP signature and by the build attestations, checked once after download. Consider adding the same caveat to the checksum paragraph at docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:756-765. Rebuild dist/README.md.
- **Required verification:** docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md and the rebuilt dist/README.md no longer present mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 as tamper protection. SECURITY.md, docs/API.md and the browser guide agree on what covers tampering. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-fastmode-tamper-doc/check.sh exits 0.
- **Verification:** confirmed: At b6fca69, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:740-742 says verbatim: "Tampering is for `SHA256SUMS` and its OpenPGP signature, the build attestations and, in fast mode, the page's `mhfe-fast-mode.sha256`." scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:54 copies this file whole into dist/README.md, so the same text sits at dist/README.md:740-742 of the baseline build. git blame traces the three lines to d52dff8 (2026-10-07). SECURITY.md:222-226 says the checksum file catches only a damaged, swapped or partly updated page, because "someone who can change the page can change the checksum file next to it too". SECURITY.md:290-293 and docs/API.md:1068-1069 name only SHA256SUMS and its signature for tampering.
  
  I reproduced it myself with two runs, logged as v01 and v02. I replaced a page and kept the released checksum file: both launchers refused with exit 2. I then rewrote mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 beside the replaced page: both mhfe serve (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:181-209) and packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py (472-498) printed 'SHA-256 of tool.html verified' and served it. The launchers check the page only against the file next to it, and package-release.sh ships no page checksum, so nothing signed covers that file. The guide therefore claims a stronger guarantee than the code gives (DOC-07), and its documents disagree (DOC-06). This is not an AUD-023 finding and not a duplicate of any confirmed finding.

##### AUD-024-DOC010 — Low — The browser documents and comments say that the Argon2 build's 1 MiB known answer runs before a rekey's confirmation refusals, but RekeySession::recover refuses before it runs any known answer, unlike check()

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package documentation and WebAssembly bindings (rekey)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** Documents and comments that make the claim:
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:252-253, shipped as dist/README.md:252-253: '`REFERENCE_REQUIRED` before the first round (only the 1 MiB known answer of the Argon2 build runs first, as for `check()`)'.
  - docs/API.md:921-922: 'All these refusals come before the first round; in a browser the worker has then run only the small known answer of its Argon2 build'. This covers rekey's REFERENCE_REQUIRED and the walletHasPassphrase INVALID_REQUEST refusals.
  - web/client.js:706-707, also dist/core/client.js:706-707: 'These refusals come before the first round; only the 1 MiB known answer of the Argon2 build runs first.'
  - src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:219-221: 'only the Argon2 build's 1 MiB known answer runs before them'.
  
  The code:
  - src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:104-129 (with_rekey_confirmation): the refusals of the kind, of a passphrase with builtInCheck or owner, and of the reference come first.
  - src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:251: passphrase_answer.
  - src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:252-255: check_confirmation. In src/rekey.rs:236-243, refuse_for gives REFERENCE_REQUIRED and wallet_passphrase (src/rekey.rs:342) gives the INVALID_REQUEST answer refusals.
  - All of these run before mhfe_with at src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:258, the only place that runs verify_known_answer (src/wasm_api/core.rs:646-653).
  - RekeySession::new (rekey.rs:146) and set_new (rekey.rs:183) run no Argon2.
  - web/core-worker.js:266-288 (rekey) and :420-424 (argon2For) start the build without a known answer, and :370-380 (recoverConfirmed) calls session.recover.
  
  Contrast: in CheckSession::new (src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:104), mhfe_for runs the known answer before recover_for_check_in_stages. So the library's own refusals in check() do follow the known answer, as docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:168-170 says.
  
  Builds affected: the browser package (every mode). The command-line tool is not affected.
- **Reproduction:** Run from the repository root, with the browser package built (dist/ and target/wasm-bindgen from the baseline):
  
  node /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/skeptic-rekey-known-answer/probe.mjs
  
  The probe loads scripts/package-check/package.mjs and passes an Argon2 bridge that records each derive call, alters the tag of the 1 MiB known answer and throws on any other cost. It runs:
  1. A RekeySession on REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER with words 0, setNew, then recover('builtInCheck', ..., false).
  2. The same at 12 words with walletHasPassphrase undefined.
  3. The same with walletHasPassphrase "no".
  4. Control: the same at 12 words with false, an accepted confirmation.
  5. Control: a CheckSession on REDUCED_COST_SAME_LENGTH_CONTAINER with reference kind 'words'.
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-06 (Code and documents agree) requires that the documents and comments state the code's behaviour. Here they say that in a rekey, as in check(), the Argon2 build's 1 MiB known answer runs before REFERENCE_REQUIRED and the walletHasPassphrase refusals. So a refusal would arrive only after the known answer had run, and an Argon2 build that fails its known answer would surface as SELF_CHECK_FAILED first.
- **Observed behavior:** In rekey(), no known answer runs before these refusals.
  
  The probe gives 0 Argon2 derive calls before each of these refusals:
  - REFERENCE_REQUIRED (case 1).
  - 'INVALID_REQUEST: invalid request: say whether the wallet has a BIP39 passphrase' (case 2).
  - 'INVALID_REQUEST: ... walletHasPassphrase must be true or false ...' (case 3).
  
  The same faulty build gives one derive call (1024/1) and SELF_CHECK_FAILED in both controls: an accepted rekey confirmation (case 4) and a check() reference the library refuses (case 5).
  
  So check() runs the known answer before its library refusals, and rekey() refuses before running any Argon2. Even with a broken Argon2 build, rekey() reports the confirmation refusal and not SELF_CHECK_FAILED.
- **Impact:** A page author or reviewer is misled about which checks have run when a rekey refusal arrives. With a faulty Argon2 build, the page gets REFERENCE_REQUIRED or INVALID_REQUEST instead of the SELF_CHECK_FAILED the documents lead it to expect. There is no security impact: no secret reaches Argon2, and refusing earlier is safer.
- **Evidence:** Probe log: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/skeptic-rekey-known-answer/rekey-refusal-order.log (exit 0, 2026-10-14T11:24:04Z; log SHA-256 0555e44ca7be93d1ffe3a82eee8c5a7063c89cd8d6aeefa65171601bd6cff95d). The command record is rekey-refusal-order.command.json beside the log. Cases 1-3: 0 derive calls before the refusal. Cases 4-5: 1 derive call [1024/1], then SELF_CHECK_FAILED.
  
  Source read at b6fca69:
  - src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:1-275
  - src/wasm_api/core.rs:1-30 and :600-690
  - src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:60-150
  - src/rekey.rs:236-268
  - web/core-worker.js:258-312, :365-385 and :410-540
  - web/argon2-engine.js:1-80
  - web/client.js:145-300 and :690-720
  - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:160-175 and :240-265
  - docs/API.md:900-926 and :960-972
  
  A grep shows these are the only places that make the claim, apart from the audit records. The existing package check (scripts/package-check/core-rekey.mjs:440-480) asserts only that no Argon2 round ran, never whether the known answer did.
- **Recommended fix:** Correct the four texts. One wording: 'these refusals come before any Argon2 work, the build's known answer included; check() runs that known answer before its own refusals'. This applies to docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:252-253, docs/API.md:921-922, web/client.js:706-707 and src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:219-221. Then rebuild dist/ so that dist/README.md and dist/core/client.js follow. If the documented order is the intended one, instead move passphrase_answer and check_confirmation after mhfe_with in RekeySession::recover. Either way, add a package-check case with an Argon2 bridge that fails its known answer, which pins the order chosen.
- **Required verification:** Doc review of the four texts and of the rebuilt dist/README.md and dist/core/client.js. Also re-run the probe, or an equivalent package-check case: its outcome must match the corrected text, either 0 derive calls before REFERENCE_REQUIRED or INVALID_REQUEST, or SELF_CHECK_FAILED after one 1024/1 call if the code is changed instead.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[21] (docs say the Argon2 known answer runs before a rekey's confirmation refusals; none runs), recorded there as an observation, not a finding
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced the defect at b6fca69. I ran the built package's WebAssembly bindings (the dist/ and target/wasm-bindgen output of baseline b12/b14) with an Argon2 bridge that records every derive call and fails its 1 MiB known answer. No round runs at any cost.
  
  The rekey refusals come with 0 derive calls:
  - REFERENCE_REQUIRED, for { builtInCheck } at a detected length on a 24-word container.
  - INVALID_REQUEST, for walletHasPassphrase left out.
  - INVALID_REQUEST, for walletHasPassphrase "no".
  
  The two controls each make exactly one derive call (1024/1, the known answer) and end with SELF_CHECK_FAILED:
  - A rekey whose confirmation is accepted.
  - A check() whose reference the library refuses (the built-in check on a same-length container).
  
  So check() runs the known answer before its refusals and rekey() does not, as the candidate says.
  
  The source trace agrees:
  - RekeySession::new and setNew run no Argon2.
  - The worker's argon2For starts the build without a known answer.
  - recover() calls passphrase_answer (rekey.rs:251) and check_confirmation (rekey.rs:252-255; src/rekey.rs:236-243 refuse_for gives REFERENCE_REQUIRED and wallet_passphrase gives INVALID_REQUEST) before mhfe_with (rekey.rs:258), the only place that calls verify_known_answer (core.rs:651).
  
  The candidate missed a fourth document that makes the same claim: docs/API.md:921-922.
  
  This is not a duplicate. AUD-023 recorded it only as informational observation [21], not as a finding, and its remediation moved the code into src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs but kept the false sentence. It breaches DOC-06 (Check: review, so it applies in this audit). It is low severity per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a documentation defect with bounded practical impact.

##### AUD-024-DOC011 — Low — The host-page duties in BROWSER-PACKAGE.md omit three application MUSTs of the specification, although the release note says they include every application rule. The three: send no secret or derived value over a network; ask the user not to rely on an unverified container until its check ends; do not call a replacement checked, or advise discarding the old backup, before its rehearsal.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package documentation for host pages: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md "What the page should do", shipped as dist/README.md, and the onUnverified API comments
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-07, DOC-06, CHECK-DOC-001
- **Affected files and builds:** docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:809-997, "What the page should do". It introduces itself (:811-812) as what "The specification and the command-line tool ask applications to do".
  
  Variant 1 (network, MUST NOT):
  - No duty line mentions a network, sending, telemetry or remote reporting.
  - Only :47-49 names `connect-src 'none'`, as an example policy the package works under.
  - :788-791 lists "no network" as a protection a page lacks.
  
  Variant 2 (unverified container, MUST):
  - :886-891 asks only to mark the container "not yet verified" and then report how the check ended.
  - web/client.js:374-377 and web/client.d.ts:538-539, the onUnverified comments, have the same omission.
  
  Variant 3 (replacement, MUST NOT):
  - :923-930 (rekey) and :975-980 (rehearsal) never forbid describing the new container as checked, or advising discard of the old container, before its rehearsal.
  - keepOldContainer() (src/wasm_api/core.rs:245-256, web/client.js:540-551) covers only the derived-wallets warning.
  
  Variant 4 (offline, SHOULD-level):
  - :905 asks for a trusted offline computer for recovery only.
  - Creation and the check (:918-922) carry no such duty; only the link table row at :1003 points to Getting started.
  
  The claim: docs/releases/unreleased.md:70-71, "the host page's duties include every application rule of the specification", added in 253ca3c.
  
  Shipping: the text ships verbatim as dist/README.md (scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:54), so every browser package build is affected.
  
  Command-line counterparts that meet the rules:
  - src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:421-438, with :433 "Not verified yet: write it down, but wait for the check."
  - src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:430-449: "Old backup" at :444-445 and "Next" rehearse at :447.
  - SECURITY.md:116-119 says the package and tool connect to no network.
- **Reproduction:** From the mhfe root, run /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-page-duties/probe.sh. For each rule it prints the specification lines and every matching line of BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:809-997, using whole-word patterns:
  - R1: network, send, sent, connect, telemetry, upload, remote.
  - R2: rely, "wait for the check", "until the check".
  - R3: discard, destroy, "replacement ... checked", "new container ... checked".
  
  All three print NONE, and the probe exits 1 with "Rules without an answering duty: 3 of 3".
  
  The probe also prints:
  - the duty text that does exist at :886-891, :923-930 and :975-980;
  - the onUnverified comments in web/client.js and web/client.d.ts;
  - the command-line counterparts;
  - the release note line and its commit;
  - the dist/README.md source line.
- **Expected behavior:** From the specification, mhfe_spec/README.md "Application requirements" (:465) and "Creating a container":
  - :556-560: "In every case, implementations MUST NOT send the password, the BIP39 passphrase, the source or recovered mnemonic, or any value derived from them over a network".
