##### AUD-024-DOC012 — Low — The browser documents list incompletely the endings that free a worker's secrets without overwriting them, the secret-derived results that reach the page as strings, and the work that holds secrets in a worker for longer. A failing page callback or answer (CALLBACK_FAILED), like PACKAGE_MISMATCH, an unknown worker message or a failed send, terminates the worker with its Rust session unfreed. readPhrase() and wordHints() return secret-derived strings. A rekey waiting for the owner or onConfirmAgain, and a check waiting for onNoLength, keep their sessions for as long as the page takes.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Browser package documentation of secret lifetimes (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, SECURITY.md) against web/runtime.js, web/worker-runtime.js, web/core-worker.js
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-002
- **Rules:** DOC-06, DOC-07
- **Affected files and builds:** Documents (all builds of the browser package): docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1017-1040 'What the browser cannot wipe'. Lines 1022-1025 say the Rust code overwrites its buffers and states. Lines 1030-1036 name only a cancelled operation, a hidden-wallet session closed during an open and a trap as endings without that overwrite. Lines 1036-1039 list the JavaScript strings; neither readPhrase()'s written-out phrase nor wordHints() results are listed. Lines 533-538 say a failing callback ends the worker but say nothing about memory. Lines 484-485 argue that hints are public. SECURITY.md:243-247 names only cancel and a failed Argon2 round as freed without overwriting. SECURITY.md:248-255 says 'Two kinds of work hold secrets in workers for longer' (hidden-wallet session, multi-worker draw). SECURITY.md:259-268 has Rust wiping its states, with only the trap as an exception. SECURITY.md:269-273 is the string list. Code: web/runtime.js:315-326 (stop) and 328-335 (#terminate) terminate at once. web/runtime.js:414-429 (callPage): a throwing or rejecting onProgress or onUnverified stops the job. web/runtime.js:436-453 (#answer): when the answer callback fails, the catch at 448-452 stops the job and sends no answer. web/runtime.js:395-406 (#started): PACKAGE_MISMATCH after the worker has the request. web/runtime.js:355, 375 and 440: unknown messages. web/runtime.js:292-303 (send): WORKER_FAILED. web/client.js:1512-1519: the owner wrapper turns any failure into CALLBACK_FAILED. web/client.js:1390-1411 (answerNoLength): a refused answer throws a TypeError, which becomes CALLBACK_FAILED. web/worker-runtime.js:100-105 (ask: no time limit) and 243-252 (withSession frees only after use() returns). web/core-worker.js:142-167 (check waits on noLength at 158-160), 278-308 (rekey waits on ownerCheck at 291-296) and 393-396 (confirmAgain). src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:43-55: RekeySession holds the old-password Rekey, new_password and the recovered state. src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:58-67: CheckSession holds the recovered state. Strings: web/client.js:330-336 (readPhrase requires a string) with src/wasm_api/core.rs:114-138 (describePhrase returns the phrase written out). web/runtime.js:745-748, web/wallet.d.ts:76 and web/passwords.d.ts:58 (typed: MhfeSecret, so it may be bytes) with src/wasm_api/word_hints.rs:28-59 (the result's buffer is wiped as secret, then becomes a JS string).
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, using the kept in-process harness docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/browser-isolation/in-process-worker.mjs (the built dist/ classes, the real runtime/worker.js and reduced-cost Argon2 at 256 KiB and one pass):
  (1) node --no-warnings ../tmp/aud024/verify-callback-wipe/probe.mjs runs client.rekey() on REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER, words 12, password 'public test password', a distinctive new password, and confirmation { owner } with four owners: one that throws, one that rejects (async), and the controls 'no' (false) and 'yes' (true). For each it records the messages from page to worker, whether the worker sent result or error, termination, and the number of copies of the new password in the worker's WebAssembly memory.
  (2) node --no-warnings ../tmp/aud024/verify-callback-wipe/probe-check-session.mjs runs client.check() on the same container with a distinctive wrong password, reference { words: 0 }, and onNoLength set to: throws, answers { words: 0 } (refused by the class), or null (control).
  (3) node --no-warnings ../tmp/aud024/verify-callback-wipe/probe-strings.mjs: MhfeWallet.wordHints({ typed: bytes of the test phrase up to 'abo' }), MhfeClient.readPhrase(bytes) and readPhrase('ABAN ... ABOU').
  (4) Static trace of the stop paths listed under affected.
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-07 (docs.instructions.md:41-45): documents claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides. DOC-06 (docs.instructions.md:36-39): code and documents agree. docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1022-1036 and SECURITY.md:243-247 and 259-268 present the Rust overwrite as how a worker's secrets end, and list the exceptions in which memory is freed without being overwritten (cancel, a close during an open, a trap, a failed Argon2 round). BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1036-1039 and SECURITY.md:269-273 list what reaches the page as unerasable strings. SECURITY.md:248 presents 'two kinds of work' as those that hold secrets in workers for longer. AUD-023-API002 and AUD-023-DOC006 were fixed by adding the trap and stack-copy cases to these same lists, so the lists are meant to be complete.
- **Observed behavior:** Rekey, owner throws or rejects: the rekey rejects with CALLBACK_FAILED ('The page's owner callback failed.'). The worker is terminated. Page to worker: ['rekey'] only, with no answer. Worker to page: ready, progress, ask:ownerCheck, with no result or error. So withSession never frees the RekeySession, and 1 copy of the new password stays in WebAssembly memory. Controls: 'no' rejects with NOT_CONFIRMED_BY_OWNER and 'yes' seals. Both send ['rekey','answer'], end in the worker, and leave 0 copies of the new password. Check, onNoLength throws or answers { words: 0 }: CALLBACK_FAILED ('The page's noLength callback failed.'), page to worker ['rekey'-style request 'check'] only, the worker never ends, and the CheckSession with its recovered state is never freed. The password itself is already gone (0 copies; CheckSession::new drops it before asking), so for a check only the recovered state is held. The null control sends the answer and the check resolves 'notVerified'. Statically, the same terminate-without-free path follows a failing onProgress or onUnverified (callPage), PACKAGE_MISMATCH after the worker started the request, an unknown worker message, and a failed postMessage (WORKER_FAILED). In a real browser a terminated worker's memory is freed without being overwritten, as for cancel. None of these endings is named in the exception lists. Strings: readPhrase(bytes) is refused ('TypeError: phrase must be a string.'). readPhrase('ABAN ... ABOU').phrase is the 12 words written out, as a string. wordHints on bytes of '... abo' returns {"hint":"words","words":["about","above"]} as strings; for a unique prefix the hint is the secret word itself. The Rust binding wipes that result's buffer because it 'tells its last letters' (word_hints.rs:33-35), yet the string the page receives is in neither string list; BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:484-485 only argues that hints are public. Waits: host.ask (worker-runtime.js:100-105) and #answer (runtime.js:436-453) have no time limit. A rekey waiting on ownerCheck or confirmAgain keeps the RekeySession (old and new password, recovered state), and a check waiting on noLength keeps the CheckSession. SECURITY.md:248-255 names only the hidden-wallet session and the draw, and no text asks the page to cancel such a wait when the user leaves.
- **Impact:** A page author or reviewer who relies on these lists will believe that a failing callback (including a buggy owner, onConfirmAgain or onNoLength callback, or a malformed answer) ends with the Rust code's own overwrite. They will not treat readPhrase()'s phrase or wordHints() results as unerasable secret strings, and will not cancel a rekey or check that is left waiting for the user. The real exposure equals the documented cancel case: memory freed without being overwritten, possibly swapped. That exposure is bounded, so the severity is low (AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a documentation defect with bounded practical impact).
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-callback-wipe/v1-owner-callback-failure.log (+ .command.json, exit 0): the owner-throws and owner-rejects rows against the no and yes controls, as described above. v2-no-length-callback-failure.log (exit 1, by design: it refutes the sub-claim that a check keeps the password, with 0 copies in every case). v3-no-length-session-unfreed.log (exit 0): CheckSession never freed after CALLBACK_FAILED; the null control answers and ends. v4-secret-strings.log (exit 0): wordHints on bytes returns ['about','above']; readPhrase(bytes) gives TypeError; readPhrase(string).phrase is written out. These agree with the candidate's docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/browser-isolation/p1-callback-failed-wipe.log (new password 1 copy against 0 in the control) and p3-js-strings.log. Probes: ../tmp/aud024/verify-callback-wipe/probe.mjs, probe-check.mjs, probe-check-session.mjs and probe-strings.mjs. dist/ is the baseline build of b6fca69; browser-isolation/p7-dist-matches-sources.log shows it differs from web/ only in build ids.
- **Recommended fix:** In docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md 'What the browser cannot wipe' and in the SECURITY.md browser bullets, name every ending that terminates a worker without the session's own wipe: a page callback or answer that fails or is refused (CALLBACK_FAILED, including the owner callback, which ends while the recovered phrase and both passwords are held), PACKAGE_MISMATCH or an unknown worker message, and WORKER_FAILED. Alternatively, state the rule positively: only an operation that resolves, or rejects with an error from the worker, ends with the overwrite. Add readPhrase()'s written-out phrase (a phrase can only be passed as a string) and wordHints() results to the strings a page cannot erase. Replace 'Two kinds of work' with a list that also names a rekey waiting for the owner or onConfirmAgain (old and new password, recovered state) and a check waiting for onNoLength (recovered state), and advise the page to cancel() them when the user leaves. Optionally, in WorkerJob.#answer, send the worker a closing answer (null) before stopping when an answer callback fails, so that the session is freed and wiped before the worker ends.
- **Required verification:** Documentation review against web/runtime.js (stop, callPage, #answer, #started, send) and web/core-worker.js (the ask points). If the optional code change is made, rerun ../tmp/aud024/verify-callback-wipe/probe.mjs adapted to expect 0 copies of the new password after the owner-throws and owner-rejects cases, and probe-check-session.mjs adapted to expect a page-to-worker 'answer' and a worker 'error' or 'result' after a failing onNoLength.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-API002, AUD-023-DOC006, AUD-023-SEC001
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 with reduced-cost Argon2 probes and a static trace. The candidate needed two corrections. Rekey: when the owner callback throws or rejects, the job rejects with CALLBACK_FAILED and the worker is terminated. The page sends nothing after the request, so the worker never returns from host.ask and withSession never frees the RekeySession, and 1 copy of the new password stays in WebAssembly memory. The two controls are the owner answering no (NOT_CONFIRMED_BY_OWNER, ended inside the worker) and yes (sealed). In both the page sends the answer, the worker ends, and 0 copies remain. Check with onNoLength: a callback that throws, or an answer the class refuses ({ words: 0 }, a TypeError), also ends with CALLBACK_FAILED and leaves the CheckSession unfreed. That session holds only the recovered state, not the password: CheckSession::new drops the password before the page is asked, and my scan found 0 copies. The same terminate-without-wipe path is taken by a failing onProgress or onUnverified (callPage), by PACKAGE_MISMATCH after the request was sent, by an unknown worker message and by a failed send (WORKER_FAILED). None of these endings is named where the documents list the cases in which memory is freed without being overwritten; those lists name only cancel, a close during an open, a trap and a failed Argon2 round. Strings: readPhrase accepts the phrase only as a string (bytes are refused with a TypeError) and returns it written out. wordHints given the typed line as bytes returns the matching list words as strings. Neither result is in the string lists. SECURITY.md's 'Two kinds of work' leaves out the rekey and check waits, which have no time limit. TS-07 is dropped: the code does not break it, and this is a documentation defect (DOC-06, DOC-07).

Its list states the output of encrypt (:515-517), repair (:532-534) and repair-words (:535-536). The decrypt --help (decrypt.rs:80-82) gives the output as one line per result, '<words> <verified|unverified> <phrase>'. DOC-06 (code and documents agree) and CHECK-DOC-001 (README and tool help must match actual behaviour, including each utility's accepted input and output) require the README's script contract to state it.
- **Observed behavior:** The README's decrypt bullet gives the input only. Neither README.md, SECURITY.md nor docs/*.md gives the result line format, the word count and status prefix, or the fact that a recovery with several passing readings writes several lines to standard output. The decrypt section (README.md:278-283) says several readings are shown, but not in what form a script receives them. The format has been in the code since cc91b0b (0.4.0). The README script list has never stated it, although outputs of other commands were added to that list later. AUD-023's CHECK-API-003 review recorded the README script formats as matching the code without noting the gap.

A wallet import of such a line fails because '24' and 'verified' are not BIP39 words, so no wrong wallet is silently produced. ##### AUD-024-DOC014 — Low — The command-line tool and README.md show master key fingerprints (under every phrase shown at a terminal, in the rekey summary's Next line, and in the check summary and result) without the sentence "They do not reveal the phrase." that DOC-05 attaches to showing them openly

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: fingerprint wording
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-API-003
- **Rules:** DOC-05
- **Affected files and builds:** Command-line tool, all platforms and builds (the browser package is not affected: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:901-904 and src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:144 carry the sentence).
  - src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:502-528 (print_fingerprint; the eprintln! at :522-527 prints only the label, the fingerprint and the note "(of the container itself, not your wallet)" / "(no BIP39 passphrase)" / "(with your BIP39 passphrase)" / "(if the wallet has no BIP39 passphrase)" from :509-512). print_phrase :473-484 reaches it from decrypt.rs:412, encrypt.rs:430, rekey.rs:604, container_repair.rs:508, wallets.rs:156 and new_wallet.rs:342, so it covers every phrase shown at a terminal.
  - src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:447 and :453-465 (next_rehearsal: the summary's Next line "rehearse the new container phrase with mhfe check --fingerprint and fingerprint <hex>", printed on the main screen after the private screen has closed).
  - src/bin/mhfe/check/wallet_reference.rs:156-161 with read_public :284-286 (summary record "Master key fingerprint <hex>" for --fingerprint), and :87-91 with :111 (summary record "Reference  master key fingerprint <hex>" for a fingerprint typed at the reference menu). The same text is listed in check's result as "the container's own wallet: master key fingerprint <hex>" via container_search.rs:313 and check.rs:553-554.
  - README.md:165-170 (describes the fingerprint line under shown phrases) and README.md:314-316 (the rekey gives the fingerprint for rehearsing); neither carries the sentence.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, at b6fca69, with the debug binary built by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target cargo build --locked --bin mhfe` (up to date):
  1. `printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "abandon x23 art" 'public test password' 73c5da0a | NO_COLOR=1 mhfe check --stdin --fingerprint --pim 0 --mem 0`. It is refused before any Argon2 round (exit 2, the passphrase line is missing), and the summary on standard error contains "  Master key fingerprint 73c5da0a" with no sentence after it. Wrapped in tmp/aud024/verify-doc05-fingerprint/probe_text.sh (exit 1 = defect present), which also runs `grep -rn -i reveal src/bin README.md`: only README.md:60 and :374 match, both unrelated.
  2. In a pseudo-terminal (TERM=xterm-256color), run `mhfe repair`, type the public container with word 3 as ?, then the public 4-word repair card "letter wealth borrow cable" (no Argon2). The private screen shows the repaired container, then "Master key fingerprint 5436d724  (of the container itself, not your wallet)", then "Write it down now: Enter or Escape clears this screen.", with no sentence. Script: tmp/aud024/verify-doc05-fingerprint/pty_repair.py (exit 1 = defect present).
  3. Static: rekey.rs:455-459 formats the Next line with the fingerprint and nothing else. Reaching it at runtime needs a full-cost rekey confirmed by the owner, which was not run.
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-05 (/home/user/.../bip_tools/.github/instructions/docs.instructions.md:30-34): "An original or recovered wallet fingerprint, and every encoded or container fingerprint, may be shown openly, with the sentence 'They do not reveal the phrase.'" Line 7 of that file says DOC-05 covers every text a person reads, terminal included. DOC-05 is Check: review, so it applies to the whole repository in this audit. The same library's other front ends apply the rule this way. mhfe's own docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:901-904 tells host pages to show the fingerprints openly and says "They do not reveal the phrase." The workspace's MHFE page (multi-chain-wallet-tools apps/key-derivation/src/ui/recovery-mhfe-cards.ts:26-28) adds "It does not reveal the phrase." to every fingerprint line, with the same notes as terminal.rs:509-512. mnemocode does the same in docs/SSKR.md:40 and src/cli/help-pages.ts:790.
- **Observed behavior:** No text of the command-line tool and no part of README.md carries the sentence. Every fingerprint the tool shows, under a phrase, in the rekey summary, or in the check summary and result, goes without it. The browser package's documents and wasm doc comment are the only places in the repository that carry it.
- **Impact:** Low. A person sees an eight-hex-digit fingerprint next to a phrase, or left on the main screen in the rekey and check summaries, and is not told that noting or showing it does not reveal the phrase. The command-line tool also departs from the wording the project asks host pages to use for the same values. No secret is exposed. The tool never calls fingerprints "public" or "not secrets" (grep found no such wording), and README.md:240-241 already advises keeping a reference apart from the container.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-doc05-fingerprint/build-debug.log (cargo build --locked --bin mhfe, exit 0, up to date). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-doc05-fingerprint/probe-text.log (+ .command.json; exit 1: the check summary line "Master key fingerprint 73c5da0a" without the sentence; grep -i reveal over src/bin and README.md finds only README.md:60 and :374; the static excerpts of rekey.rs:447/453-465, terminal.rs:521-528, wallet_reference.rs:87-91/111/156-161 and check.rs:547/553-554; the sentence found only at src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:144 and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:903; the multi-chain recovery-mhfe-cards.ts:27). docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-doc05-fingerprint/pty-repair-fingerprint.log (+ .command.json; exit 1: "FINGERPRINT LINE: 'Master key fingerprint 5436d724  (of the container itself, not your wallet)'", no sentence on the screen). The candidate's own log docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/output-and-scripts.log:61 shows the same summary line. Probe scripts: /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-doc05-fingerprint/probe_text.sh and pty_repair.py, which reuses the cli-ux ptydrive.py read-only.
- **Recommended fix:** Add the sentence wherever the tool shows a fingerprint. Under a shown phrase, extend the note at terminal.rs:522-527, e.g. "(of the container itself, not your wallet). It does not reveal the phrase." Add it to the rekey summary's Next line, or a line right after it (rekey.rs:453-465). Add it once to the check summary or result where a fingerprint reference is recorded (wallet_reference.rs:90/159, container_search.rs:313). Add the sentence to README.md:165-170 and README.md:314-316. It can also go in the explanations of what a fingerprint is (check.rs:115-122 --fingerprint help, length_choice.rs:68-71 hint).
- **Required verification:** Unit tests: next_rehearsal(ReplacementRehearsal::Fingerprint(..)) and the fingerprint line under a phrase both contain the sentence. Rerun probe_text.sh and pty_repair.py (both must exit 0). Review README.md.
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. (1) mhfe check --stdin --fingerprint uses public data and is refused before any Argon2 round (exit 2). Its summary prints "Master key fingerprint 73c5da0a" with no sentence. (2) In a pseudo-terminal, mhfe repair with the public container shows "Master key fingerprint 5436d724  (of the container itself, not your wallet)" under the repaired phrase, again with no sentence. (3) A static trace of rekey.rs:447/453-465 shows the summary's Next line naming the recovered wallet's fingerprint on the main screen, also without the sentence. Running that path for real would need a full-cost rekey, but the text is a plain format!. grep -i reveal over src/bin and README.md finds only two unrelated README lines. Reading DOC-05 as "a fingerprint shown openly comes with the sentence" matches the project's own browser host-page duties (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:901-904). It also matches the sibling front end of the same library: multi-chain recovery-mhfe-cards.ts:26-28 adds the sentence to every fingerprint line and uses the same notes as terminal.rs. One correction to the candidate: it said no document carries the sentence, but docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:903-904 and src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:144 do. The defect is therefore limited to the command-line tool and README.md. No AUD-023 finding or already-confirmed AUD-024 finding covers fingerprint wording. Severity stays low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md: a presentation and documentation defect with bounded impact.

##### AUD-024-DOC015 — Low — Where no private screen can open (TERM=dumb, or a Windows console without VT processing), mhfe password, decrypt, encrypt and rekey print the new password, the recovered phrase or the new container on the main screen, where it stays in the scrollback, with no wait. README.md and SECURITY.md say that at a terminal displayed secrets appear only on the private screen and never reach the scrollback.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** cli-ux: private screen and documents
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-API-003
- **Rules:** DOC-07, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** Native CLI on every platform, at any terminal where hidden_input::can_redraw() is false: TERM=dumb (hidden_input.rs:287-292, test at :290), or a Windows console that refuses VT processing (hidden_input/windows.rs:78-86, not run). Mechanism: private_screen.rs:137-139 terminal_screen_possible -> :114-116 can_show_privately -> :173-180 enter_steps returns false, so flow.rs:72-85 Flow::start is inactive; private_screen.rs:57-59 and :79 enter_to_show is inactive. Variants: (1) mhfe password: diceware.rs:230-231 start() gets an inactive Flow; show() at :265-283 prints the password at :267-268 whenever stdout is a terminal, and waits only if flow::is_active() (:278-280). The doc comments at :228-229 and :262-264 say the password is 'on a step of its own that is cleared'. (2) mhfe decrypt: decrypt.rs:212 enter_to_show is inactive; :216-219 show_single/show_ambiguous -> print_result :399-414 -> terminal::print_phrase (terminal.rs:473-485) prints the recovered phrase to stdout. :220-228 has no wait, only the hint at :227 'When you are done, clear the screen and close this terminal.' The comment at :211 says the result 'appears on a screen of its own, which is cleared'. (3) mhfe encrypt, and mhfe rekey through rekey.rs:414: encrypt.rs:255 person_reads_output is true (output_on_screen does not test TERM); :271 enter_to_show is inactive; :276 show_before_the_check (:421-439) prints the not-yet-verified container on the main screen; :307-315 waits only if screen.is_active(). The comment at :267-269 says it 'should leave no copy in the terminal's history'. Own rule contradicted: made_password.rs:105-107, 'a made password is shown only on a private screen, as a new phrase is, never on the main screen of a terminal that cannot switch (AUD-015-SEC003)'. Documents: SECURITY.md:13-19 and :50-53; README.md:153-156, :217-218, :269.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: python3 docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-dumb-private-screen/probe.py <path to mhfe built at b6fca69>. Case A runs mhfe password in a pseudo-terminal at TERM=dumb. The password line is written, ESC[?1049h is not written, the process has already exited 0 after 3 s, and no key was asked for. Case B is the control at TERM=xterm-256color. The password is written after ESC[?1049h, the tool waits, and Enter writes ESC[2J ESC[H ESC[?1049l without repeating the password. Case C runs mhfe repair-words --count 4 with the public 'abandon x23 art' container. It exercises PrivateScreen::enter_to_show, the call decrypt.rs:212 makes. At TERM=dumb no ESC[?1049h is written and the card is printed on the main screen with no wait; at xterm the alternate screen opens and the tool waits. The probe exits 1 while the defect is present. decrypt, encrypt and rekey reach their display only after suite-cost Argon2. Static trace for them: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dumb-private-screen/static-trace.log. A full-cost run would show the same, but the trace is unambiguous: no refusal or can_show_privately test lies on those paths before the display.
- **Expected behavior:** SECURITY.md:13-17: 'At a terminal they are typed on a private screen, the terminal's alternate screen ... neither the secret nor the result reaches the main screen or its scrollback. A new container and a recovered seed phrase are shown the same way'. SECURITY.md:50-53: 'At a terminal, secrets, a new container and a recovered phrase appear on the terminal's alternate screen, which is cleared before the tool returns to the main screen, so they do not enter its scrollback'. README.md:153-155: 'At a terminal, typed and displayed secrets use private screens cleared when the step ends, keeping them out of ordinary scrollback'. README.md:269: decrypt shows the phrase 'on the private screen'. README.md:217-218: encrypt, 'then clear the private screen'. The only no-private-screen qualification, SECURITY.md:19-20, is about typing ('typed without echo'). README.md:156 says that commands that require a screen 'say so below', but no document says what the others display instead. The code's own rule is made_password.rs:105-107. DOC-07 requires that documents and messages claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides, and DOC-06 requires that a code/document mismatch be named and settled.
- **Observed behavior:** pty-dumb-vs-xterm.log, case A (TERM=dumb): raw bytes '\r\nMHFE \xc2\xb7 Make a password\r\n\r\n  unless jab lecturer marshy snippet\r\n\r\n\xe2\x9c\x93 5 words from the EFF list, about 64.6 bits.\r\nShown only once and not stored: write it down, apart from the container.\r\n', 'ESC[?1049h written: False', 'still running (waiting for a key): False', 'exit code: 0'. Case B (xterm): the output begins '\x1b[?1049h', the tool is still running after 3 s, and after Enter it writes '\x1b[2J\x1b[H\x1b[?1049l' with 'password repeated after the screen was left: False'. Case C (repair-words, TERM=dumb): 'ESC[?1049h written: False', the card is on the main screen and the tool exits 0 with no wait; at xterm 'ESC[?1049h written: True' and it waits. Static trace: decrypt prints the phrase through print_phrase with no wait. In this case it adds only the hint 'clear the screen and close this terminal', and no document mentions that. encrypt and rekey print the unverified container on the main screen and give no hint to clear it. mhfe password gives no hint either.
- **Impact:** A person at a dumb terminal relies on the stated guarantee, but the new password, the recovered seed phrase or the new container stays in the scrollback. Dumb terminals include Emacs shell-mode, some IDE and serial consoles, and a Windows console without VT. The same password that encrypt and rekey refuse to make in this condition (made_password::refuse_kind, AUD-015-SEC003) is printed by mhfe password. The exposure is limited to the person's own terminal and its retained output, so this stays a low-severity documentation and behaviour mismatch, not a demonstrated remote compromise.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-dumb-private-screen/pty-dumb-vs-xterm.log (exit 1 = defect present, 2026-10-14T08:56:15Z). kept-harness-run.log: the same probe run from the repository root with the kept harness, exit 1. static-trace.log: every cited line with its number at b6fca69. binary-sha256.log: the debug binary is 183a6c8d4557d6bd05da6384e0dee4be5d567bdbf64382f5e9d806bc4fcc552e, identical to the shared AUD-024 debug build, and no source file is newer than it. Kept harness: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-dumb-private-screen/ (probe.py, README.md). Reviewer's evidence: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/cli-ux/pty-dumb-password.log, and pty-dumb-encrypt.log (encrypt proceeds at TERM=dumb to the hidden password prompt). Prior records: AUD-023 recorded the mhfe password case only as an informational observation. AUD-016 (docs/audits/AUD-016-2026-10-09.md:349) recorded 'TERM=dumb displays encrypted container words' as an observation. AUD-015-SEC003 fixed only the --new-password made-password case of encrypt and rekey. No document was changed by any of them.
- **Recommended fix:** Settle the behaviour once, per DOC-06. One option: refuse to show a secret result where can_show_privately() is false at a terminal, as new, wallets and refuse_kind already do. For mhfe password that is a refusal at start. For decrypt, encrypt and rekey it must come before any secret is asked or any Argon2 work. The other option: ask the person to confirm showing the result on the main screen and tell them to clear the scrollback afterwards. Then state that behaviour for a terminal without a private screen in SECURITY.md (Secrets, both bullets) and README.md (Commands, and the password, encrypt and decrypt sections), and correct the code comments at diceware.rs:228-229 and :262-264, decrypt.rs:211 and encrypt.rs:267-269.
- **Required verification:** Add pseudo-terminal cases at TERM=dumb to scripts/verify-hidden-input.py. mhfe password must follow the chosen behaviour. decrypt, encrypt and rekey must refuse or ask before the first secret, which can be checked without Argon2 if the refusal comes first, or else at reduced cost. Rerun docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-dumb-private-screen/probe.py and update its expectation to the chosen behaviour. Check that SECURITY.md, README.md and each command's output use the same wording in the same change.
- **Related findings:** AUD-015-SEC003
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced this at b6fca69 using the debug binary built from the clean tree (sha256 183a6c8d...). I ran `mhfe password` in a pseudo-terminal with TERM=dumb. It printed the five-word password on the main screen, wrote no ESC[?1049h, did not wait for a key and exited 0. In the control run with TERM=xterm-256color the password appeared only after ESC[?1049h, the tool waited for Enter, then wrote ESC[?1049l and did not repeat the password. PrivateScreen::enter_to_show is the call decrypt.rs:212 makes for the recovered phrase. I exercised that same call without Argon2 through `mhfe repair-words --count 4`. At TERM=dumb it stays inactive and prints to the main screen without a wait; at xterm it opens the alternate screen and waits. A static trace with line numbers confirms the decrypt, encrypt and rekey paths. The chain is can_redraw is false at TERM=dumb, so terminal_screen_possible, can_show_privately and enter_steps are false. No flow starts, enter_to_show is inactive and the result is printed with no wait. These commands do not need a full-cost run to confirm. SECURITY.md:50-53 and README.md:153-155 and :269 make unqualified claims ("At a terminal ..."), and nothing in the documents covers the display case. SECURITY.md:19-20 qualifies only how secrets are typed ('Where no private screen is possible, they are typed without echo'). The 'did not ask to export' exception at SECURITY.md:20-23 names refusals by new, wallets and rekey only. It does not say that a recovered phrase, a new container or a made password reaches the main screen and its scrollback. The code's own rule at made_password.rs:105-107 says 'never on the main screen of a terminal that cannot switch', and `mhfe password` contradicts it. This is not a duplicate. No confirmed AUD-024 finding covers it. AUD-023 has no finding on it: AUD-023-UI004 is about cursor sequences in word hints. AUD-023 recorded the `mhfe password` case only as an informational observation, and AUD-016 recorded the container case only as an observation. AUD-015-SEC003 fixed the refusal of a made password only for encrypt and rekey with --new-password. I added the rekey variant (rekey.rs:414 goes through the same show_sealing) and corrected the line numbers.

##### AUD-024-DOC016 — Low — docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/RELEASING.md leave out what their commands need. Neither names the Playwright browsers that pnpm run check:browsers needs, nor the GNU tar, gzip and zip that scripts/check.sh needs. The cached/uncached canonical comparison that RELEASING.md asks for depends on two script options that no document gives: the REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE=1 switch and the output-folder argument.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Developer and release documentation
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** CHECK-DOC-002, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** Repository documentation only (no shipped build). Affects a developer or maintainer who follows the public developer and release guides.
  
  **Browser check**
  - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:51-57 presents `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` as the installation of the Node.js tools.
  - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:60-64 then says: after scripts/check.sh, run `pnpm run check:browsers` (package.json script: `node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs`). No step downloads the browsers.
  - scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:8-10 requires `pnpm exec playwright install chromium firefox`, and line 257 calls `BROWSERS[name].launch()`.
  - CI does the download: .github/workflows/ci.yml:101 runs `pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox`.
  - The only document that mentions it is AGENTS.md:16, the agent instructions.
  
  **scripts/check.sh tools**
  - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:36-49 names scripts/check.sh but not the tools it needs.
  - scripts/check.sh:7-8 says it needs "Python 3, GNU tar and zip", and line 69 runs scripts/verify-archive-packing.sh.
  - scripts/verify-archive-packing.sh:6 says it needs "GNU tar, gzip, zip and Python 3" (lines 11, 40-41 and 52 use them).
  - packaging/pack-archives.sh:2-3 states the same needs. Line 20 uses the GNU tar option --sort=name, line 21 runs `gzip -n`, and line 33 runs `zip -X`.
  
  **Uncached canonical comparison**
  - docs/RELEASING.md:15-16 says to run "a cached/uncached canonical comparison locally".
  - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:70-74 gives only `scripts/build-reproducible.sh`.
  - scripts/build-reproducible.sh:23-28 turns on `--no-cache` (used at line 42) only through REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE=1.
  - scripts/build-reproducible.sh:17-21 takes an optional output folder `canonical-output-<name>`. Without it, every run removes and replaces canonical-output (lines 55-56), so two runs of the documented command leave only the second build to compare.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69:
  
  1. Search the three documents:
     `git grep -n -i -E 'playwright|REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE|uncached|no-cache|GNU tar|gzip|[^a-z]zip[^a-z]|Python 3' b6fca69 -- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md docs/RELEASING.md README.md`
     It finds only README.md:506 (Python 3.8 for the fast-mode launcher) and RELEASING.md:16 (the word 'uncached').
  2. Search the scripts and CI:
     `git grep -n -E 'playwright install|Needs .*(tar|zip)|REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE|--no-cache|cache_flags' b6fca69 -- scripts/verify-browsers.mjs scripts/check.sh scripts/verify-archive-packing.sh packaging/pack-archives.sh scripts/build-reproducible.sh .github/workflows/ci.yml`
     It shows each prerequisite stated only in the script headers and CI.
  3. Missing browsers. A probe resolves `playwright` from the repository's node_modules (as pnpm install --frozen-lockfile leaves it) and calls chromium.launch() and firefox.launch() with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH set to an empty folder, as on a computer that never ran `playwright install`:
     `env PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<empty dir> node tmp/aud024/verify-doc-prerequisites/playwright-without-browsers.mjs`
     It exits 1. playwright 1.64.0 has no install scripts (scripts: null), and both launches fail with "browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at .../chrome-headless-shell" (or .../firefox/firefox) and "Please run the following command to download new browsers: npx playwright install".
  4. Missing zip. With PATH set to a copy of /usr/bin that has every tool but zip, and TMPDIR inside the probe folder:
     `env PATH=<farm without zip> TMPDIR=<probe tmp> scripts/verify-archive-packing.sh`
     It exits 127 with "packaging/pack-archives.sh: line 33: zip: command not found". This is the last step of scripts/check.sh (line 69).
  5. Output folder. `git grep -n -E 'output_dir|canonical-output|build-reproducible' b6fca69 -- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md docs/RELEASING.md README.md scripts/build-reproducible.sh` shows the output-folder argument only in the script (lines 17-19, 55-56). The documents give only the bare command at DEVELOPMENT.md:73.
- **Expected behavior:** **FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE CHECK-DOC-002:** "Verify examples against real flags, script names, output paths, module prerequisites, ... installation/toolchain selection, browser revisions, ... and CI/release prerequisites." AUD-023-DOC005 applied this check to the same document's toolchain instructions, as a low finding.
  
  **docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's own claims:** line 3-4 says "The toolchains are pinned as 'Build from source' says". Line 60 presents check:browsers as runnable once scripts/check.sh has built the package. So the commands it gives should run after the steps it gives.
  
  **DOC-06 (code and documents agree):** the documents should not contradict the prerequisites the scripts state for themselves. RELEASING.md should give the commands for the comparison it requires.
- **Observed behavior:** The prerequisites appear only in script headers (verify-browsers.mjs:8-10, check.sh:7-8, verify-archive-packing.sh:6, pack-archives.sh:2-3), in CI (ci.yml:101) and in AGENTS.md:16. The uncached switch and the output-folder argument appear only in scripts/build-reproducible.sh:17-28.
  
  Following the documents as written:
  - `pnpm run check:browsers` stops at Playwright's missing-executable error.
  - On a system without zip (or with a non-GNU tar), scripts/check.sh fails in its last step.
  - Running the documented `scripts/build-reproducible.sh` twice overwrites canonical-output and never builds without the cache, so the comparison RELEASING.md requires cannot be made.
- **Impact:** A developer or maintainer who follows DEVELOPMENT.md and RELEASING.md hits failing checks they were told would run. They cannot perform the uncached canonical comparison the release procedure requires without reading the script source. There is no effect on any shipped program, package or archive, and no security impact.
- **Evidence:** Evidence folder: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-doc-prerequisites/ (each log has a .command.json beside it). All were run through docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh from the repository root.
  - docs-grep.log, exit 0: the documents match only README.md:506 and RELEASING.md:16.
  - script-prerequisites.log, exit 0: the prerequisites at ci.yml:101, pack-archives.sh:2-3, build-reproducible.sh:23-27 and 42, check.sh:8, verify-archive-packing.sh:6 and verify-browsers.mjs:10.
  - playwright-without-browsers.log, exit 1: "playwright 1.64.0 install scripts: null". Both chromium and firefox fail with "browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist ... Please run the following command to download new browsers: npx playwright install".
  - archive-packing-without-zip.log, exit 127: "packaging/pack-archives.sh: line 33: zip: command not found".
  - output-folder-argument.log, exit 0: the output-folder argument appears only in scripts/build-reproducible.sh:17-19 and 55-56.
  
  Probe sources are under the workspace's tmp/aud024/verify-doc-prerequisites/ (the Playwright probe, and a PATH copy of /usr/bin without zip). The probe's TMPDIR was cleaned by the script's own trap. The baseline b20-browsers.log (exit 0) passed only because the browsers were already installed on this machine. b19-archive-packing.log (exit 0) passed with zip present.
  
  Not reproduced: a run with a BSD tar (static trace only: pack-archives.sh:20 uses GNU tar's --sort=name, and verify-archive-packing.sh:11 falls back to whatever tar is on PATH), and an actual uncached Docker build (the audit rules forbid it).
- **Recommended fix:** **docs/DEVELOPMENT.md**
  - After the pnpm install step, add `pnpm exec playwright install chromium firefox` (with `--with-deps` on Linux, as ci.yml:101 does). State that `pnpm run check:browsers` and `node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs` need it.
  - List what scripts/check.sh needs beyond the toolchains: Python 3, GNU tar (gtar on macOS), gzip and zip.
  
  **docs/RELEASING.md** (or DEVELOPMENT.md's canonical-build section)
  - Write the comparison as commands, for example:
    `scripts/build-reproducible.sh canonical-output-cached`
    `REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE=1 scripts/build-reproducible.sh canonical-output-uncached`
    followed by a comparison of the two release/SHA256SUMS files.
  
  **Gate (optional)**
  - Have scripts/verify-pinned-versions.mjs or the code-rules gate check that a prerequisite named in a script header is also named in DEVELOPMENT.md.
- **Required verification:** 1. On a clean machine (or a container) prepared only as DEVELOPMENT.md says, run `pnpm run check:browsers` and scripts/check.sh. Each must start without a missing-browser or missing-tool error.
  2. Run the cached and the uncached canonical builds exactly as RELEASING.md then writes them. Both outputs must remain, and their release/SHA256SUMS must be comparable.
  3. Re-run the docs grep above. It must find the browser install command, the tar/gzip/zip prerequisites, REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE and the output-folder argument in the documents.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-DOC005
- **Verification:** confirmed: Every cited location reads as claimed at b6fca69, and I reproduced two of the failures with small probes that run no Argon2.
  
  1. **Playwright browsers.** Playwright 1.64.0 in the lockfile has no install scripts. With an empty PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, the same launch() that verify-browsers.mjs:257 makes fails for both Chromium and Firefox with "Executable doesn't exist ... npx playwright install".
  2. **zip.** scripts/verify-archive-packing.sh is the last step of scripts/check.sh. Run with zip missing from PATH, it exits 127 at packaging/pack-archives.sh:33.
  3. **What the documents say.** Neither DEVELOPMENT.md, RELEASING.md nor README.md names the browser download, GNU tar, gzip or zip as prerequisites. None of them names REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE=1 or the output-folder argument. Without that argument, a second build-reproducible.sh run deletes the first build's output (lines 55-56), so the cached/uncached comparison RELEASING.md asks for cannot be made with the commands the documents give.
  
  This is related to AUD-023-DOC005, not a duplicate. That finding, now fixed, covered only wasm-bindgen and Emscripten. The same CHECK-DOC-002 gap remains for the other prerequisites. I added the output-folder variant and corrected the line ranges.

##### AUD-024-DOC017 — Low — docs/API.md quotes makePassword's refusal of a count with "checkWord" in its pre-AUD-023 wording, which the WebAssembly binding no longer gives

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** docs/API.md (browser package, WebAssembly bindings: makePassword)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-API-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** docs/API.md:1046-1048 (the quote on line 1047: "checkWord takes no count: it always makes five words and their check word"). The message it should quote: src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:184-188 (makePassword; INVALID_REQUEST built from check_word::DRAWN_WORDS), and its deliberate copy CHECK_WORD_TAKES_NO_COUNT at web/passwords.js:47-49, thrown at web/passwords.js:155. The tests that pin the new wording: scripts/package-check/test-values.mjs:72 and scripts/browser-check/password-checks.mjs:270. No other file holds the old wording, and no check reads docs/API.md for it. Only the repository document is affected: docs/API.md is not shipped in dist/ (dist/README.md is docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md). Builds: browser package, both modes. Native CLI not affected.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with dist/ as built by the baseline (buildId de06b919b42eae2f), run: node --no-warnings /home/user/.../tmp/aud024/verify-api-md-refusal-quote/probe.mjs. The probe loads dist/passwords/passwords.js with the package's real worker script running in process (InProcessWorker from docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/api-contracts/harness.mjs). It rewrites the worker's 'make' message to count 5, which gets past the class's early TypeError, so mhfe.makePassword('checkWord', 5, ...) reaches the binding. It then compares the binding's message with the parenthesised quote in docs/API.md. Static trace: docs/API.md:1047 against src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:184-188. git log -S"checkWord takes no count" shows that commit 253ca3c removed the old string from passwords.rs and left it in docs/API.md, although the same commit edited docs/API.md (70 lines).
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-06 (docs.instructions.md): code and documents agree, and a change that alters behaviour on purpose updates its documents in the same change. docs/API.md's own sentence presents the parenthesised text as the INVALID_REQUEST message makePassword gives, so it should be the binding's message. The AUD-023-ARC007 fix in 253ca3c was meant to give one wording, built from check_word::DRAWN_WORDS.
- **Observed behavior:** The binding rejects with MhfeError code INVALID_REQUEST and the message 'Invalid request: count belongs only to the kinds "words" and "characters": "checkWord" always gives 5 words and their check word'. The class's TypeError says the same, with a final period. docs/API.md:1047 quotes 'checkWord takes no count: it always makes five words and their check word', the pre-253ca3c Rust wording, which no code produces any more.
- **Impact:** Documentation only. A raw-binding caller, or a reader matching the documented text against what the package gives, finds a different message. A test written from the documented string would fail. No secret or result is affected.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-api-md-refusal-quote/v01-binding-refusal-vs-api-md.log (exit 1). It records the binding refusal {code INVALID_REQUEST, message 'Invalid request: count belongs only to the kinds "words" and "characters": "checkWord" always gives 5 words and their check word'}, the class TypeError (the same text ending with '.') and the API.md quote 'checkWord takes no count: it always makes five words and their check word', then 'FAIL the binding's message is not the quoted text'. The original finder's log, docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/api-contracts/h01-check-contracts.log line 10, shows 'FAIL api-md-quotes-the-refusal'; that check compared the quote with the class's TypeError. grep -rn 'takes no count' finds the old wording only at docs/API.md:1047 and in earlier audit records. git show 253ca3c -- src/wasm_api/passwords.rs shows the old string replaced by the format! on DRAWN_WORDS.
- **Recommended fix:** In docs/API.md:1046-1048, quote the binding's current message: count belongs only to the kinds "words" and "characters": "checkWord" always gives 5 words and their check word. Or describe the refusal without quoting it. Optionally, have scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs, which already keeps the Rust and JS copies equal, also check this quote, so a later rewording cannot leave the document behind.
- **Required verification:** Rerun the probe above (expect PASS, exit 0), or check-contracts.mjs check api-md-quotes-the-refusal (expect PASS). Run the repository's prettier and Markdown checks on docs/API.md. Run grep -rn 'takes no count: it always makes' docs/API.md and expect no match.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-ARC007, AUD-024 (wave): The browser API documentation was not updated with the AUD-023 changes to check() and rekey()
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. A probe sent makePassword("checkWord", 5) straight to the real WebAssembly binding in dist/, getting past the class's early TypeError. The binding refused with INVALID_REQUEST "Invalid request: count belongs only to the kinds "words" and "characters": "checkWord" always gives 5 words and their check word". docs/API.md:1047 still quotes the older wording, "checkWord takes no count: it always makes five words and their check word". Commit 253ca3c, the AUD-023 remediation, changed that message in src/wasm_api/passwords.rs and edited docs/API.md in the same commit, but did not update this quote. DOC-06 requires that a deliberate change updates its documents in the same change. AUD-023-ARC007 had recorded the two wordings. Its fix aligned the code and left the document behind, so this is a remaining defect of that fix. It is not a repeat. The confirmed finding about check() and rekey() covers a different API section and different fixes, so this one is not its duplicate.

##### AUD-024-DOC018 — Low — Both fast-mode launchers serve only a page whose name ends in lower-case ".html". No help or document states this rule, and both refuse any other name in a well-formed sha256sum line with the message that the checksum file is not in that format.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Fast-mode launchers: mhfe serve (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs), packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py (core/mhfe-fast-mode.py in the browser package), and the start menu's fast-mode entry (src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06, CORE-48
- **Affected files and builds:** Both launchers, every platform and build (CLI release archives and the browser package, which ships the Python launcher).
  - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:41-42: MALFORMED, "must hold exactly one line: the page's SHA-256, two spaces and its file name, or one space and * before the name; nothing was served."
  - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:140-170 read_checksum_file. Line 149 builds `malformed`, and lines 162-166 return it when `!name.ends_with(".html")` (line 163), together with a non-hex digest and a name that is not plain. The extension rule has no message of its own.
  - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:85-93 file_help: "mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 holds the SHA-256 of the page in the form sha256sum writes", with no word about the name.
  - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:129-137 checked_page_in, which the start menu calls through page_next_to_program. menu.rs:143-157 then prints "The fast mode is not offered." with the same format message (menu.rs:155).
  - packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:432-435 (malformed) and :455 (`name.endswith(".html")`, folded into the same refusal). Module docstring :9-17 and help :227-229 give no name rule.
  - Documents that give the format and the refusal reasons without the rule: SECURITY.md:222-226, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:756-760 ("Without it, with another file name in it or with a different SHA-256, the launcher refuses"), README.md:503-506. Their examples imply the rule only through placeholders (`tool.html`, `<page.html>`, `<file.html>`).
  - No test covers the refusal. The serve.rs tests (:800-818) and scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py use only tool.html, other.html and *tool.html.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root, with mhfe built by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<audit target> cargo build --locked --bin mhfe`:
  1. Create a folder holding a page tool.htm and `sha256sum tool.htm > mhfe-fast-mode.sha256`. The line is `d3d389ab...921c  tool.htm`, two spaces as sha256sum writes it.
  2. `NO_COLOR=1 mhfe serve --no-browser <dir>/tool.htm` and `python3 packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py --no-browser <dir>/tool.htm` both exit 2 with "<dir>/mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 must hold exactly one line: the page's SHA-256, two spaces and its file name, or one space and * before the name; nothing was served."
  3. Tool.HTML and tool.xhtml give the same result.
  4. Controls: tool.html with one changed digest digit is refused for its real reason ("The SHA-256 of tool.html is ..., but mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 expects ..."). tool.html with the right digest is served ("Fast mode is running").
  5. Start menu: copy mhfe into a folder with tool.htm and its sha256sum line, start it without arguments in a pseudo-terminal (`script -qfec <copy> /dev/null`, TERM=xterm) and press Esc. The menu prints "! The fast mode is not offered." followed by the same format message.
  The probes are tmp/aud024/verify-fast-mode-page-name/probe.sh and menu-probe.sh in the workspace, outside the repository.
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-06 (code and documents agree): every condition under which a page is or is not served is stated in the help and the documents. A launcher refuses only a line that breaks the documented format, or refuses with the condition actually broken. CORE-48: input from outside, here the checksum file, is "refused with a clear message when it does not fit". The documents (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:756-760, SECURITY.md:222-226) and serve --help ("in the form sha256sum writes") define the accepted line as sha256sum's own line. BROWSER-PACKAGE.md lists the reasons for a refusal as no checksum file, another file name, or a different SHA-256.
- **Observed behavior:** A line that sha256sum itself wrote for the page is refused whenever the page name does not end in exactly ".html". The rule is case-sensitive, so .htm, .HTML and .xhtml are refused, although the digest's hex letters are accepted in either case (serve.rs:169). Both launchers and the start menu report the refusal as a malformed checksum file, a reason that is false for that line. The rule appears in no help, document or specification, and no test covers it.
- **Impact:** An integrator who names the tool page .htm or Tool.HTML, or whose download tool changes its case, gets a diagnosis that points at the checksum line, which is correct, and finds nothing about the cause in the documentation. Fast mode stays unavailable until the page is renamed, and the start menu does not offer it. There is no security effect: such a page is refused, never served.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-fast-mode-page-name/page-name-probe.log (+ .command.json, exit 0): format message from both launchers for tool.htm, Tool.HTML and tool.xhtml, the real-reason refusal for a wrong digest on tool.html, and the served tool.html control. menu-page-name-probe.log: the start menu prints "The fast mode is not offered." with the format message for tool.htm. serve-help.log: neither `mhfe serve --help` nor `mhfe-fast-mode.py --help` names the rule. Static reads at b6fca69: serve.rs:41-42, 85-93, 129-170; menu.rs:143-157; mhfe-fast-mode.py:9-17, 227-229, 432-455; SECURITY.md:222-226; docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:756-760; README.md:503-506. `git grep` finds no other statement of the rule in the repository outside docs/audits, and nothing in mhfe_spec. The candidate's docs-claims logs (fast-mode-page-name.log, serve-html-extension.log) agree.
- **Recommended fix:** Decide whether the .html rule is needed. If it is, state it, including that it is case-sensitive, in the serve FILE help, the Python launcher's help and docstring, SECURITY.md (fast-mode launcher section) and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md (Fast and standard mode). Give it its own refusal in both launchers, for example "mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 names <name>, but the fast mode serves only a page whose name ends in .html; nothing was served.", as a deliberate copy kept equal by scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py. If the rule is not needed, accept .htm and any letter case, or drop the rule. In either case, add a serve.rs unit test and a verify-fast-mode-script.py case for a .htm name.
- **Required verification:** A .htm or .HTML page with a sha256sum-written line is either served or refused with a message that names the extension rule, identically by mhfe serve, mhfe-fast-mode.py and the start menu. Rerun probe.sh and menu-probe.sh to show this. A serve.rs unit test and a verify-fast-mode-script.py case cover the name rule. The helps and documents name the rule if it stays.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-UI009, AUD-023-DOC008
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69 with a fresh debug build and the shipped Python launcher. A checksum line that sha256sum itself wrote is refused with the "must hold exactly one line" format message by both launchers (exit 2) when it names tool.htm, Tool.HTML or tool.xhtml. A tool.html with a wrong digest is refused for its real reason, and a tool.html with the right digest is served. In a pseudo-terminal, the start menu with tool.htm beside the program prints "The fast mode is not offered." with the same format message. The rule appears only in serve.rs:163 and mhfe-fast-mode.py:455. Neither help, README.md, SECURITY.md, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md nor mhfe_spec states it, and no test covers it. It is not a duplicate. AUD-023-UI009 fixed the wording of the format message, AUD-023-DOC008 made the menu check the page, and the confirmed fast-mode findings (size limits, universal newlines, request-head parsing) have other root causes. I removed CORE-23 from the rules: it requires stable codes and one message source, and this defect does not breach it. DOC-06 and CORE-48 fit. Severity is low per AUDIT_STANDARD.md (a limited presentation and documentation defect, no security effect).

##### AUD-024-DOC019 — Low — Address::parse's rustdoc says multisignature and script addresses are refused, but it accepts every Bitcoin or Litecoin P2SH address ('3…', 'M…', testnet '2…') as nested SegWit, multisignature ones included. A wallet search then answers 'no match' instead of refusing.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Library public API documentation: wallet address parsing (src/wallet.rs, src/wallet/encodings.rs)
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-06, DOC-07, CORE-20, CHECK-DOC-001
- **Affected files and builds:** All builds that include the wallet module: the native library and CLI, and the browser builds through AddressSearch::describe / describe_within and reference_target.
  - src/wallet.rs:255-256: the rustdoc of pub fn Address::parse (:257) reads 'Multisignature and script addresses, Zcash shielded addresses and those of other coins are refused.' The line was added in 0205a0a and extended in e5814b3.
  - src/wallet/encodings.rs:151-165, base58_versions. Bitcoin (0x05, P2shP2wpkh) is at :156 and testnet (0xc4, P2shP2wpkh) at :158. Litecoin (0x32, P2shP2wpkh) is at :163 and (0x05, P2shP2wpkh) at :164. Its own doc at :148-150 says a '3...' address 'is taken as nested SegWit'. parse_base58 (:190-197) checks only the version prefix and the 20-byte hash length, so it cannot tell a script hash from the P2WPKH witness script's hash.
  - src/wallet.rs:200-201: the doc of AddressType::P2shP2wpkh (accurate: 'HASH160 of the P2WPKH script').
  No other text makes the claim. README.md, docs/API.md, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, SECURITY.md, web/*.d.ts and the CLI --address help (src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:82-99, 'a single-key receiving address') state the requirement correctly or do not mention it.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69, public test data only, no Argon2:
  1. python3 /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-p2sh-doc/multisig_addresses.py computes, independently of mhfe, the P2SH and P2WSH addresses of the redeem scripts OP_1 <K0> OP_1 OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_2 <K0> <K1> <K2> OP_3 OP_CHECKMULTISIG. K0-K2 are the public keys m, m/0H and m/0H/1 of BIP-0032 test vector 1. The encoders were checked against BIP173's bc1qw508d6... vector and the generator key's 1BgGZ9tc... address. Output: 3KwykuxXW7pm2RB5tGyX2obpRfGG2zU1mJ (1-of-1), 34s3F7okk3e6gAekBjsangGFv4iM2W7KPs (2-of-3), 2MvRFJrjnMW9SsxHHrsVTQdFX8QvWrVCuR7 (testnet), MB5BZ1DihAVXUfveHcrvcKWfEmJo41FhVB (Litecoin 0x32), and bc1qjj2sf2a70htwmzn4gtw9q0f5nvmue5knsmxemn7uh6dek0q88r9qlum4d7 (P2WSH 2-of-3).
  2. A scratch crate (/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-p2sh-doc/probe) depends on the repository by path and calls only the public API: Address::parse, address_type, type_description, search_roots, and find_address with the 'abandon ... about' phrase and SearchLimits::default(). Build: env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.../tmp/aud024/target cargo +1.99.0 build --offline --manifest-path .../probe/Cargo.toml. Run it on the addresses above and on AUD-023's 39kh1g5VzX7eEEzAnbNZsG2w1WCYNQVu3G.
  Result: Address::parse returns Ok for all six P2SH multisignature addresses (Bitcoin, Bitcoin testnet, Litecoin M... and 3...). Each has type P2shP2wpkh, is described as 'nested SegWit (BIP49)' or 'testnet, nested SegWit (BIP49)', and has search roots [[49,0]], [[49,1]] or [[49,2]]. find_address returns Ok(None) for each, a no-match, not an error. Only the P2WSH form of the same script is refused (INVALID_ADDRESS 'only single-key addresses (bc1q with 42 characters, bc1p or ltc1q) can be checked'). The probe exits 1 ('6 multisignature script address(es) accepted').
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-06 (code and documents agree) and DOC-07 (documents claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides). CORE-20 requires the doc comment of a public item to state its contract and the errors it returns. A P2SH address carries only HASH160 of its redeem script, so parse cannot tell a multisignature P2SH from P2SH-P2WPKH. The library's own internal comment (encodings.rs:148-150) says it takes every '3...' address as nested SegWit. The public doc should therefore say that a P2SH address is read as nested SegWit (BIP49). It should also say that a multisignature or other script P2SH is not refused but is searched as nested SegWit and ends in no match. Only P2WSH and other non-single-key forms are refused.
- **Observed behavior:** The public rustdoc promises a refusal of multisignature and script addresses that the code does not perform and cannot perform for P2SH. A library user who relies on Address::parse to reject multisignature input gets Ok(P2shP2wpkh). The rehearsal then searches m/49' and reports no match. A person may read this as a wrong password or wrong phrase rather than an unusable address. Before the check, the CLI and the browser show the type 'nested SegWit (BIP49)', which hints at the reading but does not say that a multisignature address can never match.
- **Impact:** Documentation-only defect of the public library API. No secret is exposed and no wrong match is possible. A multisignature P2SH address can only give a false 'does not match', never a false 'matches'. A consumer that trusts the documented refusal may skip its own check and confuse a user with a no-match result. The defect has been recorded twice as an observation (AUD-010 and AUD-023 informationalObservations[13]) and was never corrected.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-p2sh-doc/ (each with a .command.json):
  - multisig-addresses.log (exit 0): the independent Python computation of the P2SH/P2WSH multisignature addresses.
  - probe-build.log (exit 0): build of the scratch probe crate against the repository at b6fca69.
  - parse-multisig.log (exit 1 by design): six ACCEPTED lines, each type P2shP2wpkh with find_address -> Ok(None); one REFUSED line for P2WSH; '6 multisignature script address(es) accepted'.
  - static-trace.log (exit 0): HEAD, the cited line ranges with numbers, the origin of the doc line (git log -L: 0205a0a, e5814b3), the grep showing src/wallet.rs:255 as the only multisig/script-refusal claim in src, web, docs/API.md, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, README.md and SECURITY.md, and the probe sources.
  The candidate's own log agrees: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide/address-forms.log (39kh1g5... ACCEPTED as P2shP2wpkh). Prior record: docs/audits/AUD-023-2026-10-13.json informationalObservations[13].
- **Recommended fix:** Rewrite the rustdoc of Address::parse (src/wallet.rs:255-256). It should say that a Bitcoin or Litecoin P2SH address ('3...', 'M...', testnet '2...') is read as nested SegWit (P2SH-P2WPKH, BIP49), because a script hash cannot be told apart. It should say that a multisignature or other script P2SH is therefore not refused, and that its search ends in no match. It should list what is refused: P2WSH and other witness programs that are not single-key, CashAddr P2SH, Zcash shielded and TEX addresses, and other coins' addresses. Consider adding the same sentence to the --address help and to the browser describeAddress / reference docs, so that a person with a multisignature wallet knows that a no-match is expected. Add a unit test that parses a multisignature P2SH and asserts the documented behaviour.
- **Required verification:** Doc review of the new rustdoc against encodings.rs. A unit test asserting that a known multisignature P2SH (for example 34s3F7okk3e6gAekBjsangGFv4iM2W7KPs) parses as P2shP2wpkh and that a P2WSH is refused, so the documented behaviour is pinned. Re-run the probe above, or the new test, and cargo doc.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[13] (P2SH '3…' accepted against the rustdoc of Address::parse), AUD-010 informational observation (P2SH accepted as nested SegWit, 'inherent to the encoding'), AUD-024-ARC007 (Comments state facts the code does not have), same class of defect, a different comment
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. The rustdoc of the public Address::parse (src/wallet.rs:255-256) says that "Multisignature and script addresses ... are refused". Since e5814b3 the Base58 table in src/wallet/encodings.rs:151-165 maps every P2SH version byte to P2shP2wpkh: Bitcoin 0x05 and testnet 0xc4, Litecoin 0x32 and 0x05. The function's own comment at :148-150 says a '3...' address 'is taken as nested SegWit'.
  
  My probe is a scratch crate that calls the public library API. I computed the multisignature P2SH addresses independently in Python from the public BIP-0032 test vector 1 keys. Address::parse accepted six of them (1-of-1 and 2-of-3, Bitcoin mainnet and testnet, Litecoin M... and 3..., and AUD-023's 39kh1g5...) as P2shP2wpkh 'nested SegWit (BIP49)'. For each one, find_address with the "abandon ... about" phrase returned Ok(None), a no-match, not a refusal. Only the P2WSH form of the same script (62-character bc1q...) is refused.
  
  No other document makes the claim: README.md, docs/API.md, BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, SECURITY.md and the CLI --address help, which asks for a single-key address, are all accurate. So the defect is the public rustdoc contract alone.
  
  This is not an AUD-023 finding: AUD-023 recorded it only as informationalObservations[13], and AUD-010 had recorded it as an observation before that. It is close in kind to the already confirmed 'Comments state facts the code does not have' (AUD-024-ARC007). I keep it separate for three reasons. That finding does not list it. Its cause here is an untrue refusal contract on a public API, not a stale comment. It was never fixed after two audits recorded it. The coordinator may still merge it there as a variant if findings are grouped by class. No full-cost Argon2 was needed. The CLI's final 'does not match' wording after decryption follows from the library's Ok(None), and I did not re-run it, because that would need a full-cost run.

REPAIR_LINE (src/bin/mhfe/container_repair.rs:162-163), quoted by the --stdin helps at decrypt.rs:84 and check.rs:164, says: "With --repair, the repair words come on the line right after the container, and every later answer one line further down."

Every addition and every breaking change is named under New, Library or Browser package.
  - The section order follows docs/releases/v0.6.0.md, and each entry holds one change.
  - The --stdin line agrees with REPAIR_LINE and with encrypt's --stdin help.
- **Related findings:** Earlier wave [DOC]: The browser API documentation was not updated with the AUD-023 changes to check() and rekey() (docs/API.md, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md), AUD-023-DOC001 (the --stdin helps name what --repair-words and --repair add; its fix is correct in the helps, but the draft's release-note line about it is wrong)
- **Verification:** confirmed: I reproduced every claim at b6fca69 with read-only git and grep; the log is docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-release-notes-draft/probe.log. Commit 253ca3c added keepOldContainer(), MhfeReplacementRehearsal and the rekey result's `rehearsal`, rehearsalNeedsPassphrase with the `{ passphrase }` yes-answer, evidence.passed, the oldContainer and oldPasswords keep items, and CheckOutcome::NotVerified. The same commit edited docs/releases/unreleased.md but recorded none of them. The draft has no New, Library or Reviews section, although v0.6.0.md does. Lines 53-55 say that --repair adds a second line of standard output. In fact REPAIR_LINE (container_repair.rs:162-163), which the decrypt and check --stdin helps quote, says that --repair adds an input line, and encrypt has no --repair option. This is not a duplicate. The confirmed API-documentation finding is about docs/API.md and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md, and no AUD-023 finding covers the draft release notes. I made three corrections to the details.
