##### AUD-024-DOC021 — Low — The README copied into every release archive shows assets/mhfe-mascot.png, which no archive contains, so the shipped README opens with a broken image

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Release packaging (scripts/package-release.sh) and README.md
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** CHECK-DOC-002, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** README.md:11 (<img src="assets/mhfe-mascot.png" alt="MHFE penguin mascot ..." width="240">), the only relative reference in README.md that an archive cannot resolve. Its other relative links (LICENSE-MIT at line 653, LICENSE-APACHE at 654, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at 656) point to files that ship; every other link is an absolute URL or an in-page anchor. scripts/package-release.sh:65-76 (add_common_files copies README.md, as README-mhfe.md where the folder already has a README, plus LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/, but not assets/). It is called for the CLI archives at line 112 and for the browser archive at line 141. Builds affected: every release archive (Linux x86-64 and ARM64, Windows x86-64, browser, and the macOS archives built by the same script at .github/workflows/release.yml:80) in v0.3.0 to v0.6.0 and at b6fca69.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root at b6fca69: (1) `git show HEAD:README.md | grep -nE '(src|href)="[^"h#][^"]*"|\]\([^)h#][^)]*\)'` lists line 11 (assets/mhfe-mascot.png) and lines 653/654/656 (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). (2) `grep -n 'add_common_files\|cp README\|cp LICENSE' scripts/package-release.sh` shows that only README.md and the licence files are copied, at lines 65-75, called at lines 112 and 141. (3) `tar -tzvf canonical-output-aud023/release/mhfe-v0.6.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (likewise for aarch64 and the browser archive, plus `unzip -l` of the Windows zip) lists no assets/ entry. (4) `tar -xzOf <archive> ./README.md | grep -n mascot` (./README-mhfe.md for the browser archive, `unzip -p ... README.md` for the zip) prints line 11 with the img tag.
- **Expected behavior:** Every relative reference in a document that ships in a release archive resolves inside that archive. Sources: FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md CHECK-DOC-002 ('Check relative links' and 'source/binary release inclusion'), and the project's own precedent, AUD-008-DOC003 and AUD-010-DOC002. In both findings a packaged README's relative reference to a file the package lacks was a low DOC finding, fixed by an absolute URL or by shipping the file. DOC-06 (code and documents agree) also applies: the packaging code ships the document without the asset it references.
- **Observed behavior:** In each of the four canonical v0.6.0 archives, the README (README.md, or README-mhfe.md in the browser archive) keeps line 11 <img src="assets/mhfe-mascot.png">, and the archive has no assets/ folder. A reader of the unpacked archive, typically offline as README.md:596-597 recommends, sees a broken image or its alt text at the top of the README. Every other relative link of the README resolves in the archive.
- **Impact:** Cosmetic and documentation only. The shipped README opens with a broken image. Nothing about the program's behaviour, security or verification is affected.
- **Evidence:** Logged with docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-readme-mascot/ (local-only). readme-relative-refs.log (exit 0): HEAD b6fca69, README relative references at lines 11, 653, 654 and 656, and assets/mhfe-mascot.png tracked (blob 769736aa). list-mhfe-v0.6.0-linux-x86_64.log, list-mhfe-v0.6.0-linux-aarch64.log, list-mhfe-v0.6.0-browser.log and list-mhfe-v0.6.0-windows-x86_64.log (exit 0): archive listings with README/README-mhfe.md, LICENSE-*, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/, and no assets/. archive-readme-img.log (exit 0): line 11 with the img tag in the README of all four archives. Static trace: scripts/package-release.sh:65-76, 112 and 141. `git show <tag>:README.md | grep -c mascot` gives 1 for v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.5.0 and v0.6.0, and no tag's package-release.sh mentions assets. AUD-023 informationalObservations[48] and AUD-010-DOC002's challenge note recorded this only as an observation.
- **Recommended fix:** Make the image reference absolute and tied to a tag or commit, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/v<version>/assets/mhfe-mascot.png or the github.com/.../raw/<ref>/ form. Alternatively, have add_common_files copy assets/mhfe-mascot.png into each archive and list it in the archive checks. Either way, add a packaged-README link check (as AUD-010-DOC002 recommended for the browser README) that resolves every relative src/href and Markdown link of the README inside each staged archive folder.
- **Required verification:** After the fix, rebuild the canonical archives (owner run of scripts/build-reproducible.sh) and run a link check over the README.md / README-mhfe.md inside each archive: every relative reference resolves inside the archive, or none remains. The check-release-artifacts or packaging gate fails on a README with an unresolved relative reference.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[48] (link check; the README copied into release archives shows assets/mhfe-mascot.png), AUD-010-DOC002 (packaged browser README links to API.md, which the package does not contain; its challenge note recorded the root README's relative links as an observation), AUD-008-DOC003 (packaged browser README links to an absent measurements file)
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. README.md:11 is the only relative reference in README.md that a release archive cannot resolve: <img src="assets/mhfe-mascot.png">. Its other relative links (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at lines 653, 654 and 656) point to files that ship, and every other link is an absolute URL or an in-page anchor. scripts/package-release.sh add_common_files (lines 65-76) copies README.md, the licence files and licenses/ into every archive, but not assets/. The CLI archive calls it at line 112 and the browser archive at line 141, where README.md becomes README-mhfe.md. The macOS release job uses the same script (.github/workflows/release.yml:80). In all four canonical v0.6.0 archives (canonical-output-aud023), the README keeps the img line at line 11 and the archive has no assets/ entry. The README has had this line since v0.3.0, and no tag's package-release.sh copies assets. The project already treats a shipped README whose relative reference is missing from its package as a low DOC finding (AUD-008-DOC003 and AUD-010-DOC002). AUD-010 and AUD-023 noted this case only as an observation. It is a concrete, bounded presentation defect: low severity, not a matter of taste. None of the confirmed findings duplicates it; the nearest one is about links in audit records. I corrected one claim: no project document says the README deliberately uses absolute links. The expected behaviour now cites CHECK-DOC-002 and the AUD-008-DOC003/AUD-010-DOC002 precedent instead.

##### AUD-024-DOC022 — Low — README.md's attestation command verifies only that some workflow of the repository signed the archive, on any ref and any runner, although the sentence above it says the attestations bind each archive to its source commit and workflow

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Release verification documentation
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-DOC-001
- **Rules:** DOC-07, CHECK-DOC-002, CHECK-BLD-005
- **Affected files and builds:** README.md:596-597. The sentence reads 'GitHub build attestations bind each archive to its source commit and workflow. Check them on the connected computer before carrying the archive offline:'.
  README.md:599-601 holds the only command the README gives, at line 600: `gh attestation verify mhfe-v0.6.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz --repo hobby-eng/mhfe`.
  docs/RELEASING.md:59 repeats the binding claim with no command. docs/RELEASING.md:21-24 tells the maintainer to verify 'the GitHub build attestations' before signing, also with no command.
  The only workflow that attests is .github/workflows/release.yml: trigger at lines 3-6 (push of tags v*), job permissions at lines 107-113 (id-token: write, attestations: write), and actions/attest at lines 131-134. This is documentation for every release, all platforms' archives and the browser package.
- **Reproduction:** Run from the repository root, with no network: each run is inside `unshare -rn` and uses a private HOME, config and cache.
  1. Run the probe `docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-attestation-command/probe.sh`. It runs AUD-019's gh 2.101.0 (docs/audits/AUD-019-evidence/tools/gh, release-archive checksum matches gh_2.101.0_checksums.txt) as `gh attestation verify canonical-output-signing-v0.6.0/mhfe-v0.6.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz --bundle <bundle> --custom-trusted-root <public-good trusted_root.jsonl> <flags>`. The bundle was extracted from docs/audits/AUD-019-evidence/attestation-mhfe-v0.6.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz.json.
  2. Run with README's flags `--repo hobby-eng/mhfe --format json --jq '.[].verificationResult.verifiedIdentity'`. It exits 0, and the enforced identity is subjectAlternativeName regexp `(?i)^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/` with no runnerEnvironment.
  3. Run with AUD-019's flags `--repo hobby-eng/mhfe --signer-workflow hobby-eng/mhfe/.github/workflows/release.yml --source-ref refs/tags/v0.6.0 --deny-self-hosted-runners`. It exits 0, with regexp `^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/\.github/workflows/release\.yml` and runnerEnvironment github-hosted.
  4. Run `--repo hobby-eng/mhfe --source-ref refs/tags/v9.9.9`. It exits 1 with 'expected SourceRepositoryRef to be refs/tags/v9.9.9, got refs/tags/v0.6.0'. The ref is checked only when it is asked for.
  5. Run `--repo hobby-eng/mhfe --signer-workflow hobby-eng/mhfe/.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It exits 1. The workflow is checked only when it is asked for.
  6. Run `gh attestation verify --help`. It says the identity's precision 'is up to you'. It says that ideally 'the path of the signer workflow is also validated using the --signer-workflow or --cert-identity flags'. It describes --source-ref and --signer-workflow as 'Enforce that ...' options.
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-07 (docs.instructions.md): documents claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides.
  CHECK-DOC-002 (FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md): 'describe exactly what integrity verification checks'.
  The check that README.md offers for 'bind each archive to its source commit and workflow' should enforce that binding. That means the signer workflow .github/workflows/release.yml and the release tag (refs/tags/v<version>), plus a GitHub-hosted runner, as AUD-019 did (docs/audits/AUD-019-evidence/attestation-linux.command.json). Otherwise the text should say that the command checks only that a workflow of hobby-eng/mhfe signed the file.
- **Observed behavior:** The documented command enforces only the repository prefix of the certificate SAN (`(?i)^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/`) and the source repository. It exits 0 for an attestation made by any workflow file of hobby-eng/mhfe, on any branch or tag, including one on a self-hosted runner.
  Genuine archives of every earlier release, attested by release.yml at refs/tags/v0.5.0 and the like, also pass it under any file name. The sentence above the command nevertheless presents it as the check of the commit and workflow binding. docs/RELEASING.md gives no attestation command at all, for the downloader (line 59) or for the maintainer's pre-signing check (lines 21-24).
- **Impact:** A reader who runs the README's command believes the archive was built by the release workflow for that release tag, but the check proves less.
  The following would pass it:
  - an archive attested by another workflow, or by release.yml on another ref, pushed by anyone with write access or a token with workflow scope;
  - an older genuine release archive offered as the current one (downgrade).
  Impact is bounded: the OpenPGP-signed SHA256SUMS that README.md asks the reader to check first does not list such an archive, and today only release.yml on v* tags requests id-token and attestations write. The secondary provenance check is still weaker than the README states.
- **Evidence:** Logs are in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-attestation-command/, each with a .command.json from run-logged.sh:
  - gh-attestation-verify-help.log: gh 2.101.0 help, exit 0.
  - readme-repo-only.log: README flags, exit 0.
  - readme-repo-only-json.log: README flags, exit 0, verifiedIdentity SAN regexp (?i)^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/.
  - aud019-flags-json.log: AUD-019 flags, exit 0, regexp ^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/\.github/workflows/release\.yml, runnerEnvironment github-hosted.
  - repo-plus-other-ref.log: exit 1, the ref mismatch is reported only when --source-ref is given.
  - repo-plus-other-workflow.log: exit 1 with --signer-workflow ci.yml.
  probe.sh is kept beside the logs. Archive SHA-256 a97d4380...0b1c equals its line in canonical-output-signing-v0.6.0/SHA256SUMS.
  Static reads at b6fca69: README.md:594-606, docs/RELEASING.md:15-60, .github/workflows/release.yml:1-40 and 95-140, and grep of id-token and attestations permissions across .github/workflows/*.yml (only release.yml:112-113). AUD-023 informationalObservations[42] recorded this only as an observation.
- **Recommended fix:** In README.md:600, give the full command: `gh attestation verify mhfe-v<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz --repo hobby-eng/mhfe --signer-workflow hobby-eng/mhfe/.github/workflows/release.yml --source-ref refs/tags/v<version> --deny-self-hosted-runners`. Leave out --source-digest, which fails for v0.3.0 to v0.5.0 after the history rewrite.
  Add the same command to docs/RELEASING.md's 'Verify a downloaded release' section and to its pre-signing step. Alternatively, reword README.md:596-597 to say exactly what --repo alone checks.
- **Required verification:** Doc review of README.md and docs/RELEASING.md. Then, on a connected machine, run the new command against a published release archive: it should exit 0. Run it with a wrong --source-ref or --signer-workflow: it should exit 1. The offline probe in docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-attestation-command/probe.sh can repeat steps 2 to 5 without network.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023 informationalObservations[42] (README attestation command does not bind workflow or tag)
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. README.md:596-597 says GitHub build attestations bind each archive to its source commit and workflow, and asks the reader to check them with the command at README.md:600. That command passes only `--repo hobby-eng/mhfe`.
  
  I ran the gh 2.101.0 binary kept by AUD-019 offline, inside a network namespace, against the public v0.6.0 linux-x86_64 archive, its AUD-019-downloaded attestation bundle and the cached Sigstore public-good trusted root:
  - With the README's flags only, the enforced identity is the SAN regex `(?i)^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/`. That accepts any workflow file of the repository, on any ref, with no runner condition.
  - With AUD-019's flags, the regex narrows to `^https://github\.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/\.github/workflows/release\.yml` and adds `runnerEnvironment: github-hosted`.
  - `--source-ref` and `--signer-workflow` are enforced only when they are given: refs/tags/v9.9.9 and ci.yml each fail.
  
  gh's own help says the precision of the identity is up to the caller, and that the signer workflow should ideally be checked with --signer-workflow.
  
  This is not a duplicate of a confirmed finding. AUD-023 recorded it only as informational observation 42 (BLD), not as a finding or a disposition.
  
  Severity is low. The OpenPGP-signed SHA256SUMS remains the primary check, and it would catch both the downgrade and an archive from another workflow. The attestation check that the README presents as binding commit and workflow is weaker than stated.

##### AUD-024-DOC023 — Low — SECURITY.md says the browser package contains no network code, and the package gate says no script of the package does, although the package ships core/mhfe-fast-mode.py, a loopback HTTP server, and the gate reads only the package's .js files.

- **Category:** DOC.
- **Severity:** low.
- **Status:** open.
- **Release blocking:** false; No demonstrated secret compromise and no failure of an integrity, isolation or recovery guarantee; the impact above is bounded.
- **Subsystem:** Security documentation of the browser package and its fast-mode launcher; browser package no-network gate
- **Procedure task:** CHECK-SEC-002
- **Rules:** DOC-07, DOC-06
- **Affected files and builds:** SECURITY.md:116-118 ('The browser package loads no remote resources and contains no network code'), which contradicts SECURITY.md:203-205 ('The browser package's mhfe-fast-mode.py is the same launcher' as mhfe serve). docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:35-37 (the core holds mhfe-fast-mode.py, 'the package's launcher for the fast mode'). packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:535-537 (socket.socket, bind to 127.0.0.1, listen), :390 (accept) and :544 (webbrowser.open). scripts/build-wasm.sh:67 copies it byte for byte to dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py, and dist/modules.json lists it among the core module's files. The gate: scripts/package-check/manifest.mjs:166-169 (comment 'No script of the package contains code that could reach the network'), :170-178 (scriptsOf keeps only names ending in .js, at :172), :94-97 (doc comment) and :349-351 (success line 'no script of the package contains network code'), run as part 3 of scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs (:73). Build affected: the browser package (dist/, version 0.6.1), on every platform where it is distributed. The command-line tool is not affected: SECURITY.md uses 'the tool' for it, and its only network code is mhfe serve.
- **Reproduction:** From the repository root: docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/run-logged.sh docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/skeptic-package-network v1-package-network-code ../tmp/aud024/skeptic-package-network/probe.sh. The probe prints SECURITY.md:116-119 and :203-205, the core files in dist/modules.json, build-wasm.sh:67 and a cmp of packaging/ against dist/, and the socket calls in dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py. It then runs the packaged launcher with --no-browser on a synthetic page with its sha256sum checksum file, sends GET to the printed 127.0.0.1 address and stops the launcher with SIGTERM. Last, it applies the gate's .js filter (manifest.mjs:170-178) to dist/modules.json and lists the packaged scripts the scan skips. It uses loopback only, no secret and no Argon2.
- **Expected behavior:** DOC-07 (docs.instructions.md:41-45): documents claim no stronger guarantee than the code provides. DOC-06 (docs.instructions.md:36-39): code and documents agree. By SECURITY.md's own usage, a 127.0.0.1 listener is network code: :118-119 say the only network code in the tool is mhfe serve, 'which listens on 127.0.0.1'. SECURITY.md:203-205 and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:35-37 place mhfe-fast-mode.py, 'the same launcher', inside the browser package. So the package contains network code, and a statement about the package's network code or scripts has to name or exclude the launcher.
- **Observed behavior:** SECURITY.md:116-118 reads 'Nothing connects to a network. The browser package loads no remote resources and contains no network code'. The package's core module ships mhfe-fast-mode.py (dist/modules.json core files: argon2-mt.js, argon2-st.js, client.d.ts, client.js, mhfe-fast-mode.py), byte-identical to packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py. Run from dist/core, it printed 'Open http://127.0.0.1:36855/ in your browser.' and answered GET / with 200 and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin. The package gate scans runtime/runtime.js, runtime/worker.js, core/argon2-mt.js, core/argon2-st.js, core/client.js, repair/repair.js, passwords/passwords.js and wallet/wallet.js. core/mhfe-fast-mode.py is the only packaged script left out, yet the gate prints 'no script of the package contains network code'. The rest of the sentence ('the only network code in the tool is mhfe serve') is accurate, because 'the tool' means the command-line program in SECURITY.md.
- **Impact:** A reader who sizes the browser package's attack surface from SECURITY.md:116-118 misses the package's Python listener. So does an integrator who embeds the package and trusts the gate's 'no script of the package contains network code'. The impact is bounded: the listener binds only 127.0.0.1, checks the Host header, serves one public page and never receives a secret (SECURITY.md:201-227). The browser-side guarantee, that the package's JavaScript fetches nothing, is true.
- **Evidence:** docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/skeptic-package-network/v1-package-network-code.log, sha256 f18ac40cff59b19c721ddd30b9024f392256b3ae4c6b04f9862f2643cc85082b, with v1-package-network-code.command.json (exit 0, 2026-10-14T07:51:57Z). Key lines: core files ['argon2-mt.js', 'argon2-st.js', 'client.d.ts', 'client.js', 'mhfe-fast-mode.py']; 'dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py is byte-identical to packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py'; '535: listener = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)', '536: listener.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))', '537: listener.listen(MAX_CONNECTIONS)'; 'GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ -> 200 COOP: same-origin body bytes: 32'; 'not scanned, not .js or .d.ts/.wasm: core/mhfe-fast-mode.py'. The reviewer's log docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/browser-isolation/p15-package-network-code.log shows the same static facts. In git history the sentence dates from cc91b0b (2026-09-29), and build-wasm.sh has copied the launcher into dist/core since d52dff8 (2026-10-07). Not reported before: AUD-023-BLD008 covered only the gates' JS pattern lists, and AUD-023's CHECK-DOC-001 listed SECURITY.md:115-136 among the claims that hold.
- **Recommended fix:** Reword SECURITY.md:116-118. The package's scripts (runtime, worker, classes and the Argon2 builds) load no remote resources and contain no code that reaches the network. The package's one network code is core/mhfe-fast-mode.py, which, like mhfe serve, listens only on 127.0.0.1 for the one page it serves and never receives a secret. Keep 'the only network code in the tool is mhfe serve' for the command-line program. In scripts/package-check/manifest.mjs:94-97, :166-169 and :349-351, say that the gate scans the package's JavaScript and name mhfe-fast-mode.py as the deliberate exception, covered by scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py.
- **Required verification:** Documentation review: SECURITY.md's network statements name or exclude every file in dist/modules.json that opens a socket. The gate's comment and success line state its .js-only scope. node scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs still passes on the current dist.
- **Related findings:** AUD-023-BLD008
- **Verification:** confirmed: Reproduced at b6fca69. SECURITY.md:116-118 says the browser package "contains no network code". The same sentence counts a 127.0.0.1 listener (mhfe serve) as network code, and SECURITY.md:203-205 calls the package's mhfe-fast-mode.py "the same launcher". The build copies that launcher into the package (scripts/build-wasm.sh:67), and dist/modules.json lists it as a core file. It creates, binds and listens on a TCP socket at :535-537. In my probe the packaged copy, run on a synthetic page, answered GET over 127.0.0.1 with status 200. The package gate's comment (manifest.mjs:166-169) and its success line (:349-351) say "no script of the package contains network code", but its filter at :172 keeps only .js names, so core/mhfe-fast-mode.py is the one packaged script it never reads. I narrowed one claim of the candidate. SECURITY.md uses "the tool" for the command-line program throughout (lines 24, 34, 51, 75, 79, 138), so "the only network code in the tool is mhfe serve" holds for the command-line program. The false part is the browser-package clause. This is not a repeat of AUD-023: AUD-023-BLD008 covered the gates' pattern lists, and AUD-023's CHECK-DOC-001 marked SECURITY.md:115-136 as holding. The severity is low: a documentation overstatement with bounded impact, since the listener is loopback-only, serves one public page and receives no secret.

### Informational observations

General advice and observations without a demonstrated defect, by reviewer; not findings.

- **The summary line 'Secrets kept in locked memory, out of swap' is broader than what is locked** (secrets-native): settings.rs:383-387 and 439-453 print it when the 8,192-byte typed-line probe locks; SECURITY.md:68-82 lists secrets that are not locked (BIP39 seeds and keys, each round's Argon2 key, salt and mask, the frame lines) and the Argon2 work area, which cannot be locked and may be swapped. The line can stand next to the warning that swap is not encrypted. A narrower label ('typed secrets locked') would match the probe.
- **The empty-network read-back checks interface names and IPv4 routes only** (secrets-native): protect.rs:395-417 (network_empty) accepts the namespace when /proc/self/net/dev lists only lo and /proc/self/net/route has no route; it does not read IPv6 routes or whether lo is down, which SECURITY.md:126-127 states ('only inactive loopback'). Harmless today because the kernel creates lo down in a new namespace and the seccomp filter refuses sockets.
- **Usage errors repeat an unexpected argument verbatim** (secrets-native): main.rs:281-295 shows clap's rendered error: `mhfe decrypt abandon abandon about` prints "Unexpected argument 'abandon' found" and `mhfe check --fingerprint 'abandon abandon about'` repeats the whole quoted text. CORE-24 forbids repeating typed text, but here the shell already shows and keeps the command line, so the extra exposure is small; a generic message for positional arguments would avoid it.
- **`mhfe password` still prints its password on the main screen where no private screen is possible** (secrets-native): diceware.rs:265-286 writes the password to standard output when it is a terminal, also at TERM=dumb or with standard input not a terminal, where flow::is_active() is false; AUD-023 recorded this as an observation. CORE-39 allows plain sequential output at TERM=dumb, so it is not reported as a defect.
- **Two unlocked secret copies are not named in SECURITY.md's list** (secrets-native): rekey.rs:350-353 copies the reference passphrase into an unlocked Zeroizing<String> for the 16-bit source check, and chosen_words.rs:165 copies the chosen word into an unlocked Zeroizing<String>; both are wiped. SECURITY.md:68-74 lists the copies that are wiped but not locked and names neither.
- **Panicking invariant checks outside tests lack the RUST-05 exception form** (secrets-native): src/memory.rs:44-48 and 105-109 (assert_eq! that a locked buffer did not grow) and src/bin/mhfe/check_word.rs:133 (unreachable!) panic in release (abort) without the `#[expect(clippy::expect_used, reason = ...)]` form RUST-05 asks for; clippy's panic lint does not see assert!/unreachable!. None is reachable on the paths reviewed.
- **Windows-only unwiped copies in console handling** (secrets-native): hidden_input/windows.rs:127-153 peeks up to 32 INPUT_RECORDs, which may hold keys typed ahead during a list, into an unwiped stack array; anstream's legacy-console adapter (used when VT processing cannot be enabled) collects printed text in an ordinary String. Both fall under SECURITY.md:39-41's caveat about dependency buffers; not executed (no Windows host).
- **Start-menu commands run without a network namespace by design** (secrets-native): SECURITY.md:129-132 and protect.rs:592-606: the menu process has the ctrlc thread, so unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) is refused for its command threads; the filter and the ruleset still apply. Running each menu command as a re-executed child process would give it the namespace too.
- **Protections verified as holding at b6fca69** (secrets-native): Core dumps off and non-dumpable (read back after the user namespace by the startup checks; s11 'Core dumps off'); seccomp refuses sockets and io_uring with EACCES and Landlock refuses opening for writing and creating files (s03/h01, in both the direct and the menu case); LockedText/LockedBytes reserved and locked before filling and wiped before unlocking, with page hold counts; the Argon2 work area wiped by the C code and by Rust after a failed call (engine/ffi.rs:172-195), MADV_DONTDUMP on Linux; typed lines locked (s11 'Locked memory works'); hint rows built in final-size wiped buffers (AUD-023-SEC001 fix); swap writeback attribute followed (AUD-023-SEC002 fix); result writes to a closed pipe or full device exit 1 (AUD-023-FUN001 fix, s07); rekey's new settings and --confirm refused before the container (AUD-023-UI002 fix); secret commands refuse at start without a terminal (AUD-023-UI006 fix).
- **WorkerJob uses a worker's result, questions and news before the worker has said it is of this build** (browser-isolation): web/runtime.js:159-166 says a handler runs only once the worker has said that it is of this build (#started, 389-406), and the casts of TS-04 rely on it, but #receive (342-377) accepts 'result', 'ask' and news without a prior 'ready'; the scripted-worker probe resolves parameters() with a result sent without 'ready' (p4-worker-protocol.log). No practical mix found: workers before v0.6.0 (no handshake) expect another request shape and glue and fail to instantiate this WebAssembly, so they end in an error, not a silent mix. Requiring 'ready' before any other reply would make the comment true.
- **An error code from the worker is used as it arrives** (browser-isolation): web/runtime.js:364-368 passes any text code to MhfeError; the scripted worker's NOT_A_CODE reached the page as code NOT_A_CODE (p4). The build-time gate (scripts/package-check/manifest.mjs:50-80) keeps library, API.md and MhfeErrorCode equal, so this matters only for a worker of another build that slipped past the handshake.
- **The class file's build is compared only in the startup check** (browser-isolation): A core/client.js of another build beside this runtime is refused with PACKAGE_MISMATCH by readContainer() and startupCheck(), but parameters() resolves (p12-class-build-ungated.log), and selfTest() (not gated, web/client.js:922-924) runs the same way, while BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:63-65 and SECURITY.md:290-291 say files of different builds are refused before they work together. The worker, WebAssembly and Argon2 builds are still compared, so the computation is consistent; low impact.
- **Sixteen idle connections keep the fast-mode page from loading** (browser-isolation): SECURITY.md:217-219 says a slow or stalled client cannot keep the page from loading; that holds per client, but a local program that holds MAX_CONNECTIONS (16) idle connections and reopens each at its 10 s deadline has every further connection closed at once (serve.rs:277-280, mhfe-fast-mode.py:400-402; both launchers' tests show the 17th closed). Within the stated threat model (other programs on the same computer); availability only.
- **The Python launcher waits for a browser that $BROWSER names before it serves** (browser-isolation): packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:544-553 calls webbrowser.open() before serve(); CPython's GenericBrowser (used for $BROWSER entries that are not registered GUI controllers, and for console browsers) waits for the browser process, so that browser requests the page while nobody accepts it. The stand-in browser got no answer within 5 s and serving started only after it gave up (p6-console-browser.log). Console browsers cannot run the page anyway; mhfe serve spawns its opener without waiting (serve.rs:301-312).
- **Both launchers accept whitespace before a header's colon and send a body with HEAD error responses** (browser-isolation): RFC 9112 section 5.1 requires a 400 for whitespace between a field name and its colon; both launchers serve 'Host : 127.0.0.1:<port>' (serve.rs:439-442, mhfe-fast-mode.py:323-326; launcher-parity probe). A HEAD with a wrong Host or path gets its error body (serve.rs:392-401, mhfe-fast-mode.py:305-306). No intermediary is involved, so no smuggling risk; conformance only.
- **Self-check results are shared by WebAssembly object identity, and a Uint8Array is kept by reference** (browser-isolation): CompiledModule (web/runtime.js:63-103) keeps the page's Uint8Array and compiles it lazily; passedOnPage (872-878, 1251-1268) skips parts that another class passed with the same object. A page that changes those bytes between classes would get parts skipped for different bytes. Outside the accidental-mix model (tampering is for SHA256SUMS), but copying the bytes at construction would make the identity hold.
- **The WebAssembly's imports include generic reflection** (browser-isolation): runtime/mhfe.wasm imports Error, Function.prototype.apply/call, Reflect.get, Array new/push, the derive/fill/reserve bridges and wasm-bindgen intrinsics (p9-wasm-imports.log). With the page policy's script-src without 'unsafe-eval', a reflected Function constructor cannot compile code; a host page that allows unsafe-eval relies on the reviewed Rust code alone.
- **The module classes start one worker per call without a limit** (browser-isolation): MhfeRepair, MhfePasswords and MhfeWallet run every call in a new worker (web/runtime.js:947-961), so a page that calls wordHints() on every keystroke starts unbounded concurrent workers, each instantiating the 1.3 MB WebAssembly (CORE-50 asks for explicit concurrency limits). BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:483-484 advises asking once typing pauses; drawPhrase() is bounded (1 to 256 workers).
- **Positive results of the residue scans** (browser-isolation): In the in-process instance, after a decrypt, a check with a fingerprint and TREZOR, a hidden-wallet session opened and closed while waiting, and a sealed rekey, the WebAssembly memory held only the static copies of the self-check vectors (22 of the all-zero phrase, 3 of 'public test password', 1 of 'TREZOR') and no copy of the new or hidden passwords (p13, p1 control, p2). The Argon2 bridge wipes and frees its C-heap copies (web/argon2-engine.js:54-60). This is Node's instance, not a terminated browser worker.
- **dist/ is the reviewed source** (browser-isolation): dist/ (build de06b919b42eae2f) equals web/ and packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py apart from the stamped build identifiers; the worker parts at the end of dist/runtime/worker.js equal web/ in build-wasm.sh's order; dist/README.md's SHA-256 list matches every file (p7-dist-matches-sources.log).
- **Usage example of check() destructures a field the API no longer returns (outside this role's scope)** (browser-isolation): docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:117-123 writes 'const { matches, path, evidence } = await client.check(...)' and 'matches is true', but check() resolves to { outcome, path, evidence } with outcome "matches" | "notVerified" | "doesNotMatch" (web/client.js:463-472, web/client.d.ts:582-605); a page copying the example reads undefined and could report a match as failed. The comment's 'evidence: { builtInCheck, walletCheck }' also omits matchingLengths and passed. Flagged for the documentation reviewer.
- **An unreachable binding message uses Debug formatting** (browser-isolation): src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:508-511 words a refusal 'the owner confirms a reading of {:?} words here', which prints a Rust list such as [12, 15]; the client refuses the same case first with its own TypeError (web/client.js:1437-1443), so a page never sees it.
- **A trailing space makes five check-word words read as six with an erased check word** (core-crypto): PasswordReview::of("jovial trailing pavilion cresting ninth ") splits at U+0020 into six tokens, the last one empty. It reads Restorable and offers the repair '... ninth sushi' at position 6, although the person left out word 3 (c04-probe-check-word-trailing-space.log). This conforms to the literal rule (spec README.md:845-854, 'splits the typed string at U+0020'), and the repair is only offered: repairs_first() is false, and the text as typed stays the default. A trailing or leading empty token could still be treated as no token, so that such an input is not presented as uniquely repairable.
- **Cancellation is modelled as an error variant** (core-crypto): MhfeError::Cancelled (src/error.rs:130) is how a person's cancel travels through the round callbacks (feistel.rs:40-42, mhfe.rs:26-29) and the draws (wallet_check.rs:113-118). Read literally, CORE-22 asks that 'a person cancelling uses return values'. VerifierMismatch for a stated short length that no check passes is defensible as wrong input under CORE-22. Left as an architecture question, not a finding.
- **Recorded independent full replays name earlier verifier scripts** (core-crypto): tests/fixtures/suite3-vectors/independent-verification.json names verifier SHA-256 544649a4…, and suite4's names 72a9b15b…. Commit 61a5c41 changed scripts/independent-suite3.py (now 057e04c8…) and independent-suite4.py (now 6b36cf42…) after those runs. The commit message says so, and every recorded file hash still matches its fixture. The baseline trusted-key runs of the current scripts pass (b23, b24). A new full run would re-anchor the record.
- **Container phrases and a check-word repair are not handled as secrets everywhere** (core-crypto): The library holds containers in Zeroizing buffers in NewContainer, encrypt's result and ContainerFacts. It returns plain String in repair::Repaired.container and Change.read/word (repair.rs:321-344, which also derive Debug), check_container (phrase.rs:148-150), repair_words (repair.rs:281-292) and word_numbers' lower-case copies (phrase.rs:205). check_word::Repair derives Debug, which prints a word of the password (check_word.rs:86-93). RUST-13 and CORE-24 cover secrets explicitly, and the container phrase's status (private, not the seed) is not stated, so this is recorded as an observation.
- **The strength estimate's 100-character limit does not apply to the dice-word path** (core-crypto): strength.rs:19-21 says 'Only the first 100 characters are read', but different_dice_words scans every token against the 7,776 words. 'zoom ' x 200,000 (1 MB) takes 0.72 s natively (c04-probe-strength-time.log). Fast for real passwords; the doc and the code differ (DOC-06).
- **Password::new normalizes the whole input past the 1,024-byte limit** (core-crypto): password.rs:56-72 keeps running NFKD after the limit, to report the exact length in PASSWORD_TOO_LONG, as the fixture expects (1,056 and 1,025). The work grows with the input; inputs are bounded elsewhere (8,192 bytes on the CLI), and browser-supplied strings are not bounded here (CORE-50).
- **Encapsulation of the permutation** (core-crypto): feistel::Permutation (feistel.rs:116-121) exposes its engine, password, work factor and geometry as pub fields, and RoundTrace's fields are pub, inside a private module. Mhfe::with_engine likewise takes the work factor and the engine separately. All construction sites pair them correctly (mhfe.rs:272, wasm_api/core.rs:650-652, core/hidden.rs:38-43). CORE-02, CORE-11 and RUST-06 would keep fields private.
- **Public functions whose docs do not name their errors** (core-crypto): Several public functions of this scope describe what they do but not the errors they return (CORE-20): for example repair::repair_words, WordWishes::new, PasswordRecipe::make and random::uniform_below. The missing_docs gate checks only that a doc exists.
- **Independent confirmations without defect** (core-crypto): Argon2 context layout equals vendor argon2.h. All engine tags, the BLAKE2b-256 and HMAC known answers, the feistel salt test value and the EFF list SHA-256 were recomputed independently. The NFKD expansion bound of 11 (wallet/keys.rs:87) equals the true maximum in Unicode 17.0.0 (U+FDFA). The length rules (detection.rs:69-85) match every branch of the spec's recovery rules. The suite selection and admission table (spec README.md:638-646) is enforced before Argon2 (mhfe.rs:395-448).
- **Minor wording** (core-crypto): random.rs:1-3 says every draw goes through uniform_below, but entropy draws fill bytes directly (wallet_check.rs:230). SECURITY.md:104 calls the wallet check 'a draft over the BIP39 seed', which is probably meant to read 'a filter'. clippy.toml sets too-many-lines-threshold = 100, where RUST-01 names 150; this is stricter and belongs to the tooling scope.
- **Unbounded wallet-check draw loop** (core-crypto): PhraseDraw::draw (wallet_check.rs:257-271) loops until a phrase is found or the caller's on_draws stops it. The expected number of draws is stated (WishOdds), and the CLI and worker can cancel, so this is reported only as context for the random-source finding.
- **Normative statement map: where each specification rule is met** (spec-parity): The inventory is in normative-inventory.log: 93 sentences with BCP 14 keywords in mhfe_spec/README.md. Each item gives the spec lines, then where mhfe meets the rule.

Vector requirements (1172-1205): the fixtures are byte-identical, and the replays are wired: tests/vector_share/replay.rs, recorded-key cipher-rounds.
- **Specification defect: the Reference Implementation section understates v0.6.0's rehearsal deviations** (spec-parity): mhfe_spec/README.md:1146-1150 and CHANGELOG.md:16-18 say that v0.6.0 follows the rules "except for the rehearsal outcome when several lengths match and none was stated".

AUD-023-FUN002 established more. v0.6.0 also reported "matches" on a 16-bit source-check pass, and "does not match" where "not verified" was due, such as a 24-word reading with no reference.

This was handed to the specification session by AUD-023 and is still uncorrected at mhfe_spec 79c69d5.
- **Specification defect: the rehearsal outcome is undefined for a wallet reference that does not match while one reading is verified** (spec-parity): mhfe_spec/README.md:486-488 reports "matches" when the length rules give exactly one verified reading "or when a supplied wallet-identity reference matches". Read literally, an address that does not match beside a verified 12-word reading would still give "matches".

mhfe reports "does not match" there (src/rehearsal.rs:373-385, compare_state). That is the sensible reading. The specification should state it.
- **mhfe's wallet-check reference turns a failing 16-bit check into "does not match"** (spec-parity): src/rehearsal.rs:366-372 gives DoesNotMatch for Reference::WalletCheck when the 16-bit check fails. This is documented at API.md:107-108 and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:185-187.

The specification says a source-check failure "is not an error and does not block the reading". Its rehearsal says "does not match" only when no reading is given (README.md:428-430, 489-491).

mhfe's reason is that the owner says the phrase was drawn with the check, which the specification lets matter ("means something only if the owner knows"). Under DOC-06 the deviation should be named as deliberate in one of the two repositories, or settled in the specification.
- **mhfe check with a stated length among several passing lengths does not name the others** (spec-parity): For `--words 12` on a container whose state passes both 12 and 21, the outcome is Matches. passed_lines (check.rs:541-578, through own_checks_passed at rehearsal.rs:49-62) lists only "the built-in check of a 12-word original seed phrase", without the 21.

The recovery rule says "use it, and name every other length that matches" (mhfe_spec/README.md:416). The rehearsal's list of allowed facts (:478-481) does not require it.

The browser's evidence.matchingLengths carries the lengths, but the page duty does not ask pages to show them. The case is rare, about 2^-32.
- **README describes a stated length after detection imprecisely** (spec-parity): README.md:256-262 says that after detection finds no single length, "a stated short length that does not pass does not match".

When detection found several lengths and the person then states another short length, the tool reports "not verified": BuiltInCheck gives Several, then NotVerified (check.rs:478-507). The case is rare.
- **The CLI shows the full words read only as hints while typing** (spec-parity): After a phrase or container is accepted, the CLI records only "12 words, valid" or "24 words, valid" (encrypt.rs:440-458, terminal.rs:585-636). The expanded words of four-letter abbreviations are never shown back. The live hint lists the matching word while typing, but there are no hints at TERM=dumb or in scripts.

The specification SHOULD (mhfe_spec/README.md:326-327) is met for the browser through readPhrase/readContainer and the duty at :892. For the CLI it is met only partly.
- **The wallet-check explanation in mhfe new appears only on request** (spec-parity): The specification MUST (README.md:676-678) is to explain the benefits, false matches, entropy conditioning and deniability costs before the owner chooses.

In mhfe new, explain() (new_wallet.rs:202-261) appears only when `?` is pressed. With --wallet-check yes it is skipped entirely (new_wallet.rs:121-151): only the funds warning and the weak-passphrase warning appear. The question line states the entropy cost alone.

AUD-023 accepted explain() as meeting the MUST, and CORE-40/CORE-41 explain the design. The browser duty (:939-947) requires the full explanation before the choice.
- **Rekey keeps suite 4 without asking** (spec-parity): A rekey of a same-length container always seals a same-length replacement:
- src/rekey.rs:349-352, "a container of the old one's kind";
- README.md:289, "in the old container's format";
- the browser rekey.

The specification lets re-encryption change the suite (README.md:502-503) and says "an application MUST use suite 4 only when the user has chosen it for that container" (:604-605). This is a documented design choice, not named as a deviation.
- **Smaller SHOULD gaps in the CLI** (spec-parity): Level above 0 (spec :544-545): the reminder at settings.rs:404-412 omits that such a computer "must still be available years later". The --mem help says only to choose a level the recovery computer can provide.

Repair card (:804-806): the on-screen card hint (container_repair.rs:690) says to keep the card apart, but not to guard it like the container phrase. README.md:430 says it.

Suite 4 rehearsal (:652-654): the CLI's "Next" line is the same for both suites and does not stress, for suite 4, rehearsing from the finished backup (encrypt.rs:193-200).
- **The repair card is computed before the creation check** (spec-parity): Encryption::run computes the repair card before the creation check (src/operation.rs:253-258) and releases it only through Sealed after the check passes. The bytes are identical, so nothing observable changes.

The specification wording (README.md:747-748) is "computed from the final verified container after its creation check has passed". The CLI comment at encrypt.rs:302-303 says the card "is made from the container once its check has passed", which is inaccurate (CORE-19).
- **The negative serialization vector of the wallet check is not a known answer** (spec-parity): The specification publishes the case "Omitting BE32(256) from the first row gives f2c9f765 and fails" (vectors/profiles/README.md). It is not among mhfe's wallet-check known answers (profile-vectors.log, exit 1 for this value only).

The whole-digest comparison of the positive vectors would already detect an omitted BE32.
- **No current document says that suite 2 containers are not readable** (spec-parity): README.md, SECURITY.md, API.md and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md never say that containers of suite 2 (mhfe 0.3.0 and earlier) cannot be read. Read here as suite 3, a 24-word suite 2 container gives another valid phrase with no error.

Only docs/releases/v0.4.0.md:6-8 says so. The specification points to v0.3.0 (README.md:1143-1145).
- **The rehearsal check skips the 16-bit check where a 24-word reading exists** (spec-parity): With a stated length (Reference::BuiltInCheck), evidence.wallet_check is always None (rehearsal.rs:487-491). In the rare case of a stated short length beside several passing lengths, the length rules do give a 24-word reading, and it is not put through the 16-bit source check.

The specification says "Every 24-word reading MUST also go through the source check" (README.md:425-427). No reading is displayed in a rehearsal, so the practical effect is only a fact not reported.
- **API.md softens a MUST NOT to "should"** (spec-parity): docs/API.md:64-67 says "a result for another program should come from `encrypt`". The specification has "MUST NOT be released before the check has passed" (README.md:392-393). The weaker word is used where API.md relays the rule.
- **The rekey help note words the old-container warning on its own** (spec-parity): The help note of rekey (src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:139-149) says "keep the old container until their funds are moved", without its passwords or settings.

The runtime warning (rekey.rs:163, from Keep::old_container) and the browser keepOldContainer() now share one source. This is a remaining wording copy from AUD-023-ARC016 (CORE-10).
- **The specification repository had untracked files at review time** (spec-parity): mhfe_spec at 79c69d5 had untracked AGENTS.md and docs/drafts/. Only tracked files (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, vectors/) were compared.
- **Wallet derivation and address encodings agree with every published vector and the independent oracle** (wallet-derivation): The oracle passed 186 literal published values. Every check through mhfe passed: all 43 rows of mhfe's address table (0 mismatches), 50 SLIP-0014 rows, BIP84/86/49, DIP-0018, 1,104 differential addresses over 12 coins and every address type, boundary paths at 2^31-1, and hardened derivation after zero-leading parent keys. The same holds natively (1,445 cases) and in the built WASM (85 cases). The self-check tables were independently confirmed: BIP32 vectors 1 and 3, the 24 TREZOR seeds equal trezor/python-mnemonic vectors.json in order, the NFKD passphrase seed, the four wallet-check digests, zero-24's digest prefix 49f67bdf, zero-12's decoy fingerprint 487a156e, and the candidate tables.
- **Path text forms that map to the same path** (wallet-derivation): DerivationPath accepts leading zeros ("m/084'/0'/0'/0/00" reads as m/84'/0'/0'/0/0) and mixes ' and h. It refuses BIP32's own "H" notation ("m/0H") with the generic message "it is not a path like m/84'/0'/0'/0/5". This is common practice and no rule is clearly broken, but CORE-48 asks that different-looking inputs not map silently to one meaning; consider refusing leading zeros or naming the accepted forms.
- **Wallet-check reference failure on a lone 24-word reading** (wallet-derivation): Besides the finding about a verified short reading: on a 24-word reading without a short length, { walletCheck: true } that fails gives "does not match". The specification says a 16-bit failure "is not an error and does not block the reading; it means something only if the owner knows", and labels such a reading "not verified". mhfe reasons that choosing the reference says the owner knows (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:186-187). The specification defines no such reference; if mhfe keeps this, the Reference Implementation section should record it.
- **Remaining runtime coverage of the rehearsal self-check (AUD-023-ARC015)** (wallet-derivation): src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs now covers the length rules, the built-in check's refusal, detection and a failing wallet check. Not covered at run time: a passing wallet-check reference (no published container of a wallet-check phrase exists), Reference::OwnChecks with a passphrase, and the wallet_check field of CheckEvidence, which LengthCase does not compare. A public passphrase that makes zero-24 pass the 16-bit check, found once offline as AUD-010 did for 'aud010 public probe 11656', would allow both cases without Argon2.
- **Leftover provenance wording after AUD-023-DOC009** (wallet-derivation): The self-check comments are now accurate (src/wallet/known_answers/addresses.rs:33-39, src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:17-18, src/wallet/known_answers.rs:209-211). The unit-test comment at src/wallet.rs:700-701 still calls 73c5da0a "the published value"; BIP-0084 publishes the root key from which it is derived.
- **Own-checks search stops at the first passing candidate** (wallet-derivation): ContainerSearch::search_wallet with the own checks (src/search.rs:177-196) returns the first candidate that passes; with the 16-bit check a wrong earlier candidate passes with probability about 8 x 2^-16 for one missing word of 24. The odds are documented. Checking the remaining candidates (minutes) and reporting several would make a false pick visible.
- **Container's own password in a hidden-wallet session** (wallet-derivation): For a 24-word original without the wallet check, HiddenWallets::open with the container's own password shows the main wallet as a hidden wallet. The library cannot tell; the CLI help says "every password other than the container's own" (src/bin/mhfe/wallets.rs:38-42). A short original is refused by rule I29.
- **Scope limits of the address check (by design, stated before the check)** (wallet-derivation): Refused or not searched: CashAddr token-aware P2PKH ('z' type), refused with "only single-key addresses (bitcoincash:q…)" although it is single-key; Ethereum Classic EIP-1191 checksums; Ledger-legacy 4-level Ethereum paths (m/44'/60'/0'/i, reachable only with an explicit path); Dash Core and Litecoin test networks. The supported list in README.md:241-249 and the per-search pattern state the scope.
- **Other thread spawns that panic on refusal (outside this role's scope)** (wallet-derivation): Besides src/search.rs:312, Scope::spawn is used in src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:276 (CLI). The spawns in src/memory.rs:532 and src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs are in tests. The coordinator may want the CLI role to check menu.rs under a thread limit.
- **Decoy search scope argument judged with an explicit path** (wallet-derivation): For two missing words, search_decoy computes decoy_address_limits(scan_gap) before looking at the reference (src/search.rs:142), so an address with an explicit path and scan gap 0 is refused although the gap is unused. The client and CLI require a gap of at least 1, so this is not reachable through them.
- **AUD-023 fixes confirmed in this scope** (wallet-derivation): These were confirmed by code and probes. Three outcomes and the matching lengths (CheckOutcome, CheckEvidence::matching_lengths, own_checks_passed); exit 5 for not verified. One container-fingerprint rule (container_fingerprint used by every binding). The replacement rehearsal decided in the library (ConfirmedPhrase::replacement_rehearsal, used by the CLI and the RekeySession seal result). The old-container keep list from Keep::old_container (CLI and keepOldContainer). The client refuses a passphrase inside a reference and searchWallet refuses one beside builtInCheck (contrast probe passes). After a WebAssembly trap, withSession skips session calls and describeError maps the trap to STOPPED_DETAIL (code reading only).
