A JavaScript instance of the wave-confirmed [ARC] finding about joined Rust doc blocks; no check detects it.
- **Further gaps of the wave-confirmed documentation finding** (api-contracts): docs/API.md never names the keepOldContainer binding or class method (export list at :1002-1009 omits it); the crate-root exports container_fingerprint, grouped, PassedCheck and Settings (src/lib.rs:76-98) are not mentioned in docs/API.md; docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:283 types the owner callback as `(check) => boolean | Promise<boolean>`, :287 lists what it receives without rehearsalNeedsPassphrase, and :290-291 says 'anything but true stops it', while :293-296, web/client.d.ts:366-376 and web/client.js:686-692 describe the { passphrase } yes. Same root cause as the confirmed [DOC] finding (documents not updated with the AUD-023 rekey/check changes).
- **onConfirmAgain accepts { builtInCheck: true }** (api-contracts): web/client.js:1423-1457 passes a { builtInCheck: true } answer through describeConfirmation, although MhfeConfirmAgainAnswer (web/client.d.ts:417-426) and the documents list only address, fingerprint and owner. After AMBIGUOUS_LENGTH or LENGTH_DIFFERS the core refuses it again in the same way and asks again (web/core-worker.js:381-413), so a page that keeps answering it loops without bound. Not confirmed with the real core (it needs a full recovery).
- **Bindings echo page-supplied names unquoted** (api-contracts): INVALID_REQUEST messages repeat the value a page passed, unquoted and unescaped: src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:191-193 ('unknown password kind {other}'), core.rs:521-524, core/rekey.rs:120-123, wasm_api.rs:337-339; src/error.rs:202-208 has quoted() for such names. Through the classes only MhfePasswords.make's kind can carry arbitrary page text (p05: 'Invalid request: unknown password kind Words'); no person-typed text is documented to reach it, so CORE-24 is not clearly breached.
- **Boundary normalisation differs between fields** (api-contracts): p13: an address, a coin id and a fingerprint are trimmed (and coin and Bech32 case-folded) while a derivation path with a leading or trailing space is refused (src/wallet.rs:327-351 does not trim). Refused, not silently mapped, so only a consistency remark.
- **A failed compile is cached for good and reported as a CSP problem** (api-contracts): CompiledModule.get() keeps a rejected compile promise (web/runtime.js:95-102), and PackageCheck reports it as browser-features failed with 'as when the page's Content-Security-Policy lacks wasm-unsafe-eval' (:1221-1234), closing the class for good even when the cause was transient (for example memory). Documented for the CSP case only; not reproduced.
- **No public seam for the Argon2 engine** (api-contracts): Argon2Engine, Mhfe<E> and engine::browser::BrowserEngine::new are public, but Mhfe::with_engine is pub(crate) (src/mhfe.rs:279-283) and Mhfe::new exists only natively (:265-274), so no program outside the crate can build an Mhfe on wasm32 or pass a fake engine in its own tests; docs/API.md:33-39 presents BrowserEngine as the browser build's engine. Possibly deliberate (it keeps cheaper engines out of production); worth stating in API.md.
- **WorkerJob does not require the worker's ready handshake before news or results** (api-contracts): web/runtime.js:342-377 compares builds only when a ready message arrives; a worker script that never sends ready but sends news or a result would be served without the build comparison that the ArrivedHandler comment (:159-165) describes. The package's own worker always sends ready first, so this matters only for scripts of other builds.
- **Small wording issues** (api-contracts): encodeSecret's refusal says 'The chosen words contains' / 'The dice digits contains' (web/runtime.js:691-694); describeConfirmation says 'owner must be a function' when owner is a function but another key is present (web/client.js:1504-1507); AmbiguousLength joins three lengths as '12 and 15 and 18' (src/error.rs:345-358).
- **Previously fixed behaviour re-verified** (api-contracts): The class's early refusals of PIM, memory level, word count and repair-word count now carry the library's sentences with the value and 'the new PIM' for a rekey (p14); a passphrase inside a reference or confirmation, a misspelled reference key and a passphrase beside { builtInCheck: true } are refused by the class and the binding (p11); session refusals, BUSY and SESSION_CLOSED behave as documented (p06).
- **Browser UI-001 has no product page in mhfe** (cli-ux): The browser package ships modules and a README (dist/), no page; the only page is the test page that scripts/build-browser-check.mjs writes into target/browser-check. Viewport checks of CHECK-UI-001 therefore have no product subject in this repository.
- **Progress and self-test status lines use carriage-return redraws at TERM=dumb** (cli-ux): terminal/progress.rs:39 and self_test.rs:178 decide 'same line' by stderr().is_terminal() alone, so at TERM=dumb the bar and the 'Testing …' line are redrawn with \r. No ESC byte is written (anstream strips CSI there), but this is not the plain sequential output CORE-39 describes; a judgement call.
- **Ctrl+D at a visible prompt ends with an error, at a secret prompt with a cancel** (cli-ux): At the container or address prompt Ctrl+D gives '✗ Error: No answer was typed.' and exit 2 (terminal.rs:164-167, :181-184); at a secret prompt it cancels with exit 130 (terminal.rs:405-408). README.md:577 documents only the secret prompt case.
- **mhfe alone at TERM=dumb prints the help and exits 2** (cli-ux): main.rs:244 opens the menu only when can_redraw(); otherwise clap's arg_required_else_help prints the help to standard error with exit 2. README.md:129 says that with no command it opens the start menu.
- **Help and version written to a failing standard output exit 0** (cli-ux): mhfe --version > /dev/full and mhfe encrypt --help > /dev/full exit 0 (clap's Error::exit ignores the write error). Results are covered by style::out (AUD-023-FUN001 holds). output-and-scripts.log.
- **Stopping mhfe serve with Ctrl+C, as it instructs, reports 'Cancelled. Nothing was saved.' and exit 130** (cli-ux): serve.rs:255-259 tells the person to press Ctrl+C; the shared handler (terminal.rs:362-381) then prints the cancel message of a secret command. Consistent with README's exit table, but an odd message for a server stop.
- **Windows: Ctrl+Z at a hidden prompt is probably not kept as data (not verified)** (cli-ux): Rust std's Windows console reader drops a trailing Ctrl+Z (0x1A) of a read as end of input; edit_line (hidden_input.rs:491-493) then ends the line or closes the input, so a key-by-key Ctrl+Z would submit the password typed so far or cancel, where Unix keeps 0x1A for the password check to refuse (SECURITY.md:30 lists Ctrl+Z). scripts/verify-hidden-input-windows.py:228-230 types 'synthetic\x1ax' in one write, where std keeps a Ctrl+Z inside the chunk. Needs a run on a Windows console with Ctrl+Z typed alone; no rust-src was available to cite the std line.
- **Windows launcher pauses twice after a failed startup check** (cli-ux): menu.rs:73-78 waits for Enter after a startup failure and exits 1; packaging/mhfe-launch.bat then runs 'pause' because errorlevel is 1.
- **The check-word review and its hint are skipped at TERM=dumb** (cli-ux): check_word.rs:71 returns NotChecked when no private screen is active, and the 'type ? for a forgotten word' hint is shown only on a private screen, so a '?' typed at a dumb terminal is used literally. Plausibly deliberate (the review shows password words), but README.md:197-202 does not say so. AUD-010 recorded it as an observation.
- **A wrong coin choice in check --address has no way back but Ctrl+C** (cli-ux): wallet_reference.rs:163-195 asks the coin, then asks the address again until it parses for that coin; an address of another coin is refused forever ('Please type it again.'), and leaving loses the container and password typed.
- **clap's range text reaches the person** (cli-ux): --scan-gap 0 gives '0 is not in 1..=2147483648' (usage-errors.log), Rust range syntax rather than plain language.
- **AUD-023 cli-ux observations still standing** (cli-ux): Command helps end with a grey note; only the main help ends with the yellow safety line (CORE-37 is written for the help as a whole). A phrase is drawn in a frame although CORE-36 says results have no boxes; mhfe is the model the rule names.
- **repair and repair-words without --stdin read piped lines as answers** (cli-ux): They have no reading_secrets() refusal (container_repair.rs:476, :529); with empty input they end with 'No answer was typed.' without naming --stdin. Consistent with AUD-023-UI006's fix scope (commands that read no secret keep working).
- **The start menu runs with standard output redirected** (cli-ux): main.rs:244 checks can_redraw() (stdin and stderr) only; with stdout redirected the menu opens and results and the help entry (menu.rs:104) go to the file.
- **The menu shows only the base command of entries that ask a further question** (cli-ux): The repair entry shows 'mhfe repair' also when 'Make repair words' runs mhfe repair-words; password and self-test entries never show --check-word, --chars or --vectors (menu.rs:162-176).
- **Startup checks take about five hundredths of a second** (cli-ux): Release binary: repair-words --stdin (startup checks of every part, no Argon2) 0.053-0.056 s over five runs; serve refusal 0.006 s (startup-time.log). README.md:442 'a few hundredths of a second' holds.
- **clippy.toml sets too-many-lines-threshold = 100, not the 150 of CORE-15 and RUST-01** (guide-lib-core): clippy.toml:5-6 ('CORE-15: at most 100 lines per function') and Cargo.toml:106 ('threshold 100, CORE-15'). The guide sets the gate at 150 and leaves 101 to 150 to review. The stricter gate is not a defect of the scope files; the config belongs to the tooling role.
- **The only unsafe module mixes the Argon2 C binding with operating-system memory calls** (guide-lib-core): src/engine/ffi.rs holds the Argon2 FFI, the work-area allocation, MADV_DONTDUMP, sysconf, mlock/munlock and the Linux, macOS and Windows free-memory queries (about 500 non-test lines); src/lib.rs:32 says it is the module 'which calls the C code'. RUST-07 asks for operating-system calls in small modules of their own; concentrating all unsafe code in one module is defensible, so this is recorded as an observation; the memory -> engine edge it causes is part of the dependency-edges finding.
- **Identifiers name known answers 'expected'** (guide-lib-core): GLOSSARY.md lists 'expected value' under Avoid for 'Known answer'. Fields such as DigestCase.expected, KeepCase.expected, DrawCase.expected, RepairCase.expected and the Expected enum (src/repair/known_answers.rs:74) use it. CORE-17 applies to new code; a rename is a matter of terminology.
- **Public result records expose their fields** (guide-lib-core): Repaired and Change (src/repair.rs:320-344), WishOdds (src/word_wishes.rs:68-83), Completion (src/word_hints.rs:57-63) and Argon2Cost (src/engine.rs:18-24) are public with public fields that the CLI reads. CORE-02 read strictly asks for private fields; for plain result records this is recorded as an observation (NewContainer, which has an invariant, is in the visibility finding).
- **Impossible cases are hidden by fallback values instead of an expect exception** (guide-lib-core): src/detection.rs:129 wallet_check::passes(self.state, "").unwrap_or(false) (comment: the test cannot fail) and src/word_hints.rs:191 from_utf8(...).unwrap_or_default(). RUST-05 asks for expect with a reasoned exception where an invariant cannot fail; both values are safe today.
- **Keep::old_container has no startup known answer** (guide-lib-core): src/operation.rs:189-198, added for AUD-023-ARC016, is checked only by the unit test at :334-349; the keep-advice self-check (src/operation/known_answers.rs) covers Keep::new through Sealed::keep. The settings helper both use (changed_settings, :155-159) is covered at startup, so only the old-container items are not.
- **PublishedRoundKeys answers unknown rounds with INTERNAL_ERROR, outside the Argon2Engine contract** (guide-lib-core): src/engine.rs:35-36 documents MhfeError::Argon2 or a memory error; src/mhfe/known_answers/published.rs:136-138 returns MhfeError::Internal, and the cipher-rounds refusal AtPim relies on that code (src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:347-351). CORE-07 substitution; the engine is a self-check engine, so this is recorded as an observation.
- **Encryption::run takes the original phrase again** (guide-lib-core): src/operation.rs:217-231 checks `original` in new() but does not keep it; run() (:237-267) takes an original again and checks it again. Data clump (CORE-52); probably chosen so that the secret is not held between the two calls.
- **OriginalFacts::container_choices decides from the word count** (guide-lib-core): src/container.rs:249 (`self.word_count < packing::STATE_WORDS`) restates the rule of Suite::require_original (src/suite.rs:94-99) instead of asking the suite (CORE-14).
- **rustdoc misreads two private doc comments** (guide-lib-core): With --document-private-items: src/repair.rs:69 'log[0]' is read as an intra-doc link, and src/eff.rs:12 '<TAB>' as unclosed HTML tags (g03-rustdoc-private-items.log). The published docs are not affected.
- **phrase::parse_container is a pass-through of parse** (guide-lib-core): src/phrase.rs:73-77: its doc describes suite 3 and suite 4 containers, but it only calls parse; CORE-51 deletion test / CORE-52 middle man.
- **Repair reads every token before the length check** (guide-lib-core): src/repair.rs:408-416 (word_numbers over the whole text, one lowercase String per token) and ContainerReading::read (:370-374, a Vec of every token) process input of any size before refusing a wrong length; the CLI limits a line to 8 KiB, the browser binding passes any string (CORE-48).
- **Memory tests pass without checking when mlock is refused** (guide-lib-core): src/memory.rs:442-445, :470-473, :526-529 return early when the lock is refused (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK 0), and src/engine/native.rs:183-185 when no memory figure exists; environment-dependent, silent rather than skipped.
- **Test placement** (guide-lib-core): src/test_support.rs:89-94 holds a #[test] outside a tests module; src/new_password.rs:284-293 has a test before `use super::*` (RUST-08).
- **The self-check hub joins every module** (guide-lib-core): Every module's known_answers depends on src/self_check.rs and src/self_check/sets.rs depends on every module's checks; together with error.rs this closes the one cycle of 30 modules (s08-module-cycles.log). The self-check area is outside this role's scope.
- **unreachable_pub also reports 33 items in src/wasm_api** (guide-lib-core): g02-unreachable-pub-wasm.log: src/wasm_api/core.rs 7, core/search.rs 3, core/self_test.rs 4, passwords.rs 5, repair.rs 5, wasm_api.rs 1, wallet.rs 7, word_hints.rs 1 (bindings role).
- **Two UNREADABLE constants** (guide-lib-core): src/check_word.rs:37 and src/repair.rs:395 both define '?'; the specification defines the marker separately for each profile (mhfe_spec/README.md:782 and :849), so two constants are defensible.
- **The container phrase is wiped in some owners and kept in plain Strings in others** (guide-lib-wallet): ContainerFacts.words (src/container.rs:24), NewContainer.words (src/mhfe.rs:251) and search::Found.container (src/search.rs:68) hold container text in Zeroizing; HiddenWallets.container (src/hidden.rs:54, copied from facts.words() at :83) and repair::Repaired.container (src/repair.rs:323) hold it in plain Strings, and ContainerSearch keeps the container's word numbers and candidates in unwiped Vecs (src/search.rs:55-62, :248-254, :440-482). The specification says to keep the container phrase private (anyone who has it can try passwords offline, mhfe_spec/README.md:43-44) but does not list it among the values to erase, and SECURITY.md's 'phrase' is not explicit about containers, so no contract could be established. Probe: HiddenWallets.container is alloc::string::String; Found's Debug prints 'Found { container: Zeroizing { .. }, words: [(24, "peace")], path: None }' (probes-copy.log), i.e. the restored word but not the container.
- **Impossible references answered with a valid outcome** (guide-lib-wallet): compare_until returns DoesNotMatch for Reference::BuiltInCheck and Reference::OwnChecks (src/rehearsal.rs:561 and :584) instead of an error. Every current caller filters these references out first (refuse_impossible, compare_state's arms, Confirmation::wallet_reference, require_wallet_reference), so it is unreachable today; a future caller would get a silent 'does not match'.
- **vectors::inputs_of swallows a parse error** (guide-lib-wallet): src/vectors.rs:390-392 turns a phrase that does not parse into an empty phrase with unwrap_or_default(). It is unreachable because record() parses the same phrase first through password_and_entropy() (:257, :488-493), but it is an error swallowed rather than passed on (CORE-22).
- **Copy kept with the independent oracle without the marker** (guide-lib-wallet): STATED_READING_ONLY (src/vectors.rs:542-548) is kept in step with scripts/independent-suite3.py by a test (src/vectors.rs:667-685) and its reason is given, but neither side says 'deliberate copy' as CORE-10 asks. Whether a list inside an independent oracle counts as a copy is a judgement; the earlier wave's marker finding covers the browser package only.
- **Hidden-wallet session codes typed as strings** (guide-lib-wallet): HiddenWallets::KEEPS_SESSION_OPEN (src/hidden.rs:65-75) lists nine error codes as strings rather than asking MhfeError; scripts/browser-check/client-checks.mjs:53-63 types the same list a third time. No test ties the list to the codes of src/error.rs, so a renamed code would leave the page closing the session; not shown to be wrong today.
- **Avoided glossary words in pre-existing comments** (guide-lib-wallet): 'expected value(s)' (GLOSSARY.md: avoid, use 'known answer') at src/search/known_answers.rs:4, src/validation_fixtures.rs:5, src/repair/known_answers.rs:5, src/new_password/known_answers.rs:5, src/container/known_answers.rs:6, and 'wrapper' at src/self_test.rs:168. The glossary was committed on 2026-10-14 and CORE-17 applies to new text; these lines date from 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-09. The guide itself uses 'expected value' in CORE-28.
- **Strength known answers derived by hand from the code's rules** (guide-lib-wallet): src/strength/known_answers.rs:3-17 derives each millibit value by hand from src/strength.rs's rules (all five values recomputed by this reviewer and correct). No published vectors exist for the estimate (the specification leaves strength policy to the application), so CORE-28's independent source is only weakly met; recorded, not a finding.
- **Checked phrase draw has no limit of its own** (guide-lib-wallet): PhraseDraw::draw (src/wallet_check.rs:253-271) loops until a phrase passes and relies on the caller's on_draws callback to stop it. With a source that is stuck after check_source's two probes, a checked draw never passes and never ends; this is a variant of the earlier wave's random-source finding (one-time probe only).
- **Duplicate check and duplicated fingerprint rule inside the self-checks** (guide-lib-wallet): SHA-256("abc") through bitcoin_hashes is checked by both bip39-words (src/phrase/known_answers.rs:186-194) and wallet-hashes (src/wallet/known_answers.rs:100-107); since AUD-023-BLD010 every set with bip39-words also runs wallet-hashes. Bip32Check recomputes the fingerprint rule (first four bytes of HASH160 of the master public key) at src/wallet/known_answers.rs:333-339 rather than calling the library (src/wallet.rs:567-571); SeedCheck and AddressesCheck do call master_fingerprint, so production is covered.
- **Unused public report method** (guide-lib-wallet): SelfCheckReport::warnings (src/self_check.rs:201-206) has no caller outside its own unit test in src/ or web/; it is library API surface, not unreachable code.
- **Module cycle through the CLI's infrastructure** (guide-cli-infra): g07-module-graph.log finds one strongly connected component of 12 modules: check, check_word, choice, container_repair, container_search, flow, hidden_input, phrase_length, settings, style, terminal and typed_line. The lowest layers depend on features: terminal.rs (read_password, read_container) runs check_word::review and container_repair::review, and style depends on flow, which depends on terminal. This compiles within one crate, but the output and input layers cannot be read or tested apart from the features (CORE-05, CHECK-ARC-001). A split such as terminal (I/O) against command-level reading helpers would break the cycle.
- **protect.rs allows unsafe for its whole production body** (guide-cli-infra): protect.rs:18-22 is #![allow(unsafe_code)] over 639 production lines. About 13 OS calls (setrlimit, prctl, sigaction, getrlimit, the socket, io_uring and open probes, unshare) sit among pure logic: CoreDumps::outcome, probe_claims, network_empty, IsolationCheck and Isolation::names. RUST-07 asks for OS calls in small modules of their own. hidden_input.rs (unix.rs and windows.rs) and protect's own seccomp.rs and landlock.rs already follow it. The guide names protect.rs as the model for what to protect, so this is recorded here and not as a finding.
- **Signal interception is read back but not reported by the checks** (guide-cli-infra): interrupt_on_quit_and_suspend (protect.rs:55-87) and the Ctrl+C handler (terminal.rs:350-360) are protections in protect.rs's own list (line 4). They are read back, but they are not parts of the startup or self-test reports (the self-test rows have none). A refusal prints only a grey hint, written before the command's private steps (Flow), which then cover it on the alternate screen. RUST-11 asks that protections be reported by the startup checks and the self-test.
- **The library also has unreachable pub items (other role)** (guide-cli-infra): cargo clippy --lib -- -W unreachable_pub reports 27 items: src/feistel.rs (11, e.g. :47, :57, :103, :116), src/packing.rs (10, :16-:88), src/suite.rs (4, :13-:22) and src/phrase.rs (2, :40, :75). These are pub items in private modules of the library (RUST-06), for the library role.
- **Front-end refusals carry no stable code** (guide-cli-infra): src/bin/mhfe builds 32 failures with Failure::invalid_input or Failure::internal from free text (terminal.rs 7, serve.rs 5, hidden_input.rs 3, test_tools.rs 3, made_password.rs 3, and others). Scripts can tell them apart only by exit code class. CORE-23 asks for a stable code per error, with the text built in one place per front end. Read strictly it covers the CLI's own refusals too.
- **Typed-line metadata not wiped in one of two places** (guide-cli-infra): typed_line.rs:43-45 wipes `advances` because 'the widths tell something of a password's characters'. hidden_input.rs:465 LineEditor::entries holds each character's UTF-8 byte length and is a plain Vec, freed unwiped. That is more telling metadata of the same password, which RUST-13 asks to keep wiped. Practical impact is very small, since the process is non-dumpable.
- **The menu's help goes to standard output** (guide-cli-infra): menu.rs:104 writes `mhfe --help` through clap to standard output, while the menu is drawn on standard error. With standard output redirected (mhfe > log at a terminal), the menu runs, the help goes into the file, and the menu waits for Enter.
- **Command helps end without the safety line** (guide-cli-infra): Only `mhfe --help` ends with the yellow 'Experimental: not independently reviewed; do not use it to protect real funds.' (main.rs:229-232). Command helps end with examples or a grey note (for example `mhfe encrypt -h`). CORE-37 reads 'Help has ... grey notes and a yellow safety line at the end'; whether this covers every command's help is a reading question.
- **Test names and a narrow test** (guide-cli-infra): protect.rs:1134 g10_isolated_command is not a sentence (CORE-34; it is the ignored child of a sentence-named test). hidden_input.rs:784-792 hidden_input_refuses_when_echo_stays_on only compares the refusal's text and code. The read-back that refuses is tested in hiding_reads_the_terminal_back.
- **The phrase frame is a box** (guide-cli-infra): style.rs:479-510 boxed_words draws the phrase in a ┌─┐ frame on result screens. CORE-36 says results are laid out 'without boxes or rules'. The frame looks deliberate, for copying words, and mhfe is the guide's model, so it is recorded as a question of reading.
- **Ambiguous boolean arguments** (guide-cli-infra): Call sites pass bare booleans: hidden_input::read_line(prompt, true, ...) at terminal.rs:181, style::number_word(n, true), container_repair::ask_count(input, false), and landlock::forbid_writes(!needs.network). Readability only (CORE-16).
- **The menu's command thread can panic on a thread refusal** (guide-cli-infra): menu.rs:276-287 starts each command with std::thread::scope(...).spawn, which panics when the system refuses a thread. Under panic=abort this aborts the menu. This is the same class as the earlier wave's compare_candidates finding. Here it is reachable only if threads run out after the start checks have passed.
- **Untested infrastructure modules** (guide-cli-infra): flow.rs (the summary grouping, OffTheRecord), terminal/progress.rs (stage and time-left arithmetic), exit.rs (the MhfeError to exit code map), system_random.rs and test_tools.rs have no unit tests. CORE-32 asks unit tests of library code; the terminal suite (b11) exercises the flows end to end.
- **readme.rs keeps its own list of links** (guide-cli-infra): readme.rs tests keep an ALL list (lines 44-58 of the file) that repeats the 13 link constants. A new link constant that is not added there would not be checked against README.md. Complete at b6fca69.
- **clippy.toml is stricter than the guide** (guide-cli-infra): clippy.toml:6 sets too-many-lines-threshold = 100 with the comment 'CORE-15: at most 100 lines per function', and Cargo.toml:106 says the same. CORE-15 and RUST-01 set 150 as the gate, with 101 to 150 left to review. Stricter, so not a defect, but the comment misstates CORE-15.
- **serve after SIGTERM** (guide-cli-infra): mhfe serve stopped by SIGTERM (timeout) prints '! Cancelled. Nothing was saved.' (g13), the message of a secret command, for a launcher that saves nothing.
- **The check command module hosts the passphrase and reference readers of five other commands** (guide-cli-commands): Other commands use these shared helpers through `pub use` (check.rs:33-39):
- check/passphrase.rs: ask_passphrase, read_passphrase_named, read_passphrase_of, passphrase_screen, PassphraseUsedOption;
- check/wallet_reference.rs: WalletReference.

The users are decrypt, new_wallet, rekey, wallets and container_search. In the same way, encrypt.rs hosts seal, show_sealing, read_new_password, read_typed_password and what_to_keep for new, rekey and wallets.

The resolved crate:: graph has a 12-module strongly connected component (check, check_word, choice, container_repair, container_search, flow, hidden_input, phrase_length, settings, style, terminal, typed_line). This is allowed within a Rust crate. Whether these shared terminal services should leave the command modules (CORE-05) is a judgement call.
- **RUST-06: the binary's modules use `pub` throughout** (guide-cli-commands): Every item of the command modules that another module uses is `pub`, never `pub(crate)`, although the binary has no library API. A few are `pub` but used only in their own file: container_repair.rs:196 ScanGapOption, container_repair.rs:560 ask_count. No functional effect in a binary.
- **Command modules build library error values with their own text** (guide-cli-commands): Sites:
- check/wallet_reference.rs:73 MhfeError::InvalidAddress("nothing was typed");
- wallet_reference.rs:77-79 ("an address or a fingerprint is one word");
- wallet_reference.rs:186-191 (wraps the library reason in a CLI sentence);
- made_password.rs:173-175, which reports the impossible PasswordKind::Own as MhfeError::InvalidRequest, exit 2 "Invalid request: own passwords are typed". Callers never pass Own there (encrypt.rs:507-510); the impossible state could be ruled out by the type.

The text a person reads is thus built partly in the library's Display and partly in the CLI (CORE-23, RUST-04). This relates to the earlier-wave finding on the crate-wide MhfeError.

- **The macOS release job installs gnu-tar from Homebrew, unpinned, before building attested archives** (guide-tooling-other): release.yml:73 runs `brew install gnu-tar`, which runs Homebrew's auto-update and possibly upgrades the formula. - **CI's release checks build the browser package with an emsdk cloned by tag, not with the canonical image** (guide-tooling-other): ci.yml:74-79 clones emsdk at branch 6.0.12 and runs `emsdk install`, which downloads with no recorded hash. Chromium and Firefox then test that CI-built dist/. The shipped package comes from the digest-pinned image in the canonical job, so the browsers never run the exact released bytes.
- **A manual CI dispatch shares the push concurrency group of its branch** (guide-tooling-other): The ci.yml:20-25 group has no event component. A push to a branch therefore cancels a running workflow_dispatch release check of that branch (hours long), and the reverse also holds.
- **The browser step's time budget has a small margin** (guide-tooling-other): ci.yml:99 allows 245 minutes for `playwright install --with-deps` plus four pages, each bounded by PAGE_LIMIT_MS = 60 min. The comment's claim that the step limit "never cuts a page off" holds only if the install and browser start-ups stay under 5 minutes. This was not observed on CI.
- **Several fast checks never run on push, and two only in the non-blocking vectors workflow** (guide-tooling-other): verify-fast-mode-script.py (2.6 s), third-party-licenses.py --self-test/--check, generate-published-rounds.py --check, verify-vendored-argon2.mjs and the blame-revs check run only in check.sh (release or dispatch). generate-cell-widths.py --check and the independent checkers' fast modes run only in vectors.yml, which the release draft does not wait for. A change to packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py is not tested by push CI.
- **audit.yml uses ubuntu-latest** (guide-tooling-other): audit.yml:39 runs on ubuntu-latest, while every other workflow pins ubuntu-24.04.

It is kept as a defensive path.
- **Weak assertions in a few test cases** (guide-tooling-other): verify-fast-mode-script.py:257 asserts len(idle) == MAX_CONNECTIONS, which is always true. Several terminal-suite cases discard the tool's exit code: options.py:95, :104, :116, :129; recovery.py:300; repair.py:248, :263, :276; and passwords.check_password, whose return value is unused.

The coordinator may merge them.

- **The release target list is typed in five places with no test keeping them in step** (build-release): packaging/remap-builder-paths.sh:28-29 (REMAPPED_TARGETS), scripts/third-party-licenses.py:59-67 (NATIVE_TARGETS, whose comment names the Dockerfile and release.yml as the source), scripts/package-release.sh:7 and :120-153, packaging/Dockerfile.reproducible:68-70 and :107-114, .github/workflows/release.yml:58-62. - **BUILD-INFO.txt's '(clean)' comes from the host's git status, which does not see what the Docker context contains** (build-release): scripts/build-reproducible.sh:32-36 uses git status --porcelain; the context is filtered by packaging/Dockerfile.reproducible.dockerignore instead. The vendored gate refuses extra files under vendor/, and no build step globs such files today.

- **The SSE2/SSSE3 speed difference is quoted three ways** (docs-claims): From docs/measurements/full-operation-2026-09-30.json, the SSSE3 build took 5.7-9.5 % less time (6.1-10.5 % faster); measurement-ranges.log. docs/measurements/README.md:10-11 says "6 to 10 percent less time", which fits. - **SECURITY.md says CI runs the hidden-input suites on all three systems; on Linux it runs only for release tags and manual runs** (docs-claims): SECURITY.md:36-38. Since 16808d9, ci.yml runs scripts/check.sh, which runs scripts/verify-hidden-input.py on Linux, only when RELEASE_CHECKS is true (a tag or workflow_dispatch). macOS and Windows run their suites on every push. The sentence is true but does not say that a branch push does not cover Linux.

- **The bridge's direct HEAPU8 reads are correct only because no lane thread allocates** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): web/argon2-engine.js:32-33, :53 and :55-59 read module.HEAPU8 without the glue's growMemViews(). The view is current because every heap growth happens on the calling thread: the work-area malloc in initialize, and pthread_create's stack allocation. Lane threads run fill_segment only. If a future build let another thread grow the memory, HEAPU8.set would throw. heap.fill in wipeAndFree (:85) would instead clamp silently on a stale view and skip the wipe; src/engine/browser.rs check_key_written would catch only the unwritten key. The -Wno-pthreads-mem-growth comment (build-argon2-wasm.sh:65-67) speaks to the warning's performance cost, not to this. No defect today.
- **More unmarked copies of library values in the Argon2 bridge and build script** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): web/argon2-engine.js:6-8 restates ARGON2_KEY_BYTES = 32 and ARGON2_LANES = 4 from src/engine.rs KEY_BYTES/LANES. scripts/build-argon2-wasm.sh:61 restates the lane count as PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=4. None of them carries a 'deliberate copy' marker. The known answers keep the first two in step. A pool smaller than the lane count would hang rather than fail, which only the browser suite's one-hour page limit would show. This is the same root cause as the confirmed AUD-024 ARC finding on missing deliberate-copy markers, whose evidence (v-arc-deliberate-copy/markers.log) does not list these sites. Not reported again.
- **wipeAndFree is another free-function wipe without an owner type** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): web/argon2-engine.js:83-88 wipes the bridge's three C-heap copies through a free function called from finally. It works: 0 copies were found. It is another site of the confirmed AUD-024 ARC finding on TS-07 owner types (wipe() and [Symbol.dispose]()), not a new root cause.
- **A rekey comment speaks of a browser work area that the engine does not hold** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): src/wasm_api/core/rekey.rs:256-257 says "The old work area is freed when this engine is dropped, at the end of this block". A BrowserEngine (src/engine/browser.rs:39-42) holds no work area. The Emscripten code allocates, wipes and frees the work area inside every derive (core.c initialize/finalize). The outcome the comment wants is still true, since nothing of the old area is kept for the owner's wait. This is a further instance of the confirmed AUD-024 ARC finding 'Comments state facts the code does not have'.
- **reserve() would wrap above 4 GiB, which no browser level reaches** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): web/argon2-engine.js:65 passes memoryKib * 1024 as a JS number to _malloc, whose wasm parameter is i32. 2 GiB arrives correctly as 0x80000000. 4 GiB would arrive as malloc(0) and 'succeed'. src/engine/browser.rs:11 and :47 refuse every level above 0, so this is unreachable. argon2 itself refuses 4 GiB with -15 (g1-bridge-edges.log).
- **The lane workers end with the operation worker in both browsers** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): Playwright saw 5 workers (the operation worker and 4 lane workers) before the page terminated the operation worker, and 0 two seconds later, in Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Firefox 157.0 (g1-browser-lane-workers.log). So the shared memory does not outlive the operation through its lane workers. The browser frees it without overwriting, as the documents already say for cancelled operations.
- **The single-threaded build's residue matches its documentation** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): In argon2-st.js, the last block of lane 3 only stays as an XOR pair on the main stack (62,544) until the 1 MiB known answer overwrites it. The key is never rebuildable. About 2,291 non-zero bytes remain after the known answer. This matches docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:730-734, '2 KiB of allocator records and of the stack of the last block computation'.
- **A failed Argon2 round leaks its work area unwiped in the browser, which SECURITY.md discloses** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): vendor/phc-winner-argon2/src/argon2.c:89-93 returns before finalize when fill_memory_blocks fails: a thread-array calloc gives -22 (core.c:299-309), a thread fails with -33. The work area is then neither wiped nor freed in the Emscripten builds. The bridge maps -22 to MEMORY_ALLOCATION_FAILED. SECURITY.md:245-247 discloses this, and natively src/engine/ffi.rs:184-192 wipes the area. No finding.
- **The AUD-023 earlier probes and these probes agree** (gap-1-browser-argon2-heap-residue): docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/audit-records/o2-threaded-residue.log and verifier-refuted-records/threaded-residue.log used fixed offsets. These probes find the same pairs without assuming offsets. The 16-byte difference from 33,694,912 comes from a 32-byte salt in those probes against 16 bytes here. Here the addresses are tied to the recorded lane-thread stack bounds of the call's last segment.

- **Minor wording and documentation notes** (gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide): SECURITY.md:136 refers to 'the offline environment described above', but SECURITY.md describes none (README.md:136 does). web/runtime.d.ts:42 gives TOO_MANY_MISSING_WORDS no doc comment, unlike its neighbours. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:156 says '7 to 10%' and docs/measurements/README.md:10 '6 to 10 percent'. docs/RELEASING.md:22 keeps a v0.5.0 example folder. README.md's bare 'original' has no glossary rule (mhfe_spec has no glossary yet). The settings.rs test module puts tests before its `use` and `const GIB` (:522-566). (AUD-023 obs 49, 51.)
- **API surface notes** (gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide): RecoveredPhrase::into_phrase (src/mhfe.rs:155) has no caller and no test. The release CLI ships '[test only]' test-vectors and test-benchmark. wordHints accepts 'eff' in the wallet-only build. The parity script still compares a subset of shared features. (AUD-023 obs 31, 53, 56, 72.)
- **The menu's fast-mode command is cut for page names over 9 characters** (gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide): src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:148 shows 'mhfe serve <page>'. Its fit test (:433-446) assumes 'tool.html', so 'index.html' or a longer host page name is cut with '…' in the list. (AUD-023 obs 70.)
- **A native residue scan for the hash-state finding was inconclusive** (gap-1-aud023-observations-under-current-guide): hash-state-residue-zeroize-off/on.log found no master-key copy in [stack] after master_fingerprint with the zeroize features either off or on. The scanner's own calls reuse the dead stack, so the probe cannot show residue there. The hash-state finding therefore rests on the source and the feature graph.
- **Real-browser trigger for the confirmed Python launcher request-head finding: any UTF-8 cookie for 127.0.0.1 makes the page fail to load** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): Browsers keep cookies per host, not per port, so a cookie that any other local service set for 127.0.0.1 is also sent to the launcher.

With one cookie 'service=café' added for 127.0.0.1, both browsers get 400 Bad Request from packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py, while `mhfe serve` serves the page (200): Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 (cookies.mjs, g12-cookies.log, exit 1 as designed). The cause is the already confirmed earlier-wave [FUN] finding: read_request_head decodes the head as ASCII (mhfe-fast-mode.py:347). This run shows that the documented route fails in a real browser, not only for a hand-made request, so the coordinator may wish to raise that finding's impact. It is not reported again here.
- **More than 16 KiB of cookies for 127.0.0.1 makes both launchers answer the page with a bare '400 Bad Request'** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): Cookies of 20,000 bytes in all, added for 127.0.0.1, are sent by both browsers. mhfe serve and the Python launcher both answer 400, because the head passes MAX_REQUEST_HEAD = 16 KiB (serve.rs:47-48, mhfe-fast-mode.py:36). The body is only '400 Bad Request', and the launchers log nothing, so the person gets no hint.

serve.rs:47 says 'real browsers send far less'. That holds unless other local services keep large cookies on 127.0.0.1, which is rare. The limit is deliberate, so this is recorded as an observation (g12-cookies.log).
- **A page using localhost instead of 127.0.0.1 gets a bare '403 Forbidden'** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): http://localhost:<port>/ is refused with 403 in both browsers and through both launchers (g03), as SECURITY.md:211-213 documents. The body is only '403 Forbidden', with no hint that the printed 127.0.0.1 address must be used. This is by design against DNS rebinding.
- **The CSP cannot stop the served page from navigating away** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): Top-level navigation is not governed by the page policy. A link clicked from the served page reaches a loopback sink, with no Referer thanks to no-referrer (g03). It is the run-time side of the confirmed [BLD] network-code finding: navigation and window.open are neither covered by the CSP nor detected by the gates. The package itself never navigates; its own run requested nothing but itself and blob: URLs.
- **The launchers' error documents are same-origin documents without a script policy** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): Their header CSP holds only frame-ancestors. A 404 or 403 answer is therefore a cross-origin isolated document of the page's origin with no script-src restriction. It reflects no input (a fixed '404 Not Found'), so nothing can be injected into it.

This audit used it to show nosniff's own effect: in Chromium, opaque-response blocking refuses a cross-site load of the page with or without nosniff, so nosniff's effect shows only on a same-origin load.
- **Firefox asks for /favicon.ico for every served page, and the page's own img-src 'none' refuses it first** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): The page's img-src 'none' (default-src 'none' under the minimal policy) refuses Firefox's favicon request before any request is made. Firefox logs 'resource:///modules/FaviconLoader.sys.mjs' violations, and the page's securitypolicyviolation listener sees 'img-src http://127.0.0.1:<port>/favicon.ico'. This is the browser's request, not the package's; no request reached the launcher.
- **The menu cuts the fast-mode command at 78 columns, so most page names show cut** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): With mhfe beside index.html, the first entry shows 'mhfe serve index.ht…' even on a 120-column terminal (g04). choice.rs cuts a note at style::TEXT_WIDTH, and the width test in menu.rs:434-447 assumes the name 'tool.html'. Any page name longer than nine characters is cut. The cut is a documented choice (choice.rs:354-355), but the entry no longer shows a command the person can type.
- **target/browser-check/index.html is not a build of b6fca69** (gap-1-fast-mode-launchers-real-browser): The page in the repository's target folder dates from 2026-10-07 and carries BUILD_ID a58cc7a5a1567164; dist/ of b6fca69 is de06b919b42eae2f. It still passes in fast mode through both launchers in both browsers (14 workers: it predates the selfCheckProcess worker). - **CORE-07: native and WebAssembly search differ in progress and stopping** (gap-1-unapplied-review-rules): src/search.rs:280-364 (native) reports progress every 100 ms from a waiting thread and nothing more on a match, so a search that matches within 100 ms reports no progress; the WebAssembly version (:374-386) reports after every candidate, and the binding's filter (wasm_api/core/search.rs:122-127) relies on that. Natively a comparison under way can stop mid-candidate through the stopped closure; the WebAssembly passes || false. Natively an error of any worker wins over a match found by another; the sequential version returns the first match. No user-visible defect established; the browser Argon2 build is also re-verified before and after every operation, the native engine only by the startup checks.
- **CORE-09: the library owns its native threads and reads /proc** (gap-1-unapplied-review-rules): The missing-word search (search.rs:289-310) and the checked phrase draw (wallet_check.rs:292, wallet_check/threads.rs:57) start OS threads inside the library, cfg-split from the WebAssembly code, with no parameter or trait a test could use to pass a fake that refuses a thread (related to the confirmed spawn-panic finding). The free-memory check reads /proc/meminfo and cgroup files directly (engine/ffi.rs:390, engine/cgroup.rs:31-33), although cgroup parsing takes a reader. Randomness, Argon2, progress and the terminal reach the library through traits or callbacks.

### Refuted candidates

- **mhfe self-test words the verdicts of the memory-locking and random-source parts by retyping the library's check ids, so a renamed id silently turns 'works' and 'healthy' into 'as published'**: refuted: The code looks the way the candidate says. src/bin/mhfe/self_test.rs:248-249 types "memory-locking" and "random-source" as literals in verdicts(). The ids are literals in src/memory.rs:196 and src/random/health.rs:172, and any other id falls through to ("as published", "NOT as published") at self_test.rs:250. The defect it claims does not hold. The title, observed and impact fields say a renamed id "silently" changes the verdict words, with "no failing check" and "no test catches" it. At b6fca69, two gates that already exist fail on exactly that rename. The candidate's mutant did not see this because it ran only three CLI unit tests: every_help_states_the_limits_of_the_constants, each_outcome_reads_as_its_kind and chars_alone_means_the_default.

My reproduction uses evidence folder docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-selftest-verdict-ids/ and scratch folder tmp/aud024/verify-selftest-verdict-ids/:
- v01-make-mutant: git archive of b6fca69 with only the two renames, random-source to random-health and memory-locking to memory-lock, the same seds as the candidate's mutant.sh. The log shows the diffs.
- v02-mutant-lib-set-tests: `cargo test --locked --lib self_check::sets` on the mutant exits 101. Three library tests fail on the renamed ids:
  - the_native_set_has_every_check_once (src/self_check/sets.rs:257, NATIVE_IDS at :225-252);
  - the_browser_sets_hold_their_own_parts (:273);
  - the_browser_process_set_reports_each_process_part_as_not_available (:310).
  CI runs `cargo test --locked` on every OS (.github/workflows/ci.yml:131-132).
- v03-mutant-build: the mutant built under its own profile, so the shared target/debug binary is not overwritten.
- v04-mutant-terminal-self-test: only the fast terminal suite's check_self_test (scripts/terminal_suite/self_test.py:87-112) runs against the mutant. It exits 1. Its assertion shows the rows 'Random source ... as published' and 'Locked memory ... as published', which do not match the expected SELF_TEST_PARTS. Those are scripts/terminal_suite/constants.py:198 ("Random source", "healthy") and :201 ("Locked memory", "works"), and the comment at :166-167 names "verdicts in src/bin/mhfe/self_test.rs" as their source. This case is part of scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:210, which runs:
  - on every push on macOS (ci.yml:136-139);
  - in scripts/check.sh:57;
  - in the coordinator's baseline b11-terminal-suite-fast (log line 98, exit 0).
- v05-head-build and v06-head-terminal-self-test (control): the same build and check of unmodified b6fca69 pass, so the rename is the only cause of the failure.

So the rename the candidate describes cannot reach a release unnoticed. Both the library tests and the end-to-end self-test report check fail on it.

What remains is a matter of form, not a demonstrated defect. Unlike the process ids (ProcessPart in src/self_check/process.rs:17-39), the two library ids have no exported named constant, and self_test.rs and the sets.rs tests match them by literal. Tests hold the copies in step, and nothing user-visible is wrong. Per AUDIT_STANDARD.md, a record with no demonstrated defect or actionable risk is an observation (info), not a finding. If the coordinator keeps it, it belongs under observations, related to AUD-023-ARC005's ProcessPart change, with the note that tests already hold the copies in step.

No full-cost Argon2 was run. The self-test runs used only the fast tier (at most 256 MiB), which the baseline also runs.
- **The classes take an original seed phrase, and a chosen word, only as a JavaScript string, never as UTF-8 bytes, so a page cannot keep them in a Uint8Array it wipes, as it can a password or passphrase**: refuted: The behaviour is real, but no cited rule or contract is broken. My probe (docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-phrase-as-bytes/vp1-type-checks.log, run with node on dist/runtime/runtime.js of b6fca69, which equals web/runtime.js apart from the build id) shows what happens. requireText (web/runtime.js:756) refuses a Uint8Array with "phrase must be a string." encodeSecret (web/runtime.js:686) would accept the bytes, and requireSecret and secretOrEmpty accept bytes for passwords and passphrases. The cited lines check this: web/client.js:331 and :393, and web/wallet.js:100, :124 and :369.

It is still not a defect, for five reasons.

(1) TS-07 governs how the code holds a secret. It explicitly expects secrets that arrive as strings ("an input field, a library that takes strings") and requires that they be turned into bytes. The classes do this before the worker: client.js:334 and :1020, wallet.js:376 (phraseRequest) and :172 and :268. No guide rule (TS-07, WEB-04, CORE-24, or any other rule in .github/instructions) requires a public method to accept a secret as bytes. The missing owner type with wipe() and [Symbol.dispose]() is already a separate confirmed TS-07 finding.

(2) WEB-04 is about a page's concealed field. The package ships no page; there is no HTML under web/.

(3) The candidate misquotes its expected-behaviour source. docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1039-1040 and SECURITY.md:272 advise passing "passwords and passphrases" as Uint8Array, not secrets in general. The same paragraphs (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:1035-1039, SECURITY.md:269-271) document a phrase typed into the page, and any recovered or new phrase, as JavaScript strings the browser cannot erase. client.d.ts:531 and :544, wallet.d.ts:42 and :73-74, and docs/API.md:733 and :881-882 all declare the phrase as a string. Observed behaviour matches the documented contract.

(4) Every phrase the package itself produces reaches the page as a string: the readPhrase result (client.d.ts:97), the decrypt readings (:189), the rekey owner phrase (:367 and :430) and drawPhrase (wallet.d.ts:16). Accepting bytes on input would remove no string from any flow of the package. The benefit is limited to phrases that come from other modules.

(5) CHECK-SEC-001 tells the audit to record immutable strings as a limit, not to report them as a defect.

This is an API improvement, so it belongs in observations. Two related observations:
- wordHints accepts its typed line as bytes (runtime.js:747), and the docs say that line may be part of a seed phrase. A full phrase is refused as bytes. The API is inconsistent, but no rule is broken.
- wishesOf builds a new JavaScript string from the chosen words (web/wallet.js:378, words.join(" ")) before encodeSecret. This is minor, and it is not the root cause claimed here.

No full-cost run was needed.
- **The module classes and MhfeClient's quick operations start one worker per call with no limit on how many run at once**: refuted: The mechanism is real, but the claimed breach of CORE-50 is not. Static trace at b6fca69: ModuleWorker.run/start (web/runtime.js:947-959) builds a new WorkerJob for every call. WorkerJob.run (web/runtime.js:228-285) makes one `new Worker` per job at :248. MhfeClient#quick (web/client.js:941-947) does the same. wordHintsOf is at web/runtime.js:745-748. Only drawPhrase has a worker bound (web/wallet.js:52-58).

I reproduced it with docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-unbounded-workers/q1-concurrent-workers.log. The probe is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verifier-unbounded-workers/q1-concurrent-workers.mjs, run on the dist build of b6fca69 (it differs from web/ only in the stamped build ids). Calling MhfeWallet.wordHints, MhfeRepair.parameters or MhfeClient.parameters 200 times each without waiting made 200 workers per method, all 200 alive at once. All ended afterwards, and BUSY was never raised. This matches log gb06.

Why this is not a clear breach:
1. CORE-50 accepts concurrency limits "that the person sets or the program states". The package states its concurrency rule in several places:
   - docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:515-518: each operation runs in a new worker; the core's parameters and reading words never wait; the other modules run every call in a worker of its own, and their calls never wait for each other.
   - SECURITY.md:243: every operation runs in a worker of its own.
   - The header comments of web/wallet.js:15, web/repair.js:15 and web/passwords.js:15.
   The number of calls in flight is set by the page, which is the caller.
2. Each call's work is bounded: one worker, terminated when the call ends. No input to a single call makes the work grow. That growth is what CORE-50's second sentence and the bounded drawPhrase `workers` count (AUD-012-SEC001) are about.
3. The impact scenario goes against the package's own documented guidance. For wordHints, BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:483-484 and web/wallet.js:111-112 / web/passwords.js:114 say each call starts a worker, so a page may ask once typing pauses. At human typing speed only a few short-lived workers are alive at once. Reaching hundreds needs a page that starts hundreds of calls without awaiting them. Such a page could as easily construct the Workers itself, and no trust boundary is crossed.

A queue or pool with a stated limit would be a possible improvement, but no rule or documented contract is broken. It belongs in observations, not findings. The finding below is returned unchanged.
- **No gate runs clippy on macOS-only code, and code only for Windows or ARM64 meets clippy only in the canonical Docker build of a release, so the deny lints of RUST-01 and the SAFETY-comment lint RUST-07 relies on are not applied there on any push**: refuted: The facts about where clippy runs are correct at b6fca69, but none of the cited rules or project documents requires clippy for every target, and no lint breach exists in the code that clippy does not reach. Under the task's own definition, this is a possible improvement with no broken rule or contract, so it belongs in the observations.

1. The cited rules hold. RUST-02 (code-rust.instructions.md:34-37) requires `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` "for every crate it holds", and the gate definition in code-core.instructions.md:20 says the same: "for every crate". mhfe has one crate, and scripts/check-fast.sh:33-39 runs clippy on it on every push, for the host and for every WebAssembly feature set. RUST-01 only requires the lints table, and Cargo.toml:97-108 has it. RUST-05 and RUST-07 are rules about the code. "Check: clippy" names their gate; it does not require the gate on every target.

2. The code clippy does not reach does not breach any of these rules. Only src/engine/ffi.rs:411-462 is compiled for macOS alone: one extern block and one function, about 50 lines. I compiled these exact lines (ffi.rs:411-475 at b6fca69, with only their three cfg lines made always true) on Linux. They ran against stub declarations that copy the signatures and deprecations in libc 0.2.190's Apple module. The run used mhfe's own [lints] table and clippy.toml, both checked identical by diff. Clippy -D warnings passes (exit 0). The control is the same code with one SAFETY comment removed; it fails with undocumented_unsafe_blocks (exit 101). Every unsafe block there has a SAFETY comment, and there is no unwrap, expect or panic. The candidate itself says no violation was shown.

3. Some of the candidate's locations are wrong:
   - src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:302 uses the `cfg!()` macro. All of its branches are compiled, and linted, on Linux.
   - No code has a cfg that names MSVC (`git grep target_env` finds nothing in src or build.rs). The x86_64-pc-windows-gnu clippy run therefore covers all of the Windows Rust code, and the portable job compiles the MSVC build with `-D warnings`.
   - `#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]` stubs (protect.rs:188, 469, 608; swap.rs:84; ffi.rs:303) are also compiled for Windows.

4. Windows and ARM64 clippy runs before every release. release.yml:105 makes `publish` need `canonical`, and that job's Dockerfile.reproducible:106-110 runs clippy -D warnings for both cross targets. Running only fast checks on push is what CI-04 asks for. The comment in ci.yml:122-123 ("warnings fail the job") correctly describes the RUSTFLAGS -D warnings of rustc. The v0.6.0 note (docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:420-421) also matches the workflows. This is the remediation of AUD-007-BLD002, whose expected behaviour was warning-free compilation, and that is met.

Observation for the report (not a finding): clippy never runs for an apple target. Adding `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` to the portable job on macos-15 and windows-2025 would gate future macOS-only code at little cost. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:40 says check-fast.sh runs "clippy for every build". Read against check-fast.sh's own header ("for the native program and for every WebAssembly build"), that wording is loose, not a false contract.

Evidence (paths relative to /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/mhfe):
- docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-clippy-targets/clippy-sites.log (exit 0): every clippy invocation, the publish dependency, the macOS cfg sites, no target_env, and the unsafe/SAFETY lines of ffi.rs:411-462.
- docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-clippy-targets/macos-code-clippy-probe.log (exit 0): the verbatim run passes and the control fails. Probe scripts: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-clippy-targets/{sites.sh,probe.sh}.

Limit: no Apple or Windows std is installed. Lints that depend on types and differ by platform (for example, a cast that is needed on Linux but unnecessary on macOS) cannot be ruled out without a real apple-target clippy run. A static scan of the casts in cfg(unix) code found none that could lint only on macOS. No full-cost Argon2 is involved.

No cited rule or project contract is broken, so this belongs in observations, not findings.

What reproduces (static trace at b6fca69, docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-release-target-runs/static-trace.log, exit 0; it agrees with build-release/release-target-runs.log):

Why this is not a finding:
1. AUDIT_STANDARD.md:41 says coverage gaps go in separate sections without finding IDs unless they describe a concrete tracked defect. No defect is shown in any of the three programs.
2. CORE-33 does not cover this. It asks for a regression case for each feature and a failing-first test for each bug fix, and says nothing about build targets.
3. CHECK-BLD-002 is an audit-procedure item, not a repository rule, and the candidate truncates the quote. The full sentence reads 'Compiler success is insufficient for dynamic installer/function requirements and template pruning'. The item asks for 'representative combinations', and CI already runs one per OS and per architecture:

ARCH 0xC00000B7 is AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64 (EM_AARCH64 0xB7 with the 64-bit and LE bits set). after_arch = 7 sends a foreign ABI to index 9, and each of the five tests jumps to index 9 = ret(refuse).
5. The project's documents do not promise more than CI does:

   - SECURITY.md:36-38 says CI runs the pseudo-terminal suites 'on all three systems', which is true.

   - ci.yml:112-114 says 'this runs their code natively', which holds for the source code.
   - README.md:587-588 only lists the archives.

Suggested observation: three of the six shipped CLI programs are built but never executed by any check. Running the container-built mhfe.exe `self-test --startup` on windows-2025, the x86_64 macOS binary under Rosetta, and the aarch64 binary on ubuntu-24.04-arm would close the gap. No full-cost Argon2 run would change this verdict. What is missing is running the programs on their platforms, which this audit cannot do locally either, so it also belongs in areasNotCovered.
- **Since 16808d9 no push or pull-request check runs the licence-notices gate or the vendored-Argon2 gate, so a Dependabot cargo update passes CI with THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md out of date and is caught only when a release tag's checks stop the release**: refuted: The placement it describes is real. My logged static trace (docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-fast-gate-coverage/static-trace.log, SHA-256 2bc28356bd5f6dc1...) shows the following at b6fca69:
- On a push or pull request, ci.yml runs only scripts/check-fast.sh (ci.yml:33, :71-73). scripts/check.sh runs only when RELEASE_CHECKS is true (:86-90).

That is not a defect, because no cited rule or contract is broken:
1. CI-04 says a push or pull-request workflow 'runs the fast checks only'. That limits what a push may run. It does not require any particular check on a push. The deferred list (vector replays, full-size runs, reproducible builds, browser suites) says what must not run on a push, not that everything else must.
2. Which gates count as fast is left to the repository. CORE-43 says 'the repository's AGENTS.md names them'. mhfe/AGENTS.md:10 names `scripts/check-fast.sh` as the fast checks CI runs on every push, and :20 classes `scripts/check.sh` as release-level. CORE-43 is also a rule for whoever finishes a change, not a CI requirement.
3. The project's own documents describe exactly this behaviour:
   - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:36-43 lists what check-fast.sh runs, without either gate, and says CI runs check.sh 'for a release tag and by hand'.
   - DEVELOPMENT.md:146-151 and vendor/phc-winner-argon2.md:72-76 say check.sh and both canonical-build stages run the vendored gate. That is true.
   - No document claims these gates, or the notices, are checked on a push or pull request.

4. CHECK-BLD-003 ('updater/checker coverage') and CHECK-BLD-005 ('mandatory verify jobs cannot be bypassed by the normal release path') are met. The checker exists, its self-test passes (baseline b05), and it passes at HEAD (b06). release.yml:95 and :105 make publish wait for ci.yml, which runs check.sh on the tag. The candidate itself says no stale notice can be published. AUD-023's Dependabot note was an informational observation, not a contract.

The impact claim is also wrong. The candidate says the stale notices are 'caught only when a release tag's checks stop the release'. But docs/RELEASING.md:14-16 requires running `scripts/check.sh` locally before tagging, and that runs both gates. A stale notice therefore stops the documented procedure before any tag exists.

The cited location scripts/check-fast.sh:88-118 does not exist (the file has 49 lines). The harness fast-gate-coverage.py only tests the tautology 'gate string in check-fast.sh'.

What remains is a judgement call: both gates take about a second and could run on pull requests, so a Dependabot cargo PR would fail until THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is regenerated. Under the rule that coverage gaps without a broken rule or contract are observations, it belongs in observations (CI coverage, info), not in findings.
- **argon2id's SAFETY argument holds only when threads equal lanes, which nothing enforces: with fewer threads, a failed thread creation makes the vendored C code join threads that it has already joined**: refuted: Refuted as a finding. The C mechanism is real, but only for a narrower set of inputs than the candidate claims, and no code at b6fca69 passes those inputs.

(1) threads = 1 never reaches the threaded code. fill_memory_blocks sends threads == 1 to fill_memory_blocks_st (vendor/phc-winner-argon2/src/core.c:383-384), which creates and joins no thread. So the candidate's reproduction cannot happen: lanes 4, threads 1, a join at l = 1, then a failure at l = 2. Its impact claim that "the binding's own tests use the unsound combination" is also false. When threads exceeds lanes, argon2_ctx lowers threads to lanes (argon2.c:75-77). The second join needs 2 <= threads < lanes.

(2) Reproduction. docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/verify-argon2-threads/run.sh (README beside it) links probe.c with the unmodified vendored sources (argon2.c, core.c, encoding.c, thread.c, blake2b.c, ref.c). It uses -Wl,--wrap=pthread_create,--wrap=pthread_join: the create wrapper fails the Nth creation with EAGAIN, and the join wrapper counts joins of an already-joined handle. Log: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-argon2-threads/argon2-double-join.log with .command.json. It exits 1 by design and the log has SHA-256 b810e01c...
- threads 1 with lanes 3 or 4: 0 creations and 0 joins, even when the first creation would fail.
- threads equal to lanes (4/4 and 2/2), with a creation failure in the first or second slice: 0 second joins.
- lanes 4 with threads 2 or 3, and lanes 3 with threads 2: 1 or 2 second joins after a failed creation.

(3) Static trace of every Argon2Inputs built at b6fca69 (log threads-call-sites.log). Each one passes threads 1, threads equal to lanes, or threads above lanes (lowered to lanes by the C code):
- native.rs:146-147: lanes 4, threads 4.
- known_answers.rs:221-222 (RFC call): 4/4.
- known_answers.rs:276-278: lanes 4, threads 4 or 1.
- known_answers.rs:437-438: 2/2.
- ffi.rs:516-517 and :771-772: 4/4.
- ffi.rs:593-594: threads 1 or equal to lanes.
- ffi.rs:640: lanes 4, threads 1.
- ffi.rs:661: lanes 2, threads 4, lowered to 2.

So for every input that reaches the unsafe block at ffi.rs:180, the SAFETY argument holds: every running thread is joined and no invalid handle is passed. No undefined behaviour is reachable from production code or tests, even when a thread creation fails.

What remains: argon2id is pub(super), internal to the engine module. It neither states nor enforces the precondition "threads is 1 or at least lanes", on which the comment's words "which the C code never passes" depend. No input passed at b6fca69 breaks that precondition, so no defect follows from it. AUD-023 already recorded this as an informational observation (informationalObservations[76]). Under AUDIT_STANDARD.md's 'info' definition ("no demonstrated defect"), it belongs outside the findings list. Keep it as an observation, corrected on two points: the unsafe domain is 2 <= threads < lanes, not threads 1, and the tests do not use it. Adding an assertion or deriving threads from lanes would be a hardening improvement.
- **The WebAssembly bindings and the CLI count the words of phrases and containers themselves, by splitting text, instead of asking the library's types that read them**: refuted: I re-read every cited line at b6fca69. All nine expressions are there as the candidate says. The defect it claims, front ends bypassing the library's types for a word count, does not hold up. Evidence is in /home/user/.../mhfe/docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-reproduction-wordcount/, files split-count-sites.log, word-count-accessors.log and callers-at-hand.log, all exit 0.

(1) For 7 of the 9 sites, the value the front end holds has no word-count method it could call:
- search::Found has public fields only (src/search.rs:66-74).
- repair::Repaired has public fields only (src/repair.rs:321-332).
- wallet_check::NewPhrase has only phrase() and checked() (src/wallet_check.rs:360-375).
- encrypt.rs:427 counts the &str that the library's pre-check callback passes in (encrypt.rs:265-276).
- print_card at container_repair.rs:665 counts plain card text.
- inspectContainer: ContainerReading carries a count only in WrongLength (src/repair.rs:351-367).
CORE-14 asks callers to ask the owning type. A method that does not exist cannot be asked. Adding word_count() to these types is an extension of the API, which makes it an improvement, not a broken rule.

(2) The library has no single source for "how text divides into words" that the front ends could be bypassing. It splits and counts the same way in at least seven places: phrase.rs:41, rehearsal.rs:362 and :396, repair.rs:371, container.rs:206, operation.rs:291 and eff.rs:97. The accessors the recommended fix would have front ends call are themselves split(' ').count(): Sealed::container_words (operation.rs:290-291) and OriginalFacts::read (container.rs:206). The CORE-10 root cause the candidate names, "front ends instead of the library", is therefore misattributed. The candidate's own impact, a changed splitting rule leaving counts behind, applies just as much inside the library.

(3) No site decides anything from the count. CORE-14 forbids "deciding again from word counts or literals", for example what a container allows or which lengths a suite holds. Here each count is only printed in a heading or a JSON field. The text it counts is library output whose documented format is words "one space apart" (search.rs:67, repair.rs:322, wallet_check.rs:366, container.rs:69-71). Counting that text uses the documented contract.

(4) The two splitting rules both give the right answer for their inputs: single-spaced library text in one case, typed text read with the same split_whitespace as ContainerReading::read in the other. The candidate itself says no wrong count arises, so there is no defect to demonstrate. AUDIT_STANDARD.md puts such a record under severity info, outside the findings list. AUD-023 recorded the same matter as informational observation 25. CORE-14's wording gives no new basis: it targets decisions, not displayed counts.

Residue for observations, not a finding: two sites recount what the value already at hand answers, with identical results by construction.
- container_repair.rs:494/505 counts read.facts.words() although read.facts is a ContainerFacts with word_count() (container.rs:77). terminal.rs:610 in the same flow does use word_count().
- wallets.rs:113/149 counts wallet.phrase() although the wallet is a RecoveredPhrase with words() (mhfe.rs:134).

A separate lead outside this candidate's root cause: new_wallet.rs:164 types the literal "24 words" when it records the drawn phrase, three lines after showing a counted value (new_wallet.rs:337). This may deserve its own CORE-10 check (a value with a meaning typed as a literal).

What I reproduced (static trace at b6fca69, logged as docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verify-rekey-other-lengths/rekey-other-lengths-trace.log, exit 0, sha256 b94cc31c83e3d618...; probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verify-rekey-other-lengths/trace.sh):

   - Sealed::keep adds WordCount whenever other lengths exist (operation.rs:316-324), marked to keep apart (operation.rs:148-149; core.rs keep_json).
   - BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:879-885 requires the page to show that keep list in full.
   - The specification's overview (README.md:30-31) asks only that the software "asks at creation to note the word count". It does.
2. README.md:520-521, the re-encryption MUST. Rekey::seal runs the complete creation procedure, including the creation check.
3. DOC-06. The documents state exactly this behaviour: "After an encryption or a rekey, the result's otherLengths says the same, and keep then lists the word count" (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:898-900). Code and document agree.
4. CORE-01. Not engaged. The CLI calls the library's OriginalFacts::other_lengths_in, and no front end restates a rule.
5. Workspace rule "Every feature in the browser too". The warning is offered in the browser (otherLengths, plus a wordCount keep item marked apart). Only its moment differs, and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md already says the page has its own layout and screens.

Other points against a finding:
- Impact: no container is wrong and no recovery fails. The other lengths depend only on the phrase, not the password, so they are the same ones the original encryption reported.
- Harness: check C4 of the gap-1 harness only greps rekey()'s declaration for the text "otherLengths". It restates the design rather than testing a contract.
- Prior audit: AUD-023 recorded this same item as an informational observation, not a finding (AUD-023-2026-10-13.md:1313; JSON informationalObservations[66], CHECK-FUN-006). Nothing in this code path has changed since in a way that would raise it.

Suggested record: an observation (a parity improvement: an optional pre-seal value such as RecoveredJson.otherLengths).
- **What mhfe check says beside each outcome (what a match does not prove, why a recovery is not verified with the 16-bit check's false-pass odds, why nothing matched) is written only in the CLI binary; the browser result and the page duties give a page none of it, and MhfeClient.parameters() lacks the wallet check's size**: refuted: I re-read every cited location at b6fca69 and logged a static trace with run-logged.sh: docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/verifier-check-outcome-limits/static-trace.log (probe at /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/aud024/verifier-check-outcome-limits/probe.sh, exit 0). The CLI text is as quoted: check.rs:483-495 no_match_reason, :500-526 not_verified_reason and :595-606 match_limit. The check() result is also as described: { outcome, path, evidence }, with no reason (src/wasm_api/core/check.rs:12-38). Even so, the candidate's central claims do not hold.

(1) The package does give a page what each outcome and reference does and does not prove:
- Fingerprint: "quick but weaker" (web/client.d.ts:274) and "(quick, weaker)" (web/client.js:460).
- { words }: "confirms the password, not the wallet" (client.d.ts:284-285).
- notVerified: "a wrong password gives one too; a pass of the 16-bit check does not verify it", and for several lengths "the page says so" (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:181-184; client.d.ts:597-603; client.js:466-468).
- doesNotMatch: defined at BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:185-187.
- The once-in-65,536 odds, with walletCheckBits: BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:941-942 and client.js:609.
- The page duties tell the page to show the three outcomes apart as the CLI does (:918-922). They also tell it to link each topic to its README section as the CLI's "More:" lines do (:815-816), and the link table maps "What a check can and cannot tell" to README#mhfe-check. That is exactly the style::more(readme::CHECK) line the CLI prints after these outcomes. README.md:233-264 then says that a fingerprint is only 32 bits, what "not verified" means, that the phrase + passphrase check does not identify the wallet, and that a mismatch cannot tell which input is wrong. So "give a page none of it" is false.

(2) The spec citations are not breached:
- README.md:477-491 defines what the rehearsal check reports: "matches" for exactly one verified reading, "does not match" when it gives no reading, plus a closed list of facts. So a page that shows "matches" for a built-in check uses the spec's own word. That does not describe a verifier match as confirmation of the wallet's identity, which is what :437-438 forbids.
- :484-485 and :709-711 are descriptions, not duties to display anything.
- :419-420 ("say that the password or a setting is probably wrong…") is a recovery length rule. For the check, :489-490 replaces it with its own report ("When it gives no reading, it reports 'does not match'"). The library's decrypt path gives that sentence anyway (src/error.rs:340-344, VerifierMismatch).

(3) MhfeClient.parameters() lacking walletCheckBits breaks no rule. The value has one source, MhfeWallet.parameters().walletCheckBits (src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:32,52), and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:941 directs pages there. The candidate's harness check C2 only tests where this key lives, so it is an improvement, not a defect.

(4) The CORE-01 part is the CLI deciding from its Choice enum what a match proves, and match_limit's dead WalletCheck row (check.rs:595-606). That is the already confirmed finding "mhfe check decides from its own Choice enum which reference proves the wallet, instead of asking Reference::identifies_wallet, and that table's wallet-check row is dead". not_verified_reason and no_match_reason only word library outcome data (CheckEvidence::matching_lengths, wallet_check::WALLET_CHECK_ODDS). CORE-01 allows that: front ends "translate input and output".

What remains is a matter of documentation style: the page duties could ask for the CLI's one-line hints in place, not only through the README link. That belongs in observations, not findings.
