### Coordinator's comparison in place of the final skeptic

The final skeptic agent did not run: the owner stopped the workflow during the second completeness round to save resources. The coordinator compared all 159 confirmed findings instead, by category, title, affected locations and rule: no two share one root cause (related ones, such as the stale comments or retyped values of different areas, need separate fixes and stay separate, as in AUD-023), none duplicates a holding AUD-023 fix, and severities follow the skeptics' calibration; one finding was marked release-blocking.

### Assessment and limitations

159 findings are confirmed, each by an independent skeptic. 6 medium, 153 low. The baseline (26 commands) passed. What was not run or not covered:

- Full-size Argon2 work was not run: the vector replays, the independent checkers' full runs and the terminal suite's --full cases (owner's choice; the machine's memory was shared with the review agents).
- The canonical Docker build was not run; the canonical build was reviewed statically.
- macOS and Windows were reviewed in the code only; no run on those systems.
- Reviewers and skeptics are AI agents (claude-opus-5-5); this is not an independent expert review or a certification. Reasoning effort was not retained by the client.
- The coding guide changed during the audit: CORE-15 (commit f09d363 of the workspace repository, 2026-10-14 06:51 UTC) now lets a function that is one whole reach 150 lines, with gates at 150; every agent read the new text. mhfe's gates were still set to 100 at the reviewed commit (observation).
- Physical erasure of memory, allocator copies and terminal buffers were not measured.
- The second completeness round (six gap reviewers) and the final skeptic agent were stopped on the owner's decision to save resources; the six gaps that round named are listed but not reviewed, and the coordinator compared the confirmed findings for duplicates and severity instead of the final skeptic.
- Not covered: secrets-native: Windows and macOS builds were reviewed from source only (no host): the swap and protection findings for those systems are static, and hidden_input/windows.rs was not executed.
- Not covered: secrets-native: No command was run at suite cost (2 GiB Argon2) under the audit rules: prompts that follow a recovery (decrypt's passphrase, rekey's new password, further hidden wallets) and end-to-end secret lifetimes past the first prompt are inferred from the code paths shown cheaply at the first prompt; no heap or /proc/self/mem scan of a full recovery was made.
- Not covered: secrets-native: The check-word label residue was measured with the freed-block criterion on a copy of the format strings, not inside the binary, and no scan of surviving freed bytes was repeated.
- Not covered: secrets-native: Landlock ABI 1-2 behaviour (truncate by path allowed) comes from the kernel documentation; the host has ABI 8.
- Not covered: secrets-native: zram writeback was checked on synthetic /proc and /sys trees only; no host with a real zram writeback device was available.
- Not covered: secrets-native: Library modules owned by core-crypto (feistel.rs, mhfe.rs, rehearsal.rs, rekey.rs, search.rs, wallet.rs, wallet_check.rs, random.rs, container.rs, packing.rs, new_password.rs and their known_answers modules) were scanned for wipe and copy patterns by grep and read in part, not in full.
- Not covered: secrets-native: CLI modules read only in part: check.rs, rekey.rs (lines 1-129, 420-748), container_repair.rs, container_search.rs (after line 130), settings.rs (lines 215-336, 500-626), style.rs beyond out/paint/boxed_words, flow.rs (after line 140), self_test.rs, test_tools.rs, made_password.rs tests, diceware.rs (lines 1-120, 300-333); serve.rs was not read (no secret, outside this role).
- Not covered: secrets-native: The browser package and its WebAssembly memory are outside this role; AUD-023-DOC006 was checked in the documents only.
- Not covered: secrets-native: Typed-ahead keys (AUD-023-UI003) were checked statically, not re-run in a pseudo-terminal.
- Not covered: browser-isolation: The minified Emscripten Argon2 builds (dist/core/argon2-mt.js, argon2-st.js) were checked by token scans and at the replaced loader texts, not read line by line; scripts/build-argon2-wasm.sh and the Emscripten flags were not reviewed.
- Not covered: browser-isolation: The wasm-bindgen glue in dist/runtime/worker.js was read for its helpers, import table, session classes and a sample of bindings, not every generated function (they follow one generated pattern).
- Not covered: browser-isolation: No real-browser run by this role: termination, memory freeing after terminate, garbage collection, CSP enforcement in workers and nested Argon2 lane workers were not observed directly; the in-process Node harness is not a browser, and the baseline's Chromium and Firefox run (b20) was relied on.
- Not covered: browser-isolation: No suite-cost Argon2 ran: residue scans and probes use 256 KiB/1-pass rounds and Node's WebAssembly instance; a terminated browser worker's freed memory was not inspected.
- Not covered: browser-isolation: Windows and macOS behaviour of both launchers (drive-relative names, NTFS streams, console colours, the opener) was assessed by code reading only; Python 3.8 compatibility was not run (only 3.14.4 is installed).

Conformance at full cost rests on the published records and the reduced-cost oracle.

## Remediation continuation

This is the uncommitted remediation of AUD-024, performed sequentially by Codex without a new
audit or subagents. The finding register above preserves the discovery snapshot; current per-ID
dispositions are in the JSON report's `remediation` array. No commit, push, tag or release was made.

- **140** findings are verified within the authorized scope. SEC007 excludes the owner-deferred
  Windows extension.
- **9** have working implementations and reduced Node class/worker coverage, with actual
  Chromium/Firefox verification pending separate approval: ARC003, ARC005, ARC006, ARC007, ARC036,
  ARC038, ARC047, ARC048 and ARC050. They are recorded as `fixed`, not `verified`.
- **9** remain deferred by the owner: SEC010, SEC012, BLD007, BLD009, ARC001, ARC013, ARC014,
  ARC023 and ARC052. UI019 retains the frame around phrases.

The current source fingerprint is `89da154e662ad2380b463454fa5b1916e012fc8c226f104463bc3b62c2ea3b8a`. Its local, ignored per-file manifest is
`AUD-024-evidence/codex-remediation-source.json`; local test-artifact hashes are in
`codex-remediation-artifacts.json`. The JSON continuation records their SHA-256 and the original
commands, UTC times, exit codes and log hashes. Raw outputs and execution adapters stay in ignored local storage. Reproducible in-place probes
are retained in [the continuation harness](AUD-024-harnesses/codex-remediation/README.md).

The fast gates, native known-answer checks, four independently linked WASM modules, fresh browser
package build and reduced Node class/worker checks pass. The native startup budget passes. The
release test CLI rebuilt to exactly the same bytes used by the PTY checks. New cases executed 21
required command/flag pairs; independent negative controls catch a stale `--new-pim` and an ignored
`decrypt --passphrase-used`. Every deliberately changed source byte was restored.

Default terminal coverage is segmented: the initial prefix, corrected middle tail and final tail
cover every case. The first two runs exposed stale expectations for the private-result refusal at
`TERM=dumb` and the library-owned zero-gap error; both were corrected without removing the refusal,
input-editor or terminal-restoration assertions. No clean all-in-one final rerun is claimed. Test
names now describe behaviour, and an AST check preserves the original calls' order.

Shared public inputs, fingerprints, Unicode/NFKD data, counters, repair tables, vector lookup, hash
adapters and damage application have one source. All distinct independent repair cases remain in
the full-tier table. The self-test reports `SELF_TEST_ROUNDS`; help facts derive from their owning
constants. A 37-site question/option inventory and actual clap-option checks guard CLI coverage.
The ordinary 50-token copy gate passes; the 30-token diagnostic retains unrelated overlaps and is
not claimed clean.

Python uses the owner's agreed 99-column code and 72-column prose widths, enforced with AST-based
controls. Executable ASTs were compared during wrapping. Checker/source identities changed;
retained full-cost records are historical and are not represented as fresh results for this tree.
The owner subsequently authorized commits; see the publication checkpoint below.

No full-cost vector replay, `--full` terminal cases, canonical Docker build, or Windows/macOS run
was performed. Chromium/Firefox approval remains pending. The specification's current uncommitted
guessing-bounds text was rechecked; suite 3's stated random-oracle games do not extend to suite 4.
The handover's recheck after the specification commit remains applicable. This remediation does
not establish release-level verification or that every possible defect has been found.

Final bookkeeping checks pass: `final-remediation-fast-8` (exit 0) and the full metadata/schema
checks (exit 0). A later tooling-only edit retains the baseline policy check for `fixed`/`verified`
rows; `final-audit-policy-scope` verifies that final checker, schema, code rules and whitespace.
Native/browser sources and test artifacts did not change after the fast run. The failed earlier
metadata run remains recorded: it mistook historical DOC006 evidence for this report's own policy.
